Neque aliter S. Sanctus ipse exponit per os Dauidis Psal. 22. Reminiscentur & conuertentur ad Iehouam omnes fines terræ & inclinabunt se coram te vniuersa familiæ gentium. Per fidem enim & conuersionem, omnes gentes ad terminos vsque terræ, fiunt hæreditas atque peculium Dei: quæ peculiaris olim dignitas erat Israëlis. Cuius gratiæ intuitu Abrahamo etiam promissum fuit, quod mundi hæres futurus esset. Verum interim est, quod ad dominium, omnia Christo esse subiecta; non tantum omnes homines, verum etiam quæcunque alia in cœlo & in terra.
units.tr: I grant it: but not of all human beings whom each nation contains. For the apostolic teaching, says Augustine in book 1 of On the Sermon on the Mount, calls adoption that by which we are called to an eternal inheritance, so that we may be fellow-heirs of Christ and, as sons with God, enjoy eternal life, reformed in the knowledge of him to the image of God. But this is not for all. Hence, as the same writer explains, the sense is: "Ask of me," that is, that the nations may be joined to the Christian name and so be redeemed from death and possessed by God; "and I will give you the nations as your inheritance," which you may possess, of course, for their salvation, so that spiritual things may bear fruit for you. Nor does the Holy Spirit himself explain it otherwise through the mouth of David in Psalm 22: "All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to Jehovah, and the whole family of the nations shall bow down before you." For through faith and conversion, all nations to the very ends of the earth become the inheritance and peculiar possession of God, which was once the peculiar dignity of Israel. In view of this grace it was also promised to Abraham that he would be "the heir of the world." It is true, however, that as regards dominion, all things are made subject to Christ, not only all human beings but also whatever else is in heaven and on earth.

units.la: Quod vltimò affertur de hirco emissario, Levit. 16. quod quemadmodum hirco isti imponebantur peccata omnia filiorum Israël portanda in desertum; ita etiam Christus peccata omnia populi portauerit & abstulerit; nostram, non aduersarij sententiam confirmat. Neque enim omnium hominum peccata, sed Israëlis duntaxat, hirco imponebantur. Similiter Christus abstulit peccata populi Christianorum: qui testante Apostolo, est Israël Dei, præfiguratus per carnalem illum Israël.
units.tr: Lastly, what is brought forward about the scapegoat in Leviticus 16, namely that just as all the sins of the children of Israel were laid upon that goat to be carried into the wilderness, so Christ also bore and took away all the sins of the people, confirms our view and not the opponent's. For the sins of all human beings were not laid on the goat, but only those of Israel. Likewise Christ took away the sins of the people of the Christians, who, as the Apostle testifies, are the Israel of God, prefigured by that fleshly Israel.

units.la: Atque hæc de prima classe argumentorum. Vbi iam æquus lector iudicet, nobisne an aduersario probra adhæreant, quibus nos conspuere voluit; quasi videlicet necesse habeamus linguam Spiritus sancti per totum Evangelium corrigere & emendare, interpolare, succidere, colaphis denique inceßere. Nugæ.
units.tr: So much for the first class of arguments. Now let the fair reader judge whether the shame adheres to us or to the opponent, with which he wished to spatter us, as if we forsooth had to correct and emend the tongue of the Holy Spirit throughout the whole Gospel, interpolate, cut back, and finally assail it with blows. Trifles.

units.la: AD SECVNDÆ CLASSIS ARGVMENTA.
units.tr: TO THE ARGUMENTS OF THE SECOND CLASS.

units.la: Caput VIII.
units.tr: Chapter VIII.

units.la: Quo solutiones continentur generales.
units.tr: Which contains general solutions.

units.la: Responsum adhuc est ad τὰ καθόλου dicta: Sequitur altera classis, qua adversarius peculiariter probare instituit, reprobos, seu ut in Compendio thesium loquitur, non credetes, æque à Christo redemtos: atque illos qui per fidem salutis in Christo participes fiunt.
units.tr: A reply has so far been made to the universal [τὰ καθόλου] statements. Now comes the second class, by which the opponent sets out to prove in particular that the reprobate, or, as he puts it in his Compendium of Theses, the unbelievers, were redeemed by Christ no less than those who become partakers of salvation in Christ through faith.

units.la: Antequam autem loca scripturæ, quæ hac classe proferuntur, singillatim expendamus, in genere notandum est, omnia illa loca esse particularia de aliquibus tantummodo reprobis, & quidem dem eiuscemodi, qui ad tempus bonis in Ecclesia permixti sunt, atque in credentium numero habentur, quantisper contrarium in ipsis non apparet. Ex particularibus vero,cum vel ambæ, vel alterutra præmissarum talis est, costat non sequi conclusionem vniuersalem, qualis hæc est aduersarij, omnes reprobos & incredulos non minus quàm electos & verè credetes redemtione & remissione peccatorum in Christo habere. Vt hanc probet, aliis argumentis per totam hanc classem opus erat.
units.tr: Before we weigh the passages of Scripture that are brought forward in this class one by one, it must be noted in general that all those passages speak of particular reprobates only, and indeed of those who for a time are mixed with the good in the Church and are counted among the believers, for as long as nothing contrary appears in them. From particular premises, when both or either of the premises is of this kind, it does not follow the universal conclusion that the opponent draws: that all the reprobate and unbelievers have redemption and forgiveness of sins in Christ no less than the elect and truly believing. To prove this he needed other arguments, and he needed them throughout this whole class.

units.la: Deinde, cùm omnibus iis locis agitur de iis qui credetibus & sanctificatis in Christo annumeratur, & postea vocationis suæ immemores, in graues lapsus incidùt; aut etiá de veritate plane deficiũt, præpostere facit, qui inde contendit, redemtionem vniuersaliter tam esse incredulorum quàm verè credentium. Etenim probationes quæ prose-runtur, descriptiones habent beneficij Christi pro statu fidei, & ijs accommodatas, qui Ecclesiæ Dei, qui fidelibus & sanctis in Christo, qui dilectis & electis
units.tr: Next, since in all those places the subject is those who are counted among the believers and sanctified in Christ, and who afterwards, forgetful of their calling, fall into grievous lapses or altogether fail in the truth, he acts absurdly when he infers from this that redemption belongs universally to unbelievers just as much as to those who truly believe. For the proofs that are adduced contain descriptions of the benefit of Christ suited to the state of faith, and suited to those who were counted among the Church of God, among the faithful and holy in Christ, among the beloved and elect of God,

units.la: Rom.1. Eph.1. Colos.1. Psalm. 1. ðis Dei accensebantur, ob externam fidei & refipiscentiæ professionem & susceptum sacri baptismatis lauacrum. Ex talibus enim, pro vt caritatis dictat ingenium, Ecclesia iudicat, occulta interim Deo scrutatori cordium, relinquens, qui nouit suos, & scit discernere peruersos & rectos corde.
units.tr: Rom. 1; Eph. 1; Col. 1; Ps. 1 — on account of their outward profession of faith and repentance and their reception of the washing of holy baptism. For the Church judges such persons as charity dictates, while leaving the hidden things to God, the searcher of hearts, who knows his own and knows how to distinguish the perverse from the upright in heart.

units.la: Animaduertendum porro est, sic labentes esse aut electos aut reprobos. Nam etiam electi & vere credentes quandoque in peccata ruunt contra conscientiam, & enormiter à recta via exorbitant: sicut Dauid & Petrus: attamen nō errant finaliter, sed reparantur & in viam redeunt, antequàm vita ista finiatur, ac deleta, quæ intercurrerat, iniquitate, vsque in finem perseuerantia ijs deputatur: vt copiose August. docet de correptione & gratia cap. 7.
units.tr: It must further be noted that those who fall in this way are either elect or reprobate. For even the elect and truly believing sometimes rush into sins against conscience and stray greatly from the right way, as David and Peter did. Yet they do not err to the end: they are restored and return to the way before this life ends, and when the iniquity that had intervened has been blotted out, perseverance to the end is credited to them, as Augustine teaches at length in On Correction and Grace, ch. 7.

units.la: Firmum quippe stat fundamentum Dei, habens sigillum hoc, Nouit Dominus qui sint sui. Et vt Dominus ipse in Euangelio dicit, fieri non potest vt electi seducantur: nempe finaliter. Horum enim si quisquam perit, fallitur Deus, & vitio vincitur humano. Sed nunquam fallitur, aut re vlla vincitur Deus: Ex electis igitur nullus perit. Neque id tantum, sed etiam vere credentes (cum viua in Christum fides non omnium, sed electorum sit) virtute Dei ad salutem custodiuntur per fidem, vt Petrus testatur. Atque idem volunt promissiones; Dabo iis cor vnum, & viam vnam, & feriam cum eis pactum sempiternum, & timorem meum dabo in cor eorum, vt non recedant a me. Item, Ego plantabo eos in terra sua, nec euellentur vltra e terra sua, dicit Dominus. Qui sunt isti nisi fideles, plantati in atriis Domini, & Christo vera fide insiti? Et teste Iohanne, qui natus est ex Deo, non peccat: quia semen Dei manet in eo: nec potest peccare, eo quod ex Deo natus est. Neque enim ex mortali, sed immortali semine renascimur per sermonem Dei viui manetis in aeternum. Quod cum ita sit, verbum illud semel regenerante fide apprehensum, & corde susceptum, manet in aeternum, nec potest amplius excidere, vt recte Lutherus in eum locum annotauit.
units.tr: For the firm foundation of God stands, bearing this seal: The Lord knows who are his. And as the Lord himself says in the Gospel, it is not possible for the elect to be led astray, that is, finally. For if any of these perish, God is deceived and overcome by human fault. But God is never deceived, nor is he overcome by anything; therefore none of the elect perishes. And not only this, but also those who truly believe (since living faith in Christ belongs not to all but to the elect) are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation, as Peter testifies. The promises also mean the same: I will give them one heart and one way, and I will make with them an everlasting covenant, and I will put my fear in their hearts, so that they do not depart from me. Likewise: I will plant them in their own land, and they shall no more be plucked up out of their land, says the Lord. Who are these, except the faithful, planted in the courts of the Lord and grafted into Christ by true faith? And, as John witnesses, whoever is born of God does not sin, because the seed of God remains in him; nor can he sin, because he is born of God. For we are born again not of mortal but of immortal seed, through the living word of God that abides forever. Since this is so, that word, once apprehended by regenerating faith and received in the heart, abides forever and cannot fall away again, as Luther rightly noted on that passage.

units.la: Quod obiicitur, nonnullos à fide deficere, & naufragium eius facere, scien-dum est fidem sæpè accipi pro doctrina fidei. Et sic multi à fide deficiunt, à doctrina quam profitebantur resilientes, item doctrinis adhærentes dæmonio-rum, dum Christum videri voluntse-ctari: quemadmodum Chrysostom. & Theophyl. ista explicant: & apud Cy-ril. Alexandrinum habetur. Hyme-næum & Alexadrum circa fidem nau-fragium fecisse, quòd dicerent resurre-ctionem iam factam esse. Eodem reci-dit responsio, aliud esse fidem historicam, aliud fidem iustificantem & salutiferam. Seu aliud esse credere Deo, aliud credere Deum, aliud credere in Deum. Credere Deo, est credere vera esse quæ loquitur, quod & mali multi possunt. Credere autem ipsum esse Deum, & dæmones possunt. Credere vero in Deum, soli nouerunt qui diligunt illum, & non solùm nomine Christiani sunt, sed & factis & vita. Fides enim sine dilectione, fides dæmonis & inanis est, cum dilectione, fides Christiani. Atque hæc fides
units.tr: As for the objection that some fall away from the faith and make shipwreck of it, it must be known that "faith" is often taken for the doctrine of faith. In this sense many fall away from the faith, shrinking back from the doctrine they professed, and cleaving to the doctrines of demons while wishing to seem to follow Christ; so Chrysostom and Theophylact explain these things, and it is found in Cyril of Alexandria that Hymenaeus and Alexander made shipwreck concerning the faith in saying that the resurrection had already taken place. The same answer comes to this: that one thing is historical faith, another justifying and saving faith. Or that one thing is to believe God, another to believe that God is, another to believe in God. To believe God is to believe that what he says is true, which many wicked people can also do. To believe that he is God the demons too can do. To believe in God, only those know who love him, and who are Christians not only in name but also in deeds and life. For faith without love is the faith of a demon and empty; faith with love is the faith of a Christian. And this faith

units.la: Aduersus Anthropomorph. cap.9.
units.tr: Against the Anthropomorphites, ch. 9.

units.la: Fidei diuersa significatio.
units.tr: The different meanings of faith.

units.la: Auguft.de tempore serm. 181. fides Christiani in fundamento posita, neminem perire permittit, vt scribit Augustinus, quod ipsû &Lutheri quædam glossa in 7. Matth. confirmat, his verbis, Ea fides, quæ per opera efficax est, cor purificat: & eiusmodi probitas immota stat contra omnem impetum ventorum, & potestiam inferorum: quia super petram Christum fundata est. Alia ratio est fidem duntaxat habentium historicam, dæmoniacam atque mortuam, & propterea simulatam & minimè verâ, quia viva non est, licet interim vera dici possit, quantum ad notitias veras & consentientes diuinis patefactionibus.
units.tr: Augustine, On Time, sermon 181. The faith of the Christian, grounded on the foundation, permits no one to perish, as Augustine writes; which a certain gloss of Luther on Matthew 7 also confirms, in these words: That faith which is effective through works purifies the heart; and such integrity stands unmoved against every assault of the winds and the power of the underworld, because it is founded upon Christ the rock. Another account is that those who have only historical faith, demonic and dead, are therefore feigned and not true, since it is not living, although it may still be called true as far as true knowledge is concerned and agrees with the divine revelations.

units.la: Hæc de perseuerantia electorum & verè credentium, perspicuè confirmat Heerbrandus Disputatione Tubingensi de Electione, quam hic adduco, vt minus nobis succenséant disputatores noui, qui contrarias nunc ex eadem schola opiniones disseminant. Sic enim statuit: ad vitam prædestinatos finaliter non excidere: tales verò esse, qui vera fide se Christo insitos intelligant: quod autem multi deficiât, qui fidem habuisse scribûtur, eos tempe- N poraporaneam tantum habuisse fidem, absq; vera animi regeneratione. Hæc illè, disput. dicta, thesibus 40. 45. & 47.
units.tr: Heerbrand clearly confirms these things about the perseverance of the elect and of those who truly believe, in his Tübingen Disputation on Election, which I cite here so that the new disputants, who now spread opinions contrary to one another from the same school, may be less angry with us. For he lays down this: that those predestined to life do not finally fall away; that such are those who understand that they are grafted into Christ by true faith; and that the many who are written of as having had faith fall away because they had only temporary faith, without true regeneration of soul. Thus he, in the disputation, in theses 40, 45 and 47.

units.la: Iam, quod alterum membrum erat, de reprobis aliquandiu in Ecclesia inter filios Dei locum obtinentibus, prodentes et redemptionis be tenenda est regula 1. Iohan. 2. E nobis egressi sunt, sed non erant ex nobis. Nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum. Loquitur de iis, quemadmodum Augustinus locum istum pulcre enarrat, qui forte exeuntes non redeunt, qui & intus cum sunt, no ex nobis sunt, nec ut membra intus sunt in corpore Christi, sed ut humores mali, quandoquidem adhuc curatur corpus ipsius, & sanitas perfecta non erit nisi in resurrectione mortuorum. Interim quia hominibus manifesti non sunt eiusmodi, donec exeundo & non reuertendo manifestentur, plane dicuntur credentes, conuersi, iustificati, sanctificati, redemti, discipuli & membra Christi, templa & filij Dei, imo electi Dei: plane inquam ista appellantur, quos eandem fidem & conuersationem nobiscum ChriChristianam profiteri cernimus, licet interim vere apud eum, qui cogitationes & cogitationes cordis diiudicat, & cuius oculis nota & patentia sunt omnia, sæpe nō sint, quod vocantur. Rectè Ambrosius li. 1. Com. in Luc. cap. 1. Non omnis, inquit, qui iustus est ante homines, iustus est ante Deum. Aliter vident homines, aliter videt Deus: homines in facie, Deus in corde, idem arbiter mentis & facti. Perfecta igitur laus est, ante Deum iustum esse. Et multis id ipsum docet Augustinus de corrept. & grat. cap. 7. & 9. Et citat huc dictum Christi, Si in sermone meo manseritis, vere discipuli mei eritis. Cūdti quidem Christo nomen dates, discipuli eius, & Christiani à Christo vocari solet, ratione professionis: sed ij demum vere sunt quod vocantur, qui in sermone eius manent. Sicut & Apostolus ait, nos domus Christi sumus, si fiduciam & spem illam de qua gloriamur, ad finem usque firmam tenuerimus. Et mox, Christi participes facti sumus, si modo principium illud quo sustentamur, firmum tenuerimus ad finem usque. Sin minus, Christi quidem confortes, domestici & filij & hæredesDei, ciues sanctorum, redemti & credentes appellamur coram hominibus, sed non veré id sumus coram Domino, dictu-ro olim, nunquam novi vos, discedite à me qui facitis iniquitatem. Tertullianus de præscript. hæret. in principio: Nemo sapiens est, nemo fidelis, nemo maior nisi Christianus. Nemo autem Christianus nisi qui ad finem usque perseuerauerit. Tu ut homo, extrinsecus unumquemque nosti, putas quod vides: Vides autem quousque oculos habes. Sed oculi Domini alti. Homo in faciem, Deus in præcordia contemplatur: & ideo cognoscit Dominus qui sunt eius &c. Præclarè etiam Chrysostomus in 7. Matth. Ecclesiam quam Christus fundauit, non pluuia mendacis doctrina corrumpit, neque Diabolicus flatus impellit, neque fluminum violentorum impetus monet. Nec est contrarium, ait, quod nonnulli de Ecclesia cadunt. Non enim omnes qui Christiani dicuntur, Christi sunt: sed nouit Dominus qui sunt eius. Multi siquidem nomine Christiano palliati, ut loquitur Augustinus, sub velamine religionis occulte mali sunt, nomen Christi in labiis, non in corde habentes, de quibus dictum est, Populus iste labiis me honorat, sed cor ipsorum procul est à me.
units.tr: Now, as to the other member, concerning the reprobate who for some time hold a place among the sons of God in the Church, the rule to be kept is 1 John 2: They went out from us, but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would certainly have remained with us. He speaks of those who perhaps go out and do not return, who, while they are within, are not of us and are not within as members of the body of Christ, but as bad humours, since the body of Christ is still being healed and perfect health will not come until the resurrection of the dead. Meanwhile, because such people are not manifest to men until by going out and not returning they are revealed, they are plainly called believers, converted, justified, sanctified, redeemed, disciples and members of Christ, temples and sons of God, indeed elect of God: plainly I say they are so called, since we see them professing the same faith and way of life with us, although before him who judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart, and to whose eyes all things are known and open, they are often not what they are called. Ambrose rightly says in his first book on Luke, ch. 1: Not everyone who is righteous before men is righteous before God. Men see in one way, God sees in another: men see the face, God sees the heart, the same judge of mind and deed. Perfect praise, therefore, is to be righteous before God. Augustine teaches the same thing in many places, On Correction and Grace, chs. 7 and 9. And he cites the saying of Christ: If you remain in my word, you will truly be my disciples. Those who have given their name to Christ are called his disciples and Christians, by reason of their profession; but they truly are what they are called only if they remain in his word. As the Apostle also says: We are the house of Christ, if we hold fast the confidence and the hope of which we boast firmly to the end. And soon after: We have become partakers of Christ, if we hold firmly to the beginning by which we are sustained, to the end. If not, we are indeed called companions of Christ, members of the household, sons and heirs of God, citizens of the saints, redeemed and believers before men, but we are not truly so before the Lord, who will one day say: I never knew you; depart from me, you who work iniquity. Tertullian, On the Prescription of Heretics, at the beginning: No one is wise, no one faithful, no one greater, except the Christian. But no one is a Christian except one who has persevered to the end. You, as a man, know each person only from outside; you think what you see. But you see only as far as your eyes reach. The eyes of the Lord, however, are high. Man looks at the face, God at the inmost heart; and therefore the Lord knows who are his, etc. Chrysostom too says admirably, on Matthew 7: The Church that Christ founded is not corrupted by the rain of false doctrine, nor pushed by the devilish blast, nor moved by the rush of violent rivers. Nor is it contrary, he says, that some fall away from the Church. For not all who are called Christians belong to Christ; but the Lord knows who are his. For many, cloaked under the Christian name, as Augustine puts it, are secretly evil under the veil of religion, having the name of Christ on their lips but not in their heart; of whom it is said: This people honours me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

units.la: Lutherus quoque in Psalm.2.in illud, Ego constitui regem meum super Sion, montem sanctum, discernit sanctitatem generalem, & specialem. Generalis est, cū aliqua Ecclesia constans bonis & malis, sancta vocari solet: Specialis vero est illa, qua veri credentes vere & re ipsa sanctificati sunt coram Deo, per Spiritum S. cum reliqui tantum coram hominibus, professione & sacramētorum vsu, sancti nominentur, & pro sanctis habeantur. Et de seruo arbit. ca. 61. discernit iudiciū caritatis & fidei. Iudicium, seu, vt ipse loquitur, canon caritatis, sanctum vocat quemlibet baptizatum; quia caritas omnia credit, ac praesumit de proximis bona: canone autem fidei sanctus non est, nisi qui diuino iudicio talis declaratur, inquit.
units.tr: Luther also, in his commentary on Psalm 2, on the words "I have set my king upon Zion, my holy mountain," distinguishes a general and a special holiness. The general holiness is that by which a Church made up of good and bad people is usually called holy; the special holiness is that by which true believers are truly and in fact sanctified before God through the Holy Spirit, while the rest are called holy and regarded as holy only before men, by profession and by the use of the sacraments. And in On the Bondage of the Will, chapter 61, he distinguishes the judgment of charity from the judgment of faith. The judgment, or, as he himself calls it, the rule of charity, calls every baptized person holy, because charity believes all things and presumes good things of its neighbours; but by the rule of faith a person is not holy unless he has been declared such by the divine judgment, he says.

units.la: CAPVT IX.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX.

units.la: Examinantur scriptura quaedam dicta de redemtione reproborum.
units.tr: Certain passages of Scripture said about the redemption of the reprobate are examined.

units.la: His ita praemonitis pro generali solutione, nunc testimonia huius classis ordine percurramus.
units.tr: With these points set out beforehand as a general answer, let us now go through the testimonies of this class in order.

units.la: Primum citatur ex Heb.6. Fieri non potest, ut qui semel illuminati fuerint, gustarintque donum coeleste, & participes fuerint sancti Spiritus, si prolabantur, ut denuo renouentur ad resipiscentiam, rursum crucifigentes sibi ipsis filium Dei, & ignominia exponentes.
units.tr: The first is cited from Heb. 6. It is impossible that those who were once enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have been made partakers of the Holy Spirit, if they fall away, should be renewed again to repentance, crucifying again to themselves the Son of God, and exposing him to shame.

units.la: Qui hic describuntur, redemtionis sunt participes, & tamen reprobi. Sequitur conclusio particularis in tertia figura; Ergo aliqui reprobi sunt redeti.
units.tr: Those described here are partakers of redemption, and yet reprobate. The particular conclusion follows in the third figure: therefore some reprobate are redeemed.

units.la: Respondeo. Primum aduersarius debuit probare conclusionem uniuersale, non particularem, ut dictum est. Secundo ad minorem: qui post acceptam illuminationem prolabuntur, non statim reprobi iudicandi, & a gratia arcendi sunt, cum Montano & Nouato. Nam & electi graviter quandoque labuntur, sed denuo eriguntur à Domino.
units.tr: I answer: first, the opponent ought to have proved a universal conclusion, not a particular one, as has been said. Second, as to the minor premise: those who fall away after receiving enlightenment are not to be judged reprobate at once and shut out from grace, as Montanus and Novatian held. For the elect too sometimes fall grievously, but they are raised up again by the Lord.

units.la: Quod autem Apostolus relabentibus videtur adimere spem veniæ, omissis aliis expositionibus, Chrysostomus, Theodoritus, Theophylactus in commentarijs, & Epiphanius hær. 59. Augustinus in fine expositionis ad Rom. Ambro. lib. 2. de pœnit. cap. 2. aliique veteres magno consensu, & non inconcinnè locum intelligunt, quod videlicet baptismatis iteratio, non autem pœnitentiæ medicina ex Ecclesia auferatur: ne Iudæi existimarent sanctissimum baptismum esse similem baptismis Iudaicis, qui multi & frequentes adhibebantur. Sed ut semel Christus mortuus est, & mors ei amplius non dominatur: ita semel in morte Christi baptizamur lavacro regenerationis, & renovationis spiritus, & impossibile est, si prolabamur, denuo nos per id renovari ad pœnitentiam. Quod si quis illud tentet, Christum quantum in se est, denuo crucifigit & contemtui habet.
units.tr: As for the Apostle seeming to take away hope of pardon from those who fall back, leaving aside other interpretations, Chrysostom, Theodoret, Theophylact in commentaries, Epiphanius heresy 59, Augustine at the end of his exposition of Romans, Ambrose (book 2 on penance, chapter 2), and other ancient writers with great agreement, understand the passage, not without reason, to mean that the repetition of baptism, and not the remedy of repentance, is removed from the Church; so that the Jews would not think that most holy baptism was like the Jewish washings, which were applied many times and often. But as Christ died once, and death no longer has dominion over him, so we are baptized once into the death of Christ, by the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Spirit, and it is impossible, if we fall away, to be renewed again to repentance through that. Whoever tries it, crucifies Christ afresh as far as he is concerned and holds him in contempt.

units.la: Dehinc, ad maiorem: Licet non inuitus dem, Apostolum loqui de redem-tis, vel quasi redemtis, fecundum difcri-men electorum & reproborum prius explicatum, tamen probationes quae ab aduersario inducuntur, non militat. Harum prior est, illuminationem & participationem spiritus sancti, fructus esse redemtionis: fructuum autem redemtionis qui participes sunt, & ipsius redemtionis esse participes.
units.tr: Next, as to the major premise: although I readily grant that the Apostle is speaking of the redeemed, or those who are as if redeemed, according to the distinction between elect and reprobate explained earlier, yet the proofs the opponent brings forward do not hold. The first of these is that enlightenment and participation in the Holy Spirit are fruits of redemption; but those who share in the fruits of redemption are also sharers in redemption itself.

units.la: Refponfio: Paulus ad Coloff. 1. & alibi redemtionem definit remissione peccatorum: peccata autem alicui esse remissa, ac proinde eum iustum esse coram Deo, & haeredem vitae aeternae, non statim colligi ex eo potest, quod veritatis agnitione illustratus fit, aut alia aliqua dona Spiritus S. perceperit: multa quippe sunt dona spiritus communia pijs & impijs (Matth. 7. v. 22. & 1. Cor. 12, verf. 3.
units.tr: Response: Paul, to the Colossians 1, and elsewhere, defines redemption as the remission of sins. But it cannot be gathered at once from the fact that someone is illumined by the knowledge of the truth, or has received some other gifts of the Holy Spirit, that his sins are forgiven, and therefore that he is righteous before God and an heir of eternal life. For many gifts of the Spirit are common to the godly and the ungodly (Matt. 7:22 and 1 Cor. 12:3).

units.la: Posterior Huberi probatio talis est, Quod denuo fit, semel iam factum esse oportet. At perditi denuo fibiipfis crucifigunt filium Dei. Ergo iam ante ipsis crucifixus erat, ipsorum nemnempe, commodo & redemtione.
units.tr: Huber's second proof runs thus: what is done again must have been done once already. But the lost crucify the Son of God again to themselves. Therefore he had already been crucified by them, namely for their own benefit and redemption.

units.la: Sed sophisma hoc ex meris fallacijs, copositionis & dictionis confutū est & plus concludit quàm erat in præmissis. In minore illud denuo non construendū est cum sibiipsis, sed cum verbo crucifi-gunt: sicut græcè est vna voce ἀνασταυροῦν-τες. Quare tantum sequitur, si denuò crucifigitur, semel iam in crucem actū fuisse Christum. Deinde, cum reuera filium Dei in crucem agere nequeant homines pro sua libidine, correctionis loco additum est, quod sibi ipsis, id est quantum in se est, eum denuo crucifigant: eritque impius plane sensus, si exponas, quod sibi ipsis, id est, suo ipsorū commodo & redemtione Christum crucifigant denuò, sicut in conclusione accipitur.
units.tr: But this sophism is refuted by mere fallacies of composition and division, and it proves more than was in the premises. In the minor premise the word again is not to be construed with to themselves, but with the verb crucify; in Greek it is a single word, anastaurountes [ἀνασταυροῦντες]. So it follows only that if Christ is crucified again, he was once already put to the cross. Next, since men cannot in fact put the Son of God to the cross at their own pleasure, the phrase to themselves was added as a qualification, meaning that they crucify him again as far as it lies in them. And the sense would be plainly absurd if you explained to themselves as meaning that they crucify Christ again for their own advantage and redemption, as the conclusion takes it.

units.la: Alter locus est ad Heb.10. Cùm igitur, fratres, habeamus libertatem ingrediendi in sacrarium per sanguinem Iesu, accedamus cū vero corde & fiducia. Nam si vltrò peccauerimus post acceptam cognitionem veritatis, non adhuc reliqua est pro peccatis hostia. Et paulo post, quanto (putatis) acerbiori supplicio dignus censebitur, qui filium Dei conculcârit & sanguinem fœderis, per quem fuerat sanctificatus, profanum duxerit, & spiritum gratiæ contumelia affecerit?
units.tr: Another passage is Heb. 10. Since therefore, brethren, we have boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, let us draw near with a true heart and in full assurance of faith. For if we sin wilfully after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more sacrifice for sins. And a little later: Of how much sorer punishment, think you, will he be judged worthy who has trodden under foot the Son of God, and counted the blood of the covenant, by which he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?

units.la: Locum istum Hub. simpliciter intelligit de reprobis; sed non illico pro reprobis habendi, & à spe veniæ arcendi sunt cum Nouatianis, qui post veritatis cognitionem, scientes volentes forte labuntur. Quod autem dicitur ijs non esse reliquam hostiam pro peccatis, sed iudicij exspectationem, de hoc aliud aliis videtur: mihi tanquam simplicissimum probatur, non plures esse hostias pro peccato, vt olim sub vmbris legalibus: Christum semel oblatum, vt multorum peccata tolleret, non denuò pro peccatis, vt pro ijs iteratò moriatur, sed ad iudicium vęturum, in salutem quidem se exspectantibus, in suppliciû vero peccantibus: præsertim qui vltrò peccant post acceptam veritatis cognitionem. Intellige tamen conditionaliter, nisi scilicet pœnitentiam egerint, sicut rectè explicat Theophylactus, & scripturarum exigit consuetudo 1. Cor. 6. v. 6. v.9. Apocal. 22. v.15. Ier.18. v.7. Enimuero hos de quibus agit Apostolus, in numero redemtorum ponendos esse facile concedo ex fundamento prius tradito, quatenus videlicet eandem nobiscum fidem & conuersationé profitentes, pro fratribus nostris, pro domesticis & hæredibus Dei, proq; sanctificatis per sanguinem Christi agnoscere tenemur, donec forte manifestetur ex nobis non fuisse. Omnia certe ista, tàquam pro statu fidei, non autem infidelitatis, nedū reprobationis apud Apostolum dici, textus perspicuè ostedit.
units.tr: Huber takes this passage plainly to refer to the reprobate; but they are not at once to be regarded as reprobate and shut out from hope of pardon, with the Novatians, who, after knowing the truth, fall knowingly and willingly. As to what is said, that no sacrifice for sins remains for them but a fearful expectation of judgment, opinions differ on this. To me it is proved most simply that there are not many sacrifices for sin, as there were of old under the legal shadows; Christ, offered once to take away the sins of many, does not die again for sins so that he dies again for them, but is to come to judgment, bringing salvation to those who look for him, and punishment to those who sin; especially to those who sin wilfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth. Yet it should be understood conditionally, namely unless they repent, as Theophylact rightly explains, and the custom of the Scriptures requires (1 Cor. 6:9–10; Rev. 22:15; Jer. 18:7). Indeed, I readily concede that those of whom the Apostle speaks are to be counted among the redeemed, on the foundation laid down before: insofar, that is, as they profess the same faith and way of life as we do, and we are bound to acknowledge them as our brothers, members of our household and heirs of God, and sanctified by the blood of Christ, until perhaps it becomes plain that they were never of us. Certainly the text clearly shows that all these things are said by the Apostle with respect to the state of faith, not of unbelief, much less of reprobation.

units.la: Tertius locus est 1. Epistola ad Corinthios 3. Estis templum Dei, & Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis: si quis templum Dei destruit, destruet eum Deus.
units.tr: The third passage is 1 Cor. 3. You are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you. If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him.

units.la: Quod hic loquatur de reprobis, vt censet Hub. alienū est; loquitur enim de Ecclesia. Eam vocarat ædificationem Dei, nunc templum Dei vocat, pro vt alibi spirituale hoc ædificium & habitaculum Dei viuentis pluribus describitur. Comminatio autem pertinet net ad schismatum autores, qui mera ambitione Ecclesiam Corinthi, quam Deus sibi in templum confecrârat, per factiones distrahebât profanabantque.
units.tr: That this speaks of the reprobate, as Huber thinks, is beside the point; for it speaks of the Church. Having called it God's building, he now calls it God's temple, just as elsewhere this spiritual building and dwelling place of the living God is described at length. The threat, moreover, applies to the authors of schisms, who by sheer ambition divided and profaned the Church of Corinth, which God had consecrated to himself as a temple, by their factions.

units.la: Recurrit similis locus cap. 6. An ignoratis corpus vestrum esse templum Spiritus sancti, qui est in vobis? Ibi singulos credentes compellans, templa eos vocat Spiritus sancti: quemadmodû & membra Christi, inquiens: An ignoratis corpora vestra membra esse Christi? vt eo nimirum maiore folicitudine inquinamenta omnia carnis deuitent. Sed hinc non sequitur, aliquos vere membra Christi & templa Spiritus sancti existetes, perpetuò perituros. Fit quidem vt tales horribiliter quandoque se ipsos polluant, verum non finaliter. Documento est resipiscentia Dauidis: & attestantur promissiones: iustus fi ceciderit, non collidetur, quia Dominus eum sustentat, velut subiecta manu. Oues meas nemo rapiet e manu mea. Et apud Paulum, Dona & vocatio Dei sunt ἀμεταμέλητα. Vt autem in peccatis pereant, qui membra Christi & templa Dei reputabantur, nouum non est, sed
units.tr: A similar passage recurs in 1 Cor. 6. Do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you? There, addressing the believers one by one, he calls them temples of the Holy Spirit, just as he calls them members of Christ, saying: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? so that they might avoid all defilements of the flesh with the greater care. But it does not follow from this that some who are truly members of Christ and temples of the Holy Spirit will perish forever. It does happen that such people at times defile themselves dreadfully, but not finally. The repentance of David is a proof of this; and the promises bear witness: though the righteous fall, he shall not be cast down, for the Lord upholds him with his hand. No one shall snatch my sheep out of my hand. And in Paul: The gifts and calling of God are [ametamelēta] irrevocable. But that those who were counted members of Christ and temples of God should perish in their sins is not new; yet if they had been true members of the Church, they would surely have remained with us, as John says.

units.la: Psal. 37. 24. Iohan. 10. Rom. 11. 29. sed si ex veris Ecclesiæ membris fuisset, mansissent utique nobiscum, vt ait Iohannes. Enimuero sunt filij Dei, inquit Augustinus, qui nondum sunt nobis: & sunt rursus quidam, qui propter susceptam temporaliter gratiam filij Dei dicuntur a nobis, nec sunt tamen Deo. Sicut autem filij, ita etiam templa Dei, & membra Christi.
units.tr: Psalm 37:24; John 10; Rom. 11:29. Indeed, as Augustine says, there are children of God who are not yet ours; and there are again some who are called children of God by us because of grace received for a time, and yet are not so to God. Just as there are children of God, so too there are temples of God and members of Christ.

units.la: Eadem est responsio ad dicta: peribit frater infirmus in tua scientia, propter quem Christus mortuus est, 1.Cor.8. Item Rom.14. Ne esca tua illum perdito, pro quo Christus mortuus est: nec cibi causa destruito opus Dei.
units.tr: The answer to the sayings "the weak brother will perish in your knowledge, for whom Christ died" (1 Cor. 8) is the same. Likewise Rom. 14: "Do not destroy with your food the one for whom Christ died; do not, for the sake of food, destroy the work of God."

units.la: Quantum ad electos, damus etiam verè credentes, sed infirmos in fide, perşepe offendiculis grauiter concuti, imò destrui perdique, quatum ad scandalorum autores attinet, per quos non stat, quo minus illi pereant. Sed Dominus potens est eos, nutantes licet atque vacillantes, stabilire, atque etiam stabiliet. Quantum vero ad reprobos, propter scandala aut alias causas à veritate resilientes, atque funditus pereuntes, dicitur illi redemti & iustificati morte Christi, quatenus Ecclesiæ iudicio inter iustificatos & redemtos Christi locum aliquandiu obtinent, vt sæpè iam dixi.
units.tr: As for the elect, we also grant that they are truly believing, but weak in faith, and often gravely shaken, indeed overthrown and destroyed, by stumbling blocks, so far as the authors of the scandals are concerned, through whom it is not for want of effort that they perish. But the Lord is able to establish them, though they waver and totter, and he will indeed establish them. As for the reprobate, who fall away from the truth on account of scandals or other causes and perish utterly, they are said to be redeemed and justified by the death of Christ, in the sense that by the judgment of the Church they hold a place for a time among the justified and redeemed of Christ, as I have often said already.

units.la: Similiter accipiendum est, quod de perditis Pseudoprophetis legimus, eos nempe Dominum, qui ipsos mercatus est, abnegare. Nimirum Dominus mercatus eos dicitur, quatenus ad tempus numerantur inter fideles, quos non auro nec argento, sed pretioso suo sanguine Christus redemit. Etenim ex ipsa Ecclesia oriuntur lupi graves, non parcentes gregi, & loquentes peruersa, vt discipulos post se abstrahant. Sed quid dicit Iohannes? E nobis egressi sunt, sed non erant ex nobis: vtique enim mansissent nobiscum. Deinde, recte hoc ad gloriationem pseudoprophetarum refertur: quod quem Dominum ac redemtorem suum vocent, re ipsa abnegent: & libertatem iactet, cum reuera serui sint corruptionis & peccati, vt Petrus ipse declarat, & Epistola Iudæ confirmat. Sic enim ibi describuntur impostores isti subreptitij, quod vi-delidelicet Dei nostri gratiam trăsferrent ad lasciuiam, & solum illum herum, Deum ac Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum negarent.
units.tr: What we read about the false prophets who perished should be understood in the same way, namely that the Lord, "who bought them," they deny. Indeed the Lord is said to have bought them, inasmuch as for a time they are counted among the faithful, whom Christ redeemed not with gold or silver but with his precious blood. For fierce wolves arise from the Church itself, not sparing the flock and speaking perverse things so as to draw the disciples away after them. But what does John say? "They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would surely have remained with us." Then, rightly, this is attributed to the boasting of the false prophets: that they deny in deed the one whom they call their Lord and Redeemer, and boast of liberty, when in truth they are slaves of corruption and sin, as Peter himself declares and the Epistle of Jude confirms. For there those deceitful impostors are described as turning the grace of our God into licentiousness, and denying the only Master, God and our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Sed & sequentia consideremus.sub-iicit enim Petrus:quod si qui inquinamẽta mundi per agnitionem Domini ac Seruatoris Iesu Christi effugerint, vsq; postea rursus im-plicati superentur, vltimam eorum conditio-nem deteriorem fieri priori, & melius eis esse non cognouisse viam iustitiæ, quàm cognita illa regredi,instar canis ad vomitum.
units.tr: But let us also consider what follows. For Peter adds: "If, after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled and overcome, their last state becomes worse than the first, and it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than, having known it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them, like a dog returning to its vomit."

units.la: Ex his verbis aduersarius conatur colligere, multos vera fide & conuer-sione donatos, ac proin per mortem & sanguinem ablutos & iustificatos,æter-num perire.
units.tr: From these words the adversary tries to infer that many who were endowed with true faith and conversion, and who were therefore washed and justified through the death and blood of Christ, perish eternally.

units.la: Respondeo vt antea, hîc proprie nō quæri, an aliqui vera fide & conuersio-ne præditi ita relabantur vt pereant: sed hoc probandum erat aduersario, reprobos vniuersaliter nō minus quàm electos, omnes item infideles non mi-nus quam fideles,redemtionis in Chri-sto factos participes: id quod ex Apo-stoli verbis concludi minimè potest,cū non nisi de iis loquatur, qui per agni-tionem Christi inquinamenta mundi effugerant, quod Hub.ipse ad fidem & conuersionem eorum referri vult.
units.tr: I answer as before: the question here is not properly whether some who possess true faith and conversion so fall back that they perish; rather, the adversary had to prove that the reprobate universally, no less than the elect, and all unbelievers no less than believers, are made partakers of redemption in Christ. This cannot in any way be concluded from the words of the Apostle, since he speaks only of those who had escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Christ, which Huber himself wants to refer to their faith and conversion.

units.la: Secundo, quantum ad eos qui lapsi non resurgunt, nego tales morte & languine Christi vere fuisse ablutos, & iustificatos, aut vera ac viua in Christum fide fuisse praeditos. Nam contrarium supra ex Petri aliorumque Christi ser-uorum doctrina expositum est. Neque vero Petrus hic dicit, satius fuisset ijs nunquam habuisse veram fidem, aut iustitiam consequutos fuisse, quam postea a vera fide & iustitia relabi: sed tatum ait, satius fuisset non cognouisse viam iustitiae, quam cognita illa retrogredi a sancta doctrina ipsis tradita. Nos autem non inficiamur, multos qui prauas opiniones de Deo & rebus ad religionem pertinentibus abiecerat, veritatemque amplexi fuerat, postea a vera doctrina ad pristinos vel ad etiam nouos errores deficere, & hoc modo a fide, id est, a fidei doctrina relabi. Fatemur etiam multos, qui, vt Augustinus locum hunc per-pen-
units.tr: Second, as for those who have fallen and do not rise again, I deny that such people were truly washed and justified by the death and blood of Christ, or were endowed with a living and true faith in Christ. For the contrary has been set out above from the teaching of Peter and of the other servants of Christ. Nor does Peter here say "it would have been better for them never to have had true faith or to have attained righteousness, than afterwards to fall back from true faith and righteousness"; he says only that it would have been better not to have known the way of righteousness than, having known it, to turn back from the holy doctrine delivered to them. We do not deny that many who had cast off false opinions about God and about things pertaining to religion, and had embraced the truth, afterwards fell from the true doctrine into their former errors or even new ones, and in this way fell away from faith, that is, from the doctrine of faith. We also admit that many, who, as Augustine weighs this passage in his book On Faith and Works, had left behind the pollutions of the world, such as adultery, fornication, impurity, wantonness, idolatry, drunkenness, carousing and the like, by feigned promise or by an outward reform of morals, bound themselves again to the same things and lived in every filthiness, and so incurred a heavier judgment than if they had never known the way of righteousness. But those who somehow escape the pollutions of the world are not at once to be counted as washed in the blood of Christ and justified before God. For in that way all who lived honourably among the heathen, or who, having put aside the baseness of their former life, began to live uprightly, would also have to be regarded as washed and justified by the blood of Christ.

units.la: De fide & operibus pendit, vel pollicitatione ficta, vel ex-terna morum emendatione, inquina-menta mundi, puta adulterium, fcortationem, impuritatem, proteruiā, idolatriam, beneficiū, ebrietates, compotationes & similia reliquerāt, iisdem seipsos de integro mancipare, vitamq; in omni turpitudine degere, atque ita grauius iudicium incurrere, quàm fi viam iustitiæ nunquam cognouissent. Sed non statim qui quoquo modo effugiunt inquinamenta mundi, sanguine Christi abluti, & coram Deo iustificati censendi sunt. Nam eo modo pro ablutis & iustificatis sanguine Christi, etiam habendi effent, quotquot inter Ethnicos honestè vixerunt, aut relicta ante actæ vitæ turpitudine, frugi esse coeperunt.
units.tr: Nor do the Huberian inferences hold: they escaped the pollutions through the knowledge of Christ, they are said to have known the way of righteousness, and the holy commandment, that is, the holy doctrine of the Gospel, is said to have been delivered to them. Therefore they were endowed with true faith in Christ. As if the faith of Christians were nothing other than the bare knowledge of Christ, or of the way of righteousness and the holy commandment. Indeed, even the devils have a knowledge of Christ, and a greater one than men.

units.la: Nec valent illationes Huberianæ: refugerant ab inquinamentis per agnitionem Christi, & viam iustitiæ dicuntur cognouisse, & sanctum præceptum, id est, sancta doctrina Euangelij, dicitur iis traditum. Ergo vera in Christum fide donati erant. Quasi verò fidesChriftiasi anorum nil aliud sit quàm nuda cognitio Christi, aut viæ iustitiæ & sanċti præcepti. Equidem vel dæmonibus ipsis cognitio Christi inest, & maior quidem quàm hominibus.
units.tr: Nor do the Huberian inferences hold. They say that men fled the defilements of the world through knowledge of Christ, that they are said to have known the way of righteousness, and that the holy commandment, that is, the holy doctrine of the Gospel, was delivered to them. Therefore they were endowed with true faith in Christ. As if the faith of Christians were nothing more than bare knowledge of Christ, or of the way of righteousness and the holy commandment! Indeed, knowledge of Christ is found even in the demons themselves, and in them it is greater than in men.

units.la: At implicantur rursus: Ergo semel erant explicati & soluti. Concedo secundum quid: explicati fuerant erroribus pristinis, & externa morum perueꝛsitate: quibus dum rursum implicantur, de integrò polluûtur, & canum more resorbent impuritates illas, quas iam abiecerant & quasi vomuerant, eo quo dictū est modo: videlicet vel pol. licitatione ficta, vel etiam re ipsa, ὑπορ, vt Petrus loquitur, dum positis pristinis erroribus atque moribus, ad tempus sunt honesti, nō amplius inceden-tes in proteruiis, cupiditatibus, vinolentiis, comessationibus, compotatio-nibus, & nefariis simulacrorū cultibus, nec currentes amplius cū asotis hominibus ad eandem luxus profusionem, vt scribitur 1.Pet.4. Verum non omnes in quibus morum qualiscunque cernitur emendatio, animabus sunt purificatis, per spiritum & fidem ἀνυπόκριτον cum caritate simulationis experti, ex puro corde & conscientia bona.
units.tr: But they object again: then they were once set free and released. I grant this in a qualified sense. They had been set free from their former errors and from outward corruption of morals. When they are entangled in these again, they are polluted afresh, and like dogs they swallow back those filths which they had already cast off and, as it were, vomited up. They do this in the way I have described: either by a feigned profession, or in fact, ὑπορ [ὑπόκρισις], as Peter puts it, while for a time they lay aside their former errors and manners and are honest for a season, no longer walking in wantonness, lusts, drunkenness, revelling, drinking parties and abominable worship of idols, nor running any longer with the same riotous excess as dissolute men, as it is written in 1.Pet.4. Yet not all those in whom some kind of reform of morals is seen have had their souls purified, having experienced through the Spirit and faith an unfeigned love without pretence, out of a pure heart and a good conscience.

units.la: Citantur etiam verba 2.Pet.1. Vbi inquit de eo qui fidem profiteatur, opera autem non habeat, eum caecum esse, & obliuisci purgationis à veteribus suis peccatis. Pseudochristiani igitur & hypocritae tandem pereuntes, à peccatis suis purgati & iustificati aliquando fuerunt, non minus quàm quorum fides per bona opera efficax est & manet.
units.tr: They also cite the words of 2.Pet.1., where he says that the one who professes faith but does not have works is blind, and has forgotten the cleansing of his former sins. Therefore pseudo-Christians and hypocrites, who in the end perish, were at some time cleansed and justified from their sins, no less than those whose faith is effective and abides through good works.

units.la: Responsio eadem est quae antea: Intelligendum id secundum consuetudinem scripturarum, quae sanctos, iustos, & à peccatis mundatos appellant, quotquot in Christum baptizantur, & Ecclesiae ipsius inseruntur. Quia Ecclesia pro talibus eos habere debet secundum iudicium caritatis: licet coram Deo quandoque tales non sint.
units.tr: The answer is the same as before: this must be understood according to the custom of the Scriptures, which call holy, righteous and cleansed from sins all who are baptized into Christ and engrafted into his Church. The Church ought to regard them as such according to the judgment of charity, even though they are sometimes not such before God.

units.la: Deinde, potest esse sensus, tales obliuisci baptismi sui, qui visibilis quaedam est sanctificatio & purgatio à peccatis, secundum illud, Baptizare & ablue peccata tua. Sed vt rectè Augustinus inter
units.tr: Next, the sense may be that those who forget their baptism, which is a certain visible sanctification and cleansing from sins, are such as these, according to that saying, Baptizare & ablue peccata tua. But, as Augustine rightly distinguishes between visible and invisible sanctification,

units.la: O ij vi-
units.tr: O ij vi-

units.la: visibilem & inuisibilem sanctificatio-nem distinguit: homo visibilibus Sa-cramentis per ministerium sanctificat: Dominus autem inuisibili gratia per Sp.sanctum, vbi est totus fructus etiam visibilium Sacramentorum: & inuisi-bilis quidem sanctificatio quibusdam adest & prodest sine visibilibus sacra-mentis; visibilis vero sanctificatio, quæ fit per visibilia sacramenta, sine ista in-uisibili adesse potest, prodesse non po-test. Nihil quippe profuit Simoni Ma-go visibilis baptismus, cui sanctificatio inuisibilis defuit. Hæc August. super Le-uiticum lib. 3. quæst. 84. quibus suffragatur & Lutherus in Psal. 2.
units.tr: visible and invisible sanctification: a man sanctifies by the ministry of visible sacraments, but the Lord sanctifies by invisible grace through the Holy Spirit, and in this lies the whole fruit even of the visible sacraments. The invisible sanctification is present in some and benefits them without the visible sacraments, but visible sanctification, which is effected through visible sacraments, can be present without this invisible sanctification, yet it cannot benefit. For the visible baptism profited Simon Magus nothing, since invisible sanctification was lacking in him. These are the words of Augustine, super Leviticum lib. 3. quæst. 84., which Luther also supports in Psal. 2.

units.la: Nimis vero importunum & alienum est, quòd luculentam illam gratiæ Dei erga fideles descriptionem apud Pe-trum initio capitis, etiam ad institutū suum torquere conatur antagonista. Petrus, inquit, vere testatur eos dãnari posse, qui fidem & salutem, omniáque ad pietatem pertinentia iam adepti erant.
units.tr: It is indeed far too forced and out of place that the opponent tries to twist that famous description of God's grace towards the faithful, given by Peter at the beginning of the chapter, to serve his own purpose. Peter, he says, truly testifies that those can be damned who already possess faith and salvation and all things pertaining to godliness.

units.la: Sed quid si hoc ipsi negetur, quomo-do do probabit? Quia, inquit, obijcit eis cæcitatem. At bone vir, cuiuis ex contextu planum est, exprobrationem ista pertinere non ad vere credentes, quorum fides per caritatem efficax est, sed adpseudochristianos: qui hoc ipsoquod fidem per opera non ostendunt, satis declarant se vera fide haud præditos, sed cæcos esse nihilq; cernere. Certè duo ista diuersissima hominum genera, quæ Petrus ex professo discernit, inter se miscere velle, nec attendere quid quibus conueniat, plane Sophisticum est. Primum ad vere conuersos, & viua in Christum fide præditos spectat prædicatio ista gratiæ, quod diuina vis omnia ipsis donarit ad vitam & pietatem spectantia: quod vocati sint ad gloriam & virtutem, quod maxima ac pretiosa consequuti promissa, & diuinæ consortes efficiantur naturæ, elapsi ex corruptione in mundo. De ijs enim ista dicuntur, qui æquè pretiosam fidem cum Petro & eius similibus sortiti erant, quod sane de his dici nequit, quibus historica tantum ac mortua, id est dæ-momonum, non Christianorum, fides in-est. Deinde per modum exhortationis viuam atque mortuam fidem accurate discernit: quod qui viua fide praediti sunt, eam per opera ostendunt, & subministrantes in fide virtutem, in virtute scientiam, in scientia temperantiam, tolerantiam, pietatem, caritatem, minime inertes atque infructuosi reperiantur in cognitione Iesu Christi. Contra pronunciat caecos esse, nec quicquam cernentes, & oblitos purgationis veterum peccatorum, quibus bona opera non adsint. Vbi iam per antithefin in hypocritas & pfeudochriftianos stylum dirigit: qui vt Iacobus eos depingit, auditores solum sunt verbi, non factores, ac fallunt seipsos & seducunt cor suum: ac licet videantur religiosi, tame religio ipsorum mera est vanitas, & fides mortua. Sed quid hoc ad vere credentes? an illis propterea damnationis periculum est, quia hypocritae in vanitate sua pereunt? Imo tantum abest vt Apostolus vere credentes damnari doceat, vt e contrario testetur, tales qui in co-
units.tr: But what if this is denied them? How will he prove it? "Because," he says, "the Apostle charges them with blindness." But, good sir, it is plain to anyone from the context that this reproach applies not to truly believing people, whose faith works through love, but to pseudo-Christians. By the very fact that they do not show their faith through works, they sufficiently declare that they do not possess true faith but are blind and see nothing. It is certainly sophistical to want to mix up these two very different kinds of people, which Peter expressly distinguishes, and not to consider what applies to whom. This preaching of grace first concerns those who have truly been converted and possess a living faith in Christ: that divine power has given them all things pertaining to life and godliness; that they have been called to glory and virtue; that they have obtained the greatest and precious promises and are made partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world. For these things are said of those who obtained a precious faith equal to that of Peter and his like, which cannot truly be said of those who have only a historical and dead faith, that is, the faith of demons, not of Christians. Then, by way of exhortation, he accurately distinguishes living faith from dead faith: those who have living faith show it through works, and supplying in faith virtue, in virtue knowledge, in knowledge temperance, endurance, godliness, and love, they are found to be by no means idle or unfruitful in the knowledge of Jesus Christ. On the other hand, he pronounces those who lack good works to be blind, seeing nothing, and forgetful of the cleansing of their former sins. Here, by way of antithesis, he directs his pen against hypocrites and pseudo-Christians, who, as James depicts them, are hearers of the word only and not doers, and who deceive themselves and beguile their own hearts; and although they seem religious, their religion is mere vanity and dead faith. But what has this to do with truly believing people? Are they in danger of damnation because hypocrites perish in their vanity? Nay, so far is the Apostle from teaching that truly believing people are damned that, on the contrary, he testifies that such as are fruitful in the knowledge of the Lord make their calling and election ever more firm, and will never stumble, but will obtain an abundant entrance into the kingdom of heaven.

units.la: * ... cognitione Domini fructuosi sunt, vocationem & electionem suam magis magisque firmare, & fore ut nunquam impingant, sed introitum in regnum cœlorum copiosè consequantur.
units.tr: * ... in the knowledge of the Lord, make their calling and election ever more firm, and they shall never stumble, but shall richly obtain entrance into the kingdom of heaven.

units.la: Quod insuper ex 1.Pet.2. obijcitur, etiam reprobos impositos fuisse lapidi angulari Christo, simpliciter repudiamus, tanquam à verbis Petri alienum, qui de immorigeris Iudæis, & quibus Christus offendiculo erat, scribit, eos ad hoc positos esse, non dicit, impositos Christo.
units.tr: As for the objection, drawn from 1 Peter 2, that even the reprobate were appointed to Christ the cornerstone, we simply reject it as foreign to Peter's words. He speaks of disobedient Jews, to whom Christ was a stumbling block; he writes that they were appointed to this, but he does not say that they were appointed to Christ.

units.la: Ex epistola ad Gal. duo præterea loca citantur: ut, quod cap. 3. Paulus Galatas admonet: Adeò amentes estis? cum Spiritu cœperitis, nunc carne consummamini? tam multa passi estis frustra? Ite capite 5. In libertate igitur, qua Christus nos liberavit, state, & ne rursum iugo servitutis implicamini. Ecce ego Paulus dico vobis, si circumcidamini, Christum nihil vobis profuturum: facti estis inanes Christi: quicunque per legem iustificamini, à gratia excidistis. Ex his sequi videtur, quod reprobari possint, quibus redemtio atque libertas per Christum iam obtigerat, quique verè iustifiati ac re-
units.tr: Two further passages are cited from the epistle to the Galatians. One is that in chapter 3 Paul admonishes the Galatians: Are you so foolish? Having begun in the Spirit, are you now being made perfect in the flesh? Have you suffered so many things in vain? Likewise, in chapter 5: Stand fast, therefore, in the liberty by which Christ has made us free, and do not be entangled again in the yoke of bondage. Behold, I Paul say to you, that if you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing. You have become empty of Christ; whoever is justified by the law has fallen from grace. From these it seems to follow that those to whom redemption and liberty through Christ had already come, who were truly justified and re-

units.la: Ecce ego Paulus dico vobis. regenerati, & Christo tanquam viua membra insiti erant.
units.tr: Behold, I Paul say to you. regenerated, and grafted into Christ as living members.

units.la: I. respondeo de Galatis non liquere eos defecisse finaliter; imo secundum Augustinum, necdum ceciderant aut cesserant impostoribus, sed nutabundi erant, nondum autem corruerant, neque corruerunt. Vt tamen de eo non contendam, de quo alijs interpretibus aliud videri scio, id certum est, si errore pseudapostolorum iam abrepti erant, non errasse finaliter, dicente Apostolo, confido de vobis in Domino, vos aliud non sensuros. Vnde etiam non ait categorice, tanta passos frustra: sed correctionem addit, quam Hub. studiose dissimulauit, si tamen frustra: significans meliora se & cum salute coniuncta persuasum de Galatis, tametsi asperius loquetur ad eos increpandos. Cur igitur ita eos tractat, tanquam in extremo salutis discrimine versantes? Quia horrenda illa mala, quae seductores illis machinabantur, maiora erant quam vt fado aequari possent: & conducebat ea ipsa asperitas Galatis in doctrina fidei retiretinendis,cogitatione exitij.
units.tr: I. I answer that it is not clear the Galatians fell away finally. Indeed, according to Augustine, they had not yet fallen or yielded to the impostors, but were wavering; they had not yet collapsed, and they did not collapse. But, so that I need not contend about this point, on which I know other interpreters think otherwise, this much is certain: if they had already been carried away by the error of the false apostles, they did not err finally, since the Apostle says, I trust in you in the Lord that you will think no otherwise. Hence he also does not say categorically, "you have suffered so many things in vain," but adds a qualification, which Hub. carefully concealed: if indeed in vain. This signifies that he was persuaded of better things about the Galatians, things connected with salvation, although he speaks more harshly in order to rebuke them. Why, then, does he treat them as though they were in extreme peril of salvation? Because those dreadful evils that the seducers were plotting against them were too great to be matched in fact; and that very harshness served to hold the Galatians back in the doctrine of faith by the thought of ruin.

units.la: II. negatur consequentia propositi argumenti. Hub. tripliciter eam probare videri vult. Primùm quod aliqui Spiritu incipiétes,carne consumment. Syllogismus erit talis:
units.tr: II. The consequence of the proposed argument is denied. Hub. seeks to prove it in three ways. First, that some who begin in the Spirit are consummated in the flesh. The syllogism will be this:

units.la: Spiritu incipientes sunt iustificati atque redémti.
units.tr: Those who begin in the Spirit are justified and redeemed.

units.la: Aliqui Spiritu incipientes reprobantur: quia posteaquam Spiritu coepe-runt,carne consummant.
units.tr: Some who begin in the Spirit are reprobated, because after they began in the Spirit they are consummated in the flesh.

units.la: Ergo aliqui ex numero reprobandorum erant iustificati atque redemti.
units.tr: Therefore some of the number of the reprobate were justified and redeemed.

units.la: Hìc Maior vniuersaliter sumta negatur: ideo concluditur ex puris particularibus. Maior vera duntaxat est de habentibus spiritum iustificationis & regenerationis, sed qui sic spiritu coeperunt, eos non patitur Deus carne consummare: verum perficit in ipsis opus suum bonum,ad diem Iesu Christi. Interim multi spiritu incipiunt; quatenus doctrinam spiritus seu Euangelij de gratuita per Christum iustificatione profitentur, aut etiam dona aliqua acceperunt spiritualia: qui dum postmo-
units.tr: Here the major premise, taken universally, is denied; hence the conclusion is drawn only from particular premises. The major is true only of those who have the Spirit of justification and regeneration. But God does not allow those who have thus begun in the Spirit to be consummated in the flesh; rather he perfects in them his good work unto the day of Jesus Christ. Meanwhile, many begin in the Spirit insofar as they profess the Spirit's doctrine, or the gospel teaching of justification freely through Christ, or have even received some spiritual gifts. When these, having afterwards fallen into errors contrary to the gospel, do not return, or else by their ingratitude are deprived of those spiritual gifts, they are understood to be consummated in the flesh, though they began in the Spirit.

units.la: Philip. dum lapsi in errores cum Euangelio pugnantes non redeunt, autalioquin ingratitudine sua donis illis spiritus priuantur, carne intelliguntur cófum-mare, cum spiritu inceperint.
units.tr: Philip. Those who, having fallen into errors contrary to the gospel, do not return, or who otherwise through their ingratitude are deprived of those gifts of the Spirit, are understood to be consummated in the flesh, though they began in the Spirit.

units.la: Altera eius probatio nititur dicto, Tantane frustra passi estis?
units.tr: The second proof rests on the saying, Have you suffered so many things in vain?

units.la: Sed maior iterum falsa est vniuersaliter sumta, nimirum haec: Quod quicunque frustra pro Euangelio patiuntur, reprobentur accepta semel gratia iustificationis. Nam fieri potest, teste Apostolo, vt qui caritatem, ac proinde etiam veram fidem & iustificationem non habent, extrema tamen patiantur, sed frustra.
units.tr: But the major premise is again false when taken universally, namely this: that whoever suffer for the gospel in vain are reprobated after receiving the grace of justification. For, as the Apostle witnesses, it can happen that those who lack love, and consequently also true faith and justification, nevertheless suffer extreme things, but in vain.

units.la: Tertio sic probat. Quotquot ex operibus legis sunt, seu per opera iustificari volunt, sunt exsecrationi obnoxij. Sed aliqui redemti ab exsecratione legis, recidunt in errorem Pharisaicum de operum iustitia. Ergo aliqui semel redemti, de integro exsecratione inuoluuntur.
units.tr: Thirdly, he proves it thus. All who are of the works of the law, or who wish to be justified by works, are liable to the curse. But some who were redeemed from the curse of the law fall back into the Pharisaic error about the righteousness of works. Therefore some who were once redeemed are again involved in the curse.

units.la: Hic responsio patet ad minorem: quod qui vere participes facti sunt redemtionis per fidem, non errent eo modo finaliter. Qui autem in errore isto de operum iustitia permanent, siue veritatem Euangelicam cognouerint aliquando, siue non, eos probari non potest vere vnquam ab execratione legis fuisse redemtos. Nam redemtio isthæc eorum demum est, qui per veram in Christum fidem, semen sunt Abrahæ, & secundum promissionem hæredes, vt copiose ad Gal.3. docetur.
units.tr: Here the answer to the minor premise is clear: those who have truly become partakers of redemption through faith do not err finally in that way. But those who persist in that error about the righteousness of works, whether they have at some time known the truth of the gospel or not, cannot be proved ever to have truly been redeemed from the curse of the law. For that redemption belongs only to those who, through true faith in Christ, are the seed of Abraham and heirs according to the promise, as is taught at length in Galatians 3.

units.la: Quod ad locem ad Gal.5. State in libertate qua Christus nos liberauit, colligit aduersarius semel liberatos, per sanguinem scilicet & mortem Christi, rursus libertatem posse amittere, dum in libertate non stant, sed iugo seruitutis rursum implicantur, atque ita Christū sibi inutilem reddunt, gratiaq; excidunt.
units.tr: As for the passage in Galatians 5, "Stand fast in the liberty by which Christ has made us free," the adversary infers that those once freed, namely through the blood and death of Christ, can again lose their liberty, when they do not stand in liberty but are entangled again in the yoke of bondage. In this way they render Christ useless to themselves and fall from grace.

units.la: Respondeo. Textus non habet, state in libertate qua Christus vos liberauit, vt Hub. deprauat: sed, qua liberauit nos. Et antithesis filiorum ancillæ & liberæ, credentium atque operariorum, qui nempe propriam studentes iustitiā erierigere, iustitiæ Christi non fiunt participes, manifeste ostendit, liberationem hanc per Christum non esse omnium absque exceptione, credentium & non credentium: sed qui credit in Christum, habet illam libertatem, nec amittit eam finaliter, quia æterna est. Libertas enim Christiana, vt Lutherus etiam in hunc locum monet, tale donü est, quo loco peccati & mortis habemus iustitiam ac vitam æternam, ac perpetuò propitium & fauentem Deum per Christum.
units.tr: I answer: the text does not read "stand in the liberty by which Christ made you free," as Hub. distorts it, but "by which he made us free." And the antithesis between the sons of the handmaid and of the free, between believers and works-people, who, striving to establish their own righteousness, do not become partakers of the righteousness of Christ, clearly shows that this liberation through Christ is not for everyone without exception, believers and unbelievers alike. Rather, he who believes in Christ has that liberty and does not finally lose it, because it is eternal. For Christian liberty, as Luther also remarks on this passage, is such a gift that in place of sin and death we have righteousness and eternal life, and God propitious and favouring us perpetually through Christ.

units.la: Fatemur nihilominus, multos non stare in libertate, quia Christus nos liberauit. Primùm, quia electi etiam & vere credentes nonnunquam tentantur & implicantur erroribus cum fundamento pugnantibus, sed vt sæpissimè dictū est, non finaliter. Secundò, quia multi fidem & libertatem Christianam profitentes, atque eatenus inter libertos Christi locum aliquandiu habentes, seruituti legis & traditionum humanarum, imò mundi & Satanæ, denuò implicantur cum salutis dispendio. Ac
units.tr: We nevertheless admit that many do not stand in the liberty that Christ has won for us. First, because the elect and truly believing are sometimes tempted and entangled in errors that clash with the foundation; but, as has been said very often, not finally. Second, because many who profess faith and Christian liberty, and for a while have a place among the freed of Christ, are again entangled in the slavery of the law and of human traditions, indeed of the world and of Satan, to the loss of their salvation.

units.la: ytrique vtrique horum sibi ipsis inanem Christum reddunt, gratiaq; & consolatione excidunt: hi quidem simpliciter ac perpetuò, illi tantisper duntaxat quoad resipuerint.
units.tr: Both kinds of people make Christ empty for themselves and fall from grace and consolation: the first simply and permanently, the second only for as long as they do not repent.

units.la: Eadem est solutio ad alia duo loca, de Iudæis nimirum tanquâ ramis quibusdam oleæ defractis, deque gentibus excidendis nisi in benignitate Dei permanserint. Et, omnem palmitem in me non ferentem fructum tollit pater: & omnem qui fert fructum purgat, vt plus fructus adferat. Nisi quis in me manserit eijcitur foras & exaresset: & colligunt eos, & in ignem coniiciunt.
units.tr: The same answer applies to the other two passages, namely those concerning the Jews as branches broken off from an olive tree, and concerning the Gentiles who will be cut off unless they remain in the goodness of God. And every branch in me that does not bear fruit the Father takes away; and every one that bears fruit he prunes, that it may bear more fruit. Unless someone remains in me he is cast out and withers; and they gather them and cast them into the fire.

units.la: Horum sententia simpliciter est, non omnes qui externa vocatione sunt in populo Dei, olea illa viridi & pingui & vinea electa, & sic inter palmites Christi annumerantur, seruatum iri: multos tales iam pridem excisos & excidendos porrò ob ingratitudinem. Multi enim sunt hypocritæ, gratiæ & ipsi aliquatenus participes, licet non ad iustificationem; qui quoniam in speciem ad tempus florent & virent, sed in reddendo fru-
units.tr: Their view is simply this: not everyone who belongs to the people of God by outward calling, those green and fat olive trees and the chosen vine, and who is thus counted among the branches of Christ, will be preserved. Many such people have already been cut off, and more will be cut off later for their ingratitude. For there are many hypocrites who themselves share in grace to some degree, though not unto justification. Since they flourish and look green for a time in appearance, but in yielding fru-

units.la: { } Ioh. 15. Rom. 11. Ier. 11. Ier. 23. Matth. 21. do fructu spem agricolæ frustrantur, & fidem in labiis magis quàm in corde habent, tandem abijciuntur.
units.tr: Ioh. 15. Rom. 11. Ier. 11. Ier. 23. Matth. 21. it, they disappoint the hope of the farmer, and they have faith more on their lips than in their heart, and in the end they are cast off.

units.la: Quòd autem ex electis & verè pijs contingat aliquos ita excidi, non modò testimonijs istis non probatur, verùm etiam contrarium aperte ijs demon-stratur.
units.tr: That some of the elect and truly godly are cut off in this way is not only not proved by those testimonies, but the contrary is clearly shown from them.

units.la: Primò, qui erant Iudæi quos Deus reiecit? increduli, non auscultátes Euangelio, iustitiam Dei ignorantes & propriam studentes iustitiam constituere, & quibus datus erat à Deo, iusto ipsius iudicio, spiritus soporis: oculi, vt non viderent, & aures vt non audirent, quemadmodum Apostolus reprobos istos describit. Sed ab iis electos & pios discernens inquit, non abiecit Deus populum suum quem præcognouit. Item, quod requirit Israel, hoc non est assequutus: sed electi assequuti sunt: cæteri vero occalluerunt. Reiecti quidem illi sunt ob infidelitatem; quis negat? Sed iusto Dei iudicio ad fidem non peruenerant: quia ex electis ipsius non erant. Quis enim vel stultissimus hoc dixerit, inquit Augustinus, quod quòd inimici Iudæi, qui in suis inimicitijs perierūt, quique aduersantes Christo de gente ipsa adhuc pereunt, ipsi sint electi atque dilecti?
units.tr: First, who were the Jews whom God rejected? Unbelievers, who did not listen to the Gospel, ignorant of God's righteousness and seeking to establish their own righteousness, and to whom, by God's just judgment, a spirit of stupor was given: eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, as the Apostle describes these reprobates. But distinguishing the elect and pious from them, he says, God has not cast away his people whom he foreknew. Likewise, what Israel seeks, this it has not obtained; but the elect have obtained it; the rest were hardened. Those men were indeed rejected on account of their unbelief; who denies it? But by the just judgment of God they had not come to faith, because they were not among his elect. For who, even the most foolish, would say, as Augustine does, that those Jews who were enemies, who perished in their enmity, and who still perish opposing Christ from that same nation, are themselves elect and beloved?

units.la: Secundò, Paulus non tam electos singulos ex gentibus, quàm totum corpus conuersorum, in quo multi erant titulo tenus duntaxat fideles & membra Christi, in commune apellat, cùm exemplo Iudæorū incredulorum ipsis minatur. Quanquam concessō etiam ad singulos electos & fideles directam Apostoli admonitionem, nihil dum effectum est: quia loquitur hypothetice, excidendos, nisi permanserint in bonitate Dei. Permanent autem electi, & vt permaneant, & magis magisque vocationi respondeant, nec gratia Dei frustra receperint, in eum ipsum finem vtiles ipsis sunt tales hortationū & comminationum stimuli, ad excutiendam securitatem carnis, cum qua assiduè nobis lucta est.
units.tr: Second, Paul addresses not so much individual elect from the Gentiles as the whole body of converts together, among whom many were faithful only in name and members of Christ in appearance, and he threatens them with the example of the unbelieving Jews. Even granting that the Apostle's admonition is also directed to individual elect and faithful, nothing is yet settled: for he speaks hypothetically, that they will be cut off unless they remain in the goodness of God.
