But the elect do remain, and so that they may remain, and respond more and more to their calling, and not have received the grace of God in vain, such goads of exhortations and threats are useful to them for this very purpose: to shake off the security of the flesh, with which we always have a struggle.

units.la: Tertiò, Christus Ioh. 15. aperte discrimen constituit duplicium palmitum, fructuosorum & infructuosorum: ve-rè piore piorum, & hypocritarum formam duntaxat pietatis habentiu,qui nihilominus ob externam professionem in vite censentur. Et de his ait Dominus, omnem palmitem non ferentem fructum in se,auferendum vt igni tradatur. Qui sunt isti, nili fidem habentes sine operibus, id est,fidem mortuam? De palmitibus autem fructum ferentibus dicit,omnem palmitem qui fert fructum, purgabit pater, vt plus fructus afferat. Sub hac propositione nunc assumamus:
units.tr: Third, Christ in John 15 clearly makes a distinction between two kinds of branches, the fruitful and the unfruitful: the former are truly pious, the latter hypocrites who have only the form of piety, who nevertheless are reckoned in the vine on account of their outward profession. Of these the Lord says, "Every branch not bearing fruit in me is to be taken away and given to the fire." Who are these, unless those who have faith without works, that is, dead faith? But of the branches bearing fruit he says, "Every branch that bears fruit the Father will prune, that it may bear more fruit." Let us now assume this proposition:

units.la: Atqui omnes vere credetes, in quibus fides illa per caritatem efficax & corda purgans animasque purificans, viget,sunt palmites fructuosi. Ergo pater eos indies magis magisque purgabit:tantum abest,vt excidendi sint.
units.tr: But all who truly believe, in whom that faith flourishes which is effective through love, cleansing hearts and purifying souls, are fruitful branches. Therefore the Father will prune them day by day, more and more: so far is it from being the case that they are to be cut off.

units.la: Parabola quoque debitoris Matt.18. astruere videtur redemtionem, hoc est, remissionem peccatorum in aliquibus reddi irritam. Nam cui debitum donatum erat, propter sæuitiam in conseruum suum tortoribus tradebatur, quo ad vniuersum debitum soluerret. Respondeo, Similitudini in disputando conuenientia tanta non conceditur, vt ei rei cui adhibenda est, ex omni parte coaptetur: Alioquin similitudo non esset similitudo, sed res ipsa. Spectanda est mens & scopus Christi, qui non voluit docere, an peccata semel remissa, redeant nec ne: sed requiri ostendit, vt nos fratribus nostris remittamus offensas suas, si remissionem nostrarum offensarum apud Deum obtinere velimus. Vnde & Christus parabolam istam sic concludit: ita & pater meus caelestis faciet vobis, nisi remiseritis quisque fratri suo ex corde offensas eorum: id est, vt Christus ipse Matth.6. pluribus docet, sinos remiserimus hominibus offensas ipsorum, remittet etiam nobis pater coelestis: sin autem non remiserimus, nec pater remittet nobis.
units.tr: The parable of the debtor in Matthew 18 also seems to show that redemption, that is, the remission of sins, is in some cases made void. For the man to whom the debt had been forgiven, because of his cruelty toward his fellow servant, was handed over to the torturers, until he should pay the whole debt. I answer: in disputation, such close correspondence is not granted to a similitude that it fits the thing it is applied to in every respect; otherwise the similitude would not be a similitude but the thing itself. We must look to the mind and aim of Christ, who did not intend to teach whether sins once forgiven return or not, but shows that we are required to forgive our brothers their offenses if we wish to obtain forgiveness of our own offenses before God. Hence Christ also concludes the parable thus: so also my heavenly Father will do to you, unless each of you forgives his brother his offenses from the heart; that is, as Christ himself teaches more fully in Matthew 6, if we forgive men their offenses, our heavenly Father will also forgive us; but if we do not forgive, neither will the Father forgive us.

units.la: An autem peccata dimissa redeant, Scholasticorum sententiam legere est 4.sent.dist.22. & parte 3. Thomae quaest. 88.
units.tr: For whether forgiven sins return, one may read the opinion of the Schoolmen in 4 Sent. dist. 22 and in Thomas, part 3, question 88.

units.la: Sicut ibi videre est, dubitanter admodum & intricate eam rem disputant: multoque planiora sunt testimonia sa-
units.tr: As may be seen there, they dispute the matter rather doubtfully and intricately; but the testimonies of the holy letters are much plainer.

units.la: P cracrarum literarum: Quos praedestinauit, eos vocauit: quos vocauit, eos etiam iustificauit: quos iustificauit, eos etiam glorificauit. Iniquitatum ipsorum non recordabor amplius, dicit Dominus. Quod item peccata suorum quibus propitius est, delet ut nubem; eaque proiecit post tergum suum, imo in profundum maris. Hae locutiones satis indicant, cum peccata Deus remittit, ita remittere, ut perpetuae tradat obliuioni, & quasi in fumum atque in nihilum ea redigat, ac proinde quae remittit peccata, in perpetuum remittere.
units.tr: "Whom he predestined, these he also called; whom he called, these he also justified; whom he justified, these he also glorified." "I will remember their iniquities no more, says the Lord." Likewise, that he blots out the sins of those toward whom he is merciful like a cloud, and has cast them behind his back, indeed into the depths of the sea. These expressions sufficiently indicate that when God remits sins, he remits them so as to consign them to perpetual oblivion, and to reduce them as to smoke and nothing; and therefore the sins he remits, he remits for ever.

units.la: {x}Bis autem ineptus, ne ipsius more dicam insanus, est Huberus: qui ex divina parabola intelligi vult omnibus ex aequo condonata peccata, & aeque reprobos per Christum saluatos, ac quoslibet alios. Non videt in seruo isto contrarium? remissionem peccatorum nō esse omnium, sed eorum qui peccata sua confitentur, & supplices veniam eorundem petunt, etiam coseruis suis ex animo ignoscere parati?
units.tr: {x} Huber, moreover, is inept, not to say insane, in his manner: he wants it understood from the divine parable that sins are forgiven to all alike, and that reprobates are saved through Christ just as any others are. Does he not see the contrary in that servant? That the remission of sins is not for all, but for those who confess their sins and humbly seek their pardon, and who are ready also to forgive their fellow servants from the heart?

units.la: Superest locus unicus 1. Iohan. 1. quod qui Deo non credunt, mendacem ipsum faciant. tiant. Ex quo dicto antagonista colligit, promissiones gratiæ & vitæ in Christo adipsos quoque infideles & reprobos pertinere. Contra Iohannes expresse promissionem vitæ restringit ad credentes, cum ait, qui habet filium, habet vitam. Increduli autem nec patrem nec filium habent, sed absque Christo, & Dei expertes in mundo degunt, extranei à pactis promissionis, spem non habentes teste Paulo. Hoccine est reprobos & non credentes vitam in filio Dei recipere, vt iste nugatur?
units.tr: One passage remains, 1 John 1: "that those who do not believe God make him a liar." From this saying our opponent gathers that the promises of grace and life in Christ pertain also to unbelievers and reprobates. On the contrary, John expressly restricts the promise of life to believers, when he says, he who has the Son has life. But unbelievers have neither the Father nor the Son, but live without Christ and strangers to God in the world, aliens from the covenants of promise, having no hope, as Paul witnesses. Is this what he is trifling about, that reprobates and unbelievers receive life in the Son of God?

units.la: Et placet sibi homo cofidens in tam crassa inscitia, ac superbi instar Goliathi prouocat omnes, quomodo nō credentes, vt est apud Iohannem (pro quibus ipse reprobos substituit) Deum mendacé faciant, si vitam in filio ipsius non recipiant? Quasi vero hic acumen nescio quod requiratur. Qui Deo fidé non adhibent, mendacem ipsum faciunt: Euangelio autem non credentes fidem Deo non adhibent. Mendacem igitur eum faciunt.
units.tr: And this man, confident in such crass ignorance, and like the proud Goliath, challenges everyone: how, as in John (for whom he substitutes reprobates), do unbelievers make God a liar if they do not receive life in his Son? As if some subtle cleverness were required here! Those who do not give faith to God make him a liar; but those who do not believe the Gospel do not give faith to God. Therefore they make him a liar.

units.la: Maior patet. Minor probatur ex textextu, quia Euangelium est teftimo-nium Dei de suo filio, quòd credentes in ipsum vitam æternam habeamus. Qui igitur vel nulla cura salutis tangū-tur, vel extra Christum eam quærunt, vel alia ratione Euangelio increduli sunt, Deo ipsi fidem non habet;ac pro-inde,quantum in se est,medacem eum faciunt;sicut contra,testimonium eius recipientes, obsignant quòd Deus ve-rax sit.
units.tr: The major premise is clear. The minor is proved from the text: the Gospel is God's testimony concerning his Son, that those who believe in him should have eternal life. Therefore those who are either untouched by any concern for salvation, or seek it outside Christ, or are unbelieving in the Gospel in some other way, do not really have faith in God himself; and so, so far as it lies in them, they make him a liar. On the other hand, those who receive his testimony set their seal to the truth of God.

units.la: At, inquis, ad quos beneficia Euan-gelij, redemtio, iustitia, & vita æterna non pertinent, Euangelio non tenen-tur credere ; imò veracem Deum fa-ciunt non credendo, recalcitrando, blasphemando. Sic enim spiritus iste loquitur. Ad reprobos autè Euange-lij beneficia non pertinent ex nostra hypothesi: Ergo non tenetur credere.
units.tr: But you will say: those to whom the benefits of the Gospel (redemption, righteousness and eternal life) do not pertain are not bound to believe the Gospel; indeed, by not believing, by kicking back and blaspheming, they make God true. For that is how this spirit speaks. But on our hypothesis the benefits of the Gospel do not pertain to the reprobate. Therefore they are not bound to believe.

units.la: Gordius scilicet nodus. Sed distin-guo minorem; licet ipsa beneficia Eu-angelij ad reprobos & quoscunque in-fideles quatenus tales sunt, non perti-neāt fruitione, idque propria ipsorum culpa, pertinere tamen inuitatione, quaquatenus omnes promiscuè absq; discrimine electorum & reproborum iubetur resipiscere & credere Euangelio cū promissione vniuersali : quisquis crediderit, habebit vitam æternam. Atque id præsenti instituto satis est.
units.tr: A Gordian knot indeed! But I distinguish the minor. Although the benefits of the Gospel do not pertain to the reprobate, or to any unbelievers so far as they are such, for enjoyment (and that through their own fault), they do pertain to invitation, in so far as all, without distinction between elect and reprobate, are commanded indiscriminately to repent and believe the Gospel, with the universal promise: whoever believes will have eternal life. And that is enough for the present purpose.

units.la: Rectè omnino Lutherus, quem isti in aliis solum mirantur, hic extremè contemnunt, præfat. ad Rom. inquit, ex prædestinationis sententia sola pendere omnia, qui accepturi sint verbum, qui non: qui credituri, qui non; qui liberandi à peccato, qui occæcandi; qui damnandi, qui iustificandi. Interim curiosos habenis compescendos monet, qui antequam Christum & virtutem crucis discant, abyssum prædestinationis scrutantur. Tu verò, inquit, disce cognitionem Christi, cum carne tua per fidem assiduè luctare, tum quàm plena sit consolationis prædestinatio senties. Et passim docet, nobis non à priori, sed à posteriori, ut loquimur, de Deo & ipsius erga nos voluntate ac beneplacito statuendum: exequendum quod Deus iubet, intuendum filium incarnatum, & simpliciter acquiescendum verbo revelato: secundum illud
units.tr: Luther is entirely right, whom these men admire in other matters but here utterly despise. In the preface to Romans he says: everything depends on the sentence of predestination alone: who are going to receive the word and who not; who will believe and who not; who are to be freed from sin and who blinded; who damned and who justified. Meanwhile he advises that the inquisitive be curbed with reins, those who, before they learn Christ and the power of the cross, scrutinise the abyss of predestination. "But you," he says, "learn the knowledge of Christ, wrestle constantly with your flesh through faith, and then you will feel how full of consolation predestination is." And throughout he teaches that we must determine concerning God and his will and good pleasure towards us not a priori but, as we say, a posteriori: we must do what God commands, look upon the incarnate Son, and simply acquiesce in the revealed word, according to that saying:

units.la: In Genef. cap. 16. & 41. Item de seruo arbit. In Psal. 9.
units.tr: In Genef. cap. 16. & 41. Item de seruo arbit. In Psal. 9.

units.la: Lib.1 De Redemtione
units.tr: Book 1, On the Redemption

units.la: Eccles.3. Altiora te ne quaesieris, & fortiora te ne scrutatus fueris; quae autem tibi a Deo mandata fuerint, ea sancte meditare: neque enim opus est quae arcana sunt oculis cernere.
units.tr: Ecclesiastes 3. Do not seek after things too high for you, nor search into things too hard for you; but meditate diligently on whatever commands God has given you, for there is no need to see with your eyes the things that are hidden.

units.la: AD ARGVMENTA TERTIAE CLASSIS.
units.tr: To the Arguments of the Third Class.

units.la: Caput X.
units.tr: Chapter 10.

units.la: Veniamus ad tertiam classem, quae absurda continet, tam congesta absurde ut nihil absurdius. Nam si origo spectetur absurditatum istarum, non ex nostra doctrina, sed ex cerebro hominis maleuoli & inusitata rabie petulanter in veritatem inuadentis, oriuntur, rixandi studio & calumniandi improbitate, quod libitum fuit, effutientibus; iuxta regulam; calumniare audacter, semper aliquid haeret. Tractatio vero ipsa merum est chaos, indigestáque moles, praeter loquacitatem & impudentiam nihil spirans; tot digressionibus, repetitionibus, coccysmis ubique scatet, & quasi nullo proposito scopo, aliud ex alio arripit, vt qui ista legit, idê ei vsu veniat, quod olim Lacedæmoniorum regi, qui cū legatum aliquādo prolixè sed perturbatè orantem audiuisset, respondebat Laconicè: prima oblitus sum, postrema non intellexi.
units.tr: Let us come to the third class, which contains absurdities, heaped together so absurdly that nothing could be more absurd. If we look at the origin of these absurdities, they arise not from our doctrine but from the brain of a malicious man who, in an unusual rage, attacks the truth wantonly, and who utters whatever pleases him out of a love of quarrelling and a wicked readiness to slander, following the rule: slander boldly, something always sticks. The treatment itself is pure chaos and a shapeless heap, breathing nothing but chatter and impudence. It is everywhere full of digressions, repetitions and sneers, and, as if with no aim in view, he snatches one thing after another, so that whoever reads it suffers what once happened to the king of the Spartans, who, when he had listened to an envoy making a long but muddled speech, replied tersely: I forgot the beginning, and I did not understand the end.

units.la: Sed bene factum, quod vitilitigator iste, qui in libro suo contendendi libidine nescio quò abreptus fuit, in compendio thesium, stupenda illa absurda, quæ ex Caluiniana, vt vocat, doctrina, de redemtione nimirum generis humani (de hac enim quæritur) necessario sequi dicit, ordine enumerat, vt quid velit constare possit. Sunt autem hæc:
units.tr: But it was well done that this wrangler, who was carried off somewhere in his book by a lust for contention, sets out in order, in a summary of theses, those stupendous absurdities which he says must necessarily follow from what he calls the Calvinian doctrine of the redemption of the human race (for that is the question here), so that his meaning can be grasped. They are these:

units.la: I. In dubium vocari totam religionem Christianam & fidem.
units.tr: I. That the whole Christian religion and faith is called into doubt.

units.la: II. Scripturæ talem adscisci faciem, vt mendacissimo Alcorano, quàm Dei æterni veritati similior fiat.
units.tr: II. That Scripture is given such a face that it becomes more like the most lying Alcoran than the truth of the eternal God.

units.la: III. Damnari Ecclesiam Catholicam & veram, quæ crediderit & vno semper ore confessa sit, Christum esse mortuum pro omnibus hominibus.
units.tr: III. That the Catholic and true Church is condemned, which has believed, and has always with one voice confessed, that Christ died for all men.

units.la: IV. Adigi homines ad desperationem, cum nulli nulli de falute fua quicquam conjtare pofsit. Confolationem enim & Theologiam noftram conjtare ex puris particularibus.
units.tr: IV. That men are driven to despair, since nothing whatever about one's own salvation can be established. For our consolation and our theology, he says, consist of purely particular points.

units.la: V. Abrogari vniuerfam Euangelij prædi-cationem.
units.tr: V. That the whole preaching of the Gospel is abolished.

units.la: VI. Sacramenta tolli.
units.tr: VI. That the sacraments are taken away.

units.la: VII. Accufari Deum fraudis & mendacij.
units.tr: VII. That God is accused of fraud and lying.

units.la: VIII. Chriftum accufari tanquam illufo-rem Dei & hominum.
units.tr: VIII. That Christ is accused of being a deceiver of God and men.

units.la: IX. Sequi & hoc, præfertim fi prædeftina-tionis quoque dogma, pro vt noftri de eo fen-tiant, fpectetur, Deum (quod abfit) merito ac-cufari crudelitatis, ἀπιγιαι ἀγνωσίας, iniuftitia, & breuiter pefsimorum fcelerum.
units.tr: IX. It follows also, especially if the doctrine of predestination is considered as our people hold it, that God (far be it from us) is rightly accused of cruelty, unbelief and ignorance [ἀπιστίαι ἀγνωσίας], injustice, and in a word of the worst crimes.

units.la: O fcelera omnium abominatione digniffima! Quis non attonitus ad tam graues criminationes obftupefcat?
units.tr: O crimes most worthy of all abhorrence! Who would not be stunned and struck dumb by such grave accusations?

units.la: Sed audiamus quomodo fua ifta profbet, & veritate freti, qua nihil eft validius, contra Sycophantæ morfus nos defendamus.
units.tr: But let us hear how he proves these things of his, and, relying on the truth, which is the strongest of all things, let us defend ourselves against the bites of this slanderer.

units.la: CAPVT XI.
units.tr: Chapter 11.

units.la: Apologia ad primam & secundam criminationem.
units.tr: Defence against the first and second accusations.

units.la: PRIMVM igitur calumniatur nostram de vniuersali redemtione sententiam, totá scilicet religionem Christianam & fidem ea in dubium vocari. Qui sic? probationem tanti criminis abs te requirimus Hubere, cùm nemo sit innocens futurus, si accusare sufficiat.
units.tr: First, then, he charges that our teaching on universal redemption calls into doubt the whole Christian religion and faith. How so? We require you, Huberus, to prove so grave an accusation, since no one would be innocent if it were enough merely to accuse.

units.la: Si quisquam articulus, inquis, in scriptura comprobatus & per omnes pagellas traditus & illustratus est, hic sane est, quod Christus pro toto mundo sit mortuus, nullo hominū excepto. Hunc articulum igitur negare, nihil aliud est quàm totam scripturam falsitatis arguere. Si enim istis nulla tribuitur fides tam solidè & copiosè à S. sancto dictatis, & summam continentibus totius Euangelij, quid tribuetur vniuersæ scripturæ?
units.tr: "If any article," you say, "has been established in Scripture, and is handed down and illustrated throughout all its pages, it is surely this: that Christ died for the whole world, with no one excepted. To deny this article, then, is nothing else than to charge the whole of Scripture with falsehood. For if no trust is given to these statements, dictated so firmly and so fully by the Holy Spirit and containing the sum of the whole Gospel, what trust will be given to Scripture as a whole?"

units.la: Respondeo. Negatur antecedens, quòd nimirum doctrina de redemtione vniuersali, quemadmodum Hub. Pv eam interpretatur, quasi omnibus hominibus, credentibus & non credentibus, recipientibus & contemnentibus Euangelium, peccata omnia morte Christi ex æquo remissa sint, doctrina sit S. Sancti. Neque enim, vt supra vidimus, congerie testimoniorum quæ afferuntur, hoc demonstrari potest: sed hoc est vnanime omnium Prophetarum & Apostolorum testimonium, & Euangelij summa, remissionem peccatorum videlicet accepturum per nomen Iesu Nazareni, quemuis qui in eum crediderit. Act. 10.
units.tr: I answer: the antecedent is denied, namely that the doctrine of universal redemption, as Huberus interprets it, that all sins are equally forgiven by the death of Christ to all men alike, both believers and unbelievers, both those who receive the Gospel and those who despise it, is a doctrine of the Holy Spirit. For, as we saw above, this cannot be shown by the heap of testimonies that are cited. Rather, the unanimous testimony of all the Prophets and Apostles, and the sum of the Gospel, is this: that everyone who believes in him will receive forgiveness of sins through the name of Jesus of Nazareth (Acts 10.).

units.la: Infra etiam cum ad probationem veræ sententiæ ventum erit, multis planum faciemus, quid scripturæ de præsenti controuersia nos doceant. Quare hominum, non Christi Euangelium est, remissionem peccatorum per nomen eius accipere quemuis siue credat siue non.
units.tr: Further on, when we come to the proof of the true opinion, we will make clear to many how the Scriptures teach us about the present controversy. Therefore, it is the Gospel of men, not of Christ, that one receives forgiveness of sins through his name "whether he believes or does not believe."

units.la: Facessat igitur ifthæc de scriptura gloriatio apud eos, qui scripturæ fundamento tam aperte contradicunt, viderintque ne laqueo quem tetenderunt, captus hæreat pes ipsorum. Si enim bellum contra scripturam excitare, atque que religionem & fidem Christianam euertere dicendi sunt, qui summæ totius Euangelij contradicunt, quo loco ipsos habebit orbis Christianus?
units.tr: Let this boasting about Scripture therefore cease among those who so openly contradict the foundation of Scripture; and let them see that the foot they have set in the snare they laid may be caught there. For if those who contradict the sum of the whole Gospel are to be said to stir up war against Scripture and to overthrow the Christian religion and faith, in what place will the Christian world rank them?

units.la: Altera criminatio nihil nisi Mahometismum, paganismum, Iudaismum crepat, eodem Spiritu mendacij, quo furentes Iudæi Christo Samaritanismum, & vt sic dicam, Satanismum exprobrabant. Vnde etiam, cum seruus non sit supra Dominum, nec discipulus supra magistrum suum, probrum hoc, vt alia innumera, flocci facimus.
units.tr: The second accusation does nothing but clamour about Mohammedanism, paganism, Judaism, with the same spirit of lying with which the raging Jews reproached Christ with being a Samaritan, and, if I may so put it, with being a Satanist. Hence also, since the servant is not above his lord, nor the disciple above his teacher, we make little account of this reproach, as of countless others.

units.la: Ac vt futilitas appareat, omnis criminationis prætextus in hoc est; In Alcorano Deus Mahometis sic loquitur; Si vellemus, cuique gentium bonam viam & certam daremus, sed iam verbum nostrum firmatum est, vt infernus de Dæmonum & hominum consortio impleatur. Mahometica igitur doctrina est, Deum posse quidem populos, gentes, homines omnes saluare, verum nolle; idque ideo quia ab æterno & immutabiliter decreuerit, Dæmonum & reproborum hominum damnatione iustitiam suam declarare.
units.tr: And so that its futility may appear, the whole pretext for the accusation lies in this: in the Koran, God speaks thus to Muhammad: "If we willed it, we would give every nation a good and sure way; but now our word is confirmed, that hell be filled with the company of demons and men." Therefore the Mohammedan doctrine is that God indeed could save the peoples, nations and all men, but is unwilling; and this because from eternity and immutably he has decreed to declare his justice by the damnation of demons and reprobate men.

units.la: Etsi vero calumnia hæc ad præsens institutum non multū pertinet, ideoqʒ præteriri poterat (controuersia enim nunc est de redetione, non de prædestinatione, quæ Antagonista vbiqʒ miscet, ea prorsus methodi dexteritate, qua accusationem hanc in secundam classem infarciuit, cum ad tertiam spectaret) tamen vt frontem istam perfri-ftam omnes norint, dico meram esse cauillationem & garritum. Etenim sicut in scriptis Ethnicorum, ita etiam in religionibus gentium, Turcarū & aliorum, quemadmodum etiam hæreticorū, multa reperire est cum veritate religionis Christianæ consentientia. Quæ tantum abest, vt fidem Christianam vlla ex parte suspectam reddant, aut quicquam ei derogent, vt e contrario eandem stabiliant atque corroborent. alioquin tanquam erronea, falsa, delira, Mahometica, & Ethnica, ex Christiana religione cuncta expungi oporteret, in quibus consensus talis reperitur. Verbi gratia, vnum Deum, eumque omnipotentem, creatorem cœli & terræ,
units.tr: Although this calumny does not greatly pertain to the present undertaking, and could therefore be passed over (for the controversy now is about redemption, not about predestination, which the Opponent mixes in everywhere, with that very dexterity of method by which he crammed this accusation into the second class, when it belonged to the third), nevertheless, so that everyone may know this brazen effrontery, I say it is sheer quibbling and wrangling. For just as in the writings of the Gentiles, so also in the religions of the heathen, the Turks and others, and likewise of heretics, many things can be found that agree with the truth of the Christian religion. These are so far from making the Christian faith suspect in any way, or detracting from it in any respect, that on the contrary they establish and strengthen it. Otherwise, all such points of agreement would have to be erased from the Christian religion as erroneous, false, delirious, Mohammedan and heathen. For example, the Turkish religion knows one God, and that God almighty, creator of heaven and earth,

units.la: Lib.2 De Redemtione is the running head; no other notes. terræ, Turcica nouit religio: Christum item Mariæ filium prædicat à Deo missum, cuius præcepta omnis Euangelij seruus iudicando sequi debeat: & alia eiusmodi. Neget igitur Hub. Deum vnum, neget omnipotentem, neget creatorem omnium, neget Christum Mariæ filium, neget à Deo missum, neget præcepta eius seruanda Christianis & similia, ne quicquam commune habere videatur cum Mahometistis: denique capite ipse incedat, quoniam pedibus Mahometani insistunt. Quod si hoc ridiculum est, plus quam Mahometicus furor atque rabies est, propositionem hanc tanquam Mahometicam damnare, Quod Deus possit quidem omnes saluare, sed nolit, quia secus ab æterno decreuerit. Quid Alcoranum de hoc doceat, aut non doceat, nostra nihil interest, qui non ex graue olentibus hominum lacunis, sed ex limpidissimis fontibus Israëlis veritatem haurire didicimus, & scripturarum diuinarum vnice stamus iudicio. Eæ autem nos docent, quod Deus misereatur cuius ius vult,& induret que vult, quodque Pharaone,& eius exemplo in genere vasa irę coagmetata ad interitu excitauerit, atqį excitet quotidie,vt in ipsis oltedat potetiam atque iram suam: queadmodum contra vasa misericordiæ præparauit ad gloriam,vt notas faciat diuitias gloriæ suæ. Quid, quod ijs qui ad sinistram erūt, dicet Iudex die nouissima, Maledicti abite in ignem sempiternum, qui paratus est Diabolo & Angelis eius? Hæccine obscure testantur, si spiritus quàm carnis iudicium sequi malimus, quòd licet omnes seruare Deus possit, velit tamen ex danabili malsa generis humani alios quidē seruare, alios verò damnare, secundum æternum consilium voluntatis suæ?
units.tr: (The running head reads "Book 2, On Redemption"; there are no other notes.) the Turkish religion knows one God, and that God almighty, creator of heaven and earth; it also proclaims Christ, the son of Mary, sent by God, whose precepts every servant of the Gospel ought to follow in judging; and other things of this kind. Let Huberus then deny that God is one, deny that he is almighty, deny that he is creator of all, deny that Christ is the son of Mary, deny that he was sent by God, deny that his precepts are to be kept by Christians, and similar things, lest he seem to have anything in common with the Mohammedans; in short, let him walk with his head down, since the Mohammedans tread on feet. But if this is ridiculous, and more than Mohammedan frenzy and rage, to condemn as Mohammedan this proposition: that God could indeed save all, but is unwilling, because he has decreed otherwise from eternity, what the Koran teaches or does not teach about this does not concern us. We have learned to draw the truth not from the foul-smelling pools of men but from the most clear fountains of Israel, and we stand solely by the judgment of the divine Scriptures. These teach us that God has mercy on whom he wills, and hardens whom he wills; and that he raised up Pharaoh, and in his example, vessels of wrath fitted for destruction in general, and raises them up daily, that in them he may display his power and his wrath; just as, on the other hand, he prepared vessels of mercy for glory, that he might make known the riches of his glory. What of the fact that the Judge on the last day will say to those on the left, "Depart from me, accursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels"? Do these things not testify plainly, if we prefer to follow the judgment of the spirit rather than of the flesh, that although God could save all, he nevertheless wills to save some and to damn others out of the damnable mass of the human race, according to the eternal counsel of his will?

units.la: Deinde,cum extra omnem dubitationem sit,alios saluatum,alios damnatum iri; necesse est,aut volente,aut nolente Deo id siat. Non nolente,omnipotens enim non esset. Ergo volente,& quia volete,ideo ab æterno volete; nisi existimare velimus Deum casu vel temere aliquid agere, vel in præscientiam &c &voluntate ipsius aliquid noui cadere.
units.tr: Further, since it is beyond all doubt that some will be saved and others damned, it must happen either with God willing it or with God unwilling it. Not unwilling, for then he would not be omnipotent. Therefore with God willing it, and because he wills it, he wills it from eternity; unless we are willing to think that God acts by chance or rashly, or that something new falls into his foreknowledge or his will.

units.la: Confirmat argumentum hoc Au-gust.Enchir.ad Laur. 103.cap. Nullo modo credendum est, inquit,omnipotentem Deum aliquid fieri voluisse, factumque non esse; quia sine vllis ambagibus in cælo & in terra, sicut veritas cantat, omnia quæcunque voluit, fecit: ac propterea facere profecto noluit quodcunque non fecit. Idem de correptione & gratia cap. 14. Deo volenti, inquit, saluum facere, nullum resistit liberum arbitrium: sic enim velle vel nolle, in volentis aut nolentis est potestate, vt diuinam voluntatem non impediat, nec superetpotestatem. De iis enim qui faciunt quæ Deus non vult, facit ipse quæ vult.
units.tr: Augustine confirms this argument in the Enchiridion, to Laurentius, chapter 103: "By no means must we believe," he says, "that Almighty God has willed something to be done and it has not been done; for without any ambiguity, in heaven and on earth, as truth sings, he has done all that he willed; and therefore he certainly did not will whatever he did not do." The same, in On Correction and Grace, chapter 14: "When God wills to save, no free will resists him; for to will or not to will lies in the power of the one who wills or does not will, so that it does not hinder the divine will nor overcome its power. For he himself does what he wills, of those who do what God does not will."

units.la: Lutherus quoque præfatione ad Rom. aperte scribit, à prædestinatione pendere omnia, qui credituri sint, qui non: qui seruandi, qui damnandi. Et addit, quod diligenter aduersariis notandum relinquo; stabilem esse sententiam & immotam prædestinationis necessitatem, vt mutari non possit, nec ab vlla creatura conuelli. Præcipuè verò in libro de seruo arbitrio, multis adstruit, quòd alij saluentur, alij damnentur, id omne inde proficisci, quod
units.tr: Luther too, in his preface to Romans, writes plainly that everything depends on predestination: who are to believe and who not; who are to be saved and who damned. And he adds, which I leave to be carefully noted by our adversaries, that the sentence and the necessity of predestination is fixed and immovable, so that it cannot be changed nor torn away by any creature. Above all, in his book On the Bondage of the Will, he maintains at length that some are saved and others damned, and that all this proceeds from the fact that

units.la: Deus vult alios seruari, alios damnari, iuxta illud Pauli, Quorum vult miseretur, & quos vult indurat. De reprobis vero nominatim scribit cap.161. Deum mera voluntate sua homines deserere, indurare, damnare. Et adiicit expresse, hoc illud esse, quod maxime sensum commune & rationem offendat, quasi Deus delectetur poenis & cruciatibus miserorum. Item cap.168. inquit, quod aeternus & immutabilis sit amor: aeternum item odium Dei erga homines, antequam mundus fieret. Multaque eiusmodi liber iste continet, ut, quod occulta & metuenda voluntate sua Deus ordinet, quos & quales praedicata & oblata misericordia participes esse velit: quod voluntas maiestatis ex proposito aliquos relinquat & reprobet, ut pereant, quod secreta illa voluntate maiestatis vel relicti vel indurati, non suscipiant volentem, loquentem, facientem, offerentem Deo, quod item induret volendo, voluntate illa imperscrutabili, &c. Piaque admodum est illa eiusdem admonitio, in talibus nostrum non esse scrutari diuinae voluntatis causam, sed eam reuereri, diligere & adorare coercita rationis temeritate: cum & Christus Christus (Matth. 11.) nullam aliam causam adferat, cur sapientibus abscondatur, paruulis reueletur Euangelium, quàm patris beneplacitum.
units.tr: God wills some to be saved and others damned, according to that saying of Paul: "Whom he wills he has mercy on, and whom he wills he hardens." Concerning the reprobate, he writes by name in chapter 161 that God by his mere will abandons, hardens and damns men. And he adds expressly that this is what most offends common sense and reason, as if God took delight in the punishments and torments of the wretched. Likewise, in chapter 168, he says that the love of God is eternal and unchangeable; likewise his hatred toward men is eternal, before the world was made. And this book contains many things of this kind, such as: that God, by his hidden and dreaded will, ordains whom and what sort of people he wishes to share in the preached and offered mercy; that by the purpose of his majesty's will he leaves some behind and reprobates them, so that they perish; that by that secret will of his majesty, those who are left behind or hardened do not accept God willing, speaking, doing and offering; that he likewise hardens by willing, by that inscrutable will, and so on. And that admonition of the same author is quite pious: that in such matters it is not for us to search into the cause of the divine will, but to revere, love and adore it, restraining the rashness of reason; since Christ too (Matt. 11) gives no other cause why the Gospel is hidden from the wise and revealed to little ones, than the Father's good pleasure.

units.la: Hæc Lutheri doctrina est, Hubere, longè certius spiritu Dei redolàs, quàm vaticinia illa quæ tu ex eo prolata ad omnes teplorum valuas adscribi, & omniu cordibus insculpi optas. Quid ni igitur in tepla omnia eam admittitis, & vestris aliorumque animis insculpitis, contentione sublata? Id si feceritis, recte: sin autem in nobis eam culpare, & soli-ta audacia velut Mahumeticam, aut Mahumetismo aliisque ineffabili malo fores aperientem, petulati stylo & lingua proscribere perrexeritis, maturè dispicite moneo, quo præcipitaturi fitis Lutheri autoritatem, in qua ad coelum vsque euehenda hactenus tanto-pere defuadastis.
units.tr: This is Luther's doctrine, Hubert, and it smells far more certainly of the Spirit of God than those prophecies which you wish to be attached to the doors of every temple and engraved on the hearts of all. Why then do you not admit it everywhere, in all temples, and engrave it on your own minds and those of others, with the quarrelling set aside? If you do so, well and good. But if you go on, with your usual audacity, to condemn it in us, and to banish it with a petulant pen and tongue as Mahometan, or as opening the door to Mahometanism and other unspeakable evils, I advise you to consider carefully over what precipice you are about to hurl Luther's authority, the authority you have so strongly urged up to now, raising it to the heavens.

units.la: CAPVT XII. Ad tertiam criminationem.
units.tr: CHAPTER XII. Against the third accusation.

units.la: Impvdens porrò oratio est, damnari nari à nobis Ecclesiam Catholicam & veram, quæ crediderit & vno semper ore confessa sit, Christum esse mortuū pro omnibus hominibus.
units.tr: Moreover, it is an imprudent claim that the Catholic and true Church, which has believed and has always confessed with one voice that Christ died for all men, is condemned by us.

units.la: Confitemur & nos Christum mortuum pro omnibus. Quis enim neget sine distinctione, quod sacris literis aliquoties expressè traditum est? Sed de hoc quæstio est, an omnes, credentes simul & non credentes, ab omni peccato & condemnatione per mortem Christi liberati, iustificati, & à patre tanquam filij hæredes, in gratiam recepti sint? Id Ecclesiam catholicam vnanimiter credidisse, salsissimum est: quin potius hoc semper credidit, & vno semper ore confessa est, quo remissionem peccatorum per meritum Christi adipiscamur, fidem requiri, sine qua impossibile est Deo placere. Sed enim quid veteres de præsenti controversia senserit, ex iis quæ supra hic illic ex veterum scriptis retulimus clarum est, & ostendetur copiosissimè cum ad sententiæ nostræ confirmationem ventum erit. Iam hoc sufficerit, si ad testimonia ab ad-
units.tr: We too confess that Christ died for all. For who would deny without distinction what the sacred letters have stated expressly on several occasions? But the question is this: have all, believers and unbelievers alike, been freed from all sin and condemnation through the death of Christ, justified, and received into grace by the Father as heirs with the Son? That the Catholic Church has unanimously believed this is most untrue. Rather, she has always believed and always confessed with one voice that we obtain forgiveness of sins through the merit of Christ, and that faith is required, without which it is impossible to please God. What the ancients thought about the present controversy is clear from the things we have related above, here and there, from the writings of the ancients, and it will be shown very fully when we come to the confirmation of our view. For now it will be enough if we briefly answer the testimonies brought forward by the ad-

units.la: uaruerfario prolata paucis responderi- mus.
units.tr: versary.

units.la: Principio ex Cyrillo adducitur, in Ioh.lib.2.cap.53.quod ait, iudicatum iam esse incredulum, quod ipse in se ipsum, largitorem indemnationis contemnendo, condemnatio- nis ferat sententiam. Quid hoc ad rem? aut quis negat, infideles autorem falu- tis respuere, dum in nomen vnigeniti filij Dei non credunt, & idcirco condé- nationem & iram Dei manere super ipsos?
units.tr: First, a passage from Cyril is cited, In Ioh. lib. 2. cap. 53. where he says that the unbeliever is already judged, since by despising the giver of indemnity he pronounces the sentence of condemnation upon himself. What does this have to do with the matter? Or who denies that unbelievers reject the author of salvation, since they do not believe in the name of the only-begotten Son of God, and therefore the condemnation and wrath of God remain upon them?

units.la: Rei aliquato accommodatio ra sunt Athanasij verba, in Euangelium de pasf. & cruce Christi: Caluariae locum, inquit, Hebraeorum magistri dicunt esse sepulchrum Adae. Quod si ita res se habet, miror eius loci genium & proprietatem. Congruum enim erat, Dominum, cum vellet reuocare primum Adam, in eo loco pati, vt illius abolito peccato, ab vniuerso eius genere illud profligaret. Et paulo ante ea verba inquit, Dominum immolatum, vt sua immolationis sanguine omnes liberaret. Quod dictum miror aduersarium praeteriisse, si Athanasium ipsemet legit. Q ij
units.tr: The words of Athanasius are somewhat more suited to the matter: in the Gospel on the passion and cross of Christ: The masters of the Hebrews say, he says, that the place of Calvary is the sepulchre of Adam. If this is so, I marvel at the fitness and appropriateness of that place. For it was fitting that the Lord, when he wished to recall the first Adam, should suffer in that place, so that, his sin being abolished, he might overthrow it for his whole race. And a little before those words he says, The Lord was sacrificed, that by the blood of his sacrifice he might free all. I marvel that the adversary passed over this saying, if he has read Athanasius himself.

units.la: Sed vel de sufficientia hoc intellexit, vt alios patres similia dicta sua accipi voluisse mox audiemus: vel Synecdochicè locutus est de vniuersitate fidelium, qui ex toto genere humano concurrunt. Nam secundum declarationem Prosperi lib. 2. cap. 1. de vocatione gentium, neutra pars, bonorum inquam & malorum, seruandorum & damnandorum, nuncupatione omnium hominum priuatur: habente quidem salutis suæ damnum rebellium portione, sed obtinente plenitudinis censum fidelium dignitate. Et eò citat dictum r. Ioh. 2. Ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris, non pro nostris tantum, sed totius mundi. Et lib. 1. cap. 3. idem ex variis scripturæ dictis in hunc modum concludit: Habet ergo populus Dei plenitudinem suam, & quamuis magna pars hominum Salvatoris gratiam aut repellat aut negligat, in electis tamen & præscitis, atque ab omnium generalitate discretis, speciali quadam censetur vniuersitas, vt de toto mundo totus mundus liberatus, & de omnibus hominibus omnes homines videantur assumti: sicut etiam cum cum de impijs sermo est, ita locutionem suam stylus diminus ordinat, vt quae de parte qua- dam dicuntur, ad omnes homines pertinere videantur. Atque id ipsum variis ibi- de documentis demonstrat, etiam pro parte terrae omnem terram, & pro par- te mundi totum mundum, & pro parte hominum omnes homines nominari. Et sic Ambrosius in 3.cap.ad Rom. decla- rat illud, Omnes declinauerunt. Neque enim, inquit, quia dicit Omnes, totam penitus plebem significat, sed hac partem plebis, in qua omnes mali continentur. Et adducit quod apud Ieremiā est, omnes insurrexisse in Prophetam Domini, vt eum occiderent. Et sequitur: Omnis autem populus non permisit. De quo exemplo ita Ambrosius. Illos ergo omnes dicit, sed malos: & hos omnes, sed bonos. Semper enim duo populi sunt in vna plebe.
units.tr: But either he understood this of sufficiency, as we shall soon hear that the other Fathers wished their similar sayings to be understood; or he spoke synecdochically of the whole body of believers, who come together from the entire human race. For according to Prosper's explanation, book 2, chapter 1, on the calling of the Gentiles, neither part, I mean of the good and of the evil, of those to be saved and those to be damned, is deprived of the name of all men: the rebels indeed have the loss of their salvation as their portion, but the believers hold the dignity of the full count. And to this he cites the saying of 1 John 2: "He himself is the propitiation for our sins, not for ours only, but for the whole world." And in book 1, chapter 3, he concludes the same from various sayings of Scripture in this way: The people of God therefore has its fullness, and although a great part of men either reject or neglect the grace of the Saviour, yet among the elect and foreknown, distinguished from the general mass of all, a certain special totality is counted, so that of the whole world the whole world is seen to be freed, and of all men all men are seen to be taken up; just as also when there is talk of the impious, the style of speech so arranges its wording that what is said of a certain part seems to pertain to all men. And he demonstrates this very thing by various examples there: that for a part of the earth the whole earth, for a part of the world the whole world, and for a part of men all men are named. And so Ambrose, on chapter 3 of Romans, explains that saying, All have turned aside. For, he says, when it says "all," it does not signify the whole people entirely, but that part of the people in which all the wicked are contained. And he adduces what is in Jeremiah, that all rose up against the prophet of the Lord to kill him. And it follows: "But all the people did not consent." Of this example Ambrose says: He calls them all, but meaning the wicked; and these all, but meaning the good. For there are always two peoples in one populace.

units.la: Sed ne dubitemus de Athanasij mete, ea ipsa oratione gratiam redemtionis ita describit: Christum hominem factum & mortuum, vt nos mortales viuificaremur, neque vlterius pateremur regnum mortis: ideo crucifixum, vt maledictionem redimeret, & nos benedictionem possideremus. Si hoc de omnibus sine exceptione hominibus intelligatur, non erunt amplius quibus mors & infernus dominentur. Deinde Athanasius ibidem dictam Synecdochen frequenter inculcat, vt quod ait, Diabolo ex inferno eiecto, omnes vinctos eius virtute Christi eductos: id quod de vniuersitate sanctorum, qui cum Adamo liberati sunt, ipsè statim explicat. Similiter ait, Diabolum omnia suaspolia amisisse, & Iro factum pauperiorem. Loquitur autem de conuersis, qui vbique locorum ex potestate Satanæ in regnum Christi transferuntur. Eadem ratione indubitanter dicit, in omnes & omnia in loca venisse cognitionem Dei, omnes conculcare Diabolum, omnes ei illudere Christi auspicio, omnem machinam obliteratam, & sapientiam Gracorum vniuersam infatuatam, quoniam saluatoris mors orbem terrarum in libertatem asseruerit, causamque dederit, vt gentes Deum glorificent, Iudaeis manentibus in cognitione Christi occæcatis. Hæc manifeste ostendunt quomodo Athanasius senserit Christum mortuum, vt ab vnivniuerso genere humano peccatum propulsaret, secundum illud, Ioh.12. quod & ipse citat, Cum exaltatus fuero, traham admè omnia.
units.tr: But lest we doubt Athanasius's meaning, in the same discourse he describes the grace of redemption thus: Christ was made man and died, so that we mortals might be made alive, and that we should no longer suffer the reign of death; therefore he was crucified, that he might redeem the curse, and that we might possess the blessing. If this is understood of all men without exception, there will no longer be any over whom death and hell rule. Then Athanasius, in the same place, frequently presses the synecdoche mentioned, as when he says, The devil having been cast out of hell, all who were bound by him were led out by the power of Christ: which he himself at once explains as the whole body of the saints who were freed together with Adam. Similarly he says, The devil has lost all his spoils and has been made poorer, like Irus. But he speaks of converts, who are transferred from the power of Satan into the kingdom of Christ in every place. By the same reasoning he says without doubt, The knowledge of God has come into all places and to all, all trample down the devil, all mock him under the auspices of Christ, every machine is blotted out, and the whole wisdom of the Greeks is made foolish, since the death of the Saviour has asserted the world to freedom and has given the cause that the nations should glorify God, while the Jews remain blinded in the knowledge of Christ. These things clearly show how Athanasius thought that Christ died to drive sin away from the whole human race, according to that saying of John 12, which he himself also cites: When I shall be lifted up, I will draw all things to me.

units.la: Adhæc citatur Chrysostomus in 1. ad Tim.Hom.7. vbi dicit Christum etiam pro gentilibus & non credentibus pependisse in cruce.
units.tr: Next, Chrysostom is cited, on 1 Timothy, homily 7, where he says that Christ also hung on the cross for the Gentiles and unbelievers.

units.la: Respondeo. Non hoc tantum, sed plus etiam ille dicit, Christum pro omnibus mortuum, pro credentibus & non credentibus. Homil.17.in Epist.ad Heb. in illud Apostolus. Oblatus est vt auferret peccata multorum. Sed declarat seipsum, eiusmodi accipienda quod ad sufficientiam seu magnitudinem pretii attinet, non quod ad effectum. Sic enim multorum tantum, & non omnium; nempe credentium, non autem incredulorum peccata oblatione Christi ablata esse docet. Verba eius hæc sunt, Quare oblatus dicitur ad multorum & non omnium peccata auferenda? Quia non omnes credunt. Pro omnibus quidem mortuus est, quantum in ipso est, hoc est, mors illa eius momenti est, cuius momenti est omnium per-
units.tr: I answer: he says not only this, but even more, that Christ died for all, for believers and unbelievers. Homily 17 on the Epistle to the Hebrews, on the Apostle's words, He was offered to take away the sins of many. But he explains himself, that such things are to be taken as regards the sufficiency or magnitude of the price, not as regards the effect. For thus he teaches that the sins of many only, and not of all, namely of believers and not of unbelievers, were taken away by the offering of Christ. His words are these: Why is he said to be offered to take away the sins of many and not of all? Because not all believe. He died for all indeed, as far as he is concerned; that is, that death of his has such weight as the ruin of all men has, per-

units.la: Qiiij ditio. Theophylactus Chryfoftomi abbreuiator, eandem distinctionem expressit ad Heb. 2. & 9. & commemorat Basilium quoque ita distinxisse. Vnde & Chryfoftomus homil.39. in 1.ad Cor. in illud Apostoli, quod omnes in Christo viui-ficentur, aperte negat id accipi posse de iustitia omnium, quasi quicunque in Adamo peccatores coftituti sunt, in Christo iustitia donati sunt. Ex his perspicuum est, cui sententiæ Chryfoftomus, Theophylactus, Bafilius aliique patres accedant.
units.tr: -dition. Theophylact, the abridger of Chrysostom, expressed the same distinction on Hebrews 2 and 9, and mentions that Basil also drew the distinction in this way. Hence Chrysostom too, homily 39 on 1 Corinthians, on the Apostle's words that all are made alive in Christ, plainly denies that this can be understood of the righteousness of all, as if all who were constituted sinners in Adam were endowed with righteousness in Christ. From these things it is clear to which opinion Chrysostom, Theophylact, Basil and the other Fathers agree.

units.la: In Augustino citando nescio vafriciem, an crassitiem, in aduersario culpe. Librum inscripsit Augustt. de falso sibi impositis articulis, quorum primus erat quod ipsi falso imponebatur (quemadmodum etiam ab æmulis nobis falso imponitur hodie) ac si doceret Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum non pro omnium hominum redemtione esse passum. Ergo inquis Augustini iudicio falsa & profana opinio est, Christum non esse passum pro redemtione omnium.
units.tr: In citing Augustine, I do not know whether the adversary's fault is craftiness or crassness. He entitled a book of Augustine On the articles falsely imposed upon him, of which the first was what was falsely imposed on him (as even today our rivals falsely impose it on us), as if he taught that our Lord Jesus Christ did not suffer for the redemption of all men. Therefore, you say, by Augustine's judgment it is a false and profane opinion that Christ did not suffer for the redemption of all.

units.la: Verum sophistico aut fycophantico artiartificio praeteriit Huberus, quae Augustinus ibi pro articuli huius declaratione prolixe scribit. Nam distinctionem ante ex Chrysostomo allatam ipse quoque adhibens, inquit, Quod ad magnitudinem & potentiam pertinet, & quod ad unam pertinet causam generis humani, sanguis Christi redemptio est totius mundi: & sic redemti omnes recte dicuntur, sed cum, qui hoc seculum sine fide Christi, & sine regenerationis sacramento pertranseunt, redemptionis alieni sunt, haud dubie redemptionis proprietas penes illos est, de quibus princeps mundi missus est foras, & iam non vasa diaboli, sed membra sunt Christi: cuius mors non impensa est humano generi, ut ad redemptionem eius etiam qui regenerandi non erant, pertinerent. Poculum quippe immortalitatis quod confectum est de infirmitate nostra & virtute divina, habet quidem in se ut omnibus prosit, sed si non bibitur, non proficit. Haec ille.
units.tr: Yet Huber, with a sophistical or slanderous trick, passes over what Augustine writes at length there to explain this article. For he himself, adopting the distinction first drawn from Chrysostom, says: "As far as its greatness and power are concerned, and as far as it concerns the one cause of the human race, the blood of Christ is the redemption of the whole world, and in this sense all are rightly said to be redeemed. But those who pass through this age without faith in Christ and without the sacrament of regeneration are strangers to the redemption. Without doubt the proper possession of redemption lies with those over whom the prince of this world has been cast out, and who are no longer vessels of the devil but members of Christ. His death was not so spent on the human race that even those who were not to be regenerated should belong to his redemption." For the cup of immortality, prepared from our weakness and divine power, certainly has in itself that it may benefit all, but if it is not drunk, it does not profit. Thus he.

units.la: Quod ad dictum Maximi apud Augustinum serm. 128. de tempore: legimus in scripturis, quod totius generis humani salus redempta sit sanguine salvatoris, & totius mundi incolumitas sempiterna. Possent ea ver-
units.tr: As for the saying of Maximus in Augustine, Sermon 128, On the Time: "We read in the Scriptures that the salvation of the whole human race has been redeemed by the blood of the Saviour, and the everlasting safety of the whole world." These words could be

units.la: Qv ba exponi quantum ad magnitudinem & potentiam pretij attinet, tam diuitis, vt si vniuersi in Christum crederet, nullum diabolica vincula retinerent, sed omnes incolumitate fruerentur sempiterna. Sed genuinus sensuseft, autorem ibi loqui de vniuersitate credetium per totum mundum: quod fatebitur quisquis institutum eius considerarit. Id enim vult, mundum instar agri figuli, pretio sanguinis dominici emtum peregrinis, hoc est, inquit, Christianis, toto orbe exulibus, vt quibus non est in mundo possessio, totum possideant salvatorem. Ergo nihil redemtio illa ad incredulos, mundi filios atque possessores. Atque haec constans patrum doctrina est, prout fusius ostendetur lib. sequenti.
units.tr: explained as regards the greatness and power of the price, so rich that if all the world believed in Christ, no bonds of the devil would hold them, but all would enjoy everlasting safety. But the genuine sense is that the author is speaking there of the body of believers throughout the whole world; anyone who considers his purpose will admit this. For he means that the world, like a field of the potter, was bought with the price of the Lord's blood for strangers, that is, he says, for Christians, exiles throughout the whole earth, so that, having no possession in the world, they might possess the Saviour entire. Therefore that redemption does nothing for unbelievers, the sons and possessors of the world. And this is the constant teaching of the Fathers, as will be shown more fully in the following book.

units.la: De iis autem qui fide suscepta postea ad vomitum redeunt, parum interest, quomodo patrum quaedam dicta accipiamus, quibus gratiam indulgentiae & emundationis peccatorum, adoptione & similia talibus attribuisse leguntur.
units.tr: As for those who, having received the faith, afterwards return to their vomit, it matters little how we understand certain sayings of the Fathers, in which they are read to have attributed the grace of forgiveness and cleansing of sins, adoption and the like, to such people.

units.la: Neque enim controversiae cardo is est, an
units.tr: For the crux of the controversy is not this: whether

units.la: Vide etiā Ambros. in Luc. 23. de cassa proditoris poenitetia
units.tr: See also Ambrose on Luke 23, on the empty repentance of the betrayer.

units.la: Cypr. de ablut. pedum, Aug. serm. in monte l.1. Chrysost. Homil. 9. & 20. an qui semel fide peccatorū indulgen- tiam cōsequuti sunt,gratia illa cōtingat excidere nec ne?sed an omnes,credētes & non credentes, gratiam indulgentiæ illius & emundationis peccatorum se- mel acceperint nec ne?Negantem par- tem,quam nos tuemur,ipsa illa patrum dicta comprobant:quia de conuersis & baptizatis loquuntur , & his demum tribuunt,quod à peccatis liberati & fi- lii Dei facti sint. Quomodo autem nonnulli hanc gratiam postea amittant ad vomitum redeuntes, supra abundè expositimus: quòd scilicet, quatenus Ecclesiæ annumerantur, pro reconci- liatis & filiis Dei habeantur & habendi sint iudicio caritatis, licet apud Deum sæpe tales non sint , vt diserte Augustinus testabatur. Vnde etiam serm.Domini in monte lib.1. coniungit ista,participem fieri spiritus gratiæ qua reconciliamur Deo, & societatem sanctæ fraternitatis inire: cum interea in societatem istam multi pas- sim obrepant hypocritæ,visibilem tan- tummodo sanctificationem cum Si- mone Mago habentes,inuisibili caren- tes.
units.tr: Cyprian, On the Washing of Feet; Augustine, Sermon on the Mount, book 1; Chrysostom, Homilies 9 and 20. Whether those who have once obtained the indulgence of sins by faith can fall from that grace or not; but whether all, believers and unbelievers alike, have once received that grace of forgiveness and cleansing of sins or not. The fathers' own words confirm the side we defend, which denies it, because they speak of converted and baptized people, and they ascribe to these alone that they have been freed from sins and made sons of God. How some afterwards lose this grace by returning to their vomit, we have set out fully above: namely, that insofar as they are counted in the Church, they are and ought to be held, by the judgment of charity, as reconciled and sons of God, although before God they are often not such, as Augustine plainly testified. Hence also, in Sermon on the Mount, book 1, he joins these things: "to become a partaker of the Spirit of grace by which we are reconciled to God, and to enter into the fellowship of holy brotherhood," while meanwhile many hypocrites creep everywhere into that fellowship, having only the visible sanctification with Simon Magus, and lacking the invisible.

units.la: De Neotericis porrò, qui ob phrases quasdam in erroris trahuntur patrocinium, non est quod laboremus; quia non huius vel illius doctoris praeiudicatam opinionem, sed veritatem ipsam sectamur. In gratiam tamen studiosorum veritatis, aliquid monere visum est.
units.tr: As for the moderns, who are drawn into the defence of error by certain phrases, we need not take trouble over them, since we pursue not the prejudiced opinion of this or that teacher, but the truth itself. Nevertheless, for the sake of students of the truth, it has seemed good to offer a word of warning.

units.la: Citantur Bullingerus, Gualtherus, Musculus & alij, nec non unius vel alterius Ecclesiae per Helvetiam confessiones: Ex quibus hae & similes locutiones studiose excerpuntur: Christum videlicet, a quantum in ipso est saluatorem esse omnibus, & venisse omnibus saluandis: b Pro omnibus omnium temporum perlitasse peccatis: c Passionem eius pro omnium hominum peccato satisfacere debuisse, & totum mundum per eam vivificatum: d Gratiam remissionis peccatorum mortalibus omnibus destinatam, & id genus alia.
units.tr: Citations are made from Bullinger, Gualtherus, Musculus and others, and also from the confessions of one or another church throughout Helvetia. From these, such phrases and similar expressions are carefully excerpted: that Christ, (a) as far as in him lies, is the Saviour of all, and has come to save all; (b) has atoned for the sins of all the ages for all; (c) that his passion ought to satisfy for the sin of all men, and that through it the whole world has been made alive; (d) that the grace of forgiveness of sins is destined for all mortals, and other things of that kind.

units.la: Ad haec respondeo, quomodocunque & quocunq; sensu locutiones has & similes scriptores isti protulerint, certum esse, eos non statuisse cum adversario, efficaciter & re ipsa omnes, siue cucuiusquam exceptione, & absque vllo discrimine credentium & incredulorum, in gratiam receptos, & remissionis peccatorum, iustitiæ atque salutis in Christo factos participes. De quo ne vllus relinquatur dubitandi locus in Miscellaneis D. Hieronymi Zanchij, piæ memoriæ, extat Ecclesiæ scholæque Tigurinæ iudicium de eiusdem Zanchii thesibus aliquot, quæ eo tempore à quibusdam, eandem cum Humbero Camarinam mouentibus, odiose agitabantur.
units.tr: To these things I reply: however and in whatever sense these writers have put forward these and similar expressions, it is certain that they did not hold, with our opponent, that all, without any exception and without any distinction between believers and unbelievers, were effectively and in fact received into grace and made partakers of forgiveness of sins, righteousness and salvation in Christ. So that no ground for doubt may remain on this point, there exists, in the Miscellanies of Jerome Zanchius, of blessed memory, the judgment of the Church and school of Zurich on some theses of the same Zanchius, which at that time were being maliciously attacked by certain men who, like Humbert, were stirring up the same storm.

units.la: Promissiones de gratuita Dei misericordia, deque certa & æterna salute inquit Zanchius prpositione 13. etsi vniuersaliter omnibus proponuntur, & prædicandæ sunt, ad ipsos tamen tantum electos re ipsa pertinent. Et mox propositione 14. Quare cum Paulus ait, Deus vult omnes homines saluos fieri: si quis illam vocem omnes restringat ad electos in quocunque hominum ordine sint: item si illud 1. Ioh. 2. Christus est propitiatio totius mundi, interpretetur pro electis per totum orbem dispersis aut
units.tr: Promises concerning God's free mercy, and concerning certain and eternal salvation, says Zanchius in proposition 13, although they are proposed universally to all and must be preached, nevertheless in actual fact pertain only to the elect. And soon after, in proposition 14: Therefore when Paul says, God wills all men to be saved, if someone restricts that word "all" to the elect, in whatever order of men they are; likewise if someone interprets that saying of 1 John 2, "Christ is the propitiation for the whole world," as meaning the elect scattered throughout the whole earth, or

units.la: 1.Tim. 2. aut dispergendis,non deprauat scriptu-ram.
units.tr: (1 Tim. 2.) or to be scattered, does not distort Scripture.

units.la: Quid ad hæc lumina illa Ecclesiæ Hel-ueticæ, Bullingerus, Gualtherus, VVolfius, Martyr, Simlerus, Lauaterus & reliqui? Promissiones quod ad gratuitam Dei misericordiam,certam & æternam sa-lutem, non solùm assentiuntur ad ele-ctos tantum pertinere, verùm etiam confirmant hoc argumento;quod pro-missiones occulta sint fidei, nec aliter quam fide percipi queant:ac propter-ea eorum tantum sint, qui fide diuini-tus ornentur. Sunt quidem,inquiunt, promissiones huius generis omnibus prædicandæ, quoniam verbi ministri electos secundum propositum non a-gnoscunt, gregemq; habent ex repro-bis & electis conflatum, sed tantùm in illis facultate spiritus Dei redduntur efficaces, qui cœtui electorum accen-sentur.
units.tr: What do those lights of the Helvetic Church say to this, Bullinger, Gualtherus, Wolf, Martyr, Simler, Lavater and the rest? They not only agree that the promises concerning God's free mercy and certain and eternal salvation pertain only to the elect, but they also confirm this by an argument: that the promises are hidden from faith, and cannot be perceived except by faith, and therefore belong only to those who are divinely adorned with faith. Such promises of this kind, they say, indeed are to be preached to all, since the ministers of the Word do not recognise the elect according to God's purpose, and have a flock made up of the reprobate and the elect; but they are made effective only in those in whom the power of God's Spirit is present, who are counted in the assembly of the elect.

units.la: Postea de altera thesi, id est, de tota præsenti controuersia,puram & candi-dam & sonora voce clamantem confes-sionem edunt,his verbis: Nos profecto sufumus in eadem sententia,nec eam ex- positionem salua conscientia reiicere possumus, quam & congruā esse agnoscimus, & ab Augusti. patre omnium laudatissimo non semel allatam: cuius interpretationis ergo á nemine vnquā hæreseos est damnatus.
units.tr: Afterwards, concerning the other thesis, that is, concerning the whole present controversy, they put forth a confession which clearly and sonorously proclaims, in these words: "We certainly are of the same opinion, and we cannot, with a clear conscience, reject that explanation which we acknowledge to be fitting, and which has been brought forward more than once by Augustine, the most praised father of all; on account of this interpretation no one has ever been condemned as a heretic."

units.la: Ibidem subscribunt etiam sententiæ Zanchii,quod electis semel tantum vera fides detur, quodq; electi semel vera fide donati, Christoque per S. sanctum insiti, fidem prorsus amittere, S. sanctū omninò excutere, & à Christo excidere repenitus non possint, idque propter promissionem Dei,& precationem Christi. Fatentur interim veram fidem & spiritum in sanctis,quando labuntur, consopiri & languescere, non autem prorsus auferri: alioquin semen Dei in ipsis non maneret,vt dicitur 1.Ioh.3.
units.tr: In the same place they also subscribe to the opinion of Zanchius, that true faith is given to the elect only once, and that the elect, once endowed with true faith and grafted into Christ through the Holy Spirit, cannot wholly lose faith, wholly cast out the Holy Spirit, or fall away from Christ again, and this on account of God's promise and Christ's intercession. Meanwhile they confess that true faith and the Spirit in the saints, when they stumble, are lulled to sleep and grow faint, but are not altogether taken away; otherwise the seed of God would not remain in them, as it is said in 1 John 3.

units.la: Vides Hubere tantorum virorum, quos tu defensores tibi parasti,consentiente iudicio contra te pronunciatū? Non igitur est quod verborum tendiculas aucuperis,& in phrasibus quibusdam eorum constituas insidias,de quorum rum sententia tam aperte constat. Ne tamen in iis te haerere contingat, vel vnum consule Huldrychum Zuinglium, Helvetiae tuae decus & omnigenae eruditionis splendorem, Annotati in Euang. & epist. Pauli, per Leonem Iudae editis. Ibi non rarae sunt locutiones eiusmodi, à successoribus eius postmodum similiter vsurpatae, quod filius Dei carnem assumferit vt sacrificium fieret pro totius mundi peccatis: quod caro eius pro totius mundi vita & redemtione fit tradita, & pro omnibus ipse mortuus fit vt omnes vivificaret per se ipsum, & morte sua vitam daret vniuerso mundo: quod venerit Christus vt saluet omnes, & det omnibus vitam aeternam, &c. Solet sane vir ille ita loqui, sed sensu longe alio atque tu locutiones huiusmodi in discipulis & successoribus eius venaris. Se ipsum enim declarans exprese scribit, cum Christi mors remedium sit & malagma morborum & vulnerum nostrorum, efficaciam tamen eius multos non sentire, qui nempe peccata sua no agnoscant. Item, misit eum vt omnibus peccatoribus poenitentibus peccata remittat,
units.tr: Do you see, Huber, the agreed judgment pronounced against you by such great men, whom you have gathered as defenders for yourself? There is therefore no reason for you to set snares of words, or to lay traps in certain phrases of theirs, when their opinion is so plainly established. Yet, lest you be caught in these, consult at least one, Huldrych Zwingli, the glory of your Helvetia and the splendour of learning of every kind, in his Annotations on the Gospel and Epistles of Paul, published by Leo Jud. There are not rare expressions of this sort there, afterwards similarly used by his successors: that the Son of God assumed flesh so that a sacrifice might be made for the sins of the whole world; that his flesh was given up for the life and redemption of the whole world; and that he himself died for all, so that he might make all alive through himself, and by his death give life to the whole world; that Christ came that he might save all, and give eternal life to all, etc. That man indeed is accustomed to speak thus, but in a sense far different from that in which you hunt for such expressions among his disciples and successors. For declaring himself, he writes plainly that, although Christ's death is the remedy and plaster of our diseases and wounds, many do not feel its efficacy, namely those who do not acknowledge their sins. Likewise, he sent him that he might forgive sins to all penitent sinners,

units.la: Annotat. ad Heb. 9. In Ioh. 6. In Ioh. 12. In Ioh. 17. In Mat. 15. In Ioh. 3. remittat,& vitam æternam communi- cet:vitam eum esse & salutem piorum, vitam credentium,& similia. Et tamen tollit peccata totius mundi, vitámque donat vniuersis, cùm quia nulla in mũ-do remittuntur peccata nisi per & propter vnicum reconciliatorem Christum Iesum, tum quia seruator est vniuersa- lis,videlicet, non Iudæorum modo sed & gentium,vt qui oblatione Christi fre- ti sunt, perpetuò per ipsum ad Deum accedát, & fide per Christum omnium peccatorum suorum delectionem ha- beant:quemadmodum copiosius apud eundem videre est,tomo primo,expostul. ad Fridolinum. Attede & perpende Hu-bere,& Heluetiorum testi-monijs abuti desine.
units.tr: Annotat. ad Heb. 9. In Ioh. 6. In Ioh. 12. In Ioh. 17. In Mat. 15. In Ioh. 3. remits sins and communicates eternal life: that he is the life and salvation of the godly, the life of believers, and similar things. And yet he takes away the sins of the whole world and gives life to all, both because no sins in the world are forgiven except through and on account of the one reconciler, Christ Jesus, and because he is the universal Saviour, that is, not only of the Jews but also of the Gentiles, so that those who trust in the offering of Christ may always come to God through him and, by faith in Christ, have the forgiveness of all their sins. This can be seen more fully in the same author, in the first volume, Expostulatio ad Fridolinum. Pay attention and weigh it carefully, Huber, and stop abusing the testimonies of the Helvetians.

units.la: Idem dico de Musculo,cuius sentē- tiam qui introspicit, sat scio mirabi-tur Huberi ingenium, atque omnia peruertendi studium & Sophisticen. Eius verba sunt, Gratiam remissionis peccato-rum destinatam esse mortalibus omnibus. Hoc Huberus auidè arreptum maiu-sculis literis libro suo inseruit: sed ma-litiolitiosè prorsus à sequetibus reuulsum, quibus declaratio dicti illius inest: Gratiam videlicet remissionis peccatorum mortalibus omnibus destinatam esse, quatenus omni creaturæ annunciandū est Euangelium, & proponenda omnibus misericordia Dei. Et sic Musculus intelligit dicta, Sic Deus dilexit mundum. Christus est propitiatio pro totius mundi peccatis: nō autem quòd omnibus, sine discrimine credentium & non credentium, remissio peccatorum per gratiā Dei obtingat: quod aduersarius sentit, Musculus non sentit. Imò sic testatur palàm: Si consideremus eos qui peccatorum suorum remissione per gratiam Dei acquirūt, quemadmodum electorum, ita & istorum modicus est numerus respectu reproborum, quorum in sempiternum dicit retineri peccata. Idem cōsulatur etiam loco de redemptione, vbi inquit; scimus non omnes huius redemtionis fieri participes: Item, homines, inquit, reprobi ac deplorate impij redemtione non accipiunt. Huius contrarium plenis buccis asserit Hubern rus, omnes per Christum redemtionis factos participes: omnes eam accipere, sed reprobos semel acceptam denuò amittere.
units.tr: The same I say of Musculus. Anyone who looks closely at his opinion will, I am sure, marvel at Huber's cleverness, his zeal for twisting everything, and his sophistry. His words are: The grace of the forgiveness of sins is destined for all mortals. Huber eagerly seized on this, put it into his book in capital letters, but maliciously tore it away from the sentences that follow, which explain its meaning: namely, that the grace of forgiveness of sins is destined for all mortals inasmuch as the gospel must be announced to every creature and the mercy of God must be offered to all. This is how Musculus understands the sayings, God so loved the world and Christ is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world. He does not mean that forgiveness of sins through the grace of God falls to all without distinction, believers and unbelievers alike; what the opponent holds, Musculus does not hold. Indeed, he plainly testifies: "If we consider those who obtain the remission of their sins through the grace of God, the number of these is small compared with the reprobate, whose sins he says will be retained forever, just as the number of the elect is small." The same may be consulted also in the place on redemption, where he says: "We know that not all become partakers of this redemption"; and again: "Reprobate men and desperately wicked ones, he says, do not receive redemption." Huber asserts the opposite with full cheeks: that all have been made partakers of redemption through Christ, that all receive it, but that the reprobate, once having received it, lose it again.

units.la: Nihilominus, secundum rationes à Musculo assignatas, redemtio isthæc vniuersalis rectè dicitur. I. quia non fit defectu gratiæ, quod multi pereant, sed defectu fidei, cum gratia parata sit cunctis, eam videlicet non repudiantibus, sicut omnia parata erat ad nuptias. II. quia omnes ad illam vocantur.
units.tr: Nevertheless, according to the reasons Musculus assigns, this universal redemption is rightly so called. First, because it does not happen through any lack of grace that many perish, but through lack of faith, since grace is ready for all, that is, for those who do not reject it, just as everything was ready for the wedding. Second, because all are called to it.

units.la: III. quia sic est omnibus destinata vt extra eam nemo redimatur nec redimi queat. Vbi iam destinationem istam aliter quàm prius intelligit: rectè tamè, quia licet multi non redimantur nec iustificentur, omnes tamen per Christum redimuntur & iustificantur, quia nemo nisi per ipsum. Ex quibus omnibus liquido patet, Musculum vt alios, refragari, nō autem patrocinari quicquam aduersario.
units.tr: Third, because it is so destined for all that no one is redeemed outside it, nor can be. Here he now understands that destination differently than before, yet rightly so, since although many are not redeemed nor justified, all are nevertheless redeemed and justified through Christ, because no one is except through him. From all of this it is clear that Musculus, like the others, argues against his opponent and in no way lends him support.

units.la: Aliquid coloris habet quod ex Hemmingio Syntagm. citat, Christum videli-cet non venisse pro quibusdam selectis
units.tr: There is some plausibility in what he cites from Hemmingius' Syntagma, namely that Christ did not come for certain select persons

units.la: R ij tan-
units.tr: R ij tan-

units.la: tantum de genere humano redimedis, sed vniuersalem esse illam gratiâ, quantum quidem ad voluntatem Dei paternam. Verum, licet Hemmingius ob intellectam aliter doctrinam praedestinationis, ita scripserit, magnopere tamen dissidet a figmento aduersariorum, quod omnes indubitanter, proprie & re ipsa, accepta peccatorum remissione, in finum gratiae recepti, iustificati & saluati sint per mortem Christi, credentes & increduli. Contra testatur Iemm. thes. 28. (quam Hub. cum 27. cit. iret callidè dissimulauit) quod ad euentum, m, gratiam redemtionis esse paucorum duntaxat, quia pauci credant & fructus poenitentiae proferant. Agnoscit enim & sub inde inculcat, quod licet Euangelium omnibus, cuiuscunque nationis & status, beneficia Christi offerat, sola tamen fide recipiantur, atque ita credentis omnium fit iustificatio & salus. Et clarè dicit, conditionem fidei requiri, vt applicetur beneficium, hoc est, remissio peccatorum: & conditionem perseuerantiae, vt retineat ir acceptum.
units.tr: only of the human race to be redeemed, but that this grace is universal, as far as God's fatherly will is concerned. But although Hemmingius wrote this because he understood the doctrine of predestination differently, he is in fact far from the fiction of the opponents, that all, believers and unbelievers alike, without doubt, truly and in fact, having received the forgiveness of sins, have been taken into the bosom of grace, justified and saved through the death of Christ. On the contrary, he bears witness (in thesis 28 of Hemmingius, which Huber cunningly concealed, though he cited thesis 27) that as to the outcome, the grace of redemption belongs only to a few, because few believe and bring forth the fruits of repentance. For he acknowledges, and repeatedly insists, that although the gospel offers the benefits of Christ to everyone of whatever nation and condition, they are received by faith alone, and so justification and salvation come to the one who believes. And he states plainly that the condition of faith is required so that the benefit, that is, the forgiveness of sins, may be applied, and the condition of perseverance so that it may be kept once received.

units.la: Pro quo isti dicunt, Omnes beneficium semel
units.tr: To this they reply: all received the benefit once; believers remain in what they have received, unbelievers lose it again.

units.la: De Euang. ... (marginal note) semel accepisse, credentes in accepto manere, non credentes id denuò amittere.
units.tr: On the Gospel ... (marginal note) that they received the benefit once: believers remain in what they have received, unbelievers lose it again.

units.la: Venio ad id quod ex Catechismo nostrarum Ecclesiarũ obiicitur, quæst. 37. Vbi verba Catechismi habent, Christum iram Dei aduersus peccata vniuersi generis humani, corpore & anima sustinuisse. Sed eadē est explicatio quæ priùs ad locum Athanasij, vbi similis erat locutio.
