Certè effectus mortis Christi nō in omnibus promiscuè extat, credentibus & nō credentib. sed vt ex verbo Dei Catechismus noster docet quæst.30. qui Iesu salvatore perfectũ side amplectuntur vera, ÿ dem ü omnia possident quæ ad salutem requiruntur.
units.tr: I come to what is objected from the Catechism of our Churches, question 37, where the words of the Catechism are: that Christ sustained in body and soul the wrath of God against the sins of the whole human race. But the explanation is the same as before, regarding the passage of Athanasius, where the expression was similar. Certainly the effect of Christ's death does not indiscriminately exist in all, believers and unbelievers alike; rather, as our Catechism teaches from the Word of God in question 30, those who embrace with perfect faith the true Jesus as Saviour, they alone possess all the things that are required for salvation.

units.la: Item, quæst.20. ad interrogatum, Num igitur omnibus hominibus qui in Adamo perierunt, per Christum salus redditur? plane respondetur, non omnibus, verum ÿs tantum, qui vera side ipsi inseruntur, eiusque beneficia amplectuntur. Hoc si potes concilia Hubere cum tua opinione plena erroris, omnes videlicet qui in Adamo perierant, per Christum in gratiam receptos, iustificatos, viuificatos saluti rerestitutos. Vide etiam in Catechismo quaest.53.55.60.66.&c. quibus omnibus in locis, non alia Christi & beneficiorum eius participatio quàm per veram fidem statuitur, exclusis infidelibus & hypocritis.
units.tr: Likewise, in question 20, to the question, "Is salvation therefore restored through Christ to all men who perished in Adam?", the answer is plainly given: not to all, but only to those who are truly engrafted into him by true faith and embrace his benefits. If you can, Huber, reconcile this with your opinion, which is full of error, namely that all who had perished in Adam have been received into grace through Christ, justified, made alive, and restored to salvation. See also in the Catechism, questions 53, 55, 60, 66, and so on; in all these places, no participation in Christ and his benefits is established except through true faith, with unbelievers and hypocrites excluded.

units.la: Sed de his satis. Eat nunc aduersarius, & veterum atque neotericorum testimoniis, quibus apertissimè refellitur, errorem suum venditet.
units.tr: But enough of these matters. Let the opponent now go and peddle his error with the testimonies of the ancients and of the moderns, by which it is most clearly refuted.

units.la: CAPVT XIII.
units.tr: Chapter 13.

units.la: Ad quartam criminationem.
units.tr: Against the fourth charge.

units.la: SEQVITVR quarta absurditas nobis obiecta: Homines adigi ad desperationem, nec hominum cuiquam de salute sua quicquam constare posse. Hanc calumniam vltro citroque versat. Summa huc redit, fiduciam & consolatione omnem salutis, secundum nostram sententiam niti meris particularibus, ex quibus nil sequatur, hoc modo:
units.tr: The fourth absurdity charged against us follows: that men are driven to despair, and that no one can be certain of his own salvation. Our opponent turns this calumny over and over. In short, he says that on our view all confidence and all comfort of salvation rests on mere particular propositions from which nothing follows, in this way:

units.la: Aliqui hominum in gratia sunt apud Deum & seruabuntur.
units.tr: Some men are in grace with God and will be saved.

units.la: Ego homo sum. Ergo sum in gratia apud Deum, & seruabor.
units.tr: I am a man. Therefore I am in grace with God and will be saved.

units.la: Quasi vero ita simus stolidi & inepti, vt nos atque alios non melius ex verbo Dei consolari didicerimus. Sua enim est, vti damnadorum, ita seruandorum in perpetuum, vniuersitas quaedam in scripturis: nec potest quisquam sanae mentis inficiari, alios aliiumtum, alios abiectum: alios seruatu alios perditum iri, die nouissima; illis aeternum gaudiis in regno patris, parato ipsis ante iacta mundi fundamenta; his contra sempiterna pacis termeta in igni inextinguibili, Diabolo & angelis eius parato.
units.tr: As if we were so foolish and dull that we had not learned to console ourselves and others better from the Word of God! For Scripture contains a general account of those who are to be damned and, likewise, of those who are to be saved forever. No sane person can deny that some are taken up and others cast off, some saved and others lost on the last day: the former to eternal joys in the Father's kingdom, prepared for them before the foundation of the world; the latter to everlasting torments of unquenchable fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.

units.la: Etsi autem Deus nouit ad vitam aeternam a se ordinatos aut non ordinatos, omniaque (vt verbis vtar Lutheri) in praedestinatione posita sunt, qui seruandi, qui damnandi sint: minime tamen sine verbo & speculatiue, vt ille loquitur, ad electionem nobis accedendum est, ne in desperatione aut contemptum ruamus: sed de electione iudicandum nobis est a posteriore, vt loquuntur, a fide nimirum, aliisque electionis effectibus.
units.tr: Although God knows which men he has or has not ordained to eternal life, and although (to use Luther's words) everything has been placed in predestination, namely who are to be saved and who damned, yet we must approach election for ourselves only through the Word, and not "speculatively," as he puts it, lest we fall into despair or contempt. Rather, we must judge concerning election from what comes after, as they say: namely from faith and the other effects of election.

units.la: Ergo sum in gratia apud Deum, & seruabor. ētibus, ad causam ipsam assurgendo. Hinc sunt promissiones illę dulcissimę, credentibus factæ, vniuersales prose- rēto, Venite ad me omnes qui laboratis, ego vos reficiam. Omnis qui credit in filium non peribit. Hæc est voluntas patris ut omnis qui credit in filium, habeat vitam æternam. Huic omnes Prophetæ testimonium perhibent, remissionem peccatorum accipere per nomen eius omnes qui credunt in eum. In hoc omnis qui credit iustificatur. Iustitia Dei per fidem Iesu Christi in omnes & super omnes credentes. Omnis qui credit in eum non confundetur. Nam idem Dominus omnium, dives in omnes qui invocant eum; quisquis enim invocabit nomen Domini seruabitur.
units.tr: Therefore I am in grace with God and will be saved, rising up to the cause itself. Hence come those most sweet promises made to believers in universal terms: Come to me, all you who labour, and I will refresh you. Everyone who believes in the Son will not perish. This is the will of the Father, that everyone who believes in the Son may have eternal life. To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name. In this everyone who believes is justified. The righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ is upon all and over all who believe. Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame. For the same Lord of all is rich toward all who call upon him; for whoever calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.

units.la: Et sæpe aliàs in hunc modum repetita est promissio salutis & vitæ æternæ, facta credentibus. Promissio enim requirit fidem, & credentium respectu vniuersalis est; vt rectè etiam explicat Ambrosius lib.1. de pœnit.cap.10. Qui fide habet, habet vitam æternam, non est exclusus a venia; omnis qui credit non peribit. Cum omnis dicitur, nullus excluditur, nullus excipitur. Omnis, inquit, hoc est, ex quocunque statu, statu, ex quocunque lapsu, si credat, perire non timeat.
units.tr: And the promise of salvation and eternal life made to believers has often been repeated in this way elsewhere. For a promise requires faith, and with respect to believers it is universal, as Ambrose also rightly explains: in the first book On Repentance, chapter 10: "He who has faith has eternal life; he is not excluded from pardon; everyone who believes will not perish. When it says 'everyone,' no one is excluded, no one is left out. 'Everyone,' it says, that is, from whatever condition, from whatever fall, if he believes, let him not fear to perish."

units.la: Ex hoc iam vniuersali fundamento argumentatio talis est, quia mundum, Diabolum, peccatum, mortem & infernum vincimus.
units.tr: From this universal foundation the argument runs as follows: because we conquer the world, the devil, sin, death and hell.

units.la: Quisquis in Christum crediderit, gratia ipsius saluabitur, & non pudesiet in aeternum.
units.tr: Whoever believes in Christ will be saved by his grace and will not be put to shame for ever.

units.la: Assumit homo fidelis, Credo Domine. Sequitur conclusio: Seruabor igitur gratia Dei, & non pudesiam in aeternum.
units.tr: The believing man assumes: "I believe, Lord." The conclusion follows: "Therefore I shall be saved by the grace of God, and shall not be put to shame for ever."

units.la: Maior syllogismi patet ex promissionibus ante allatis. Minoris probationem apud se ipsum habet qui credit. Sciens enim scit se credere, ita dictante proprio sensu, & attestante studio nouae obedientiae prompto & non simulato: unde fides tanquam arbor ex fructibus dignoscitur. Nam vt Ioh. ait 1. Epist. 2. per hoc scimus nos eum nosse, si mandata eius obseruamus. qui dicit noui eum, & mandata eius non seruat, mendax est, & veritas in ipso non est. Hinc Augustinus etiam scriptum reliquit, vnumquemque fidem suam certissime videre si eam habet: quod eius dictum vt rectum & pium Luthe-rus quoque probat,super Epist. ad Gal: 4. Imo Apostolus ipse hanc regulam prae-scribit 2.Cor.vlt. Vosmetipsos probate an sitis in fide, vosmetipsos tentate. Quo satis declarat, eos qui vera fide Christo insiti sunt, id exploratum posse habere apud seipsos.
units.tr: The major premise is clear from the promises cited above. The believer has within himself the proof of the minor premise. For one who believes knows that he believes, since his own feeling tells him so and the eager and unfeigned zeal for new obedience bears witness to it; thus faith is recognised by its fruits, as a tree is known by its fruit. For John says in his first Epistle, chapter 2: "By this we know that we know him, if we keep his commandments. He who says, 'I know him,' and does not keep his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him." Hence Augustine also left it written that everyone sees his own faith most certainly if he has it; and Luther too approves this saying of his as right and pious, on the Epistle to the Galatians, chapter 4. Indeed the Apostle himself prescribes this rule, 2 Corinthians, last chapter: "Examine yourselves whether you are in the faith; test yourselves." By this he sufficiently declares that those who are grafted into Christ by true faith can have this tested and certain for themselves.

units.la: Quod si vero Satanas, vt mendax & homicida est ab initio, aufert tibi negare quod credas, tu ne cede ipsi, quisquis es, o homo, qui fidei indicia apud temetipsum perseentiscis, sed contra audentior ito, diciteque ei: Vade post me Satana, non enim sapis ea quae sunt Dei: Nam ego cui crediderim, mihique persuasum est, eum posse depositum meum seruare in diem illum. Fidelis est qui me vocauit, is etiam efficiet.
units.tr: But if Satan, who is a liar and a murderer from the beginning, takes away your ability to deny that you believe, do not yield to him, whoever you are, O man, who perceive the marks of faith in yourself. Rather, be bolder against him and say to him: "Get behind me, Satan; for you do not savour the things that are of God." For I know whom I have believed, and I am persuaded that he is able to keep my deposit until that day. He who called me is faithful, and he will also do it.

units.la: Nec est quod turberis consternatoque animo sis, ob fidei imperfectionem & contrarios motus, timorem, dubitationes, tristitiam, & multiplices tentationes, quibuscum assidue nobis luctta est, quantisper corpus hoc mortis circumferimus. Etenim nouimus eum qui dixit, Ecce seruus meus quem elegi, dilectus meus,
units.tr: Nor should you be troubled or dismayed on account of the imperfection of your faith and the contrary movements, fear, doubts, sadness and manifold temptations, with which we struggle constantly for as long as we bear this body of death. For we know him who said: "Behold my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved,

units.la: Matth. 16. 2.Tim. 1. 1.Thes. 5.
units.tr: Matth. 16. 2 Tim. 1. 1 Thess. 5.

units.la: Isai. 42. meus, arundinem quassatam non confringet, & linum fumigans non exstinguet, vsque dum proferat iudicium ad victoriam. Quoties erga discipulos suos aliosq; magna fidei infirmitate laborantes, illustribus documentis testatum Dominus fecit in Euangelio, quàm non abiiciat sed summa cum benignitate & lenitate sumat foveatque infirmos in fide, atque indies confirmatiores reddat? Fides igitur tametsi languida, dummodo vera & sincera sit, effectu suo non frustrabitur. Tantum qui sentit se dubitare, exerceat fidem, & luctetur contra dubitationem, dicat cum patre pueri spiritum habentis mutum, Credo Domine, succurre incredulitati meæ, Et oret cum Apostolis, Adauge nobis fidem Domine. Hoccine est ad desperationem homines adigere? Hoccine ex puris particularibus argumentari? Et quæ quæsto alia consolatio afferri potest, qua quis de salute sua reddatur certior, quod nempe iustus sit coram Deo & hæres vitæ æternæ? Certè si aliud consolationis fundamentum non habemus, quàm quod saluandi & damnandi, electi atq; reprobi omnes æque per Christum redemti sint, præceps ruina est in desperationem. quippe vecors atque stolidus sit necesse est, qui sic concludat:
units.tr: Isai. 42. my beloved, he will not break a bruised reed, nor quench smoking flax, until he brings forth judgment to victory." How often has the Lord, in the Gospel, shown by illustrious examples toward his disciples and others who labour under great weakness of faith, that he does not cast them off, but receives and cherishes the weak in faith with the greatest kindness and gentleness, and makes them stronger day by day? Therefore faith, though feeble, provided it is true and sincere, will not fail in its effect. Let only the one who feels that he doubts exercise his faith and struggle against doubt, saying with the father of the boy who had the dumb spirit: "I believe, Lord; help my unbelief," and let him pray with the Apostles: "Lord, increase our faith." Is this driving men to despair? Is this arguing from mere particular propositions? And what other comfort, I ask, can be offered by which a man may be made more certain of his salvation, namely that he is righteous before God and an heir of eternal life? Certainly, if we have no other foundation of comfort than that those who are saved and those who are damned, the elect and the reprobate, were all alike redeemed by Christ, then headlong ruin into despair follows. Indeed, anyone who concludes thus must be foolish and dull:

units.la: Qui seruantur & damnantur, omnes ex æquo per Christum redemti sunt:
units.tr: Those who are saved and those who are damned were all alike redeemed by Christ;

units.la: Ergo futurum est vt ego non peream, sed habeam vitam æternam.
units.tr: Therefore it will come about that I shall not perish, but have eternal life.

units.la: Apparet igitur illam quam tantopere aduersarius prædicat vniuersalitatem redemptorum, nullo hominum excepto, haud esse propriam consolationis Christianæ balin: verùm ad fide veniendum est, quæ seruandos & damnandos discernit. Christi siquidem merítum fide accipimus, nobisque applicamus: & propterea qui credit in filium habet vitam æternam: qui verò non credit filio, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eum. Atque huc tandem velit nolit deuoluitur aduersarius, quo de certitudine salutis certi aliquid assignare possit. Nos, inquit thes. 534. certam, indubitatam & constantem sciscimus esse salutem, eamq; ad illos pertinere dicimus, qui fide in Christo manent, & in fide permansuros dicimus, qui verbum vniuersalis gratiæ super omnes, sibi excuti non sinent. Dicimus idem & nos: & amplius dicimus; in verbo & fiducia gratiæ perseveraturos: qui vera & viua fide Christo semel insiti sunt: ipso pro illis orante & donante,ne deficiat fides eorum. Nam remoto hoc fundamento de perseuerantia verè credentium, quæ cuiquam gratiæ Dei in futurum, ac proinde salutis suæ certitudo constare poterit? Quid, quod vniuersalitas promissionis, quam tantopere vrgent, tum concidat necesse est. Manifeste enim pugnat, omnes credentes seruari, & aliquos credentium excidere & perire. Ceterum, si ad eos demum salus pertinet, vti pertinet, qui fide in Christo manent, quid dicemus de incredulis? Exclusi sunt. Idcirco videtur, qui contendit eos æque perChristum fuisse salvatos ac quoslibet alios, & promissiones gratiæ & vitæ ad ipsos quoque pertinere.
units.tr: It is plain, then, that that universality of the redeemed, with no one excepted, which our opponent proclaims so earnestly, is not the proper ground of Christian comfort. Rather, we must come to faith, which distinguishes those who are to be saved from those who are to be damned. For we receive the merit of Christ by faith and apply it to ourselves; and therefore whoever believes in the Son has eternal life, but whoever does not believe the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him. And here at last our opponent is carried, whether he likes it or not, to the point where he might assign something certain about the certainty of salvation. "We," he says, thesis 534, "hold that salvation is certain, indubitable and constant, and we say that it belongs to those who remain in Christ by faith, and we say that those will remain in faith who do not allow the word of universal grace, which is over all, to be shaken from them." We too say the same, and we say more: that those who have been grafted into Christ by true and living faith will persevere in the word and in trust in grace, Christ himself praying and granting for them that their faith may not fail. For if this foundation of the perseverance of those who truly believe is removed, what certainty of God's grace in the future, and therefore of one's own salvation, can stand? Moreover, the universality of the promise, which they press so hard, must then necessarily collapse. For it is plainly contradictory that all believers are saved and that some of the believers fall away and perish. But if salvation belongs, as it does, only to those who remain in Christ by faith, what shall we say of unbelievers? They are excluded. Hence it seems that the one who contends that they were saved by Christ in the same way as any others, and that the promises of grace and life pertain to them as well, is mistaken.

units.la: Ac
units.tr: And

units.la: Hub. the 266. & seq. At gratia vniuersalis est. Respondeo omni creaturæ gratia annunciari debet: sed fruitio ipsa residet penes vniuersitatem credentium, in qua non est distinctio Iudæi aut Græci, domini aut serui, maris aut fœminæ; sed iustitia Dei in omnes & super omnes qui credunt.Qui vero non credunt, vitam non videbunt, sed ira Dei manet super eos. Atque hoc satis est, vt tutò possis & debeas credere, Christum mortuum propter te & salutem tuam: quoniam omnes iubemur resipiscere & credere Euangelio, addita promissione, quod qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, seruabitur: qui non crediderit, condemnabitur.
units.tr: Hub. the 266. & seq. But grace is universal. I answer that the gospel of grace must be announced to every creature, but the enjoyment of it rests with the whole body of believers, among whom there is no distinction of Jew or Greek, master or slave, male or female, but "the righteousness of God is upon all and over all who believe." Those who do not believe will not see life, but "the wrath of God remains upon them." And this is enough for you to believe safely and rightly that Christ died for you and for your salvation, since we are all commanded to repent and believe the gospel, with the promise added that whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, and whoever does not believe will be condemned.

units.la: Cauillatur aduersarius, non sufficere quod dicamus credendum esse, Christum omnibus prodesse, qui in illum credunt; statim enim quæri, quid credam? quid mihi promittitur priusquam credam?
units.tr: The adversary carps that it is not enough for us to say that one must believe that Christ benefits all who believe in him, for at once the question arises: what am I to believe? What is promised to me before I believe?

units.la: Quid? regulam habes fidei, symbolum Apostolorum, & nescis quid credere debeas? Quod autem ad promissionem, verum est nisi promissio praecesserit, fidem subsequi non posse, cum fides sit ex auditu promissionis. Dico igitur homini necdum credenti promitti gratiam Dei, salutem & vitam aeternam in Christo, sed conditionaliter, si credide-rit. Audi Lutherum in Gen. 48. Si credis, habes: si non vis credere, nihil habebis. Tantum enim habes quantum credis. Si credis, iam omnia potes & possides: Quod si non credis, nihil habes.
units.tr: What? You have the rule of faith, the Apostles' Creed, and you do not know what you ought to believe? As for the promise, it is true that faith cannot follow unless the promise has gone before, since faith comes from hearing the promise. I say, therefore, that to a man not yet believing, the grace of God, salvation and eternal life in Christ are promised, but conditionally, if he believes. Hear Luther on Genesis 48: "If you believe, you have; if you do not want to believe, you will have nothing. For you have as much as you believe. If you believe, you already can and possess all things; but if you do not believe, you have nothing."

units.la: Caput XIV.
units.tr: Chapter 14.

units.la: Quinti absurdi discussio.
units.tr: Discussion of the fifth absurdity.

units.la: QVINTA deinceps absurditas à rixatore excitata, ea est, quod ex negatione universalis redemptionis, prout ipse eam intelligit, id est non concessa universali gratia & salutis per Christum in omnes & super omnes, absque ullo discrimine fidei vel incredulitatis, electorum vel reproborum, sequitur abrogatio totius ministerii Evangelici; eo quod nemo, si ipsi creditur, scire possit quid cui praedicandum sit.
units.tr: The fifth absurdity that the wrangler next raises is this: from the denial of universal redemption, as he understands it, that is, without granting a universal grace and salvation through Christ for all and over all, with no distinction between faith and unbelief or between the elect and the reprobate, there follows the abrogation of the whole Evangelical ministry, since no one, if he is believed, could know what should be preached to whom.

units.la: Itane
units.tr: Is that so?

units.la: Itáne vero? At Christum eiusq; Apostolos, à quibus forma lanorum sermonũ petenda nobis est, videmus eam sequutos docendi rationem, vt omnes de peccato arguerét, omnibus ad conuersionem & fidem hortatores existerent, conscientias afflictas seníu peccati ac metu iudicii territas erigerent promissionibus Euangelij, securos contrà lege terrerent, & in summa, credentibus aperirent, incredulis clauderent regnum Dei. Hos si imitari velimus autores, velle autè debemus, sciemus, quid, cui, & quomodo praedicare oporteat, atque delectu habito inter securos & compunctos corde, gratiam quidem & remissionem peccatorum praedicabimus apud eos, qui agnoscunt se habere peccata, ijsque liberari cupiunt, qui autem in peccatis secure pergunt, ijs legem proponemus, vt maledictione terreantur, & traducantur hoc modo ad timorem Dei.
units.tr: Is that really so? Yet we see that Christ and his Apostles, from whom we must take the pattern of sound preaching, followed a method of teaching whereby they convicted everyone of sin and urged everyone to conversion and faith. They raised up consciences afflicted by the burden of sin and terrified by the fear of judgment with the promises of the Gospel, while they terrified the secure with the Law. In sum, they opened the kingdom of God to believers and shut it against unbelievers. If we wish to imitate these authors, and we ought to wish it, we shall know what to preach, to whom, and how. Having made a distinction between the secure and those pricked in heart, we will preach grace and the remission of sins to those who acknowledge that they have sins and desire to be freed from them. But to those who continue securely in their sins we will set forth the Law, so that they may be terrified by its curse and so led in this way to the fear of God.

units.la: Hoc est verbum Dei recte secare, vt Deus agnoscatur & misericors peccata sua agnoscentibus, & in filium credentibus tibus
units.tr: This is to cut the word of God rightly, so that God is recognised as merciful to those who acknowledge their sins, and believers in the Son, and angry with the secure.

units.la: Ioh.9.41. Luc.14.47 Act.2.38. & ca.10.43 Rom.1.2.3 tibus, & iratus securis, atque ita singuli discamus timere Deum,& niti eius mi-sericordia,quam in missione filii declarauit. Hoc discrimine non obseruato, fit, vt qui Euangelio consolandi erant, lege crucifigantur,& qui lege terrendi, Euangelio indurentur: vt recte haec omnia monet Lutherus in Gen.18.& in illud Matth. cap.9. Confide fili, remittuntur tibi peccata. Vbi quoque inter alia notat Christum afflicto paralytico Euangelium obtulisse,Pharisaeos autem arguisse blasphemos & malos.Quid, ait, mala cogitatis?non dicit paralytico, cur mala cogitas tu? Nec Pharisaeis, confidite &c. optime secans verbum Dei.
units.tr: John 9.41. Luke 14.47. Acts 2.38 and 10.43. Romans 1.2.3. Believers, and angry with the secure; and thus let each of us learn to fear God and rest upon his mercy, which he declared in the sending of his Son. When this distinction is not observed, it happens that those who ought to be comforted by the Gospel are crucified by the Law, and those who ought to be terrified by the Law are hardened by the Gospel. Luther rightly notes all this on Genesis 18, and on that passage of Matthew 9, "Take heart, son, your sins are forgiven." There he also observes, among other things, that Christ offered the Gospel to the afflicted paralytic, but charged the Pharisees with blasphemy and evil. "Why," he says, "do you think evil things?" He does not say to the paralytic, "Why do you think evil things?" nor to the Pharisees, "Take heart," and so on. He cuts the word of God most excellently.

units.la: Hic iam consideretur,vtra doctrina ordinem istum perturbet: Nostrane, qua ex mandato Dei omnes iubentur resipiscere & credere, & credentibus vniuersis & singulis annunciatur, omnia peccata ipsis diuinitus propter meritum Christi condonari, quoties vera fide promissionem Euangelij amplectutur: contra vero omnibus infidelibus & hypocritis denunciatur,tantisper ipsis ira Dei
units.tr: Let us now consider which doctrine disturbs this order: ours, by which all are commanded by God to repent and believe, and it is announced to believers, both universally and individually, that all their sins are divinely forgiven for the merit of Christ, whenever they embrace the promise of the gospel with true faith; but on the contrary it is declared to all unbelievers and hypocrites that the wrath of God and eternal condemnation hang over them for as long as they persist in such a state? Or rather that of Huber, who, carried away in the chariot of contention through the empty fancies of paradoxes, preaches that for all men, secure and afflicted alike, unbelieving and believing alike, all judgment and divine wrath have in fact been truly and properly lifted and blotted out?

units.la: S Dei & æternam condemnationem incumbere, dum tales perseuerant? An Huberi potius qui contentionis curru raptus per inania paradoxorum, vni- uersis hominibus, tam securis quàm afflictis, tam incredulis quàm credentibus, omne iudicium iramque diuinam re ipsa, verè & proprie sublata & deleta prædicat? qui indubitater omnes simul ab omni peccato liberatos, & re ipsa totum genus humanũ, sine cuiusquam exceptione, in gratiam & sinum patris per mortem filij receptum asseuerat? qui item ad omnes in Adamo perditos, iustitiam & operationem salutis per Christum pertinere asserit, reprobosque omnes æquè ac quoslibet alios per ipsum saluatos, quanta potest ingenij contentione & styli petulantia, defendit? Quapropter culpa potius agnoscat suã, quàm alios tã audacter criminetur.
units.tr: Who affirms that all men at once are freed from every sin, and that the whole human race, without exception of anyone, has in fact been received into grace and into the bosom of the Father through the death of the Son? Who likewise asserts that righteousness and the working of salvation through Christ pertain to all who perished in Adam, and who defends, with all the vehemence of his wit and the wantonness of his style, that all the reprobate are saved through him just as much as any others? Let him therefore acknowledge his own fault rather than so boldly accuse others.

units.la: Obiicit ipse, Si gratia Dei ad omnes non pertinet, quo ore qua fronte minister & præco reconciliationis, in promulgando Euangelio audebit omnes & singulos ad gratiã Dei vocare? Si omnes nes inuitet,omnibus promittat,omnes ad pœnitentiam hortetur, mentietur: quoniam gratia nō est omnium ex hypothesi; & ad quos promissio & gratia non pertinet, illi quoque credere non debent,nec credere possunt.
units.tr: He himself objects: "If the grace of God does not pertain to all, with what mouth and what face will a minister and herald of reconciliation dare, in proclaiming the gospel, to call all and each to the grace of God? If he invites all, promises to all, and exhorts all to repentance, he will be lying, since by hypothesis grace is not for all; and those to whom the promise and grace do not pertain ought not to believe, nor can they believe."

units.la: Respondeo misceri in argumento res diuersas: præceptum pœnitentiæ, id est, inuitationem ad conuersionem & fidem; atque promissionem gratiæ. Distinctione igitur opus est. Quod ad præceptum conuersionis & fidei, id omnes obligat simpliciter, iuxta illud, Resipiscite & credite. Quare nullum hic committetur mendacium, si verbi minister ad fidem omnes inuitet, omnes ad pœnitentiam hortetur atque instiget. At promissiones gratiæ, quibus offertur misericordia, pax, salus, honor, gloria, vita, immortalitas; eæ (loquedo de adultis) non aliter quam fide percipiuntur, fides autem nō est omnium, sed quos Deus ex singulari misericordia diuino isto munere dignatur. Addequod aduersatio ipsimet, velit nolit, fatendum est, vt supra quoque meminimus, nimus,salutem ad eos pertinere, qui fi-de in Christo manent. Non igitur ad incredulos, ac proin ad omnes, perti-net: non vtique, nisi fabulam Origenis reuocare quis velit, vt omnes homines tandem seruentur. Proinde hic negatur antecedens, quòd Euangelij minister omnibus promittat, & fœdus reconciliationis omnibus annuntiet, quasi omnes ex æquo fœdere isto comprehensi sint. Simpliciter enim loquendo credentibus duntaxat & agentibus pœnitentiam promittit. Infidelibus autem & hypocritis iram denunciat, quia impio non est pax, dicit Dominus: nec promittitur iis quicquam nisi condi-tionaliter, si videlicet conuertantur, & credant toto corde. Hanc verò conditionem solus Deus præstat in quibus vult, cum vtrumque merum ipsius donum sit, fides & pœnitentia.
units.tr: I answer that different things are mixed together in the argument: the precept of repentance, that is, the invitation to conversion and faith, and the promise of grace. A distinction is therefore needed. As for the precept of conversion and faith, it binds all without qualification, according to the words, "Repent and believe." Hence no lie will be told if the minister of the Word invites all to faith and urges and stirs up all to repentance. But the promises of grace, by which mercy, peace, salvation, honour, glory, life and immortality are offered, are (speaking of adults) received only by faith, and faith is not for all, but for those whom God, by his singular mercy, deigns to grant this divine gift. Moreover, the opponent himself, whether he likes it or not, must admit, as we also recalled above, that salvation pertains to those who remain in faith in Christ. Therefore it does not pertain to unbelievers, and so not to all, certainly not, unless someone wishes to revive the fable of Origen that all men will at last be saved. Hence the antecedent is denied here, namely that the minister of the gospel promises to all and announces the covenant of reconciliation to all, as if all were comprehended equally in this covenant. For speaking simply, he promises only to believers and to those who practise repentance. But to unbelievers and hypocrites he announces wrath, because "there is no peace for the wicked, says the Lord," and nothing is promised to them except conditionally, namely if they should turn and believe with their whole heart. This condition, however, God alone grants to whomever he wills, since both faith and repentance are his pure gift.

units.la: Atque hoc sensu recte sane dicitur, promissiones prædicari & proponi debere omnibus, credituris & non credituris: quatenus officium ministrorum est, vt indiscriminatim ac publice in au-
units.tr: And in this sense it is rightly said that promises ought to be preached and set forth to all, to those who will believe and those who will not, insofar as it is the office of ministers to pour out, indiscriminately and publicly, into the

units.la: Fabula Origenis.
units.tr: Origen's fable.

units.la: Zach. 1. 3. Ezech. 18. ver. 21. Ief. 1. v. 17. Act. 2. 38. & ca. 8. 22. aures omnium verbum fidei & salutis spargant, ac proposita Dei clementia in Christo, victima pro peccatis mundi,quoscunque vocent ad donum gratiæ amplectendum, & quasi ad nuptias regias inuitent quoscunque inuenerint.
units.tr: Zech. 1:3; Ezek. 18:21; Jer. 1:17; Acts 2:38 and 8:22. ears of all the word of faith and salvation, and, with God's clemency in Christ set forth as the victim for the sins of the world, to call whomever they summon to embrace the gift of grace, and to invite as to a royal wedding whomever they find.

units.la: Impia vero vox est, non omnes debere credere, quod promissio & salus ad omnes non pertineat. Imo quia salus fidelium tantummodo est, infidelium autem mors & condemnatio, ideo omnes debent poenitentiam agere & credere Euangelio, ne cum mundo pereant, sed habeant vitam æternam.
units.tr: It is an impious utterance to say that not all ought to believe because the promise and salvation do not pertain to all. Rather, since salvation belongs only to the faithful, while death and condemnation are the lot of unbelievers, therefore all ought to repent and believe the gospel, lest they perish with the world, but have eternal life.

units.la: Nec quicquam obstat generali isti inuitationi, quod certu est multos sem per fuisse & fore contemtores oblatæ gratiæ: siquidem, dicente Apostolo, fides non est omnium: & vt Christus testatur, multi vocati, pauci electi. Etenim sufficit seruis inuitatoribus, & abunde sufficit mandatum regis: ite, dicite vocatis, venite quia parata sunt omnia. Vocate ad nuptias quoscunque inueneritis. Item, prædicate omni creaturæ. Huic imperio est quod obtemperet fidelis iustitiæ prædicator, dicator, siue suscipiatur, siue sperna-tur, siue etiā propterea quaelibet tem-poraliter aduersa patiatur. Quemad-modum etiam qui vocantur sine cun-ctatione parere debent vocationi suae, vtut multi non pareant, quia manda-tum & illi habent omni tergiuersatio-ne maius, venite, credite, respicite: Hodie si vocem eius audicritis, ne obdurate corda ve-stra, sicut patres vestri in deserto.
units.tr: Nor does anything stand in the way of this general invitation, that it is certain many have always been, and always will be, despisers of the grace offered. For, as the Apostle says, faith is not for all, and as Christ testifies, many are called but few chosen. For it is enough for the servants who invite, and the king's command is more than sufficient: "Go, tell those who are invited, Come, for everything is ready. Invite to the wedding whomever you find." Likewise: "Preach to every creature." To this command the faithful preacher of righteousness must obey: he preaches and speaks, whether he is received or rejected, and even if for that reason he suffers any temporal adversity. Just as those who are called ought to answer their calling without delay, although many do not answer, because they have a command greater than any evasion: "Come, believe, return. Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts, as your fathers did in the wilderness."

units.la: Legatur Augustinus hac de re contra Crescomium Grammaticum lib.1.cap.5. & 6. Vbi diuersis scripturae testimoniis no-minatim demonstrat, etiam non audi-turis praedicadam veritatem. Dominus dicit in Euangelio, cum ingressi fueritis, dicite, pax domui huic: si digni fuerint, qui ibi sunt, requiescet super eos pax vestra: sin mi-nus, ad vos revertetur. An eos certos fecit quod esSent eorum pacem suscepturi quibus eam praedicaret? Certos tamen fecit sine cunctatione praedicandam pacem, etiam no admissuris eam. Apo-stolus etiam Timotheum suum astrin-xit, ne propter homines quibus insua-uis est praedicatio veritatis, aliqua ipsi segnisegnitia prædicâdi obreperet, Obtestor, inquit, coram Deo & Christo Iesu: prædica verbum, iusta opportune, importune: argue, hortare, increpa. Operarius igitur nô dolosus prædicabit volétibus opportunè: renitétibus importunè. Christus quoq; quâ multa loquutus est in os Iudæorû, Pharisæorum, Sadducæorum, non solum minimè crediturorum, verum etiam maximè contradicturorum, & persecuturorum ? Et nouerat vtique, inquit Augustus. quia omnium præscius erat, nihil hæc profutura ad eorum salutem; sed nos fortasse suo firmauit exemplo, qui futuram fidem perfidiamve hominum prænoscere non valemus. Sed & Prophetas missos legimus ad homines tam inobedientes, vt Deus ipse Prophetis quos mittebat, prædiceret, eos ad quos mittebat, verbis corû ob-temperaturos non esse. Sic Ezechiel cûm verbo Dei mittebatur, inferre cer tamen Iudæis non obediturus, contra-sensuris, contradicturis. Similiter Ieremias, cui dicebatur: Loqueris ad eos omnia verba hæc, nec audient te; & vocabis eos, nec respondebunt tibi.
units.tr: Let Augustine be read on this matter, against Crescentius the Grammarian, book 1, chapters 5 and 6. There, by various testimonies of Scripture, he expressly shows that the truth is to be preached even to those who will not hear it. The Lord says in the Gospel: "When you enter, say, Peace to this house; if those who are there are worthy, your peace will rest upon them, but if not, it will return to you." Did he make certain that those to whom he preached would receive his peace? Yet he made it certain that peace is to be preached without hesitation, even to those who will not admit it. The Apostle also bound his Timothy, lest, on account of men to whom the preaching of truth is unwelcome, any sluggishness in preaching should creep upon him: "I charge you before God and Christ Jesus: preach the word, be urgent in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort." The faithful workman therefore preaches to the willing in season and to the resisting out of season. Did Christ not also speak much into the mouths of the Jews, the Pharisees and the Sadducees, who were not only least likely to believe but most likely to contradict and persecute him? And he surely knew, as Augustine says, since he foreknew all things, that these words would profit nothing for their salvation; but perhaps he strengthened us by his example, since we cannot foreknow the future faith or faithlessness of men. But we also read that prophets were sent to men so disobedient that God himself told the prophets he sent that those to whom they were sent would not obey their words. Thus Ezekiel, when he was sent with the word of God, was to deliver it while being told beforehand that the Jews would not obey, would contradict and would resist. Similarly Jeremiah, to whom it was said: "You will speak to them all these words, but they will not hear you; and you will call them, but they will not answer you."

units.la: Ezech. 1. & 3.
units.tr: Ezech. 1. & 3.

units.la: Si quis quærat, qua causa, cui bono, quo fructu, quóue effectu surdis cana-tur fabula, quod aiunt; tametsi mandatum Dei sufficit contra quod disputare nefas est, responderi tamen & alia possunt.
units.tr: If anyone asks for what reason, to what good, to what profit or effect this fable is sung to the deaf, as they say, then, although God's command is enough, and it is wrong to dispute against it, other answers can still be given.

units.la: I. Quantisper in hoc seculo viui-tur, reprobi electis adiuncti sunt, nec hominis iudicio discerni possunt : ac propterea par est, vt veritas omnibus promiscuè prædicetur, ne ob reprobos electi fraudentur, qui prædicatione verbi sunt professuri. Hinc & Augustinus de Corr. & grat. 15. & 16. Nescietes quis pertineat ad prædestinatorum numerum, quis non pertineat, sic affici debemus caritatis affectu, vt omnes velimus saluos fieri.
units.tr: I. As long as people live in this world, the reprobate are mixed with the elect, and they cannot be told apart by human judgement. For this reason the truth must be preached to all alike, so that the elect are not cheated of it because of the reprobate, who are to profess the faith through the preaching of the Word. Hence also Augustine, On Correction and Grace, chapters 15 and 16: "Since we do not know who belongs to the number of the predestined and who does not, we ought to be moved by such love that we wish all to be saved."

units.la: II. Demonstratur ea ratione miserabilis cæcitas & corruptio summa hominis perditi, & opere ipso patescit quod Paulus ait, animalem hominem non percipere ea quæ spiritus Dei sunt, stultitiam ei esse, ac ne posse quidem cognoscere.
units.tr: II. In this way the wretched blindness and the utter corruption of lost man are shown, and the fact itself makes plain what Paul says: the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God; they are foolishness to him, and he cannot even know them.

units.la: III. Pij dum cernunt alios relinqui in infidelitate, quibus tamen commumunis est doctrina, agnoscunt eo magis misericordiam Dei erga se, quâ coeruntur & salui fiunt. Hinc Dominus dicebat: Nemo venit ad me nisi pater traxerit eum, vt scriptum est in Prophetis: Erunt omnes docti à Deo. Quisquis ergo audiuit à patre & didicit, venit ad me. Item, vobis datum est nosse mysteria regni cælorum, illis non, sed impletur in ipsis Prophetia, vt audientes non audiant: audientes videlicet corporis sensu, nô audiant cordis assensu, vt exponit Augustinus. Cur autem illi habeant aures audiendi, illi nô habeant, hoc est, cur illis datum sit à patre vt veniant ad filium, illis non sit datum, quis cognouit sensum Domini? aut quis eius consiliarius fuit? aut tu quis es homo, qui respondeas Deo? inquit ibidem Augustinus. de bono perseuerantia lib. 2. cap. 14.
units.tr: III. When the godly see others left in unbelief, although the same doctrine is common to them, they recognise all the more the mercy of God towards themselves, by which they are drawn and saved. Hence the Lord said: No one comes to me unless the Father draws him, as it is written in the Prophets: they shall all be taught by God. Everyone therefore who has heard from the Father and learned comes to me. Likewise: To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but not to them; and the prophecy is fulfilled in them: hearing, they shall not hear; that is, they hear with the bodily sense but do not hear with assent of the heart, as Augustine explains. Why some have ears to hear and others do not, that is, why it has been given by the Father to some to come to the Son and not to others: who has known the mind of the Lord? or who has been his counsellor? or who are you, man, that you answer God? says Augustine in the same place, On the Gift of Perseverance, book 2, chapter 14.

units.la: IV. Impij redduntur inexcusabiles audiendo verbum Dei, ne ignorantiam excusare possint, quando ne externa quidem præstant quæ præstare porerat, quemadmodum apud Ezech. dicitur:
units.tr: IV. The wicked are made inexcusable by hearing the Word of God, so that they cannot plead ignorance, since they do not even perform the outward things they were able to perform, as is said in Ezekiel:

units.la: siue audierint siue desiterint, tu loqueris ad eos, & cognoscent quod fuerit Propheta inter ipsos. Et Christus inquit, Si non venissem & loquutus essem, peccatum non haberent, nunc autem excusationem non habent. Et alibi dicit praedicandum Euangelium regni, in universa terra, in testimonium omnibus gentibus. Quomodo etiam Apostolis praedicebat, ad praesides & reges ductum iri, eis & gentibus in testimonium: hoc est, in reprehensionem & condemnationem eorum, qui non credunt: uti utrumque locum interpretatur Theophylactus.
units.tr: Whether they hear or whether they cease, you shall speak to them, and they shall know that there has been a prophet among them. And Christ says: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse. And elsewhere he says that the gospel of the kingdom is to be preached in the whole earth for a testimony to all nations. Likewise he foretold to the apostles that they would be brought before governors and kings, for a testimony to them and to the Gentiles; that is, for the reproof and condemnation of those who do not believe. Theophylact explains both passages in this way.

units.la: Adijciam, propter antagonistam, qui vsum istum exagitat, & Augustini ac Lutheri testimonia. August. tract. 81. in Iohan. ait, Qui mandata contemnunt, vel etiam derident, & oppugnant ea, his verba Christi non erunt in beneficium, sed in testimonium. Et de praedest. sanct. ca. 9. scribit salutem religionis ab exordio propagationis humanae vsque in finem, quibusdam ad praemium, quibusdam ad iudicium praedicari. Item de corrept. & grat. cap. 13. Correptio medicinaliter omnibus adhibenda est, etiamsi salus aegrotantis incerta: ut si is qui corripitur ad numenumerum prædestinatorum pertinet, sit ei cor reptio salubre medicamentum, si autem non pertinet, sit pœnale tormentum.
units.tr: I shall add, on account of the opponent who attacks this usage, the testimonies of Augustine and Luther. Augustine, Tractate 81 on John, says: "Those who despise the commandments, or even mock them and oppose them, for them the words of Christ will not be for benefit but for testimony." And in On the Predestination of the Saints, chapter 9, he writes that the salvation of religion is preached from the beginning of human propagation to the end, to some for reward, to others for judgement. Likewise in On Correction and Grace, chapter 13: "Correction is to be applied to all in a medicinal way, even though the salvation of the one who is sick is uncertain. If the one who is corrected belongs to the number of the predestined, correction is a healthful medicine for him; if he does not belong, it is a penal torment."

units.la: Lutherus, Tom.3. in 3.cap. Ioëlis, Omnibus, inquit, hominibus annuntiatur Evangelium, & ut maximè non omnes verbo credant, tamen tam impijs quàm pijs annunciatur: his virtus Dei est ad salutem, illis iudicium. Vide etiam lib. 1. sentent. dist. 47. sub finem distinctionis.
units.tr: Luther, Vol. 3, on the third chapter of Joel: "The gospel is proclaimed to all men," he says, "and although most do not believe the word, it is nevertheless proclaimed to the wicked as much as to the godly: the power of God is to salvation for the one, and judgement for the other." See also Book 1 of the Sentences, distinction 47, near the end of the distinction.

units.la: Sed Huberum audiamus. Principiò non caret mendacio, quod nostris affingit, in nullum alium finem reprobos vocari, nisi ut indurentur & fiant ἀναπολόγητοι, inexcusabiles: plures enim fines iam redditi sunt. Citat Bezam altera responsione ad colloq. Momp. sol. 149. & 95. Item 96. sed exclusiua perperam nostris affiøta & sæpius inculcata ab Huberò, apud Bezam non reperitur.
units.tr: But let us hear Huber. First, he is not free from falsehood when he charges our side with holding that the reprobate are called for no other end than that they may be hardened and become inexcusable [ἀναπολόγητοι]; for more ends have already been given. He cites Beza, in his second reply to the Colloquy of Mömpelgard, pages 149 and 95. Likewise page 96: but the exclusive sense, wrongly attributed to our side and often pressed by Huber, is not found in Beza.

units.la: Deinde, ut cauillando exercitatus est, excipit non credituris, vt pote iusto Dei iudicio ad fidem non prædestinatis, fidem & pœnitentiam nihilominus annunciare, perinde absurdum esse, ac si quis Diabolis ipsis pœnitentiam prædicaret. At enim maxima dissimilitudo est inter homines reprobos, & spiritus illos reprobos, licet in hoc conueniant, quod vtrosq; manet ignis æternus. Etenim hominum electi atque reprobi, in hac vita permixti sunt, nec scire possumus qui credituri sint, qui non: & accedunt alia quæ diximus, præsertim mandatum Dei, quo Euangelium institutum est vniuersæ creaturæ humanæ.
units.tr: Next, as one practised in quibbling, he objects that to announce faith and repentance to those who will not believe, who are not predestined to faith by God's just judgement, is just as absurd as preaching repentance to the devils themselves. But there is the greatest difference between reprobate men and those reprobate spirits, although they agree in this, that both will remain in eternal fire. For the elect and the reprobate of men are mixed together in this life, and we cannot know who will believe and who will not; and there are other things we have mentioned, above all the command of God, by which the gospel has been instituted for every human creature.

units.la: Præterea cauillatur: si reprobis auditio verbi cedit in maius iudicium, peiore esse conditione eos, quàm sint Diaboli, qui ex prædicato Euangelio nullum tale iudicium sibi contrahunt.
units.tr: Moreover he quibbles: if the hearing of the Word turns to a greater judgement for the reprobate, then they are in a worse condition than the devils, who incur no such judgement from the preached gospel.

units.la: Paralogismus est à dicto secundum quid. Simpliciter loquendo infelicio-res sunt Diaboli, quia improbiores & nequiores: unde à Paulo τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας appellantur. Interim nihil vetat homines reprobos peiore esse conditione secundum quid, hoc est, obstrictos teneri iudicio ob causam aliquam qua non teneantur Diaboli, vt, ex contemtu verbi ipsis prædicati, ex sumfumptione indigna cœnæ dominicæ: quia indigne fumentes damnationem sibi edunt & bibunt. Id autem in Dæmonibus locum nō habet, licet nihilominus tanquam hostes iustitiæ omnis atque ordinis à Deo instituti, ac proinde etiam tanquam contemtores verbi & sacramentorum suo modo, iudicium Dei non sint effugituri.
units.tr: This is a fallacy from a statement made in a certain respect. Speaking absolutely, the devils are more wretched, because more wicked and more depraved; for this reason Paul calls them the spiritual wickednesses [τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας]. Yet nothing prevents reprobate men from being in a worse condition in a certain respect, that is, from being bound to judgement on account of some cause for which the devils are not bound: for example, from contempt of the Word preached to them, or from unworthy partaking of the Lord's Supper, since those who eat and drink unworthily eat and drink damnation to themselves. This does not apply to the demons, although nonetheless, as enemies of all justice and of the order instituted by God, and so also as despisers of the Word and the sacraments in their own way, they will not escape the judgement of God.

units.la: Impudentius etiam cauillatur; si res ita habeat, satius fore nunquam accedere verbum, siquidem cum omninò pereundum & conflagrandum sit, eo minus vapulabunt, quo minus audierint, quo d spernere potuerint.
units.tr: He quibbles even more shamelessly: if the matter stands so, it would be better never to come near the Word, since, when everyone must perish and be burned, those will be beaten less who have heard less and could have despised less.

units.la: Sile os durum & labia loquentis iniquitatem. Quid restat Hubere, nisi vt pari argumento cócludas, Cum multi in cœna Domini iudicium sibi edant & bibant, satius quoque fore vt ab ea abstineamus? Verum vt sophisticen eiusmodi omnes intelligant, vtrobique hoc tantum sequitur, præstare videlicet ad cœnam Domini non accedere, quàm indigne accedere: præstare item non audire verbum Dei, quàm auditum non recipere, aut etiam receptum abij-cere & conculcare; sed medium tenuere beati. Nam quia cum scientes voluntatem, nec tamé facientes eam, tum ignorantes eandem, vapulabunt, praecipuè si affectata sit ignorantia, oblatū Dei verbum audire dedignando; no-strum est & audire & obseruare sermonem Dei, atque ita nos ipsos comparare, vt Sacramenta percipere digne quea-mus. Ita sanè optimè nobis consuluerimus, non autem si regno Dei nos ipsos indignos iudicemus, verbum ipsius & Sacramenta respuendo.
units.tr: "Silence the hard mouth and the lips that speak iniquity." What is left for you, Huber, but to conclude by the same argument: since many eat and drink judgement to themselves at the Lord's Supper, it would also be better for us to abstain from it? But so that everyone may understand this sophistry, in both cases what follows is only this: it is better not to come to the Lord's Supper than to come unworthily; and likewise it is better not to hear the Word of God than to hear it and not receive it, or even to receive it and cast it away and trample it underfoot. But the blessed have kept the middle way. For since those who knew the will and did not do it, and those who did not know it, will both be beaten, especially if the ignorance was deliberate, scorning to hear the Word of God that is offered, it is our duty both to hear and to keep the word of God, and so to prepare ourselves that we may receive the sacraments worthily. Thus we shall indeed have consulted our good best; not by judging ourselves unworthy of the kingdom of God and rejecting his Word and sacraments.

units.la: Quartò, vt dicacitatem qua pollet, hîc quoque lectori probaret Antagonista (si tamen cuiquam sani iudicii ea probari potest aut debet) proterue ait, ministros Caluinianos carnifices esse reproborum, qui ad exquisita tormenta ab æterno damnatos rapiant, & excarnificent, si quidem verum illud sit, quod illi verbum Dei audiant ad iudicium.
units.tr: Fourthly, in order to prove to the reader here too the bitterness in which he excels (if indeed that can be approved by anyone of sound judgement), the opponent brazenly says that the Calvinist ministers are the executioners of the reprobate, who drag those condemned from eternity to exquisite torments and torture them, if indeed it is true that they hear the Word of God to judgement.

units.la: Quid ergo? Quo loco Iesaïam Prophetam habituras est, cui dictum est, cum gloriam Dei videret: Vade, impin-gua cor populi huius, & claude oculos eius. Qui quidem locus Prophetæ non temerè in nouo T.sexies repetitur de Iudæorum excæcatione. An verò scommate Huberiano, vel Prophetam, vel Christum ipsum, cuius gloriam tum vidit Iesaias, carnifices propterea reproborum dicemus? Absit proteruia ista à pectore Christiano. Quin potius, teste Apostolo, Christi bona fragrantia sumus Deo, & in ijs qui pereunt, & in iis qui seruantur: illis quidem odor mortis ad mortem: his verò odor vitæ ad vitam: interim semper bona fragrantia Christi Deo, vtrorumque respectu.
units.tr: What then? What about the place where the prophet Isaiah, who saw the glory of God, was told: Go, make the heart of this people fat, and shut their eyes. This passage is not repeated lightly in the New Testament six times, concerning the blindness of the Jews. Shall we, then, with Huber's jest, call the prophet, or Christ himself, whose glory Isaiah then saw, the executioners of the reprobate? Far from a Christian breast be such brazenness. Rather, as the Apostle witnesses, we are the good fragrance of Christ to God, both among those who perish and among those who are saved: to the one indeed a savour of death unto death, to the others a savour of life unto life; yet always a good fragrance of Christ to God, in respect of both.

units.la: Ad extremum notandum est, nihil hîc referre, siue præordinante, siue tantum præsciente Deo ita fiat, quod reprobis Euangelij annunciatio in iudicium cedit. Vtraque enim, & præscientia & præordinatio Dei, infallibilis est. Quare cum aduersarius saltem præscientiam in Deo negare non possit, eorum qui verbo non obedituri sunt ad gratuiorem condemnationem, allatæ iam cacauillationes in ipsius caput recidant necesse est. Ad de his satis.
units.tr: Finally, it should be noted that it makes no difference here whether God so ordains it beforehand or merely foresees it, that the proclamation of the gospel turns into judgment for the reprobate. For both, both God's foreknowledge and his predestination, are infallible. Therefore, since the opponent cannot at least deny foreknowledge in God, the cavils already raised must necessarily recoil upon his own head, namely that those who are not going to obey the word are condemned all the more freely. Enough on these matters.

units.la: CAPUT XV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XV.

units.la: Ad sextum absurdum.
units.tr: On the sixth absurdity.

units.la: PERGO ad id quod de Sacramentis obijciebatur; Tolli videlicet Sacramenta, nisi manibus pedibusque, vt aiunt, in Huberi eatur sententiam, de redemtionis vniuersitate. De baptismo assignat rationem hanc, quod baptizatis nulla certa gratia & salus promittatur. Argumentum tale erit;
units.tr: I now turn to what was objected concerning the Sacraments: that the Sacraments are abolished, unless, as they say, one goes with hands and feet into Huber's opinion on the universality of redemption. As for baptism, he gives this reason: that no certain grace and salvation is promised to the baptized. The argument will run thus:

units.la: Secundum quos baptizatis nulla certa proponitur gratia & salus, eorum sententia baptismus tollitur.
units.tr: According to those for whom no certain grace and salvation is offered to the baptized, their opinion abolishes baptism.

units.la: Atqui secundum eos qui sentiunt Christi morte omnes quidem sufficienter, sed non effectiue redemtos, ita vt vniuersi & singuli accepta peccatorum condonatione, in gratiam Dei recepti, iustificati & saluati sint, siue credant fiue non: secundum hos, inquam, nulla certa promittitur gratia & salus baptizatis.
units.tr: But according to those who hold that all are indeed sufficiently, but not effectually, redeemed by Christ's death, so that all and each, having received the forgiveness of sins, are received into God's favour, justified and saved, whether they believe or not: according to these, I say, no certain grace and salvation is promised to the baptized.

units.la: Ergo eorum sententia baptismus tollitur. Nisi ita formetur argumentum, non video quomodo quicquam concludi possit ad propositum.
units.tr: Therefore their opinion abolishes baptism. Unless the argument is framed in this way, I do not see how anything can be concluded to the point at issue.

units.la: Sed minor negatur. Huberus quidem thef. 1019. remittit nos ad ea quae habet a thef 386. vsque ad 431. sed si illa inspiciantur & examinentur, apparebit ibi nihil contineri, praeter male congestam, extrauagantem & mere otiosam farraginem quaestionum quarundam de baptismo. Verum missis ambagibus hoc probare debuisti Hubere, quod opinionis tuae de generalitate redemtionis contradictoria posita, euer-sio sequatur baptismi, idque ea de causa, quòd nulla certa gratia & salus promissa tum queat baptizatis. Hoc, hoc demonstrare si potes, omissis digressionibus tuis multiplicibus, quibus lectorem a propósito auocare & mistere implicare confudisti.
units.tr: But the minor premise is denied. Huber, indeed, at thesis 1019, refers us to what he has at theses 386 to 431. But if those are inspected and examined, it will appear that nothing is contained there except a badly heaped, wandering and wholly idle farrago of certain questions about baptism. Yet, setting aside the circumlocutions, you ought to have proved, Huber, that the contradictory position of your opinion on the universality of redemption entails the overthrow of baptism, and that for this reason: that no certain grace and salvation can then be promised to the baptized. Demonstrate this, if you can, with your many digressions set aside, by which you have confused the reader, drawing him away from the point and entangling him.

units.la: Enimuero ad nos quod attinet, è diuinis scripturis didicimus, & constanter docemus, sacri baptismatis vsum eò respicere, & quidem principalitet, vt
units.tr: Indeed, as far as we are concerned, we have learned from the divine Scriptures, and we constantly teach, that the use of holy baptism looks to this, and principally so, namely

units.la: Vsus principalis S. Baptismi.
units.tr: The principal use of holy Baptism.

units.la: promissionem gratiae & vitae aeternae nobis obsignet atque confirmet. Tolle enim promissionem gratiae e baptismo, & sacramenti rationem substuleris, quoniam secundum visitatam Augustt. definitionem, Sacramentum est invisibilis gratiae visibilis forma. Hinc illae promissiones: Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, salvabitur. Marc. 16. Et in verbis Petri Act. 2. Resipiscite & baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomine Iesu Christi in remissionem peccatorum, & accipietis donum Spiritus Sancti. Item 1. Pet. 3. baptisma salvos nos facit. Et Tit. 3. Ex sua misericordia servat nos per lavacrum regenerationis & renovationem Spiritus Sancti: & quae alia eiusmodi de virtute baptismi in sacris leguntur, quae scite complexus videtur Basilius exhortatione ad Baptismum:
units.tr: that it seals and confirms to us the promise of grace and eternal life. For take the promise of grace away from baptism, and you have removed the nature of the sacrament, since according to Augustine's well-known definition a sacrament is a visible form of invisible grace. Hence those promises: He who believes and is baptized will be saved (Mark 16). And in the words of Peter, Acts 2: Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit. Likewise, 1 Pet. 3: baptism saves us. And Titus 3: According to his mercy he saves us through the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit. And whatever other such things about the power of baptism are read in the sacred books, which Basil seems neatly to have summed up in his exhortation on Baptism:

units.la: Baptismus, inquit, est captivorum & aeris alieni remissio, peccati mors, animi regeneratio, amicitus splendens, caeli iter, regni caelestis conciliatio, adoptionis gratia.
units.tr: Baptism, he says, is the release of captives and of debt, the death of sin, the regeneration of the soul, a shining garment, the way to heaven, the reconciliation to the heavenly kingdom, the grace of adoption.

units.la: Sacer quippe baptismus tantarum rerum signaculum est credentibus, quemadmodum de circumcisione loquitur
units.tr: Holy baptism is indeed the seal of such great things to believers, just as the Apostle speaks of circumcision

units.la: quitur Apostolus,datam fuisse Abrahæ in signaculum iustitiæ fidei, docens, circumcisione non fuisse datam in iustitiam,sed in obsignatione iustitiæ quæ ex fide est. Dico autem credentibus,quia nec verbum nec baptismus quicquam promittit aut prodest impijs & incredulis. Verbum siquidem promissionis est; Qui crediderit & baptizatus fuerit, servabitur: qui non crediderit, condemnabitur: siue nepe is baptizatus fuerit, siue non.
units.tr: ...saying that it was given to Abraham as a seal of the righteousness of faith, teaching that circumcision was not given for righteousness but as a sealing of the righteousness which is from faith. I say, however, "to believers", because neither the word nor baptism promises or profits anything to the impious and unbelieving. For the word is a word of promise: He who believes and is baptized will be saved; he who does not believe will be condemned; whether, that is, he has been baptized or not.

units.la: Et ad Ephef.5. légimus Ecclesiā a sponso Christo sanctificatam esse & mūdatam lauacro aquæ in verbo. Cur in verbo? Quia & in aqua verbum mundat, non aqua per se:vt explicat August. tract.80. super Ioh. Et subdit idem: Vnde hæc est tāta virtus aquæ, vt corpus tangat & cor abluat, nisi faciente verbo? idque non quia dicitur, sed quia creditur. Idem in Psalm.77. de Iudæis sic scribit; Sacramenta cùm essent omnibus communia, non erat communis gratia, quæ virtus est sacramentorum; Sic & nunc commune est baptizatis omnibus lauacrum regenerationis, sed ipsa gratia, qua membra Christi cum suo capite regenerātur, non omnibus est commune. Rursum lib.5. contra Donatist.cap.24. ait, Baptisma sine spiritu esse possé: & baptizatorum alios induere Christum vsque ad Sacramenti perceptionem, alios vsque ad vitæ sanctificationem. Illud commune esse bonis & malis: hoc proprium bonorum & piorum.
units.tr: And in Eph. 5 we read that the Church was sanctified and cleansed by her bridegroom Christ with the washing of water in the word. Why "in the word"? Because in water too the word cleanses, not the water by itself, as Augustine explains in tractate 80 on John. And the same writer adds: Whence comes such great power in water, that it touches the body and cleanses the heart, unless the word works it? And this not because it is spoken, but because it is believed. The same, in Psalm 77, writes thus of the Jews: Since the sacraments were common to all, the grace which is the power of the sacraments was not common; so also now the washing of regeneration is common to all the baptized, but the grace itself, by which the members of Christ are regenerated with their head, is not common to all. Again, in book 5 against the Donatists, chapter 24, he says: Baptism can exist without the Spirit; and of the baptized, some put on Christ up to the reception of the sacrament, others up to the sanctification of life. The former is common to good and bad; the latter is proper to the good and pious.

units.la: Et sane in scholis receptissimum est, sine fide vel fide accedentes, sacramentum, non rem percipere, exemplo Simonis Magi, de quo super Leviticum quæst.84. testatur Augustinus, visibilem baptismum non profuisse ei, quia invisibilis non adfuerit.
units.tr: And indeed it is most widely accepted in the schools that those who approach with or without faith receive the sacrament, not the thing itself, after the example of Simon Magus. Of him Augustine, in his questions on Leviticus, question 84, testifies that the visible baptism did not profit him, because the invisible was not present.

units.la: Huc & Lutheri dicta referantur: baptismum insignum iustitiæ erectum omnibus qui in Christum credant. In suscipientis vsu aut fide sitam esse virtutem baptismi: Sacrum item baptismum fontem esse salutis, quem bibentes, id est, promissioni addita credentes, nunquam sitiant. Et quod generatim alibi pronunciat, sacramentum non operari gratiam sine fide, & taxat Papistarum omnium, quod baptismus prodest tibi & iustificet te, sive credas sive non.
units.tr: Let the sayings of Luther also be cited here: Baptism is a sign of righteousness set up for all who believe in Christ. The power of baptism lies in the use of the recipient, or in faith. Likewise holy baptism is a fountain of salvation, which those who drink it, that is, who believe the promise added to it, never thirst. And what he pronounces generally elsewhere: the sacrament does not work grace without faith; and he censures all the Papists for holding that baptism benefits you and justifies you, whether you believe or not.

units.la: Nec aliter Brentius explicatione Catechismi. tech.de baptismo, vbi inter alia scribit, baptismum esse signaculum, quo Christus publicè confirmet, se credenti tradere, ac propria dicare ea coelestia bona, quę Euangelio promittuntur. Item, baptismum esse velut regiam vnctionem, sacramento confirmante & promulgante id quod homo antea per fidem accepe-rat. Neque enim tum primum homine suscipi in tutelam Dei, cùm ante fit fuscep-tus per fidem: sed hominis fuscep-tionem tum primum externo signo confirmari. Et tractans illam promis-sionem, Qui crediderit, &c. diserte hanc profert sententiam: Baptismum, sicut plurimum prosit si fide suscipiatur, ita si absque fide fuerit, nihil prodesse: meminitq; exem-pli ex historia trip.lib.11.cap.14. de Iudæo quodam impostore, crebrius suscipiente baptismū, non quod in Christum crederet, sed vt hac arte à Christianis pecuniam emungeret; qui etsi baptizatus fuerit, tamen ex baptismi susceptione verè Christianus factus minimè fit. Idē Bretius in Ioh.sol.119. expresse scribit, non omnem qui baptizatur, regenera„ri. Fidem enim omninò requiri, non „ quidem ad Sacramenti integritate, sed „ ad vtilitatem percipientis.
units.tr: Brentius likewise, in his explanation of the Catechism, on baptism, where among other things he writes that baptism is a seal by which Christ publicly confirms that he hands over to the believer and dedicates to him as his own those heavenly goods which are promised in the Gospel. Likewise, baptism is, as it were, a royal anointing, the sacrament confirming and proclaiming what the man had previously received through faith. For the man is not then for the first time taken into God's protection, when he has already been received through faith; rather, his reception is then for the first time confirmed by an outward sign. And treating that promise, He who believes, etc., he expressly delivers this opinion: Baptism, just as it greatly profits if received in faith, so, if it is without faith, profits nothing. He also recalls an example from the history of the Tripartite, book 11, chapter 14, of a certain Jewish impostor who received baptism repeatedly, not because he believed in Christ but so that by this trick he might squeeze money out of the Christians; although he was baptized, by receiving baptism he by no means became truly a Christian. The same Brentius, on John, sol. 119, expressly writes that not everyone who is baptized is regenerated. For faith is by all means required, not indeed for the integrity of the sacrament, but for the benefit of the recipient.

units.la: Ad eundem modum Dauid Chytraeus Tractatu de Bapt. VVitenbergæ edito, anno 1580. ait, ministros baptizare aquâ, pronúciare verbum & adhibere aquâ: sed Christum baptizare spiritu S. & regenerare credetes. Item, Multi flumine seu aqua loti, nec afferetes ad baptismum veram fidem, non flamine sp. S. sed aqua tantum baptizantur, vt Simon Magus.
units.tr: In the same way David Chytraeus, in his treatise on Baptism published at Wittenberg in 1580, says that ministers baptize with water, pronounce the word and apply the water, but that Christ baptizes with the Holy Spirit and regenerates believers. Likewise: Many, washed with river or water, and not bringing true faith to baptism, are baptized not with the flame of the Holy Spirit but with water only, like Simon Magus.

units.la: Hæc pluribus expósita ostendunt, quorum sit promissio gratiæ in Baptismo, contra quorundam errore, & plus quàm sommium, nimirum quod regeneratio omnibus detur in Baptismo, credentibus & non credétibus; quodq; si infidelis hypocrita baptizetur, is non solum foris aqua baptizetur, sed & intus per Spiritum S. adeóque Simon Magus non minus aliis gratiam in baptismo acceperit. Hoc reuera est Baptismum, non pro Sacramento Christi, sed pro ipso Christo celebrare: vt Apologia Confess. VVitebergensis exprobrat Papistis. pistis,idem dicentibus quod isti,remis-sionem peccatorum videlicet fieri per Baptismum, per ipsam virtutem sacra-menti, diuinamque promissionem; & non solum per fidem. Vicerint igitur Papistæ,& prostrata iacebit C o n f e s-s i o D v c i s V V i r t‑e n b e r g e n s i s, cuersa ab iis ipsis qui defendere de-buissent.
units.tr: These things, set out at length, show whose promise of grace there is in Baptism, against the error of some, and more than a dream: namely, that regeneration is given in Baptism to all, to believers and unbelievers alike; and that if an unbelieving hypocrite is baptized, he is not only baptized outwardly with water but also inwardly through the Holy Spirit, so that Simon Magus received grace in baptism no less than others. This is truly to celebrate Baptism not as Christ's sacrament but as Christ himself, as the Apology of the Wittenberg Confession rebukes the Papists for doing: they say the same as these men, that remission of sins takes place through Baptism, through the very power of the sacrament and the divine promise, and not only through faith. So the Papists will have won, and the Wittenberg Confession will lie prostrate, overturned by those very men who ought to have defended it.

units.la: Sed quid dicemus de infantibus qui baptizantur? an & illis baptismus sine fide salutaris esse nequit?
units.tr: But what shall we say of infants who are baptized? Can baptism be saving for them too without faith?

units.la: Respondeo. Quanquam sunt nostra ætate, qui & infantes credere putant,idque ab omnibus credi ita volùt: simplicior tamen atque tutior est Augustini aliorumque veterum sententia in contrarium. Sic enim August. super Iohannem tract. 80. inquit,Hoc verbum fidei tantùm valet in Ecclesia, vt per ipsam credentem,offerentem,benedicentem & tangentem,etiam tantillum mundet infantem, quamuis nondum sua-lente credere corde ad iustitiam,& ore confiteri ad salutem. Similiter lib. 4. de Bapt. cap. 24. Ex ætatis indigentia, ait,infantes nec corde corde credere possunt ad iustitiam, nec ore confiteri ad salutem. Vide etiam Epist.23. ad Bonifacium. & Iustinum Martyrem quaestione 56. Eandem sententiam Bernardus probat Epist.77. vbi ait, Infantes prohibente aetate non possunt habere fidem.
units.tr: I answer: although there are people in our time who think that infants also believe, and who want everyone to believe this, the opinion of Augustine and the other ancients to the contrary is simpler and safer. For Augustine, on John, tractate 80, says: "This word of faith is so powerful in the Church that, through the believer who offers, blesses and touches the infant, it cleanses even the tiniest child, although it cannot yet believe with the heart unto righteousness, and confess with the mouth unto salvation." Similarly, in book 4 on Baptism, chapter 24, he says: "Because of the weakness of their age, infants can neither believe with the heart unto righteousness nor confess with the mouth unto salvation." See also Letter 23 to Boniface, and Justin Martyr, question 56. Bernard approves the same opinion in Letter 77, where he says: "Infants, because of their age, cannot have faith."

units.la: Ratio non obscura est; Fides quippe cognitionem credendorum praesupponit. Scire autem diuina paruulos, qui nondum humana norunt, si verbis velimus ostendere, ait item Augustinus Epist.57. verendum est, ne ipsis sensibus nostris facere videamur iniuriam: quando id loquendo suadere studemus, vbi omnes vires officiumque sermonis supe- ret euidentia veritatis.
units.tr: The reason is not obscure: faith presupposes knowledge of the things to be believed. But, as Augustine also says in Letter 57, if we wish to show by words that little children, who do not yet know human things, know divine things, we must take care not to seem to do violence to our own senses, when we strive to persuade this by speaking, where the clarity of the truth surpasses all the powers and office of speech.

units.la: Adhaec, qui fidem afferunt paruulorum, non parum opinionibus discrepant, aliis in baptismo, aliis ante baptismum fidem ijs dari sentientibus. A posteriore sententia non alienus est Brentius explicatione Catech. vbi argumentatur, Deum nullum vere agnoscere in numero populi sui, nisi credat. Et assumit de infantibus: Infantes populi Dei fuisse olim partem populi Dei, etiam iam priusquam circumciderentur, & proinde nostros infantes nunc quoque ad populum Dei pertinere, etiam antequam baptizentur, iuxta promissionē quæ dicta est ad Abrah. Gen.17. Ero Deus tuus & seminis tui post te.
units.tr: Moreover, those who attribute faith to infants disagree not a little among themselves, some holding that they receive it in baptism, others before baptism. Brenz is not far from the latter opinion in his Explanation of the Catechism, where he argues that God truly acknowledges no one among the number of his people unless he believes. And he takes up the case of infants: "The infants of God's people were formerly part of God's people, even before they were circumcised; and therefore our infants now also belong to the people of God, even before they are baptized, according to the promise given to Abraham, Genesis 17: I will be God to you and to your seed after you."

units.la: Priorem sententiam e contrario Iacobus Andreæ, Bretij successor, tuetur Colloq. Momp.sol.458. Priusquam, inquit, baptizentur infantes, non possum affirmare quod credant; quoniam fides illis in baptismo datur. Et mox, Infantes baptizati donantur gratia adoptionis, fide & spiritu sanêto. Similiter Luthe- rus (quanquam in libello De orando, aliter sensisse videri possit) in Gen.17. scri- ptum reliquit, Israelitarum liberos habuisse hanc benedictionem, vt octauo die donarentur fide, & fierent populus Dei: quod pari ratione de Christianorum liberis in Bapt. intelligi vult.
units.tr: On the contrary, Jakob Andreae, Brenz's successor, defends the former opinion in the Colloquy of Montbéliard, p. 458: "Before infants are baptized, I cannot affirm that they believe, since faith is given to them in baptism." And soon after: "Infants who are baptized are granted the grace of adoption through faith and the Holy Spirit." Likewise Luther (although in his little book On Prayer he may seem to have thought otherwise), in his commentary on Genesis 17, has left it written that the children of the Israelites had this blessing, namely that on the eighth day they were given faith and became the people of God; and he wants this to be understood in the same way of the children of Christians in baptism.

units.la: Et hæc quidem sententia magnas patitur angustias, propter infantes olim, vigente circumcisione, ante octauum diem exstinctos, & quotidie adhuc non percepto baptismo decedentes, & non contemtu aliquo sed necessitate baptismo priuatos, quos tamen vterque ipsorum magis includit numero saluandorum, cum fœdus Domini non transgrediatur aut irritum faciant. Atqui vt ipsorum fert opinio, nemo, siue is puer siue adultus sit, sine fide seruari potest. Cósequens igitur est, cum salus talibus quoque obtingat, vt fides multis passim detur infantibus, etiam antequam baptizentur; quod Iacobus Andreæ negabat se affirmare posse. Idem de fœmellis apud Iudæos posset obijci, quæ quia semen Abrahæ erant, à iustitia Abrahæ non excludebantur, sed consequebatur eam side, secundum Lutherum loco citato, etiam in infantia.
units.tr: Now this opinion suffers great difficulties, on account of infants who in former times, while circumcision was in force, died before the eighth day, and of those who daily still depart this life without having received baptism, not through any contempt but through necessity deprived of baptism; yet both of these authors include them in the number of those to be saved, since they have not transgressed the covenant of the Lord nor made it void. But, as their own opinion holds, no one, whether child or adult, can be saved without faith.
