units.la: Hinc quoque liquido patet, Christum specialiter mortuum esse pro electis vbique gentium, qui ab oriente in occidentem colliguntur in vnitatem fidei atque spiritus, vt cum Abrahamo, Isaaco, Iacobo, discumbant in regno coelorum. Et de his filiis Dei dispersis sub alia quidem similitudine, eodem tamen sensu dixerat Christus Cap. 10. alias etiam oues habeo, quae non sunt de ovili hoc, illas quoque oportet me adducere. Nam vocem meam audient, & fiet vnum ovile & vnus pastor. Monet autem Augustinus tract. 49. in Iohannem, secundum praedestinationem haec dicta esse: siquidem vocatione, neque oues eius, neque filij Dei erant, qui nondum crediderant, sed postea crediderunt. Ac vt alibi idem scribit, Serm. 50. de verbis Domini in Ioh. erant praedestinati, nondum congregati: & nouerat illos, qui praedestinauerat; nouerat, qui redimere sanguine suo venerat. Praeclare Tuitiensis Com. in Iohan.
units.tr: From this it also plainly appears that Christ died specially for the elect scattered throughout the nations, who are gathered from east and west into the unity of faith and of the Spirit, so that they may recline with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. Christ also spoke of these scattered children of God under another image but with the same meaning, in chapter 10: I have other sheep, which are not of this fold; them also I must bring. And they will hear my voice, and there will be one fold and one shepherd. Augustine, however, observes in tractate 49 on John that these words are to be understood according to predestination: for by calling they were not yet his sheep, nor children of God, since they had not yet believed, but afterwards they believed. And as he writes elsewhere, in sermon 50 on the words of the Lord in John, they were predestined but not yet gathered; and he knew those whom he had predestined; he knew those for whom he had come to redeem them with his blood. Tuitiensis splendidly says the same in his commentary on John.

units.la: Iesus Christus mortuus est pro gente, non tantum pro gente Abrahæ, sed & pro cunctis prædestinatis ab origine mundi, filiis Dei, in quatuor mundi plagas dispersis, & iam iam de massa generis humani usque ad vltimum electum recolligendis. Consulant etiam aduersarij Illyricum suum super Iohannem.
units.tr: Jesus Christ died for the nation, not only for the nation of Abraham but also for all who were predestined from the beginning of the world, the children of God, scattered into the four quarters of the world, and who are now, and will be, gathered from the mass of mankind until the last of the elect is gathered in. Let our opponents also consult their Illyricus on John.

units.la: Nonus locus Iohan.12. Nunc iudicium adest mundi huius: nunc Princeps mundi huius eiicietur foras: & ego si exaltatus fuero traham omnes ad me. Hoc autem dicebat, significans, qua morte futurus erat ut moreretur.
units.tr: The ninth place is John 12: Now is the judgement of this world; now the prince of this world will be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up, will draw all men to myself. But he said this, signifying by what death he was going to die.

units.la: Ad quos efficacia redemtionis per exaltationem Christi in cruce pertinet, ad ipsum trahatur seu conuertantur omnes necesse est, ut ipse sit caput eorum, & ipsi membra ipsius. Hoc autem tractu gratiæ, electorum, non hominum vniuersitas trahitur: quippe de hominum vniuersitate experientia repugnat: sed omnes dicit, id est omnes prædestinatos ad salutem: vel omnia hominum genera, ex quibus electorum specialis quædam censetur vniuersitas, sicut Augustinus tract.52. in Ioh. & Prosper de vocatione gentium libro 1. cap.3. dictum hoc declarant. Quapropter efficacia redemtionis propria est vniuersitatis electorum.
units.tr: Those to whom the efficacy of redemption through the lifting up of Christ on the cross applies must necessarily be drawn or converted to him, so that he may be their head and they his members. Yet it is not the whole multitude of men that is drawn by this drawing of grace, but the elect; for experience contradicts the idea that all men without exception are drawn. Rather he says all, that is, all who are predestined to salvation; or all kinds of men, out of whom a certain special multitude of the elect is reckoned, as Augustine in tractate 52 on John and Prosper in On the Calling of the Gentiles, book 1, chapter 3, explain this saying. Therefore the efficacy of redemption belongs to the multitude of the elect alone.

units.la: Decimus locus Ioh. 15. Maiorem hac charitatem nemo habet, vt quis ponat animam suam pro amicis suis. Vos amici mei eritis si feceritis, quae mando vobis. Non amplius dicam vos seruos: quia seruus nescit quid faciat Dominus: vos autem dixi amicos: quia omnia quae audiui a patre, nota feci vobis. Si specialiter pro amicis Christus mortuus est, vt est, non igitur ex aequo & pari ratione pro damnatis, qua pro Petro, Paulo aliisque amicis suis mortuus est: siquidem non omnes amici, sed alii amici, alii serui. Huic autem non repugnat, quod ad Rom. 5. dicitur: Christum pro nobis mortuu, cum adhuc inimici essemus Nam ex distinctione Bernardi serm. 10. de Psal. Qui habitat &c. Christus secundum tempus quidem pro impiis & inimicis mortuus est: secundum praedestinationem autem, pro fratribus & amicis.
units.tr: The tenth place is John 15: Greater love than this no one has, that someone lay down his life for his friends. You will be my friends if you do what I command you. I no longer call you servants, for a servant does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, because I have made known to you all that I have heard from the Father. If Christ died specially for friends, as is the case, then he did not die on equal footing and by the same reasoning for the damned as for Peter, Paul and his other friends; for not all are friends, some are servants. Nor does what is said in Romans 5 contradict this: Christ died for us while we were still enemies. For according to the distinction of Bernard in sermon 10 on Psalm 91 (He who dwells, etc.), Christ died in time indeed for the impious and enemies, but according to predestination for brothers and friends.

units.la: Vndecimus locus est Ioh. 17. vbi Apostolus & Pontifex confessionis nostrae,
units.tr: The eleventh place is John 17, where the Apostle and High Priest of our confession,

units.la: Y ij in folenni sua precatione, quam paulò ante mortem patri suo obtulisse legitur, ait, non rogo te pro mundo, sed pro ijs, quos dedisti mihi: quia tui sunt.
units.tr: in his solemn prayer, which is read to have been offered to his Father shortly before his death, says: I do not pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me, because they are yours.

units.la: Mundum pro reprobis accipi, antithesis electorum offendit, qui Christo à patre dati sunt: nec diffiteri hoc potuit D. Iacobus And.pag. 545. Col. Momp. Pro quibus autem Christus ne rogare quidem voluit, quomodo pro ijs mortuum dicemus secundum propositum, aut quomodo eis mors Christi ad redemptionem & sanctificationem proficeret? Certè sacrificium Mediatoris non prodest, nisi quibus intercessio eius prodest.
units.tr: That the world is taken to mean the reprobate is shown by the contrast with the elect, who were given to Christ by the Father; nor could Jacob Andreae deny this, p. 545, col. Montbéliard. But for those for whom Christ did not even wish to pray, how shall we say, according to his purpose, that he died, or how would the death of Christ benefit them towards redemption and sanctification? Surely the sacrifice of the Mediator profits only those for whom his intercession profits.

units.la: Excipit Hub:non detrectasse Christum in genere suam orationem pro mundo, sed in specie: quod Glossa Lutheri declarat & confirmat, Non rogo te pro mundo: hoc est, non rogo ut mundi & infidelium conatus & opera approbes.
units.tr: Huberus objects that Christ did not refuse in general to pray for the world, but only in particular; and Luther's gloss, which Huberus cites and confirms, explains I do not pray for the world: that is, I do not pray that you approve the endeavours and works of the world and of unbelievers.

units.la: Responsio expedita est ex antithesi in contextu. Quatenus pro suis Dominus orat, eatenus eodemq; respectu non orat pro mundo illo reproborum. Pro suis autem orat vt seruentur. Eatenus igitur non orat pro reprobis. Audia-mus Augustinum tract.107. Non pro mundo rogo, sed pro his quos dedisti mihi. Mundum vult intelligi, qui viuunt secundu concupiscentiam mundi, & non sunt in ea forte gratia, vt ab illa eligantur ex mundo. Idem tract.110. Est mundus damnandorum, de quo scriptum est, ne cum mundo hoc damne-mur. Pro isto mundo non rogat: neque enim quo sit praedestinatus ignorat. Et est mundus saluandorum, sicut scriptum est, vt saluetur mundus per ipsum: de quo & Apostolus dicit, Deus erat in Christo mundu sibi reconcilians. Pro isto mundo rogat, vt credat, & per fidem reconcilietur Deo. Hæc Augustinus.
units.tr: The answer is ready from the contrast in the context. Insofar as the Lord prays for his own, so far and in that same respect he does not pray for that world of the reprobate. But he prays for his own that they may be kept. So far, then, he does not pray for the reprobate. Let us hear Augustine in tractate 107: I do not pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me. By the world he means those who live according to the lust of the world, and who are not in that lot of grace by which they are chosen out of the world. The same in tractate 110: There is the world of the damned, of which it is written, that we should not be condemned with this world. He does not pray for this world; for he does not ignore who is predestined to it. And there is the world of the saved, as it is written, that the world might be saved through him; of which the Apostle also says, God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself. For this world he prays, that it may believe, and through faith be reconciled to God. Thus Augustine.

units.la: Quare non est quod scribat Hubc-rus, falsam interpretationem a nostris loco huic affingi. Fingit qui talia obiicit: quemadmodum & hoc merum figmentum est, omnes homines sine discrimine a patre datos esse filio, vt illis vitam det. Potestas quidem non omnis solum humanæ carnis, verum etiam omnium creaturarum in cœlo & in terra,data est filio: sed aliud est nos ipsi ef- fe datos, quos seruet. Nam si omnes Christo dati essent, pro omnibus oras- set: orauit enim pro omnibus,quos pa- ter ipsi dederat. Nunc autem pro ali- quibus,quos Mundum vocat, non ora- uit. Deinde sibi datis omnibus dat vi- tam aeternam. Sic enim ait, vt quotquot dedisti ipsi,det eis vitam aeternam. Proinde cum Augustino tract. CXI. inferimus per contrapositionem, non ei datos qui- bus vitam non dabit aeternam: quam- uis & ipsorum potestas data sit, cui po- testas data est omnis carnis. Ibidem: Qui sunt, inquit, isti, quos ait a patre datos sibi? Nonne illi de quibus alio loco dicit, Nemo ve- nit ad me, nisi pater qui misserit me, traxerit eum? Ipsi sunt, quos a patre accepit, quos ipse elegit de mundo, vt iam non sint de mundo, sicut non est & ipse de mundo: & sunt tamen & ipsi mundus credens & cognoscens quod Christus a Deo patre sit missus. Rursus tract. 107. Mundum pro quo non rogat, vult intel- ligi, qui sunt in ea sorte gratia, vt eligantur ex mundo: sed pro his quos ei pater dedit, ro- gare se dicit: per hoc enim, quod eos illi pater iam dedit, factum est, ut non pertineant ad eum mundum pro quo non rogat.
units.tr: Therefore Huberus need not write that a false interpretation is foisted on this passage by our people. He invents who objects such things; and it is equally a pure fiction that all men without distinction were given by the Father to the Son, so that he might give them life. Power indeed was given to the Son over not only all flesh but all creatures in heaven and on earth; but it is another matter for us to have been given, that he should keep us. For if all had been given to Christ, he would have prayed for all; for he prayed for all whom the Father had given him. But now he has not prayed for some whom he calls the world. Further, to all who have been given to him he gives eternal life; for he says, that to all whom you have given him, he may give eternal life. Therefore with Augustine in tractate 111 we infer by contraposition that those are not given to him to whom he will not give eternal life, although the power of the one to whom power over all flesh has been given is also given to them. In the same place, he says, who are they whom he says were given to him by the Father? Are they not those of whom he says elsewhere, No one comes to me unless the Father who sent me draws him? They are those whom he received from the Father, whom he himself chose out of the world, so that they are no longer of the world, just as he himself is not of the world; and yet they are also a world, believing and knowing that Christ was sent by God the Father. Again, in tractate 107: The world for which he does not pray, he wishes to be understood as those who are not in that lot of grace by which they are chosen out of the world; but he says that he prays for those whom the Father has given him; for by the fact that the Father has already given them to him, it comes about that they do not belong to that world for which he does not pray.

units.la: Hinc & Cyrillus in Ioh. lib. 11. cap. 19. Beatus Iohannes, inquit, quoniam erat Iudaeus, ne pro Iudaeis tantum paracletus esse Dominus apud patrem videretur, non autem etiam pro aliis gentibus, quae vocatae obsequutae sunt, necessario dixit, eum propitiationem esse pro toto mundo. Dominus autem Iesus SVOSa NON SVIS separans, pro eis, inquit, TANTVM MODO qui verba mea seruant & ingum meum acceperunt, rogo. Nam quorum Mediator atque Pontifex est, ipsis tantum modo mediationis bonum non iniuria attribuit.
units.tr: Hence Cyril also, in his commentary on John, book 11, chapter 19: "Since the blessed John was a Jew, lest the Lord should seem to be a paraclete before the Father only for the Jews, and not also for the other nations who were called and obeyed, he necessarily said that he is the propitiation for the whole world. But the Lord Jesus, separating his own from not his own, says: I pray for them, namely ONLY those who keep my words and have received my yoke. For he rightly attributes the good of mediation only to those for whom he is Mediator and High Priest."

units.la: Ita firmum stat hoc testimonium contra cauillationes quascunque: de quo praeclare Rupertus commeni: ad hunc locum. Va inquit mundo gaudenti, orante pro suis, id est moriente & in ara crucis se sacrificium offerente Christo vnigenito filio Dei: quia pro eis quos dedisti mihi inquit rogo, non pro mundo. Mundus enim hic accipiuntur dilectores mundi, tam diuersi ab eis pro quibus Christus rogat crucifixus, quam diuersi erant apud Deum Aegypti a filiis Israel,
units.tr: Thus this testimony stands firm against all quibbles whatever. Rupert comments admirably on this passage: "Woe to the world that rejoices, while Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, prays for his own, that is, while he dies and offers himself as a sacrifice on the altar of the cross; for he says: I pray for those whom you have given me, not for the world. For by 'world' are meant the lovers of the world, as different from those for whom Christ prays crucified, as the Egyptians were different before God from the children of Israel,

units.la: Y iiij sacro sanguine agni postes suos signantibus. Væ igitur tali mundo, quia quod rogat Chri- ftus verus agnus Dei, nihil illi proficit, vt cum rege suo principe tenebrarum, Diabolo citius in profundam inferni demergatur, solis illis quos pater filio dedit, per crucem & sangui- nem eius euadentibus.
units.tr: who marked their doorposts with the sacred blood of the lamb. Woe therefore to such a world, because what Christ, the true Lamb of God, prays for profits it nothing; it will sooner be plunged with its prince, the king of darkness, the Devil, into the deep pit of hell. Only those whom the Father has given to the Son escape through the cross and his blood."

units.la: Duodecimo accedit, quod Dominus in sua ad patrem precatione ibidem expresse dicit: pro eis ego sanctifico me ipsum, vt & ipsi sanctificati sint in veritate.
units.tr: In the twelfth place, the Lord himself says expressly in the same prayer to the Father: "For them I sanctify myself, that they also may be sanctified in truth."

units.la: Ij tantum, pro quibus Christus sanctificauit, id est hostiam obtulit semetipsum, oblatione eius sanctificantur in veritate. At sanctificauit se tantum pro electis, de quibus significanter dicit ad distinctionem mundi: Pro eis ego sanctifico me ipsum: vtique suos intelligens, datos sibi a patre, & pro quibus ipse patrem rogauit. Ergo electi tantum in veritate sanctificantur oblatione Christi.
units.tr: Those alone for whom Christ sanctified himself, that is, offered himself as a victim, are sanctified in truth by his offering. But he sanctified himself only for the elect, of whom he significantly speaks in distinction from the world: "For them I sanctify myself." Clearly he means his own, given to him by the Father and for whom he himself prayed the Father. Therefore only the elect are sanctified in truth by the offering of Christ.

units.la: Vnde Paulus etiam omnes credentes, quos caritas pro electis iubet haberi, sanctos passim vocat; quia sunt sanguine Christi sanctificati.
units.tr: Hence Paul also everywhere calls all believers, whom charity bids us regard as elect, saints, because they have been sanctified by the blood of Christ.

units.la: CAPVT III.
units.tr: CHAPTER III.

units.la: Testimonia ex epistolis Pauli.
units.tr: Testimonies from the Epistles of Paul.

units.la: PAVLVS porrò Apostolus ac Doctor gentium & eximius gratiæ Christi præco, ad Euangelizandũ inter gentes imperueftigabiles opes Christi, & in lucem proferendi omnibus,quæ fit communio mysterij illius absconditi à fecu-lis, passim quoque docet gratiam redemtionis ad incredulos nõ pertinere, sed ad credentes,qui iam non vasa Diaboli,sed membra sunt Iesu Christi.
units.tr: Paul the Apostle, teacher of the Gentiles and outstanding herald of the grace of Christ, who was sent to preach among the nations the unsearchable riches of Christ and to bring to light for all people what is the fellowship of that mystery hidden from the ages, also teaches throughout that the grace of redemption does not belong to unbelievers but to believers, who are no longer vessels of the Devil but members of Jesus Christ.

units.la: Vt è multis pauca duntaxat testimonia allegemus, ad Rom. 3. ita scribit.
units.tr: To cite only a few of the many testimonies, he writes thus in Rom. 3.

units.la: Nunc vero absque lege patefacta est iustitia Dei,comprobata testimonio legis ac Prophetarum.Iustitia inquam Dei per fidem Iesu Christi,in omnes & super omnes qui credunt.Non enim est distinctio. Omnes enim peccauerunt, ac destituuntur gloria Dei. Iustificantur autem gratis per gratiam ipsius, per redemtionem in Christo Iesu factam: quem proposuit Deus ἱλαστήριον, placamentum seu propitiationem, per fidem in sanguine ipsius, ad declarandam iustitiam suam per remissionem peccatorum. Y v Sen-
units.tr: But now the righteousness of God is revealed apart from the law, being witnessed by the Law and the Prophets: the righteousness of God, I say, through faith in Jesus Christ, toward all and upon all who believe. For there is no distinction. For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God. They are justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God set forth as a propitiation [ἱλαστήριον], a means of atonement, through faith in his blood, to demonstrate his righteousness through the remission of sins.

units.la: Sentit quidem Apostolus, omnes simpliciter mortales sub peccato esse & egere gloria Dei: verum non quibuscunque peccatum, ijs etiam iustitiam asscribit, vt vult opinio aduersariorum. Expresse enim definit iustitiam Dei esse per fidem in Iesum Christum: & subdit explicatius: iustificari nos gratis per redemtionem factam in Christo: atque hunc propositum nobis a patre propitiationem, sed per fidem.
units.tr: The Apostle certainly means that all mortals without exception are under sin and lack the glory of God; but he does not ascribe righteousness to everyone who sins, as the opinion of our opponents would have it. For he expressly defines the righteousness of God to be through faith in Jesus Christ, and he adds more explicitly: that we are justified freely through the redemption made in Christ, whom God has set forth to us as propitiation, but through faith.

units.la: Hinc autor comm. apud Hieronymum in hunc locum: Christus, inquit, in promtu ante oculos hominum positus est propitiator, vt qui redimi vult accedat. Brentius quoque quem fepiufcule propter aduersarios cito, locum hunc expendens recte scribit, manifestum esse, quod Christus redemtio & propitiatio nostra, non accipiatur, nec approprietur nobis nisi fide. Itaque non esse aliud praeter fidem ordinem, quo beneficia Dei & filij eius fruenda accipiamus. Cumque Christus & beneficia eius non nisi fide accipiantur, reliquum esse, vt non nisi fide iusticemur, hoc est Deo grati fiamus & a peccapeccatis absoluamur, ac iusti coràm Deo reputemur. Hæc ille explicatione Catechismi de iustificatione.
units.tr: Hence the author of the commentary attributed to Jerome, on this passage: Christ, he says, is placed before the eyes of men, ready, as propitiator, so that whoever wishes to be redeemed may come. Brenz also, whom I often cite because of our opponents, expounding this passage, rightly writes that it is plain that Christ our redemption and propitiation is not received or appropriated by us except by faith. Therefore there is no other order, apart from faith, by which we receive the benefits of God and of his Son to enjoy. And since Christ and his benefits are received only by faith, it follows that we are justified only by faith, that is, that we are made pleasing to God and absolved from sins, and are accounted righteous before God. So he writes in his explanation of the Catechism, on justification.

units.la: Quo iure igitur, quaue iniuria propitiatio hæc ad omnes extenditur, omnesq; ab omni peccato & condemnatione liberati, & re ipsa in sinum gratiæ recepti, id est, iustificati prædicantur, siue credetes, siue increduli sint? Non hæc Dei iustitia est, sed ab hominibus reprobæ mentis conficta, in ludibrium Euangelij ab Apostolis prædicati, atque à lege & Prophetis testati.
units.tr: By what right, then, or by what injustice, is this propitiation extended to all, and all are proclaimed free from every sin and condemnation, and in fact received into the bosom of grace, that is, justified, whether they are believers or unbelievers? This is not the righteousness of God, but a fiction devised by men of depraved mind, a mockery of the Gospel preached by the Apostles and attested by the Law and the Prophets.

units.la: Adhæc fictitia illa vniuersalitate reiecta, stabilit Apostolus veram vniuersalitatem iustitiæ atque gratiæ, in omnes & super omnes qui credunt, hoc est, Theophyl. interprete: Eiusmodi iustitia, qua iustos nos Deus efficit, ad vniuersos per fidem peruenit, & fide allata iusti omnes redduntur, Iudæi simul & Græci. Nò enim est distinctio; nec Iudæorum Deus solùm sed & Gentium: siquidem vnus Deus est, qui iustificat circumcisione ex fide, & præputium per fidem. Non enim est Iudæus neque Græcus, nò est seruus neque liber: non est masculus neque fœmina: sed omnes nos vnum sumus in Christo, omnes filij Dei & se-cundum promissionem hæredes per fi-dem in Christum Iesum.
units.tr: Moreover, having rejected that fictitious universality, the Apostle establishes the true universality of righteousness and grace, toward all and upon all who believe, that is, as Theophylact interprets it: such righteousness, by which God makes us righteous, reaches all through faith, and by faith brought in all are made righteous, both Jews and Greeks. For there is no distinction: God is not the God of the Jews only but also of the Gentiles, since there is one God who justifies the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith. For there is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither slave nor free, there is neither male nor female; but we are all one in Christ Jesus, all sons of God and, according to the promise, heirs through faith in Christ Jesus.

units.la: In eadem Epistola ad Romanos alius extat locus illustris & in extinguibilis, cap.8. Quid igitur dicemus? Si Deus pro no-bis, quis contra nos? is quidem qui proprio fi-lio non pepercit, sed tradidit eum pro nobis omnibus; qui non etiam cum eo omnia nobis gratificabitur?
units.tr: In the same Epistle to the Romans there is another famous and unquenchable passage, in chapter 8: What then shall we say? If God is for us, who is against us? He who did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all, will he not also with him freely give us all things?

units.la: Non simpliciter pro omnibus: sed pro nobis omnibus dicit, cum limitatio-ne, pro vt limitatio illa alibi quoque in sacris literis accipitur. Rom.4. Abraham pater est omnium nostrum. Sic Hierusalem illa cœlestis dicitur mater omnium nostrû Gal.4. & 1.Cor.12. ait Apostolus per vnû spiritum nos omnes in vnum corpus baptizatos, siue Judæos siue Græcos, siue seruos, siue liberos, & omnes vna potione potatos in vnum spiritum. Item loco ad Gal. qui modò citatus fuit, omnes vos vnus estis in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: He does not say simply "for all", but "for us all", with a limitation; and such a limitation is also used elsewhere in Holy Scripture. Rom. 4: Abraham is the father of us all. So that heavenly Jerusalem is called the mother of us all in Gal. 4 and 1 Cor. 12, where the Apostle says that by one Spirit we all have been baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free, and have all been made to drink of one Spirit. Likewise in the passage to the Galatians cited just now: you are all one in Christ Jesus.

units.la: Nimirum Ecclesiæ ista vox est, si Deus pro nobis quis contra nos? Obseruat hoc Augustus. ad Laurent. cap. 6r. Quæ, inquit, in hominibus est Ecclesia (quod dicit ad differentiam Ecclesiæ infanctis angelis & virtutibus Dei) ea sanguine Mediatoris nullum habentis peccatum, ab omni redemta est peccato: eiusque vox est: Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? qui filio proprio suo nō pepercit, sed dedit eum pro omnibus nobis. Hanc sententiam alibi, tract. nimirum 45. super Iohan. ex textu duplicater confirmat: ex præcedentibus & consequentibus. Præcedit enim, quos præsciuit, eosdem & prædestinauit: quos prædestinauit, eosdem & vocat &c. De quibus etiam sequitur: Quis intentabit crimina aduersus electos Dei? Deus est, qui iustificat, &c. Quid igitur est, Tradidit eum pro omnibus nobis? Quibus nobis? Præsciis, prædestinatis, iustificatis, glorificatis. Nouit Dominus qui sint eius, ipsæ sunt oues. Aliquando te ipsæ nescitunt, sed Pastor nouit eas: inquit Augustus. citato loco.
units.tr: Surely this is the voice of the Church: If God is for us, who is against us? Augustine observes this in his letter to Laurentius, chapter 6: The Church which is among men (he says this to distinguish it from the Church among the holy angels and the powers of God) has been redeemed from all sin by the blood of the Mediator, who had no sin; and its voice is: If God is for us, who is against us? He who did not spare his own Son, but gave him up for us all. He confirms this sense elsewhere, in his Tractate 45 on John, from the text on two sides: from what precedes and from what follows. For what precedes is: Those whom he foreknew, these he also predestined; those whom he predestined, these he also calls, and so on. Of these it also follows: Who will bring any charge against God's elect? It is God who justifies, and so on. What then is the meaning of he gave him up for us all? For which of us? For those foreknown, predestined, justified, glorified. The Lord knows who are his; they are the sheep. Sometimes they themselves do not know it, but the Shepherd knows them, says Augustine in the place cited.

units.la: Adde, quod pro quibus Christus mortuus est (secundum propositum videvidelicet atque efficaciam) iis etiam aduocatus est,qui interpellare non definit,vt paternæ reconciliationis in eos conferatur gratia magis magisque,eosque vt Ambrosij verbis vtar, sanguinis sui mercè seruat. Quomodo enim poterit damnare quem redemit à morte? pro quo se obtulit? cuius vitâ suæ mortis mercede esse cognoscit? Nonne dicet,quæ vtilitas in sanguine meo, si dano,què ipse saluaui? Quocirca Apostolus: Quis est qui condemnet? Christus is est, qui mortuus est,imo vero qui etiam excitatus est: qui etiam est ad dextram Dei, qui etiam postulat pro nobis. Quis nos separabit a caritate Christi? Num oppressio? num angustia? num persecutio? nu fames? nu nuditas? num periculu? num gladius? Imo in his omnibus plus quam victores sumus, per eum qui dilexit nos,&c. Ita caritas Christi insuperabiles atque inseparabiles facit, hoc est, in finem usque perseuerantes. Nam quid aliud est perseuerare, quam tentatione non vinci? Quare qui ad finem usque perseuerantes seruantur, ij demum delecti & redempti Dei sunt.
units.tr: Add that those for whom Christ died (in the purpose and efficacy of his death) are also those for whom he intercedes, and he never ceases to intercede, so that the grace of the Father's reconciliation may be conferred on them more and more; and, to use the words of Ambrose, he keeps them by the price of his blood. For how can he condemn one whom he has redeemed from death? For whom he offered himself? Whose life he knows to be the reward of his own death? Will he not say: what profit is there in my blood, if I condemn those whom I have saved? Hence the Apostle: Who is it that condemns? Christ is the one who died, or rather who was also raised, who is also at the right hand of God, who also intercedes for us. Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall tribulation? or distress? or persecution? or famine? or nakedness? or peril? or sword? No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us, and so on. Thus the love of Christ makes them unconquerable and inseparable, that is, persevering to the end. For what is perseverance but not being overcome by temptation? Therefore those who are preserved persevering to the end are at last the chosen and redeemed of God.

units.la: Ambrof lib. 1. De Iac. c. 6
units.tr: Ambrose, De Iacob, book 1, chapter 6.

units.la: Rom. 8.
units.tr: Rom. 8.

units.la: Dehinc ad Ephes.5. legimus Christum esse caput Ecclesiæ & seruatorem corporis: dilexisse Ecclesiam, & semetipsum exposuisse pro ea, vt eam sanctificaret, mundans eam lauacro aquæ per verbum, vt eam sibi sisteret gloriosam: id est, non habentem rugam & maculam aut aliquid eiusmodi, sed vt esset sancta & inculpata.
units.tr: Next we read in Ephes. 5. that Christ is the head of the Church and the Saviour of the body; he loved the Church and gave himself up for her, that he might sanctify her, cleansing her by the washing of water with the word, that he might present her to himself in glory, that is, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she might be holy and without blemish.

units.la: Multa hic concurrunt ad sententiam nostram probandam. I. Christus dicitur caput Ecclesiæ: idque non secundum creationem atque eminentiam solummodo, sicut omnis creaturæ caput est: sed ratione peculiari, quatenus Ecclesia corpus ipsius est, & plenitudo eius qui implet omnia in omnibus. Quemadmodum igitur, quæ membra corporis sunt, non autem quæ extra corpus sunt, à capite vegetantur: ita nos qui membra sumus corporis eius, ex carne eius & ossibus eius, spiritum & vitam ex Christo peculiariter haurimus.
units.tr: Many things here combine to prove our view. I. Christ is called the head of the Church, and this not merely by creation and eminence, as every creature has a head, but by a particular relation, inasmuch as the Church is his body and the fullness of him who fills all in all. Just as the members which are of the body, and not those which are outside it, are nourished by the head, so we who are members of his body, of his flesh and of his bones, draw spirit and life from Christ in a special way.

units.la: II. Idem seruator est corporis sui. Nullus enim carnem suam vnquam odio habuit: sed enutrit, ac fouet eam, sicut & Christus Ecclesiam. Recitatur hoc tantanquam documetum singularis ipsius in Ecclesiam amoris, quod nō quadra- ret, si quantum ad gratiam redemtio- nis, nullum esset discrimen inter Eccle- siam & mundum, inter ipsam Christi & ipsam Diaboli: sed omnes æquè per Christum essent saluati, vt volunt disputatores noui.
units.tr: II. Christ is also the preserver of his body. For no one has ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, as Christ does the Church. This is cited as a token of his singular love for the Church, and it would not fit if, as far as the grace of redemption goes, there were no difference between the Church and the world, between Christ's own and the Devil's, but all were equally saved through Christ, as the new disputants wish.

units.la: III. Expresse additum est, quod Christus dilexerit Ecclesiam, & seipsum exposuerit pro ea, vt eam sanctificaret & sibi gloriosam, sine ruga & macula, sanctam & inculpatam. Tantæ gratiæ prærogatiuam Ecclesiæ Apostolus defert: redemtionem inquā, sanctificationem, glorificationem: nec magis in promiscuam hominum colluuiem extra Ecclesiam redemtio & sanctificatio, quā glorificatio, competunt.
units.tr: III. It is expressly added that Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for it, that he might sanctify it and present it to himself glorious, without spot or wrinkle, holy and blameless. The Apostle attributes this privilege of so great grace to the Church: redemption, I say, sanctification, and glorification. Redemption and sanctification, no less than glorification, belong not to the promiscuous mass of men outside the Church.

units.la: Ad Coloss. item perinsignis locus est cap. 1. Gratias agimus patri, qui idoneos fecit nos, ad participandā sortem sanctorum in luce, & liberauit nos è potestate tenebrarum, ac transtulit in regnum filii sui dilecti, in quo habemus redemtionem, nempe remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: There is also a remarkable passage in Colossians, chapter 1: Giving thanks to the Father, who has made us fit to share the inheritance of the saints in light, and has delivered us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, namely the forgiveness of sins.

units.la: Quatuor hîc prædicat, tanquam fidelium propria: fortem sanctorum in luce, liberationem è potestate tenebrarum: translationem in regnum filij Dei, & redemtionem. Si propria hæc sunt fidelium, vti sunt (est enim gratiæ ista descriptio tota fidelibus accommodata) nihil eorum participant infideles. Et sic interpretatur Ambrosius, cuius hæc verba sunt, in Epistolam ad Colossenses: liberati de conditione tenebrarum, hoc est, eruti de inferno, in quo tenebamur à Diabolo, tam ex proprio, quam ex alieno delicto, translati sumus per fidem, in regnum cœleste filij Dei. Nam sine fide Christi, nullus egressus de inferno est. Proinde falluntur & fallunt noui Dogmatistæ, contendentes non eximi quenquam qui sub Diaboli potestate sit, quem Christus è Diaboli potestate non liberauerit, & in regnum suum non assumserit.
units.tr: Here he proclaims four things as the proper possessions of believers: the lot of the saints in light, deliverance from the power of darkness, transfer into the kingdom of the Son of God, and redemption. If these are the proper possessions of believers, as they are (for this description of grace is wholly suited to believers), unbelievers share none of them. So Ambrose interprets, whose words these are, on the Epistle to the Colossians: Freed from the condition of darkness, that is, rescued from hell, in which we were held by the Devil, both through our own sin and through another's, we have been transferred through faith into the heavenly kingdom of the Son of God. For without faith in Christ there is no way out of hell. Therefore the new dogmatists are mistaken, and mislead others, when they contend that no one is rescued who is under the power of the Devil, unless Christ has freed him from the Devil's power and taken him into his kingdom.

units.la: Insuper huc facit quod eodem cap. 1. ad Colossenses scribitur, his verbis: Itaque vos quondam abalienatos & hostes, mente malis operibus intenta, nunc sane reconciliauit in corpore illo carnis sua per mortem, ut sisteret sisteret vos sanctos & inculpatos coram se, si-quidem permanetis in fide fundati & firmi.
units.tr: Moreover, what is written in the same first chapter to the Colossians helps here, in these words: And you, who once were alienated and enemies in mind, engaged in evil works, now indeed he has reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and blameless before him, if indeed you remain grounded and steadfast in the faith.

units.la: Oppositio est duplicis status, incredulitatis & fidei: & incredulitatis quidem status, docente Apostolo, habet abalienationem, & inimicitias cum Deo: Fidei vero, reconciliationem & sanctimoniam. Significanter enim dicit: Nunc sane reconciliauit: ex quo nimirum in Christum credidistis.
units.tr: There is a contrast between two states, of unbelief and of faith. The state of unbelief, as the Apostle teaches, has alienation and enmity with God; the state of faith has reconciliation and holiness. For he says significantly, "Now indeed he has reconciled": namely, since you have believed in Christ.

units.la: In 1. ad Tim. 4. Apostolus scribit, Deum seruatorem omnium hominum: maxime tamen fidelium. Quae sententia subtilissimae breuitatis & validissimi roboris, si tranquillo consideretur intuitu, totam hac de qua agimus controuersiam diluit. Dicendo enim, qui est seruator omnium hominum, confirmauit bonitatem Dei super vniuersos generalem. Sinit enim exoriri solem suum super malos & bonos; & in ipso viuimus, mouemur & sumus. Haec sane communis quaedam salus est omnibus hominibus, imo & pecoribus: sicut dicitur Psal. 36. homines & iumenta saluos facies Domine. A quo enim salus hominis: ab illo salus & pecoris. Nec erubescendũ est hoc de Deo sentire, imò præsumendum & fidendum, cauendumq; ne aliter sentiamus. Qui saluos facit nos, ipse saluum facit equũ nostrum, ouem nostram, & vt ad minima etiam veniamus, gallinam nostram.
units.tr: In 1 Timothy 4 the Apostle writes, God is the Saviour of all men, but especially of believers. This sentence, of most subtle brevity and most powerful strength, if considered with a calm gaze, dissolves the whole controversy we are discussing. For by saying who is the Saviour of all men, he affirmed God's goodness as general over all. He lets his sun rise on the evil and the good, and in him we live, move, and have our being. This is indeed a common salvation for all men, even for beasts, as it is said in Psalm 36: Men and beasts you save, O Lord. For from whom the salvation of man comes, from him also comes the salvation of the beast. Nor should we blush to think this of God; rather we must presume and trust it, and take care not to think otherwise. He who saves us saves also our horse, our sheep, and, to come even to the smallest things, our hen.

units.la: Adijciendo autem maximè fidelium, ostendit esse partem generis humani, quæ interuentu fidei diuinitus inspirate, ad summam atque æternam felicitatem speciali beneficijs prouehatur.
units.tr: But by adding especially of believers, he shows that there is a part of the human race which, through the intervention of faith divinely inspired, is advanced by special benefits to supreme and eternal happiness.

units.la: Hinc etiam Psalmo citato legitur : Filij hominum in vmbra alarũ tuarum sperant: Inebriabuntur pinguedine domus tuæ, & torrente deliciarum tuarum potum dabis eis. Quoniam apud te est fons vitæ, & in lumine tuo videbimus lumen. Protrahe misericordiam tuam ad cognoscentes te, & iustitiam tuam ad rectos corde. Hanc igitur specialem salutem accipiunt qui sperant, non accipiunt, qui desperant: Accipiunt iusti, non accipiunt iniusti & ignorantes Deminum.
units.tr: Hence it is also read in the Psalm cited: "The sons of men hope in the shadow of your wings. They shall be inebriated with the fatness of your house, and you shall give them drink from the torrent of your delights. For with you is the fountain of life, and in your light we shall see light. Extend your mercy to those who know you, and your justice to the upright in heart." Those who hope therefore receive this special salvation; those who despair do not receive it. The righteous receive it; the unrighteous and those who do not know the Lord do not.

units.la: In epistola ad Hebræos, quæ & ipsa à plerisq; veteribus Paulo attribuitur, hæc habemus testimonia inter alia.Cap.
units.tr: In the Epistle to the Hebrews, which also by most of the ancients is attributed to Paul, we have these testimonies, among others. Chap.

units.la: Z ij s.quams.quamuis filius esset, tamen ex ijs quæ passus est, didicit obedientiam, & consecratus (per afflictiones nimirum ut dicitur cap. 2.) author factus est salutis æternæ, omnibus qui ipsi auscultant.
units.tr: Although he was a son, yet he learned obedience from the things which he suffered; and being made perfect (through afflictions, namely, as is said in chapter 2) became the author of eternal salvation to all who obey him.

units.la: Non igitur salus hæc allata est contumacibus & gratiam Christi incredulitate repudiantibus. Cumque salus illa per Christum parta, non sit temporaria & brevis, qualis solet afferri in bello periclitantibus, sed æterna, quomodo damnandorum ea esse dicetur, quorum pars erit, in stagno ignis inextinguibilis?
units.tr: This salvation, then, has not been offered to the stubborn and to those who reject Christ's grace by unbelief. And since that salvation, won through Christ, is not temporary and brief, such as is usually brought to those in peril in war, but eternal, how can it be said to belong to the damned, whose portion will be in the lake of unquenchable fire?

units.la: Sic cap. 9. mentio fit æternæ redemtionis: Per sanguinem proprium, ait Apostolus, ingressus est semel in sacrarium, æternam redemtionem nactus.
units.tr: So in chapter 9 mention is made of eternal redemption: Through his own blood, says the Apostle, he entered once into the sanctuary, having obtained eternal redemption.

units.la: Æterna autem dicitur redemtio: tum quia in æternum erit efficax: tum quia causa æternorum bonorum existit ijs qui eius sunt participes. Utrumque contrarium deprehenderetur in maiore hominum parte, si credentibus & incredulis, seruandis & damnandis communis esset redemtio.
units.tr: Redemption is called eternal both because it will be effective for ever, and because it is the cause of eternal goods for those who partake of it. Both would be found contrary in the greater part of mankind if redemption were common to believers and unbelievers, to the saved and the damned.

units.la: Referantur huc etiam quæ ibidem scsequuntur. Si sanguis taurorum & hircorum, & cinis iuuenca aspergés inquinatos, sanctifi-cat ad carnis puritatem, quanto magis sanguis Christi, qui per spiritum æternum obtulit semetipsum immaculatum Deo, purgabit conscientias vestras a mortuis operibus ad serviendum Deo viuo?
units.tr: Let there also be referred here what follows in the same place: If the blood of bulls and goats, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on the unclean, sanctify to the purity of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purge your consciences from dead works to serve the living God?

units.la: Describitur redemtio per hoc, quod purgat conscientias nostras ab operibus mortuis, ad seruiendum Deo viuo. Ea vero conscientiarum purgatio, & diuina seruitus, fidelium propria est. Per fidem enim corda purificantur: & liberati a peccato iustitiæ mancipamur per eandem fidem.
units.tr: Redemption is described by this: that it purges our consciences from dead works, to serve the living God. This purging of conscience and divine service is proper to believers. For by faith hearts are purified, and being freed from sin we are made servants of righteousness through that same faith.

units.la: Et mox: Itaque ob id noui fœderis mediator est, vt morte intercedente ad redemtionem præuaricationum, vocati promissione accipiant æterna hæreditatis.
units.tr: And soon after: Therefore he is the mediator of a new covenant, so that, death intervening for the redemption of transgressions, those who are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance.

units.la: Qui sunt iusti vocati, quorum est fœdus & redemtio & hæreditas? Respondet pro me scriptor de vocatione gentium lib.1.cap.3. Quoniam, inquit, alij quidem iustificantur fide, alij in sua impietate indurantur, credentium genus a non credentium sub votatorum appellatione discernitur: & qui à fide significantur alieni, ÿ quamuis audiant Euangelium, vocationis huius osten-duntur extranei. Et citat locum 1. Cor. 1. Prædicamus Christum crucifixum, Iudæis quidem scandalum: Græcis vero stultitiam: ipsis vero vocatis, tam Iudæis quàm Græcis, potentiam ac Dei sapientiam. De his vocatis non solùm ex Iudæis, verùm etiam ex gentibus, vide plura Rom. 9. 23. & cap. 8. 28. & sequentibus.
units.tr: Who are the called, to whom belong the covenant, the redemption, and the inheritance? The writer answers for me, concerning the calling of the Gentiles, in book 1, chapter 3: For, he says, some indeed are justified by faith, while others are hardened in their impiety. The race of believers is distinguished from non-believers under the name of the called, and those who are marked off as strangers from faith, though they hear the Gospel, are shown to be strangers to this calling. And he cites 1 Corinthians 1: We preach Christ crucified, to the Jews indeed a scandal, to the Greeks foolishness, but to the called themselves, both Jews and Greeks, the power and wisdom of God. On these called, not only from the Jews but also from the Gentiles, see more at Romans 9:23 and chapter 8:28 and following.

units.la: Neque vero prætereundum hîc est, quod sub finem cap. 9. ad Hebr. scriptum legimus: Christum semel oblatum, vt multorum peccata tolleret.
units.tr: Nor must we pass over here what we read near the end of Hebrews 9: Christ, once offered, to take away the sins of many.

units.la: Per hosce multos iam intelligit vocatos illos, quorum meminerat: Et sic Chrysost. ac Theoph. exponunt. Quare multorum dixit & non omnium? quia neutiquam omnes credunt. Christi quidem mors omnium æquauit perditionem, id est, sat valuit, vt omnes seruarentur, nec tamen omnium aufert peccata: quia reluctantes ipsi plane inutilem sibi ipsis reddunt eius mortem. Meminit Theoph. etiam Basilij in eundem quoque sensum concedentis, cuius didta aliquot supra retuli ad locū Matt. 26.
units.tr: By many he now means those called whom he had mentioned, and so Chrysostom and Theophylact expound it. Why did he say of many and not of all? Because by no means do all believe. Christ's death indeed was equal to the ruin of all, that is, it was sufficient for all to be saved; yet it does not take away the sins of all, because those who resist render his death plainly useless to themselves. Theophylact also mentions Basil conceding the same sense, whose words I have related a few above, at Matthew 26.

units.la: Clarissimè verò omnium Aquinas in hunc locū: Dicit ad multorum exhaurienda peccata, non omnium: quia mors Christi etsi sufficiens sit, pro omnibus, non tamen habet efficaciam nisi quantum ad saluandos. Non enim omnes subiiciuntur ei per fidem & bona opera. Ad extremum, quid potest dici breuius & validius pro tota hac controuersia decidenda, illo Apost. ad Heb. 11. Sine fide impossibile est Deo placere? Aut hoc verum non est: aut falsum est, quod dicant, omnes pęręque credentes ac incredulos, ab omni peccato & condemnatione liberatos, atque in gratiam & sinum patris cœlestis receptos. Quod quid aliud est, quàm omnes Deo placere absque respectu fidei & incredulitatis?
units.tr: Most clearly of all, Aquinas on this passage says: "He says 'of many' to exhaust sins, not of all: because the death of Christ, although it is sufficient for all, has no efficacy except as regards those who are saved. For not all are subjected to him through faith and good works." Finally, what can be said more briefly and more forcefully to settle this whole controversy than that saying of the Apostle in Heb. 11: "Without faith it is impossible to please God"? Either this is not true, or it is false that they say that all, believers and unbelievers alike, are freed from all sin and condemnation and received into grace and the bosom of the heavenly Father. And what is this other than saying that all please God without regard to faith and unbelief?

units.la: CAPVT IV.
units.tr: CHAPTER IV.

units.la: Testimonia ex aliis scriptis noui Testamenti.
units.tr: Testimonies from other writings of the New Testament.

units.la: Ad maiorem rei confirmationem adiciemus & alia quædam dicta aliorum librorum noui testamenti.
units.tr: To confirm the matter further, we shall add some other sayings from the other books of the New Testament.

units.la: In actis cap. 5. Petrus & vniuersum collegium Apostolicum, vnanimiter testantur his verbis: Deus patrum no-strorum excitauit Iesum, eumq; dextrâ sua eueƈtum, constituit principem ac seruatorem, vt det resipiscentiam Israeli & remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: In Acts 5, Peter and the whole apostolic college testify unanimously in these words: "The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree, and God exalted him at his right hand as Prince and Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins."

units.la: Indiuiduo nexu coniunguntur, resi-piscentia & remissio peccatorū. Qua-propter tàm stultum est affirmare omnibus sine discrimine, peccatorum tri-butam remissionem à Christo, quàm si quis contendat, omnibus eundem resi-piscentiam largiri. Quid illud, quod a-perte prærogatiua vtriusque beneficij illius defertur Israeli? cui nã Israeli? Ex Judæis & gentibus, qui secundum pro-positū vocati sunt, ipsi verus sunt Israel, ait Augustinus, de quo etiam dicit Apostolus: Et super Israel Dei.
units.tr: Repentance and forgiveness of sins are joined by an inseparable bond. Therefore it is as foolish to affirm that Christ grants forgiveness of sins to everyone without distinction as it would be to contend that everyone is equally given repentance. What of the fact that the privilege of both these benefits is openly assigned to Israel? For to whom but Israel? "Those from Jews and Gentiles who are called according to his purpose are the true Israel," says Augustine, "of whom the Apostle also says: 'And upon the Israel of God.'"

units.la: Secundo, Petri vox est, & consen-tiens prophetarum omnium testimonium, remissionem peccatorum accipere per nomen Iesu quemuis, qui credit in eum. Act. 10. Huic prophetico & Apostolico consensui, qui summam EuanEuangelij Christi continet, plane contrarium est commentum aduersariorum pseudoeuangelicum, remissionem peccatorum per nomen Christi accipere omnes simpliciter, absque respectu fidei vel incredulitatis.
units.tr: Secondly, it is the voice of Peter, and the agreeing testimony of all the prophets, that through the name of Jesus forgiveness of sins is received by whoever believes in him. Acts 10. To this prophetic and apostolic consensus, which contains the sum of the Gospel of Christ, the pseudo-evangelical invention of our adversaries is plainly contrary: that all people simply receive forgiveness of sins through the name of Christ, without regard to faith or unbelief.

units.la: Adhaec idem Apoft.1.Epist.1. cum de redemtione loquitur per pretiosum sanguinem Christi, tanquam agni immaculati & incontaminati, dicit eum praeordinatum quidem fuisse ante iacta mundi fundamenta, patefactu vero propter credentes.
units.tr: Likewise the same Apostle, in 1 Peter 1, when he speaks of redemption through the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb unblemished and undefiled, says that he was indeed foreordained before the foundation of the world, but revealed for the sake of believers.

units.la: Expresse declarat, mundo seruatorem exhibitum propter credentes. Ergo propter eosdem credentes pari ratione proprie mortuus est & resurrexit: non quia iam credebant, sed vt crederent; & credentes vitam haberent aeternam per nomen eius.
units.tr: He expressly declares that the Saviour was shown to the world for the sake of believers. Therefore, by the same reasoning, he properly died and rose again for those same believers: not because they already believed, but so that they might believe, and that believers might have eternal life through his name.

units.la: Suffragatur his & Ioh. 1.Epist.1. Quod si in luce incedimus, quemadmodum Deus lux est, communionem habemus cum eo, & sanguis Iesu Christi purgat nos ab omni peccato. Si dixerimus nos peccatum non habere, nos ipsos fallimus, & veritas in nobis non est. est. Si confiteamur peccata nostra, iustus est & fidelis, ut remittat nobis peccata nostra, & purget nos ab omni peccato.
units.tr: The first Epistle of John also supports these points: "If we walk in the light, as God is light, we have fellowship with him, and the blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us from all sin. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all sin."

units.la: I. Communio cum Deo non est omnium. Ergo nec gratia Dei: vbi enim gratia Dei, ibi & communio ipsius.
units.tr: I. Communion with God is not for all. Therefore neither is the grace of God, for where the grace of God is, there also is his communion.

units.la: II. Mudatio peccatorum per sanguinem Christi, eorum demum est qui in luce incedunt.
units.tr: II. The cleansing of sins through the blood of Christ belongs only to those who walk in the light.

units.la: III. Peccatorum remissio, quæ ipsissima est propitiatio, Johanne teste, præsupponit confessionem peccatorū, quæ cum omnibus non inst, nec propitiatio omnium est.
units.tr: III. The remission of sins, which is itself propitiation, according to John's testimony, presupposes the confession of sins, and this is not in all; nor is propitiation for all.

units.la: Venio ad Apocalypsin Johannis, in cuius adeo limine dedicatam consecratamque legimus redemtione aureis hisce verbis: Iesus Christus testis ille fidus & primogenitus ex mortuis, dilexit nos & lauit nos a peccatis nostris per sanguinem suum, & fecit nos reges & sacerdotes Deo ac patri suo.
units.tr: I come to the Apocalypse of John, at the very threshold of which we read redemption dedicated and consecrated in these golden words: "Jesus Christ, the faithful witness and firstborn from the dead, loved us and washed us from our sins by his blood, and made us kings and priests to God and his Father."

units.la: Quorum est redemtio, idem reges & sacerdotes sunt Deo patri. Hoc autem credentium est, non incredulorum, teste Petro 1. Epist. 2: vos genus electum, regale sacerdotium, gens sancta, populus pulus quem Deus sibi acquisiuit, vt proprium, vt praedicetis virtutes illius, qui vos vocauit è tenebris in admirabilem suam lucem. Ergo incredauli redemtionis alieni sunt.
units.tr: Those for whom there is redemption are the same kings and priests to God the Father. But this belongs to believers, not to unbelievers, as Peter witnesses in 1 Peter 2:9: "You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people whom God has acquired for his own, that you may proclaim the virtues of him who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light." Therefore unbelievers are strangers to redemption.

units.la: Bene Rupertus Tuitiensis lib.1. comment. in Apoc. Lauit ergo nos, id est omnem Ecclesiam à peccatis nostris. Neque enim eos solu lauit, qui iam credetes erant vel fuerant, sed etiam qui futuri erant: & hos quidem non actu iam tum, sed potestate lauit: quia lauari non poterant, qui nondum nati erant, vel nondum crediderant. Potestatem dedit eis lauari.
units.tr: Rupert of Deutz rightly says in book 1 of his commentary on the Apocalypse: "He washed us, that is, the whole Church, from our sins. For he did not wash only those who were already believing or had believed, but also those who were to be; and these indeed not actually then, but in power, because those who were not yet born or had not yet believed could not be washed. He gave them the power to be washed."

units.la: Similis recurrit locus Apoc. 5. vbi viginti quatuor seniores & quatuor animalia, canticum nouum canunt agno, dicentes: Dignus es qui accipias librum: & sigilla eius aperias: quoniam mactatus es, & redemisti nos Deo per sanguinem tuum, ex omni tribu & lingua & populo & natione, & fecisti nos Deo nostro reges & sacerdotes, & regnabimus super terram.
units.tr: A similar passage recurs in Revelation 5, where the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures sing a new song to the Lamb, saying: "You are worthy to take the book and to open its seals, for you were slain and have redeemed us to God by your blood, out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation, and have made us kings and priests to our God, and we shall reign upon the earth."

units.la: Hic per XXIV seniores & IV animalia, vniuersa hominum Ecclesia, Catholica dicta, intelligitur, quod partim ex verbis illis, ex omni tribu & lingua, & populo populo & natione, partim ex filo totius capitis videre est. Triplex quippe chorus siue exercitus eo capite introducitur pro Agni benedictione. Primus chorus est vniuersa hominum Ecclesia, per seniores & animalia, vt dixi, repraesentata. Secundus beatorum angelorum. Tertius denique reliquae creaturae in coelo super terram & sub terra. Hinc ita colligo: Ecclesiae, quae ex vniuerso genere humano colligitur, proprium est canticum hoc nouum, Mactatus es & redemisti nos. Nam in duobus quae sequuntur, multitudinis angelorum & omnis creaturae, testimoniis, formula illa de industria non seruata est. Ergo sola hominum Ecclesia sanguine Christi redemta est. Argumentum est Ruperti in hunc ipsum locum.
units.tr: Here, through the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures, the whole human Church, called Catholic, is understood. This can be seen partly from those words, "out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation," and partly from the thread of the whole chapter. For a threefold choir or army is introduced in that chapter for the blessing of the Lamb. The first choir is the whole Church of men, represented, as I have said, by the elders and the living creatures. The second is that of the blessed angels. The third, finally, is the rest of creation in heaven, on earth and under the earth. Hence I conclude thus: this new song, "you were slain and have redeemed us," belongs to the Church, which is gathered from the whole human race. For in the two testimonies that follow, of the multitude of angels and of all creation, that formula was deliberately not kept. Therefore the Church of men alone has been redeemed by the blood of Christ. This is Rupert's argument on this very passage.

units.la: Concurrunt & alia, vt quod redemti sanguine Christi, Deo suo facti sunt reges & sacerdotes: de quo paulo ante dictum est. Quod item regnabunt super terram: terram nempe viuentium: sicut quondam Cananaeis & Amorraeis propter peccata sua eiectis, Israelitae regnaregnarunt super terram promissionis' Hoc vero regnum in vera terra promissionis, scimus no fore omnium sed electorum duntaxat, quibus profitebitur filius hominis cum venerit in gloria sua: venite benedicti, possidete regnum, paratum vobis ante iacta mundi fundamenta.
units.tr: Other things also agree: that, redeemed by the blood of Christ, they were made kings and priests to their God, which was said a little before; and likewise that they will reign upon the earth, the land of the living, just as the Israelites once reigned over the land of promise after the Canaanites and Amorites had been cast out for their sins. But we know that this kingdom in the true land of promise will not belong to all, but to the elect alone, to whom the Son of Man will declare when he comes in his glory: "Come, blessed ones, possess the kingdom prepared for you before the foundation of the world."

units.la: CAPVT V. Testimonia ex lege & Prophetis.
units.tr: CHAPTER V. Testimonies from the Law and the Prophets.

units.la: IAM & veteris instrumenti paginae plenae sunt testimoniorum de gratia Seruatoris credentium propria, & eatenus vniuersali, quatenus in omni gente & tribu suos ille habet, qui ipsum timeant & operentur iustitiam.
units.tr: Now the pages of the Old Testament are also full of testimonies concerning the grace of the Saviour. This grace is proper to believers, and in that sense universal, in that he has his own in every nation and tribe, those who fear him and work righteousness.

units.la: Huc in primis spectat promissio Abrahae facta & semini ipsius Genes. 12. & 22. In semine tuo benedicentur omnes Gentes terrae.
units.tr: Here the promise made to Abraham and to his seed chiefly applies: Gen. 12 and 22. In your seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed.

units.la: Certum est, qui Abrahae semen non sunt, extraneos censeri a benedictione Abrahae. Multi autem in genere humano, & nominatim increduli, no sunt semen Abrahæ. Igitur extranei sunt à benedictione Abrahæ.
units.tr: It is certain that those who are not Abraham's seed are reckoned strangers to the blessing of Abraham. Many in the human race, and unbelievers in particular, are not Abraham's seed. Therefore they are strangers to the blessing of Abraham.

units.la: Minorem Paulus sepissimè probat. Manifestè enim Rom.9. docet, in hoc semine non omnes Abrahæ posteros, multò minus quicunque ex Adamo propagati sunt, sed filios duntaxat promissionis censeri. Et cap. 4. eiusdem Epistolæ, totum hoc semen refert ad credentes ex Iudæis & Gentibus. Verba eius sunt: propterea ex fide est hæreditas, ut firma sit promissio toti semini, id est, non solum ei quod est ex lege, verùm etiam ei quod est ex fide Abraham, qui est pater omnium nostrum: pater videlicet omnium credentium in præputio, & pater circumcisionis, iis videlicet, qui non solum sunt ex circumcisione, sed qui etiam incedunt vestigiis fidei patris nostri Abraham, quæ fuit in præputio. Similiter ad Gal.3. declarat, qui ex fide sunt benedici cum fideli illo Abraham: eo quod Scriptura prouidens Deum ex fide iustificaturum Gentes ante euangelizauit Abrahæ, benedicentur in te omnes gentes. Vnde etiam fidelibus ibi dicit: omnes vos
units.tr: Paul very often proves the minor premise. For in Romans 9 he plainly teaches that not all Abraham's posterity belong to this seed, much less all who are descended from Adam, but only the children of the promise are reckoned as seed. And in chapter 4 of the same Epistle he refers this whole seed to believers from among both Jews and Gentiles. His words are: therefore it is by faith, that the inheritance may be sure to all the seed, not only to that which is of the law, but also to that which is of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all: that is, the father of all believers in uncircumcision, and the father of circumcision, that is, of those who are not only of the circumcision but who also walk in the steps of the faith of our father Abraham, which he had in uncircumcision. Similarly, in Galatians 3 he declares that those who are of faith are blessed with that faithful Abraham, since the Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham: in you shall all the nations be blessed. Hence he also says there to the faithful: you all

units.la: » Marginal reference marks only. vos vnus estis in Christo Iesu: Si autem Christi estis, nepe Abrahæ femen estis, & fecundum promissionem hæredes. Vide etiamverf. 14. eiusdem capitis.
units.tr: » Marginal reference marks only. you are one in Christ Jesus. If, however, you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise. See also verse 14 of the same chapter.

units.la: Ex prophetis Iefaias cap. 53. quo paf- fionis Dominicæ non vlum tantum, verùm etiam historiam ita euidenter describit, vt Euangelistam magis quàm Prophetam agere videatur, idem con- firmat inquiens: omnes sicut oues erraui- mus, vnusquisque ad viam suam declinauit: Dominus coniecit in eum iniquitatem omni- um nostrum.
units.tr: From the prophets, Isaiah, chapter 53, describes the Lord's passion not only in its meaning but also in its history so clearly that he seems to act more as an evangelist than as a prophet. He confirms this, saying: we all like sheep have gone astray, each has turned to his own way: the Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all.

units.la: Cum limitatione id dictum est, tan- quam de vniuersitate fidelium, eo lo- quutionis genere, quo Abraham vo- catur pater omnium nostrum, itemq; sub- limis illa Hierusalem mater omnium nostrum: nempe credentium. Ac ne quis dubitandi locus relinquatur, ad- iuxit Propheta, propter prævaricationē po- puli mei plaga eifuit. Item, scientia fui iusti- ficabit iustus seruus meus multos, & iniqui- tates eorum ipse portabit: Et mox: peccata multorum tulit.
units.tr: This was said with a qualification, as concerning the whole body of believers, by that manner of speaking by which Abraham is called the father of us all, and likewise that lofty Jerusalem is called the mother of us all, namely of believers. And lest there be any room left for doubt, the prophet added: for the transgression of my people was he stricken. Likewise: by his knowledge my righteous servant shall justify many, and he shall bear their iniquities. And soon after: he bore the sins of many.

units.la: Expressè testatur Dominicæ passio- tionis fructum, iustitiam inquam & redemptionem, non omnium promiscue sed multorum esse, nempe credentium.
units.tr: He expressly testifies that the fruit of the Lord's passion, namely righteousness and redemption, belongs not to all indiscriminately but to many, that is, to believers.

units.la: Quemadmodum etiam Petrus Galatinus optime in ea Ief. verba scriptum reliquit de arcanis catholicae veritatis lib. 8. cap.14. Licet, inquit, passio Christi ad delenda omnium peccata sufficiens esse debebat, no tamen omnium peccata deletura erat: sed eorum duntaxat, qui in eum credituri essent, atque poenitentiam acturi. Eam ob rem dicit, Et ipse peccata multorum tulit. Lutherus quoq; in 53. Ief. in illud: Seruus meus iustus cognitione sui &c. definit iustitiam Christianam nihil aliud esse, quam cognoscere Christum, & hanc solam esse rationem liberationis a morte & a peccatis: hanc cognitionem liberare, nullumque aliud esse solatium. Error igitur est, liberationem a peccatis & morte omnibus simpliciter hominibus vendicare.
units.tr: As Peter Galatinus also wrote well on these words of Isaiah, in On the Secrets of Catholic Truth, book 8, chapter 14: "Although the passion of Christ ought to have been sufficient to blot out the sins of all, yet it was not going to blot out the sins of all, but only of those who were going to believe in him and to repent. For this reason it says: and he bore the sins of many." Luther too, on Isaiah 53, on the words: my righteous servant by his knowledge etc., defines Christian righteousness as nothing other than knowing Christ, and says that this is the only way of deliverance from death and sins; this knowledge delivers, and there is no other comfort. It is therefore an error to claim deliverance from sins and death simply for all men.

units.la: Idem liquidò apparet ex formula noui foederis Ierem.31. & Hebr.8. Ecce dies venient, dicit Dominus, cum pangam cum domo Israel & cum domo Iuda foedus nouum, non secundum fœdus quod pepigi cum patri-bus eorum, cum educerem eos e terra Aegypti, sed istud est fœdus quod feriam cum domo Israel, post dies illos, dicit Dominus: Indam leges meas in mente eorum & cordi eorum inscri-bam eas, & ero eorum Deus, & ipsi erunt mihi populus, neque docebunt singuli proximum suum dicendo, cognosce Dominum. Nam omnes cognoscent me, a pusillo ad magnum inter eos: & propitius ero iniquitatibus & peccatis eorum, & iniquitatum ipsorum non recordabor amplius.
units.tr: The same thing is clearly evident from the formula of the new covenant in Jeremiah 31 and Hebrews 8: Behold, the days come, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah, not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers, when I led them out of the land of Egypt, but this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their mind and write them on their heart, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people, and they shall not teach each his neighbour, saying, know the Lord. For all shall know me, from the least to the greatest among them: and I will be merciful to their iniquities and sins, and I will remember their iniquities no more.

units.la: Hinc videmus remissionem peccatorum, quæ fit morte Mediatoris interveniente, beneficium esse novi fœderis. Ex quo sequitur, ad filios dunta-xat fœderis pertinere. Iam autem non omnes esse filios fœderis, primum ex eo liquet, quod promissiones hæ, Indā leges meas mentibus ipsorum: ero ipsis Deus, & ipsi erunt mihi populus: omnes cognoscunt me, non simpliciter quadrant in hominum universitatem. Deinde quia apertè dicitur fœdus hoc pangi cum domo Israel, & cum domo Iuda: id quod de Ecclesia ex Iudæis & Gentibus, vero illo Juda & Israël, intelligédum est, de quo etiam Apostolus dicit, Omnes vos vnus estis in Christo Iesu: ac quoniam Christi estis, Abrahæ semen estis, & secundum promissionem hæredes.
units.tr: From this we see that the forgiveness of sins, which comes through the intervention of the death of the Mediator, is a benefit of the new covenant. It follows that it pertains only to the children of the covenant. That not all are children of the covenant is first clear from the fact that these promises, I will put my laws in their minds, I will be their God and they shall be my people, all know me, do not simply fit the whole body of mankind. Second, because it is plainly said that this covenant is made with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah, which must be understood of the Church from Jews and Gentiles, the true Judah and Israel, of whom the Apostle also says: you all are one in Christ Jesus; and since you are Christ's, you are Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise.

units.la: Similis est promissio Ier.23.&33. Ecce dies venient, dicit Dominus, & suscitabo Dauid germen iustum, & regnabit Rex, in cuius diebus salvus erit Israël, & Iuda habitabit confidenter.
units.tr: Similar is the promise in Jeremiah 23 and 33: Behold, the days come, says the Lord, and I will raise up for David a righteous branch, and a King shall reign, in whose days Israel shall be saved, and Judah shall dwell securely.

units.la: Videmus & hic redemtionem Messiæ populo ipsius peculiariter attribu-tam: quia, teste Angelo Gabriele, regnat super domum Jacob, id est, Ecclesiam, & regni atque pacis eius non erit finis.
units.tr: Here too we see that the redemption by the Messiah is attributed peculiarly to his people: because, as the angel Gabriel bears witness, he reigns over the house of Jacob, that is, the Church, and of his kingdom and peace there will be no end.

units.la: Passim quoque apud Prophetas, cum de aduentu redemtoris, déque salute per ipsum præstanda vaticinantur, sermo promissionis peculiariter ad Ecclesiam dirigitur nomine Sionis: vt Zachariæ 2. Gaude & lætare filia Sion, quia ego veniam & habitabo in medio tui, dicit Dominus: & congregabuntur Gentes multæ die illo, eruntq; mihi in populum, & habitabo in medio tui: & possidebit Dominus Iudam partem suam suam in terra sanctia, & eliget adhuc Ierusalem. Hoc de Ecclesia undique collecta intelligendum esse, dubitare nos non sinunt ea quæ 2.Corin.6.v.16.& Apocal. 21.v.2. legimus.
units.tr: Everywhere also among the prophets, when they prophesy about the coming of the Redeemer and about the salvation to be brought about through him, the promise is directed peculiarly to the Church under the name of Zion, as in Zechariah 2: Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Zion, for behold, I am coming and I will dwell in your midst, says the Lord; and many nations shall be joined to the Lord in that day, and they shall be my people, and I will dwell in your midst; and the Lord shall inherit Judah as his portion in the holy land, and he shall again choose Jerusalem. That this must be understood of the Church gathered from every quarter, the passages we read in 2 Corinthians 6:16 and Revelation 21:2 do not allow us to doubt.

units.la: Et Capite 9. apud eundem Prophetam est, Exulta valde filia Sion, iubila filia Ierusalem: Ecce rex tuos venit TIBI, iustus & Seruator, pauper, equitans super asinum, & loquetur pacem Gentibus, & dominium eius erit a mari ad mare: & a fluuio usque ad terminos terræ. Vniuerso quippe orbe terrarum diffusa est Catholica Ecclesia Christi, qui, ut Paulus testis est, pax nostra est, & utraque (Iudæos & Gentes) fecit vnum, inimicitiis per carnem abrogatis, vt duos conderet in semetipso in vnum hominem, & reconciliauit vtrosque in vno corpore, Deo per crucem, interemtis inimicitiis per eam: & veniens euangelizauit pacem, & iis qui procul & iis qui prope erant.
units.tr: And in chapter 9 of the same prophet: Exult greatly, daughter of Zion, shout, daughter of Jerusalem: behold, your king comes to you, righteous and a Saviour, poor, riding on an ass, and he shall speak peace to the nations, and his dominion shall be from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth. For the Catholic Church of Christ is spread over the whole world; Christ, as Paul bears witness, is our peace, and he has made both (Jews and Gentiles) one, abolishing enmities in his flesh, so that he might create the two in himself into one man, and reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, having slain the enmities by it; and coming he preached peace to those who were far off and to those who were near.

units.la: Similiter habet verbum promissionis Iesai.62. Ecce Dominus pronunciat usque ad extremum terræ: dicite filiæ Sion, Ecce salus tua veniet: Ecce merces eius cum eo, & opus eius coram illo, vocabuntq; eos populum sanctum, redemtos Domini, Tu autem vocaberis requisita: ciuitas non derelicta.
units.tr: Similarly, the word of promise in Isaiah 62 reads: Behold, the Lord proclaims to the end of the earth: say to the daughter of Zion, behold, your salvation will come; behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him; and they shall call them the holy people, the redeemed of the Lord; and you shall be called Sought-out, a city not forsaken.

units.la: Quæ est ista ciuitas, nisi sublimis illa Ierusalem quæ est mater omnium nostrum? Scriptum est enim: Lætare sterilis, quæ non paris: erumpe & clama, quæ non parturis, quoniam plures sunt liberi deserta, quam eius quæ virum habet. Ad quem modum etiam ea ipsa ciuitas Dei, spiritualis Sion & Ierusalem, cum filiis suis vbique Gentium diffusis, gloriose describitur Psal. 87. Atque hi sunt de quibus sermo Propheticus hic ait, vocabunt eos populum sanctum, redemtos Domini. Quapropter tantæ dignitatis prærogatiua, cum filiorum Ecclesiæ & domesticorum Dei propria sit, iniuria ad eos qui foris sunt extenditur.
units.tr: What is this city, if not that lofty Jerusalem which is the mother of us all? For it is written: Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not; break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for the desolate hath more children than she which hath an husband. In much the same way, that very city of God, the spiritual Zion and Jerusalem, with her sons scattered everywhere among the Gentiles, is gloriously described in Psalm 87. And these are the ones of whom the prophetic word here speaks: "They shall call them the holy people, the redeemed of the Lord." Wherefore, since this so great a privilege of dignity belongs properly to the sons of the Church and to the household of God, it is wrongly extended to those who are outside.

units.la: Sed ne longius eamus, certum est, referente Petro, omnes Prophetas testari, quod remissionem peccatorum accipiat, per nomen Iesu, quisquis crediderit in eum. Et Paulo affirmante, testimonio legis & Prophetarum comprobatur iustitia Dei, iustitia inquam Dei in omnes & super omnes, qui credunt. Iam vero iustitia illa Dei, & peccatorum remissio, ipsissima est redemtio,Coloss.1. Quapropter vnanimi Prophetarum omnium consensu, redemtio credentium propria est, nec quicquam ad incredulos pertinet.
units.tr: But, not to go further afield: it is certain, as Peter bears witness, that all the Prophets testify that whoever believes in Jesus receives remission of sins through his name. And, as Paul affirms, the righteousness of God is confirmed by the testimony of the Law and the Prophets: the righteousness of God, I say, toward all and upon all who believe. Now that righteousness of God and the remission of sins are indeed the very same thing as redemption (Col. 1). Wherefore, by the unanimous consent of all the Prophets, the redemption belongs properly to believers, and nothing of it pertains to unbelievers.

units.la: CAPVT VI. Idem typis quibusdam veteris Testamenti probatur.
units.tr: CHAPTER VI. The same is proved from certain types of the Old Testament.

units.la: TANTVM adiiciam typica quaedam veteris Testamenti, quibus iam olim id ipsum declaratum fuit. Ac principio satis constat, redemtione populi Israelitici ex Ægypto, & post ex captiuitate Babylonica, velut vmbras quasdam & figuras fuisse verę huius redetionis & gratię perChristū factæ, sicut hic illic apud Prophetas videre est. Quàm igitur Ægyptij cum principe suo pereuntes diuersi erant a filiis Israel sacro sanguine agni postes suos signantibus atque euadentibus, tàm sanè diuersus est mundus infidelium a mundo seu populo fidelium, vt cum rege suo, principe tene-
units.tr: I will add only some typological passages of the Old Testament, by which this same thing was already declared long ago. First, it is quite clear that the redemption of the Israelite people from Egypt, and afterwards from the Babylonian captivity, were like shadows and figures of the true redemption and grace made through Christ, as can be seen here and there in the Prophets. Just as the Egyptians, perishing with their prince, were as unlike the sons of Israel, who marked their doorposts with the sacred blood of the lamb and so escaped, as they were, so truly is the world of unbelievers different from the world or people of believers, so that with their king, the prince of darkness, they will sink into the depths of hell more quickly than redemption through Christ, the true Lamb of God, will profit them at all.

units.la: Aa iij brabrarum Diabolo citius in profundum inferni demergatur, quàm quicquam ei prosit redetio per Christum,verum illum agnum Dei. Quemadmodum item redemtor Israelis seruum suum Iacob & semen Abrahami apprehendit, reduxitque e Babel in terram maiorum suorum, Ægyptiis & Æthiopibus aliisq; impiis populis quasi in precium datis pro redetione populi Dei: Ita Dominus est cum Ecclesia, vt salua faciat eam, manente turbine qui imminet super caput impiorum.
