units.tr: Just as the Redeemer of Israel took hold of his servant Jacob and the seed of Abraham and led them back from Babel into the land of their fathers, giving the Egyptians, Ethiopians and other impious peoples, as it were, as a price paid for the redemption of the people of God, so the Lord is with the Church to save her, while the whirlwind that hangs over the heads of the impious remains.

units.la: Deinde in deserto contra serpentes ignitos vnicum erat remedium serpens æneus iussu Dei erectus à Mose, vt quisquis eum aspiceret non moreretur, sed viueret: idque non propter rem visam sed propter Deum omnium seruatorem, cuius verbum sanabat, secundum declarationem Sapientis. Sicut ergo ibi percussi à serpentibus non viuebant, nisi signum salutis aspicerent; ita crux Christi redemtio & vita est in ipsum credentibus, non autem increduus. Atque hoc est quod Christus ipseipsemet de se perhibet Ioh.3. Sicut Moses extulit serpentem in deserto : ita extolli oportet filium hominis, ut quisquis credit in eum non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam.
units.tr: Then in the desert, against the fiery serpents, the only remedy was the bronze serpent, raised by Moses at God's command, so that whoever looked upon it would not die but live; and this was not because of the thing seen but because of God, the saviour of all, whose word healed, according to the testimony of the Wise Man. Just as those bitten by the serpents there did not live unless they looked upon the sign of salvation, so the cross of Christ is redemption and life to those who believe in him, but not to the unbelieving. This is what Christ himself says of himself, John 3: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.

units.la: Erat etiam apud Iudaeos generalis omnium seruorum liberatio anno Jubilaeo : quatenus quidem lex libertatis copia omnibus Hebraeis faciebat. Verum, ut tu oblatae liberratis efficacia non sentiebat, qui vltro in seruitute manebant: ita efficacia redemptionis Christi non sentiunt, qui mudo addicti manet. Hanc figuram Ambrosius edisserens lib. 1. Epist. 1. eleganter ait: Qui verus est liber, Hebraeus verus, totus est Dei totum quod habet libertatis est: nihil habet illius, qui libertatem recusat dicens, diligo Dominum meum & uxorem, & infantes, non abibo liber.
units.tr: Among the Jews there was also a general liberation of all slaves in the Jubilee year, inasmuch as the law of liberty made it available to all Hebrews. But just as those who willingly remained in servitude did not feel the efficacy of the offered liberty, so those who are bound to the world do not feel the efficacy of the redemption of Christ. Ambrose, expounding this figure in book 1, Epistle 1, says elegantly: He who is truly free, the true Hebrew, is wholly God's; all that he has belongs to liberty. He has nothing of that man who refuses liberty, saying, I love my master and my wife and my children; I will not go out free.

units.la: Huc eode spectat hircus emissarius Leu.16. in cuius caput Pontifex quotannis imprecari consueuerat omnes iniquitates filiorum Israel, & vniuersa delicta atque peccata eorum : atque ita emittebat illum in desertu, & portabat ille omnes iniquitates filiorum Israel.
units.tr: To the same point belongs the scapegoat of Leviticus 16, upon whose head the High Priest used each year to lay all the iniquities of the sons of Israel and all their transgressions and sins; and so he sent it away into the wilderness, and that goat bore all the iniquities of the sons of Israel.

units.la: Si haec figura erat venturi Christi, futuræ per ipsum expiationis, uti verè erat, necesse est fateamur, Christum proprie expiare peccara populi sui, quemadmodum hircus ille proprie destinatus erat populo Dei, filijs Israël, ad expiandum omnes iniquitates ipsorum. Hinc & ad Hebræos 2. vocatur misericors & fidelis Pontifex ad expiandum peccata populi; Et cap. 13. ait Apostolus, respiciens ad totum illud legale sacrificium, Et Iesum passum esse extra portam ut sanctificaret populum per sanguinem suum: adeo ut confidenti animo dicamus, nos qui populus ipsius sumus: peccata nostra pertulit in corpore suo super lignum & vibicibus eius sanati sumus, 1.Pet. 2.
units.tr: If this was a figure of the coming Christ and of the expiation to be made through him, as it truly was, we must necessarily confess that Christ truly expiates the sins of his people, just as that goat was truly appointed for the people of God, the sons of Israel, to expiate all their iniquities. Hence also in Hebrews 2 he is called a merciful and faithful High Priest to expiate the sins of the people; and in chapter 13 the Apostle, looking back to that whole legal sacrificial system, says that Jesus also suffered outside the gate, that he might sanctify the people through his own blood. So confidently may we say, we who are his people: he himself bore our sins in his body upon the tree, and by his wounds we have been healed, 1 Peter 2.

units.la: Concludentes itaque primam classem argumentorum, affirmamus, credimus & confitemur, Seruatore mundo promissum, Christum Dei, per os omnium sanctorum Prophetarum & Apostolorum semper in Ecclesia annunciatum: propositum à patre propitiationem per fidem in sanguine ipsius, in omnes & super omnes qui credunt: hoc beneficium instaurationis & redemptionis generis humani, licet Ecclesiae, quantum ad efficaciā proprii & peculiare sit, vniuersale tamen esse, eo prorsus sensu, quo & sancta Christi Ecclesia credimus & confitemur vniuersalem.
units.tr: Concluding, therefore, the first class of arguments, we affirm, believe and confess that Christ, God's Saviour of the world, promised through the mouth of all the holy Prophets and Apostles, has always been announced in the Church; that he was set forth by the Father as a propitiation through faith in his blood, for all and upon all who believe. This benefit of the restoration and redemption of the human race, although as to its efficacy it is proper and peculiar to the Church, is nonetheless universal, in exactly the sense in which we believe and confess the holy Church of Christ to be universal.

units.la: CAPUT VII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VII.

units.la: De altera classe probationum.
units.tr: On the second class of proofs.

units.la: I N hac classe vtemur argumentis ex analogia fidei exstructis: & primum à definitione argumentor.
units.tr: In this class I shall use arguments built from the analogy of faith, and first I argue from the definition.

units.la: Iustificatio credentium est, non incredulorum.
units.tr: Justification belongs to believers, not to unbelievers.

units.la: Idem autem est Redemtio quod iustificatio. Ergo Redemtio credentium est, non incredulorum.
units.tr: Redemption is the same as justification. Therefore redemption belongs to believers, not to unbelievers.

units.la: Assumtio probatur ex Paulo Eph.1. & Coloss.1. vbi redemtionem definit remissionem peccatorum. Alibi vero, nepe ad Rom.4. in peccatorum remissione sitam esse vult iustificationem hominis coram Deo, allegans illud Psalmi, Beati quorum remissae sunt iniquitates & quorum tecta sunt peccata.
units.tr: The minor premise is proved from Paul, Eph. 1. and Col. 1., where he defines redemption as the remission of sins. Elsewhere, namely at Rom. 4., he holds that man's justification before God lies in the remission of sins, citing the psalm: Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven and whose sins are covered.

units.la: Maior est dogma Apostoli, multis expoexpositum & ftabilitu ad Rom.3. 4. & 5. captitibus.ad Gal.item 2. & 3. hominem vi-delicet iustificari per fidem in Iesum Christum. Cui doctrinae nihil magis contrarium est, quam fingere iustificationem tam generalem, & late patentem, quam generalis est & patet condemnatio,in omnes & super omnes simpliciter homines. De verbis autem ad Rom.5.supra responsum est, ne quis ea putet obiici posse ad tuendam generalem eiusmodi iustificationem, quam etiam in eum ipsum locum Ambrosius aperte reiicit, & exponit,in omnes homines gratiam redundare ad iustificationem vitae, quantum ad credentes, quorum propria quaedam est vniuersitas Christo subiecta,& gratiae ipsius participeps, non minus quam vniuersitas generis humani ex Adamo peccatum & mortem trahit.
units.tr: The major premise is the doctrine of the Apostle, set out and established at length in Rom. 3, 4 and 5, and also Gal. 2 and 3: namely, that man is justified through faith in Jesus Christ. Nothing is more contrary to this doctrine than to imagine a justification as general and far-reaching as condemnation is general and far-reaching, extending to all men and over all men simply. As for the words at Rom. 5, a reply was given above, lest anyone think they can be brought forward to defend a general justification of this kind. Ambrose also openly rejects this view at that very passage and explains that grace overflows to all men unto justification of life, as far as believers are concerned, who have a peculiar unity of their own, subject to Christ and sharing in his grace, just as the whole human race draws sin and death from Adam.

units.la: II. argumentum: Extra Ecclesiam non est remissio peccatorum. Ergo nec redemtio, quam Paulus,ut dixi, peccatorum definit remissionem.
units.tr: Second argument: outside the Church there is no remission of sins. Therefore neither is there redemption, which Paul, as I have said, defines as the remission of sins.

units.la: Antecedens probat Augustinus in priPrimam Epist.Ioh.tract. ultimo inquiens, Vbi remissio peccatorum, ibi Ecclesia. Atque inde ibidem colligit contra Donatistas Ecclesiam in Africæ parte concludentes: eo quòd remissio peccatorum in nouo testamento per omnes gentes diffusa sit, incipiendo ab Ierusalem, etiam Ecclesiam Christi toto orbe diffusam: Hæc quippe est catholica Ecclesia, id est populus Dei per omnes gentes, adiunctis atque annumeratis omnibus sanctis, qui Christum nascedi tempore præuenerunt, eidem tamen corpori, cuius ille caput est, cohærentes, credentes in eum qui prænunciabatur; vt idem scribit cap.3. de Catechizandis rudibus.
units.tr: Augustine proves the antecedent in his first Epistle of John, tractate last, saying: Where there is remission of sins, there is the Church. From this he draws the conclusion in the same place against the Donatists, who confined the Church to a part of Africa: since the remission of sins in the New Testament has spread through all nations, beginning from Jerusalem, the Church of Christ is also spread throughout the whole world. For this is the catholic Church, that is, the people of God among all nations, including and counting all the saints who came before the time of Christ's birth, yet cohering with the same body of which he is the head, believing in him who was foretold; as he writes in chapter 3 of On Catechizing the Uninstructed.

units.la: Eadem hîc valet illatio. Si redemtio tàm est vniuersalis, vt secundum aduersarios verè & indubitater omnes simul ab omni peccato & condemnatione liberentur, omnes igitur sint aut fuerint quandoque Ecclesia necesse est. Quo quid absurdius? Ecclesia enim sunt selecti è mundo: nati ex Deo: superstructi super fundamentum Prophetarum & & Apostolorum, ædificati super Petrã: oues Christi vocem audientes. Discri-men igitur est huius mundi, & Ecclesiæ in mundo :¦ quemadmodum & Bren-tius bene monet in Catechismo, explicas articulum: Credo sanctam Ecclesiam. Sunt inquit, quisentiant vniuersum mundum, seu omnes homines in mundo esse populum Dei: & Ecclesiam κυριακὴν: sed articulus fidei docet nos, quod non vniuersus mundus sit Ecclesia, & quod non omnes homines sint populus Dei electus: sed quod inter omnes homines in hoc mundo sit populus Dei, dispersus quidē iuxta externam conuersationem, congregatus autem per idem Euangelium in vna fide. Et sicut vniuersus mundus non est Ecclesia Dei: ita nec tota aliqua ciuitas aut pagus, sed in ciuitatibus aut pagis habet Dominus suam Ecclesiam. Hæc ille. Quibuscum quàm belle consentiat Huberus, alioquin Brentiani dogmatis assecla, ipse videbit. Nam parum aut nihil abest, quin omnes homines simul statuat electos Dei, & populum & regnum ipsius, ac proindeEcclesiam. Qui in hac vita regnum Christi, regnumque cœlorum Eccle-
units.tr: The same inference holds here. If redemption is so universal that, according to our opponents, all men are truly and undoubtedly freed together from all sin and condemnation, then all men must necessarily be, or at some time have been, the Church. What could be more absurd? For the Church are those chosen out of the world, born of God, built upon the foundation of the Prophets and Apostles, built upon Peter, the sheep who hear the voice of Christ. There is therefore a difference between the world and the Church in the world, as Brenz rightly warns in his Catechism, explaining the article: I believe the holy Church. Some, he says, think that the whole world, or all men in the world, are the people of God and the Church of the Lord; but the article of faith teaches us that the whole world is not the Church, and that not all men are the chosen people of God; rather, among all men in this world there is the people of God, scattered indeed according to outward conduct, but gathered together in one faith by the same Gospel. And just as the whole world is not the Church of God, so neither is any whole city or village; but the Lord has his Church in cities or villages. So far Brenz. How well Huber, otherwise a follower of Brenz's doctrine, agrees with these views, he himself will see. For he comes very close to deciding that all men together are the chosen of God, and the people and kingdom of God, and therefore the Church. He who in this life [calls] the kingdom of Christ and the kingdom of heaven the Church-

units.la: Thef.1. Ecclesia est, vt multis docet Augustinus de ciuitate Dei lib.20. cap.9.
units.tr: Thesis 1. The Church is, as Augustine teaches in many places, City of God, book 20, chapter 9.

units.la: II. argumentum : Redemti noti sunt & placent Deo, saltem pro tempore & statu redemtionis. At damnandis profitebitur Dominus. Matth. 7. nunquam noui vos: discedite a me omnes, qui operamini iniquitatem. Signanter dicit, nunquam. Sciendum autem, vt Chrysostomus monet, quod tales nesciat Dominus, non quod omnino ipsos non cognoscat qui omnium cognitor est, sed quod suos illos esse non cognoscat, nec diligat eos, quomodo Dominus dicitur nosse, id est, diligere & approbare viam iustorum Psal. 2. Ergo damnandi proprie non sunt ex numero redemtorum Christi.
units.tr: Third argument: the redeemed are known to God and pleasing to him, at least for the time and state of redemption. But the Lord will profess to the damned: Matth. 7. I never knew you; depart from me, all you who work iniquity. He says deliberately "never." But it must be understood, as Chrysostom warns, that the Lord does not know such people not because he altogether fails to know them, since he is the knower of all, but because he does not recognise them as his own, nor love them. In this way the Lord is said "to know," that is, to love and approve the way of the righteous, Psal. 2. Therefore the damned are properly not among the number of Christ's redeemed.

units.la: IV. Argumentum superiori affine esto hoc:
units.tr: IV. Argument, closely related to the previous one, is this:

units.la: Qui spiritum Christi non habent, non sunt eius. Rom. 8. Plurimi autem spiritum Christi non habent. Si enim omnes Spiritum Dei in se habitantem haberet, omnium etiam mortalium corpora viuificarentur per eundem spiritum, qui Christum excitauit à mortuis. Adde quod, vt Christus in Euangelio ait, spiritum illum veritatis mundus non potest accipere; quoniam non nouit eum, nec videt eum. Hinc sequitur, plurimos Christi non esse: ac per consequens, nec Christus eiusque beneficia ipsorum sunt.
units.tr: Those who do not have the Spirit of Christ are not his. Rom. 8. But very many do not have the Spirit of Christ. For if all had the Spirit of God dwelling in them, the bodies of all mortals would also be quickened through the same Spirit who raised Christ from the dead. Add that, as Christ says in the Gospel, the world cannot receive that Spirit of truth, because it neither knows him nor sees him. Hence it follows that many are not Christ's, and consequently Christ and his benefits are not theirs.

units.la: V. Argumentum, ab adiunćto redemtionis.
units.tr: V. Argument from the adjunct of redemption.

units.la: Quorum Christus est aduocatus, eorum duntaxat est, ἱλασμὸς, propitiatio. Sed aduocatus non est infidelium & reproborum, verùm fidelium & electorum. Ergo etiam non illorum, sed horum est ἱλασμὸς.
units.tr: Christ is the advocate of those alone for whom he is the propitiation [ἱλασμός], the propitiation. But he is not the advocate of unbelievers and reprobates, but of believers and the elect. Therefore the propitiation [ἱλασμός] is theirs, not the others'.

units.la: Ratio Maioris est, quia vnius & eiusdem Pontificis est, & orare & sacrificare pro populo: & vtrumque requiritur ad impetrandum nobis fauorem & gratiam apud Deum. Vnde etiam Johannes 1.Epist.2. ita coniungens, quem dicit esse ἱλασμὸν nostrum, eundem dicit esse aduocatum nostrum. Quomodo etiam coniungi ista videas Rom. 8. v.34.
units.tr: The reason for the major premise is that it belongs to one and the same high priest both to pray and to offer sacrifice for the people, and both are required to win for us favour and grace before God. Hence John too, in 1 John 2, joining the two, says that the one whom he calls our propitiation [ἱλασμόν] is also our advocate. You may see these things joined in the same way in Romans 8:34.

units.la: Esse autem Christum aduocatum duntaxat pro ijs qui credunt aut credituri turi sunt, & in summa pro electis suis ipse non dissimulauit Ioh. 17. Non pro mundo rogo: sed pro iis quos dedisti mihi. Quem locum supra pluribus expositum us. Si autem tum non rogabat pro mundo, neque nunc pro eo intercedit, sed tantum pro electis. Idem liquet ad Rom. 8. Quis accusabit electos Dei? Deus est qui iustificat. Quis condemnabit? Christus est qui mortuus est, & excitatus est, & sedet ad dextram patris, & interpellat pro nobis: scilicet electis, de quibus solis eo contextu loquitur. Necde aliis loquitur Johannes 1. Ep. 2. Filioli, si quis peccauerit, aduocatum habemus apud patrem Iesum Christum iustum, & ipse est propitiatio pro peccatis: Et autor ad Heb. 7. propterea quod perpetuum habet sacerdotium, seruare prorsus potest eos, qui per ipsum accedunt ad Deum, semper viuens ut interpellet pro eis, nempe accedentibus per ipsum ad Deum.
units.tr: That Christ is advocate only for those who believe, or who are going to believe, and in short for his own elect, he did not conceal in John 17: "I do not pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me." I have explained this passage at length above. If then he did not pray for the world at that time, nor does he now intercede for it, but only for the elect. The same is clear from Romans 8: "Who will accuse God's elect? God is the one who justifies. Who will condemn? Christ is the one who died, and was raised, and sits at the right hand of the Father, and intercedes for us," namely the elect, of whom alone he speaks in that context. Nor does John speak of others in 1 John 2: "My little children, if anyone sins, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous, and he is the propitiation for our sins." And the author of Hebrews 7: "because he has a perpetual priesthood, he is altogether able to save those who come to God through him, since he always lives to intercede for them," namely those who come to God through him.

units.la: Ad eundem modum autor sermonis 62. apud Ambrosium, ex dicto beati Iohannis notat, Christum aduocatum esse Christianis, iudice plane Iudeis alijsq; infidelibus. Origenes item in Leuiticum: Pro
units.tr: In the same way the author of Sermon 62, in Ambrose, notes from the saying of the blessed John that Christ is advocate to Christians, while plainly to Jews and other unbelievers he is not. Origen likewise, on Leviticus:

units.la: Pro ijs tantum exorat Pontifex & aduocatus & propitiator Christus,qui sunt sors Domini, qui eum praforibus exspectant, qui non recedunt a templo,ieiunijs & obsecrationibus vacantes.
units.tr: "Christ the High Priest, Advocate and Propitiator intercedes only for those who are the Lord's portion, who wait for him at the doors, who do not depart from the temple, devoted to fasting and prayers."

units.la: VI. Argumentum a consequentibus redemtionem: vt sunt adoptio & hæreditas.
units.tr: VI. Argument from the consequences of redemption: namely adoption and inheritance.

units.la: Vbi redemtio,ibi adoptio & hæreditas: Non omnes autem sunt filij & hæredes; hæredes nempe Dei, cohæredes autem Christi. Neque omnes igitur redemti.
units.tr: Where there is redemption, there is also adoption and inheritance. But not all are sons and heirs: heirs of God, indeed, and co-heirs with Christ. Therefore not all are redeemed either.

units.la: Minor probatur ex Paulo, Dei filios demum censente qui spiritu Dei ducuntur, & actiones corporis spiritu mortificant: vt nihil nunc dicam de tot scripturæ sententiis, quæ adoptionem credentibus tanquam propriam tribunt. Ioh. 1. quotquot acceperunt eum, dedit eis autoritatem seu dignitatem hanc vt filij Dei fierent, nempe ijs qui credunt in nomen eius. vide etiam 1.Ioh.3.v.1.
units.tr: The minor premise is proved from Paul, who counts as sons of God only those who are led by the Spirit of God and who put to death the deeds of the body by the Spirit. Not to mention for now the many sentences of Scripture which ascribe adoption to believers as its proper possession: John 1: "as many as received him, he gave them authority, or this dignity, to become sons of God," namely to those who believe in his name. See also 1 John 3:1.

units.la: Hinc & Ambrosius scribit in Epist. ad Rom.5.credentes Christu esse Dei filium, a Deo adoptamur in filios. Nihil enim vltra potuit potuit donare credentibus, quàm vt filij Dei dicantur, perfidis abdicatis. Nos enim filij Dei vocamur. Illi autem nec serui digni sunt nuncupari. Et Epist.74. totum hoc argumentum concinna breuitate completitur, inquiens : vbi spiritus Domini, ibi libertas: vbi nulla libertas, nulla gratia: vbi nulla gratia, nulla adoptio: vbi nulla adoptio, nulla successio. Vbi autem fides, ibi libertas, adoptio, hæreditas.
units.tr: Hence Ambrose also writes in his commentary on Romans 5: "Believing that Christ is the Son of God, we are adopted by God as sons. For he could give to believers nothing further than to be called sons of God, the faithless being disowned. For we are called sons of God; but those others are not even worthy to be named servants." And in Epistle 74 he completes this whole argument with neat brevity, saying: "Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty; where there is no liberty, there is no grace; where there is no grace, there is no adoption; where there is no adoption, there is no inheritance. But where there is faith, there is liberty, adoption, inheritance."

units.la: VII. Argumentum, ab alio consequenti, hoc est, à sanctificatione & conuersione.
units.tr: VII. Argument from another consequence, that is, from sanctification and conversion.

units.la: Quicunque redimuntur, ij etiam sanctificantur, conuertuntur & regenerantur, secundum promissionem: veniet ex Sion liberator, & auertet peccata à Iacob: & hoc illis fœdus à me, cùm abstulero peccata ipsorum, ait Dominus. Quæ locum ex 59. Iesu. Paulus Rom. 11. accommodat ad conuersionem Israëlis, atque inde declarat cum liberatione seu redemtione cohærere conuersionem. Quò etiam pertinet dictum Iohan. 1. Epist. 3. Qui committit peccatum ex Diabolo est; ad hoc autem patefactus est filius Dei, vt destruat opera Diaboli. Quisquis natus ex Deo, Dei, peccatum non facit. Loquitur de iustitia exercenda, velut qua filij Dei a filiis Diaboli dignoscuntur: peccantes ex Diabolo esse: iustitiam facientes ex Deo per Christum, dissoluente in nobis opera Diaboli; non modo remittendo peccata, sed & naturam depravatam renouando ad opera iustitiæ. Hac expositionem verborum circumstantia & scopus docent, & confirmat Augustinus in hypognostico lib.3. Vbi simul adducit, quod scribitur ad Hebræos 9. Sanguinem videlicet Christi, qui per spiritum æternum semetipsum obtulit Deo, purgare conscientias nostras a mortuis operibus ad seruiedum Deo viuo. Vide etiam in Cantico Zachariæ Luc.1. verf.74. ad Tit.2. v.14.1. Cor.1. v.30. Eph.5.26. Act.5. verf.31. in verbis Petri: & apud eundem 1.Epist.2. v.24. Copiosissimè vero omnium ad Rom.6. & 7. Quæ omnia loca irrefragabiliter testantur, sanctificationem seu renouationem hominis ad colendam iustitiam & bona opera, necessario coniunctam cum dono redemtionis seu sanctificationis.
units.tr: All who are redeemed are also sanctified, converted and regenerated, according to the promise: "A deliverer will come out of Zion, and will turn away ungodliness from Jacob; and this is my covenant with them, when I take away their sins, says the Lord." Paul in Romans 11 applies this passage, taken from Isaiah 59, to the conversion of Israel, and from it declares that conversion coheres with deliverance or redemption. To this also belongs the saying of John in 1 John 3: "He who commits sin is of the devil; for this purpose the Son of God was revealed, that he might destroy the works of the devil. Whoever is born of God does not commit sin." He speaks of the practice of righteousness, by which the sons of God are distinguished from the sons of the devil: those who sin are of the devil, those who do righteousness are of God through Christ, who dissolves within us the works of the devil, not only by remitting sins but also by renewing the depraved nature to the works of righteousness. The context and aim of the words teach this exposition, and Augustine confirms it in the Hypognosticon, book 3, where he also cites what is written in Hebrews 9: that the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself to God, purges our consciences from dead works to serve the living God. See also Luke 1:74 in the Canticle of Zechariah; Titus 2:14; 1 Corinthians 1:30; Ephesians 5:26; Acts 5:31 in the words of Peter; and in the same author, 1 Peter 2:24. But most fully of all, Romans 6 and 7. All these passages irrefutably testify that the sanctification or renewal of man, for cultivating righteousness and good works, is necessarily joined with the gift of redemption or sanctification.

units.la: Hîc
units.tr: Here

units.la: Hic iam assumamus, quod sacræ literæ & experientia plus satis arguunt, non omnes donari spiritu sanctificationis ad conuersionem seu renouationem vitæ.
units.tr: Here let us now assume what the sacred letters and experience argue more than enough: not all are granted the Spirit of sanctification for conversion or renewal of life.

units.la: Probatur. Quia sanctificatio hæc nō est absque donatione Spiritus Sancti. Mundus autem spiritum illum nō potest accipere Ioh. 14. Deinde, donum hoc in eo situm est, vt peccatis mortui iustitiæ viuamus, & Deo seruiamus in conspectu ipsius cum sanctimonia, & iustitia, omnibus diebus vitæ nostræ. Hoccine vero omnibus datum est? imo vero proprium est filiorum promissionis & noui fœderis, vt dicit Dominus:
units.tr: This is proved. Because this sanctification is not without the gift of the Holy Spirit. But the world cannot receive that Spirit (John 14). Next, this gift consists in this, that, dead to sins, we live to righteousness and serve God in his sight with holiness and righteousness all the days of our life. But is this given to all? Rather, it is proper to the children of the promise and of the new covenant, as the Lord says:

units.la: Indam leges meas mentì eorum & cordi eorum inscribam eas, & omnes cognoscent me, eroq; propitius peccatis ipsorum, & iniquitatum ipsorum non recordabor amplius. Item, dabo vobis cor nouum & spiritum nouum dabo in medio vestri: & auferam cor lapideum, daboq; cor carneum & efficiam vt in præceptis meis ambuletis, & iudicia mea custodiatis: eritisq; mihi populus & ero vobis Deus.
units.tr: "I will put my laws in their mind and write them on their heart, and they shall all know me, and I will be merciful to their sins, and I will remember their iniquities no more." Likewise, "I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit in the midst of you; and I will take away the stony heart and give a fleshly heart, and I will make you walk in my precepts and keep my judgments; and you shall be my people and I will be your God."

units.la: Quæ cùm ita sint, conficimus etiam redemtionem non esse omnium, sed filiorum duntaxat promissionis.
units.tr: Since these things are so, we conclude that redemption is not of all, but of the children of the promise only.

units.la: Dupliciter autem circa hoc argu- mentum impingit antagonista: Primum quod sanctificationem promiscuè ad totam hominum progeniem detorquere conatur, nullo tamen idoneo ad id Scripturæ testimonio depromto: quæ, ut vidimus, contrariû demóstrat. Tum quod vim argumenti aut callidè depravat, aut non assequitur, quási nimirum à coniunctione duplicis beneficij, redemtionis & sanctificationis, ad hunc modum ratiocinemur. Deus à redemtis suis flagitat sanctificationem. Ergo maxima pars non est redemta, quia non colit pietate. Atqui nostra argumentatio non sumitur ab officio nostro: sed à Dei beneficio, promittentis se daturum redemtis cor nouum, & spiritum nouum, atque ita effecturum, ut in præceptis suis ambulent, indendo & inscribendo ea menti eorum; non atramento, sed spiritu Dei viui, non in tabulis lapideis, sed in tabulis cordis.
units.tr: The opponent, however, attacks this argument in two ways. First, he tries to twist sanctification indiscriminately onto the whole human race, yet without bringing forward any suitable testimony of Scripture for this; whereas, as we have seen, Scripture shows the contrary. Then, he either craftily distorts the force of the argument or fails to grasp it, as if we reasoned from the conjunction of the double benefit, redemption and sanctification, in this manner: God demands sanctification from his redeemed. Therefore the greater part is not redeemed, because they do not cultivate piety. But our argument is not taken from our duty, but from God's benefit, who promises that he will give to the redeemed a new heart and a new spirit, and thus will bring it about that they walk in his precepts, by writing and inscribing them in their mind, not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone, but on the tablets of the heart.

units.la: VIII. Ar.
units.tr: VIII. Arg.

units.la: VIII. Argumentum septimo affine: in redemtis voluntas quoque redemta est per Iesum Christū, alioquin optimum in homine non esset redemtū. Ergo posita omnium redemtione, fidelium & infidelium, sequeretur voluntatem quoque in omnibus esse redemtam & sanatam: & sic stabiliretur liberum arbitrium in quibuscumque, cum tamen Christum ignorantes, nec in eum credentes, peccato serviat, nec boni quicquam possint velle aut conari, vt praeclare asseruit Lutherus de servo arbitrio.
units.tr: VIII. An argument closely related to the seventh: in the redeemed, the will too is redeemed through Jesus Christ, since otherwise the best part of man would not have been redeemed. Therefore, if redemption is posited for all, both believers and unbelievers, it would follow that the will is also redeemed and healed in all. Thus free choice would be established in everyone, although those who do not know Christ and do not believe in him are still slaves to sin, and cannot will or attempt anything good, as Luther clearly asserted in On the Bondage of the Will.

units.la: IX. Argumentum ab alio consequente, quod est beatitudo & vita aeterna. Quicunque efficaciter redemti sunt non peribunt, sed habebunt vitā aeternam. Pereunt autem increduli. Nam qui non crediderit damnabitur. Ergo increduli non sunt efficaciter redemti.
units.tr: IX. An argument from another consequence, namely blessedness and eternal life. Those who are effectually redeemed will not perish but will have eternal life. Unbelievers, however, perish, for "he who does not believe will be condemned" (Mark 16:16). Therefore unbelievers are not effectually redeemed.

units.la: Maior demonstratur dictis: iustificati eius sanguine, seruabimur nunc multo magis per eum ab ira. Nam si cum inimici essemus, reconciliati sumus Deo per mortem filij eius, multo magis seruabimur nunc per vitam eius, eius.Rom.5.Et cap.8.eiusdem: Quos iustifi-cat eosdem etiam glorificat. Item, Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? is quidem qui proprio filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit eum, qui non cum eo omnia nobis gratificabitur? Quis accusabit electos Dei? Deus est, qui iustificat. Quis condemnabit? Christus est, qui mortuus est: imo vero qui etiam excitatus est, & postulat pro nobis.
units.tr: The major premise is proved by these words: "Since we are now justified by his blood, we shall be saved from wrath through him much more. For if, while we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, now that we are reconciled, shall we be saved by his life" (Rom. 5). And in chapter 8 of the same letter: "Those whom he justified, them he also glorified." Likewise: "If God is for us, who can be against us? He who did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all, how will he not also with him freely give us all things? Who will bring a charge against God's elect? It is God who justifies. Who is to condemn? It is Christ who died, or rather who was raised, who is at the right hand of God and intercedes for us."

units.la: Expresse sentit pro quibus Christus mortuus sit, resurrexerit, intercedat, eos nunquam iri damnatum.
units.tr: He plainly holds that those for whom Christ died, rose again and intercedes will never be condemned.

units.la: Optime Ambrosius de Iacob & vita beata, lib. 1. cap. 6. Nihil excipit qui omnium concessit autore: Nihil est igitur quod negari nobis posse vereamur, nihil est in quo de munificentia divina perseverantia diffidere debeamus, cuius fuit tam diuturna & iugis ubertas, ut primum praedestinaret, Deinde vocaret, & quos vocaret, iustificaret & clarificaret. Poterit deserere quos tantis beneficiis suis prosequutus est? Sed metus est ne iudex severior sit. Considera quem iudicem habeas, nempe Christum. Poterit te ille damnare, quem redemit a morte, pro quo se obtulit, cuius vitam sua mortis mercede esse cognoscit? Nonne dicet? cet, Quae vtilitas in sanguine meo, si damnoque nos ipsi saluamus? Vide etiam, si lubet, Augustinum, hoc ipsum argumentum confirmantem de Trin. 13. cap. 16.
units.tr: Ambrose puts it well in On Jacob and the Blessed Life, book 1, chapter 6: "He who granted all things excludes nothing. There is therefore nothing we need fear to be denied, nothing in which we ought to distrust the perseverance of divine bounty, whose abundance has been so long-lasting and constant that it first predestined, then called, and those whom it called it justified and glorified. Will he desert those whom he has loaded with such great benefits? But there is fear that the judge may be too severe. Consider whom you have as judge, namely Christ. Can he condemn you, whom he has redeemed from death, for whom he offered himself, whose life you know to be the price of his death? Will he not say: 'What profit is there in my blood, if we destroy ourselves and are damned?'" And see, if you like, Augustine confirming this very argument On the Trinity, book 13, chapter 16.

units.la: Hinc est quod praetextu vniuersalis redemptionis nonnulli omnes tandem seruatum iri opinati sunt: cuius vesani erroris meminerunt Calvinus in 1. Ioh. 2. Bucerus in actis colloquij Argentinae habiti cum Melchiore Hofmanno. Nec non Vvolfgangus Musculus loco de redemptione generis humani, cauendum monens, ne vniuersalitatem redemptionis male intelligentes, cum fanaticis hominibus neminem damnari & in aeternum perire dicamus.
units.tr: Hence it is that some, under the pretext of universal redemption, have supposed that in the end all will be saved. Of this mad error Calvin makes mention on 1 John 2, and Bucer in the acts of the colloquy held at Strasbourg with Melchior Hoffman, as also Wolfgang Musculus in his chapter on the redemption of the human race, warning that we must take care, lest in misunderstanding the universality of redemption, we say along with the fanatics that no one is condemned and perishes for eternity.

units.la: Negant id quidem nostri illi, quibuscum nobis res est, Sed quid iuuat negare, cum nihilominus principium mor dicus teneant, ex quo error iste manat?
units.tr: Those opponents of ours with whom we have to deal indeed deny this. But what does denying it help, when they nevertheless stubbornly hold the principle from which this error flows?

units.la: Excipiunt, redemptos non perire, nisi incredulitate abijciant & conculcent acceptam redemptionem. Sed contra docent scripturae testimonia modo allegata, efficaciter redemptos & iustificatos iam dono Dei, certo manere vitam atque gloriam coelestem, nec vlla ratione tione auelli eos posse à Dei erga ipsos caritate in Christo Iesu. Quod autem ad exempla & loca quædam in contrarium, ad ea copiosè responsum fuit lib.2.
units.tr: They make an exception: the redeemed do not perish unless by unbelief they cast away and trample under foot the redemption received. But the testimonies of Scripture just cited teach the contrary: that those who are effectually redeemed and justified by the gift of God surely remain in life and heavenly glory, and that by no means can they be torn away from God's love for them in Christ Jesus. As for the examples and certain passages to the contrary, a full answer has been given to them in book 2.

units.la: Præterea,quomodo isthæc consentiunt, omnia omnium peccata expiata atque deleta re ipsa, & tamen propter incredulitatem maiorem hominum partem damnari? Nam si omnia peccata omnibus remissa sunt,etiam incredulitas remissa est. Quomodo igitur quenquam damnabit? Ita semper manet immotum,si omnes omninò homines efficaciter redemtionis fācti sint participes, omnes tandem saluatū iri.
units.tr: Moreover, how do these claims agree: that all the sins of all men have really been expiated and blotted out, and yet that most men are damned because of unbelief? For if all sins have been forgiven to all, then unbelief too has been forgiven. How then will he condemn anyone? So it always remains fixed: if all men without exception are made partakers of effectual redemption, all will in the end be saved.

units.la: X. Argumentum ducitur à causis redemtionis,quarū duæ sunt primariæ efficientes: vna remotior,nempe gratia Dei, filium suum nobis dantis : altera vicinissima:Filius ipse,opus redemtionis in suscepta natura humana peragens. Materialis est passio ac mors iusti pro iniustis. Instrumentalis efficiens similiter duplex est, verbum nempe gratiæ, quod Christum cum beneficijs suis nobis offert, fert, & excitandæ in nobis fidei seruit. Fides enim ex auditu est, auditus autē per verbum Dei. Et fides ipsa, qua ceu manu oblatam gratiā recipimus, eiusq; reddimur consortes.
units.tr: X. An argument drawn from the causes of redemption, of which there are two principal efficient causes: one more remote, namely the grace of God giving his Son to us; the other very near, the Son himself, accomplishing the work of redemption in the human nature he took up. The material cause is the suffering and death of the just for the unjust. The instrumental efficient cause is likewise twofold: the word of grace, which offers, brings and serves to stir up faith in us, offering Christ with his benefits. For "faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of God" (Rom. 10:17). And faith itself, by which, as by a hand, we receive the grace offered and become partakers of it.

units.la: Hinc Rom.3. Apostolus ait, Omnes peccauimus: iustificamur autem gratis, eius gratia per redemptionem factam in Christo Iesu, quem proposuit Deus placamentum per fidem in sanguine ipsius ad declarandam iustitiam suam. Vbi videmus inter alias causas redemptionis, fidem requiri, velut instrumentum, quo partam nobis sanguine ipsius redemptione nobis applicemus, eiusq; euadamus participes, ad peccatorum nostrorum deletionem.
units.tr: Hence the Apostle says in Romans 3: "All have sinned, and are justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God set forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness." Here we see that among the other causes of redemption faith is required, as the instrument by which we apply to ourselves the redemption obtained for us by his blood, and by which we become partakers of it, for the blotting out of our sins.

units.la: Redemtionis igitur & propitiationis alieni sunt increduli. Ac vt magis patescat fidei in omni salutis negotio necessitas, Apostolus Heb. 11. expresse testatur fieri non posse, vt quis sine fide Deo placeat, prolatis ad hoc pulcerrimis antiquorum exemplis, qui fide comprobātur Deo placuisse, & iustitiam quæ secundum fidem est, consequuti esse.
units.tr: Unbelievers therefore have no share in redemption and propitiation. And so that the necessity of faith in the whole business of salvation may be more clearly seen, the Apostle expressly testifies in Hebrews 11 that it is impossible for anyone to please God without faith, adducing for this the most beautiful examples of the ancients, who by faith were shown to have pleased God, and to have obtained the righteousness which is by faith.

units.la: Præclarè Augustinus in Enangelium secundum Iohannem serm. 60. Medicina omnium vulnerum, & una propitiatio pro delictis hominum, est credere in Christum, nec omnino quisquam mundari potest, sive ab originali peccato, sive a peccatis quae ipse addidit, nisi per fidem coadunetur & compaginetur corpori eius. In eum quippe credentes filii Dei sunt: quia ex Deo nascuntur per adoptionis gratiam, quae est in fide Domini nostri Iesu Christi: credentes enim filii Dei fimus, sicut scriptum est, dedit ipsis potestatem filios Dei fieri, credentibus in eum. Et serm. 181. de tempore apud eundem: Fides omnium bonorum est fundamentum, & humanae salutis initium: sine hac nemo ad numerum filiorum Dei poterit peruenire, & sine ipsa in hoc seculo nec iustificationis consequitur gratiam, nec in futurum possidebit vitam aeternam: & si quis non ambulauerit per fidem, non perueniet ad speciem. His scripturarum & maiorum secundum scripturas testimonijs, si stare velimus, stare autem debemus, apagite figmentu de omniu iustitia & operatione salutis in omnes, omniumque in gratiam receptione atque a peccatis emundatione, siue illi credant, siue non. Ex-
units.tr: Augustine says admirably in his sermon 60 on the Gospel of John: "The remedy for all wounds, and the one propitiation for the sins of men, is to believe in Christ, and no one at all can be cleansed, whether from original sin or from the sins which he himself has added, unless he is joined and knit to his body through faith. For those who believe in him are sons of God, because they are born of God through the grace of adoption, which is in the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ; for we are believing sons of God, as it is written: he gave them power to become sons of God, to those who believe in him." And in sermon 181 on the season, in the same author: "Faith is the foundation of all good things and the beginning of human salvation. Without it no one can attain to the number of the sons of God, and without it in this age one does not obtain the grace of justification, nor in the future will he possess eternal life; and if anyone does not walk by faith, he will not come to sight." If we wish to stand by these testimonies of the Scriptures, and of the Fathers according to the Scriptures (and we ought to stand by them), let us cast away the fable that all men are justified and all works of salvation are wrought in all, and that all are received into grace and cleansed from sins, whether they believe or not.

units.la: Hub. thes. 49. & 65.
units.tr: Hub. thes. 49 and 65.

units.la: Excipiunt aduersarij: fe non existi-mare, quod abíque fide meritum Chri-fti applicetur, aut fine ea quisquam pa-ternæ Dei voluntatis possit fieri particeps.
units.tr: Our opponents make an exception: they do not think that the merit of Christ is applied without faith, or that anyone can become a partaker of the Father's will without it.

units.la: Respondeo, Manifeste igitur secum pugnant; qui talia dicunt, & nihilominus mordicus tenent, omnes homines, nullo excepto, fideles & infideles, ante & post Christum natum, sanguine Christi vere & indubitanter ab omni peccato & condemnatione liberatos, inq; gratiam & finum Dei receptos, omnes peræquè saluatos, iustificatos, viuificatos: Omnes ad salutis communionem & regnum gratiæ pertinere,& similia. Si enim gratiæ Dei, iustitiæ, vitæ & salutis particeps nemo esse potest in Christo, nisi bona illa sibi applicet; applicatio autem abíque fide fieri nequit: quomodo ista sunt omnium, infidelium æqueac fidelium?
units.tr: I reply: those who say such things and yet stubbornly hold that all men, without exception, believers and unbelievers, before and after the birth of Christ, are truly and undoubtedly freed by the blood of Christ from all sin and condemnation, and received into the grace and bosom of God, that all are equally saved, justified, quickened, and that all belong to the fellowship of salvation and the kingdom of grace, and similar things, clearly contradict themselves. For if no one can be a partaker in Christ of God's grace, righteousness, life and salvation unless he applies those good things to himself, and such application cannot be made without faith, how can these things belong to all, unbelievers as well as believers?

units.la: XI. Argumentum, ab alio conse-quente.
units.tr: XI. Argument from what follows from another.

units.la: Redemtio tale beneficium est, quo de feruis peccati, filij Dei: de filijs irę, filij gratiæ, de aduenis item & igno-tis, tis, genus fimus regale & sacerdotale, sicut scriptum est Apoc. 1. & 5. dilexit nos & redemit nos Deo per sanguinem suum, & fecit nos Deo nostro reges & sacerdotes, & regnabimus super terram.
units.tr: Redemption is such a benefit that from slaves of sin we become sons of God, from sons of wrath sons of grace, and from strangers and unknown people too, we are made a royal and priestly race, as it is written Rev. 1 and 5: he loved us and redeemed us to God by his blood, and made us kings and priests to our God, and we shall reign upon the earth.

units.la: In Ecclesiam autem proprie competit ista dignitas, vt sit genus electum, regale sacerdotium, gens sancta, teste Petro. 1. Epist. 2. quod & verba Apoc. 5. iam citata confirmant, vbi Ecclesiæ vox atque confessio est, Fecisti nos Deo nostro reges ac sacerdotes.
units.tr: This dignity properly belongs to the Church, that she is a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, as Peter witnesses, 1. Epist. 2. The words of Rev. 5, already cited, also confirm this, where the voice and confession of the Church is: You have made us kings and priests to our God.

units.la: Efficitur ergo, penes Ecclesiam redemtionis esse proprietatem.
units.tr: It follows, therefore, that redemption is a property belonging to the Church.

units.la: Duodecimum argumentum ab vsu Sacramentorum.
units.tr: The twelfth argument, from the use of the sacraments.

units.la: Quibus nihil obsignatur in vsurpatione Sacramentorū, ad eos nec promissio gratiæ in verbo pertinet. Eadem enim est ratio promissionis in vtroque verbo, audibili & visibili.
units.tr: Nothing is sealed to those who do not take part in the sacraments, and the promise of grace in the Word does not pertain to them. For the reason of the promise is the same in both the audible and the visible word.

units.la: At in sacramentis, Baptismo & Cœna Domini, nihil obsignatur extraneis à foedere Dei atque incredulis.
units.tr: But in the sacraments, Baptism and the Lord's Supper, nothing is sealed to those who are outside the covenant of God and unbelieving.

units.la: Ergo nec promissio gratiæ in verbo ad eos pertinet. Pro assumtione con-susulantur quæ supra in confutatione ea de re egimus.
units.tr: Therefore the promise of grace in the Word does not pertain to them either. As for the assumption, the things we have said above in refuting this point stand against it.

units.la: XII. & vltimum Argumentum. Si quicquid est hominum per mortem & gratiam Seruatoris, in gratia & sinum Dei receptum est, nemine vnquam ex quo iam redemtus est perituro, nisi gratiam Dei fastidiat & per incredulitatem excutiat redemtionem suam: Sequetur omnes omniu liberos, Thalmudistarum, Mahumetistarum, Turcarum, Tartarorum, Anthropophagorum &c. quandiu rationis vsu ac proin peccato actuali carent, fastidiumque gratiæ nondum in ipsos cadit, in statu esse salutis, cunctosq; ea ætate decedentes, ex quacunq; gente sint, in Ecclesia vel extra eam, æternum seruari: id quod manifeste delirium est ana baptisticu, eorum, inquâ, qui Mennonis & Theodorici Philippi castra per Belgium & alibi sequuntur, ex Melchioris Hofmanni, vt videtur, sententia in eos deriuatum. Sětit enim & expresse scribit Theodorus Philippi: quia Christus agnus Dei abstuabstulerit peccatum mundi morte & sanguine suo, ob peccatum Adæ nemi- nem posse damnari: ac proinde omniū promisce puerorum esse regnū Dei, omnesq; innocentes esse & sine peccato reputari coram Deo, cum præter Adæ peccatū aliud ipsis imputari nequeat, & vero id vniuersaliter morte Christi expiatum & sublatum sit, sic vt infantes propter prævaricationem Adæ iudicari aut condemnari nequeant. Sed & Pelagiani, teste Augustino lib. 2. de nuptiis & concup. cap. 33. tale quid inferre nitebantur, paruulos nimirum esse innocentes & extra omnem reatum, postquam morte pro illis Christus obierit.
units.tr: XII. And the last argument. If whatever is of mankind has been received into the grace and bosom of God through the death and grace of the Saviour, then no one who has once been redeemed will ever perish, unless he scorns the grace of God and through unbelief casts away his redemption. It would follow that all the children of Jews, Muslims, Turks, Tartars, cannibals, and so on, as long as they lack the use of reason and so actual sin, and scorn of grace has not yet fallen upon them, are in a state of salvation; and that all who die at that age, of whatever nation, whether in or outside the Church, are kept eternally. This is manifestly a delirium, derived from the opinion of the Anabaptists, I mean of those who follow the camp of Menno and Dirk Philips through Belgium and elsewhere, and, as it seems, from the opinion of Melchior Hofmann. For Dirk Philips thinks and expressly writes that because Christ the Lamb of God has taken away the sin of the world by his death and blood, no one can be condemned for the sin of Adam; and therefore the kingdom of God belongs without distinction to all children, and all infants are innocent and reckoned without sin before God, since nothing except Adam's sin can be imputed to them, and that has been universally expiated and removed by the death of Christ, so that infants cannot be judged or condemned on account of Adam's transgression. But the Pelagians too, according to Augustine, book 2 on marriage and concupiscence, chapter 33, strove to infer something of this kind, namely that little children are innocent and free of all guilt once Christ has died for them.

units.la: Verum Scriptura nos docet discriminen hic statuendum inter infantes populi Dei, & infantes impiarum & a Deo abiectarum gentium. Et infantes quidem populi Dei, etsi cæterorum more sub peccato & ira nascuntur carnali natiuitate, promissionem habent, quod ad numerum populi Dei & sanctificatorum, atque ita ad hæreditatem regni cœlestis pertineant.
units.tr: Yet Scripture teaches us that a distinction must be drawn here between the infants of the people of God and the infants of impious nations cast off by God. The infants of the people of God, although by carnal birth they are born under sin and wrath like the rest, have the promise that they belong to the number of the people of God and of the sanctified, and thus to the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom.

units.la: Plura argumeta hîc non subijciam: his enim quæ allata sunt satis superque instituum nostrum demonstrari confido. Tantum scrupulus quidam superest:Si credentes demum pro redemtis Christi censendi veniant,an igitur tuc, cum credere incipiunt, redemtio eorum incipiat?
units.tr: I will not add more arguments here, for I trust that what has been brought forward is sufficient and more than enough to demonstrate our position. Only one scruple remains: if believers are to be counted as redeemed of Christ only when they come to faith, does their redemption then begin at the time when they begin to believe?

units.la: Respondeo: Ecclesiæ per Christum redemtio varie considerari potest. Primum quidem ratione propositi & prædestinationis, secundum quam gratia hæc data est nobis in Christo Iesu ante tempora secularia. Deinde ratione meriti & satisfactionis à Christo præstitæ, cùm in ara crucis inimicitias sustulit, & totam Ecclesiam, Judæorum & gentium, reconciliauit Deo in vno corpore per crucem, vt testatur Paulus Eph.2. Tùm sanè, vt scribit Rupertus, redemit & lauit sanguine suo à peccatis ipsorum, non solùm eos qui iam erant credentes vel fuerant, sed etiam eos qui futuri erant, quatenus potestatem dedit eis lauari. Non enim actu iam tunc, sed potestate lauit eos, qui futuri ri erant. Neque enim actu iam lauari poterant, qui nondum nati erant vel nondum crediderant. Tertiò consideratur redemtio, quatenus participes eius reddimur per fidem, cuius tanta vis est, tantaque necessitas ad reconciliationem, ante & post peractum in carne Christi opus redemtionis, vt quemadmodum patribus credentibus olim nō oberat ad sui liberationem, quòd Christus nondum passus erat: ita nunc incredulis nihil prosit ad eandem sui liberationem, quòd pridem Christus, iustus pro iniustis, morti traditus est. Postremò consideratur redemtio quatenus destructis penitus inimicis omnibus, atque adeo ipsa etiam morte, quae nouissimus hostis ab Apostolo appellatur, plena perfectaque redemtione æternum potiemur; de qua redemtione ne Christus testatur Luc. 21. 28. & Paulus Rom. 8. v. 23. Sed de hoc satis.
units.tr: I answer: the redemption of the Church through Christ can be considered in various ways. First, in respect of the purpose and predestination, according to which this grace was given to us in Christ Jesus before the secular times. Then in respect of the merit and satisfaction performed by Christ, when on the altar of the cross he removed the enmities and reconciled the whole Church, of Jews and Gentiles, to God in one body through the cross, as Paul testifies Eph. 2. Then indeed, as Rupert writes, he redeemed and washed with his blood from their sins not only those who already were or had been believers, but also those who were to be, inasmuch as he gave them the power to be washed. For he washed those who were to come not yet in act, but in power. For those who were not yet born or had not yet believed could not yet actually be washed. Thirdly, redemption is considered as we are made partakers of it through faith, whose power and necessity for reconciliation is so great, both before and after the work of redemption was accomplished in the flesh of Christ, that just as to the believers of old it was no hindrance to their deliverance that Christ had not yet suffered, so now it profits the unbelieving nothing for the same deliverance that Christ, the just for the unjust, was long ago delivered to death. Lastly, redemption is considered as, all enemies having been utterly destroyed, and indeed death itself, which the Apostle calls the last enemy, we shall obtain the full and perfect redemption for ever; of which redemption Christ testifies Luke 21. 28. and Paul Rom. 8. 23. But enough on this.

units.la: TERTIA CLASSIS PROBATIONVM, ANTIQVITATIS continens testimonia. CAPVT VIII.
units.tr: THE THIRD CLASS OF PROOFS, CONTAINING THE TESTIMONIES OF ANTIQUITY. CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: - HIs hactenus e scriptura allatis, ad quam tanquam fidei nostræ anchoram & sustentaculum, in omnibus, vt tuti esse possimus, confugiendum nobis est, subijcienda nunc videntur antiquitatis testimonia, idque vt eo consensu veritas magis magisq; elucecscat, & obstruantur ora aduersarijs, qui disserentes & disputantes nescio quas impias nouitates, nos conantur arguere, quasi noui aliquid dicamus, vt de suis & Ecclesiæ aduersarijs Augustinus olim quereba-tur. Etenim eo iactantiæ, si non inscitiæ, progredi istos videas, vt audacter criminentur, nullo vnquam tempore nostram de hac controuersia sententiam auditam in eo populo in quo Christi nomen prædicatum fit: suam asseuerationem niti totius Christianitatis consensu, scilicet: Semper enim Ecclesiam catholicam & veram credidisse, & vno ore semper confessam esse, Christum esse mortuum pro omnibus hominibus intelligi efficaciter (de quo inter nos & adversarios quaestio est) quo ad novum dogma, in Christianorum auribus (si credere fas est) ante inauditum, erupe-rit ante annos VI. colloquio videlicet Mompelgardensi, habito anno Domi-ni 1586.
units.tr: Having now set out these testimonies from Scripture, to which we must flee as to the anchor and support of our faith in all things, so that we may be safe, it seems right to add the testimonies of antiquity. The purpose is that truth may shine forth more and more through this agreement, and that the mouths of our adversaries may be stopped. These men, in their disputing and arguing, try to charge us with I know not what impious novelties, as if we were saying something new, as Augustine once complained of his own adversaries and those of the Church. Indeed, you may see them proceed to such boastfulness, if not ignorance, that they boldly charge that our opinion on this controversy was never heard at any time among the people in whom the name of Christ is preached. They assert that their position rests on the consent of all Christendom, namely that the Catholic and true Church has always believed, and has always confessed with one voice, that Christ died for all men, to be understood efficaciously (this is the question between us and our adversaries). This new dogma, hitherto unheard of in Christian ears (if it is right to believe), broke out only six years ago, at the Mompelgard colloquy held in the year of the Lord 1586.

units.la: O inscitiam antiquitatis miserabile, cum admirabili coniunctam licentia & malitia! verumque adeo est quod vulgo dici solet, <bl>Θρασὺ τὸ ἀμαθές.</bl>
units.tr: O the miserable ignorance of antiquity, joined with admirable licence and malice! It is truly what is commonly said: "Boldness is the companion of ignorance" [Θρασὺ τὸ ἀμαθές].

units.la: Principio qua fronte insimulatur novitatis dogma in Propheticis & Apostolicis literis, hoc est in canone veritatis ita fundatum, ut quisquis contra hoc robur, contra hunc inexpugnabile mu-rum arietat, ipse confringatur? Nihil dicimus extra ea quae Prophetae & Mo-ses, Evangelistae & Apostoli testificati sunt unanimiter, videlicet remissione peccatorum & fortem inter sanctifica-tos accipere quemvis qui in Christi no-men crediderit, non vero incredulos.
units.tr: First, with what face is the dogma charged with novelty when it is so firmly founded in the prophetic and apostolic writings, that is, in the canon of truth, that whoever butts against this strength, this impregnable wall, is himself shattered? We say nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses, the evangelists and apostles, have unanimously testified: that through the forgiveness of sins and by the grace of God, whoever believes in the name of Christ receives a lot among the sanctified, but unbelievers do not.

units.la: Huic doctrinae si novitatis nomine de-trahitur trahitur ab ijs, qui ipsimet nouarum opinionum autores fautoresq; sunt, ferendum nobis est cum Paulo, cuius doctrinam nouam quoque vsam fuisse ignorantibus veritatem & in idololatria demersis Atheniensibus, actis Apostolorum proditum legimus. Deinde vt magis pateat fabulae istius vanitas, age oculos auresq; inferte æqui lectores, & vnanimè antiquitatis consensum mecum perpendite.
units.tr: If this doctrine is disparaged with the name of novelty, by those who are themselves the authors and supporters of new opinions, we must bear it as Paul did. We read in the Acts of the Apostles that his doctrine, which was also new, was used for the Athenians, who were ignorant of the truth and sunk in idolatry. Then, so that the vanity of this fable may be more evident, come, fair readers, direct your eyes and ears, and weigh with me the unanimous consent of antiquity.

units.la: Ecclesiae Smyrnensis in Epistola de martyrio Polycarpi Episcopi sui, quæ recitatur ab Eusebio lib. Eccles. libro 4. cap. 15. verba sunt: Christum pro totius seruandorum mundi salute passum esse, hunc proin colendum & adorandum tanquam filium Dei, martyres vero tanquam discipulos & imitatores Domini digne propter insuperabilem in regem ac praeceptorem beneuolentiam, diligendos non colendos. Quid attinebat mundum seruandorum ipeciatim exprimi, si quod ad effectum attinet, Christus æque passus est pro vniuersis damnatis & damnandis, ac pro Petro, Paulo, omnibusque seruatis & seruandis? Sanctus Martyr Christi Iustinus, Polycarpi coætaneus & eadem feruete persequutione per Marcum Aurel. Antoninum & Lucium Commodum Ver. Impp. martyrio coronatus, lib. de veritate religionis Christianæ; Christus oblatio, inquit, factus est pro cunctis, per pœnitentiam reficere volentibus peccatoribus. Et eodem libro ultra medium, Christus noster passioni subditus & crucifixus, maledictioni ex lege subiectus non est, sed se solum clare significauit ille liberaturum illos esse, qui a terra eius non deficerent: id est fideles omnes. Atque ut eos qui in Ægypto seruati sunt sanguis paschæ liberauit, ita & credentes liberabit a morte sanguis Christi. Et hoc sensu ibidem mox addit, salutem hominum generi per sanguinem Christi obuenisse, quatenus nimirum omnes totoorbe credentes per eum a morte liberantur, non autem quasi omnes homines, absq; discrimine fidelium & infidelium, a peccato ad iustitiam, a morte ad vitam & salutem per eum traducantur, velut aducrsarij somniant.
units.tr: The Church of Smyrna, in its letter on the martyrdom of Polycarp, its bishop, which is quoted by Eusebius in the fourth book of his Ecclesiastical History, chapter 15, says: "Christ suffered for the salvation of the whole world of those who are to be saved; him, therefore, we ought to worship and adore as the Son of God, but the martyrs we should love worthily as disciples and imitators of the Lord, on account of their unsurpassable goodwill toward their King and Teacher, not worship them." Why was it necessary to specify "of the world of those who are to be saved," if, so far as the effect is concerned, Christ suffered equally for all the damned and those who are to be damned, as for Peter, Paul and all who are saved or will be saved? Saint Justin, the Christian martyr, a contemporary of Polycarp, who was crowned with martyrdom in the same fervent persecution under Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Lucius Commodus Verus, the emperors, says in his book On the Truth of the Christian Religion: "Christ, he says, has been made an offering for all, for sinners who wish to be restored through repentance." And in the same book, a little past the middle: "Our Christ, subjected to suffering and crucified, is not made subject to the curse of the law, but he clearly signified that he would deliver those who did not fall away from his land, that is, all the faithful. And just as the blood of the paschal lamb delivered those who were preserved in Egypt, so the blood of Christ will deliver from death those who believe." In this same sense, he adds shortly afterwards that salvation came to the human race through the blood of Christ, namely in so far as all believers throughout the world are delivered from death through him. But he does not say that all men, without distinction between faithful and unfaithful, are brought by him from sin to righteousness, from death to life and salvation, as our adversaries dream.

units.la: Idem, sub finem eiusdem libri, negat peccata cata remitti impœnitentibus, impuris, nullius mentis comploratisq; adeo hominibus, addu-ēto Dauidis exemplo, cui tum demum peccatum remissum est, cum pœnitentiam ageret.
units.tr: The same author, near the end of the same book, denies that sins are forgiven to the unrepentant, the impure, and those of no sound mind or wholly wretched, and he cites the example of David, to whom sin was forgiven only when he repented.

units.la: Rursum principio fere libri, testatur resipiscentiam agentes expiari fide per sanguinē Christi, qui ea ipsa de causa mortuus fit.
units.tr: Again, near the beginning of the book, he testifies that those who repent of their error are cleansed by faith through the blood of Christ, who died for this very reason.

units.la: Irenæus lib.5. Ipsum verbum Dei inarnatum suspensum est super lignum, vt vniuersa in se ipso recapitularet: Ego, inquit, cum exaltatus fuero è terra, omnia ad me traham. Hoc dicebat significans qua morte effet moriturus. Passione sua Christus in cruce suspensus solus saluat omnes, non abscedentes à terra promissionis, hoc est, fideles ad finē vsque in gratia permanētes. Idem lib.4.cap.37 dicit, Instar Rahab fornicariæ nos seruari fide signi Coccyni, (hoc est, passione & sanguine Christi per fidem) Hoc Coccyni signum nullificantes, instar Pharisæorum, partem non habere in regno cœlorum. Et lib. 2. cap. 39. dicit: Omnes venit Christus per se metipsum saluare: omnes inquam qui per eum renascuntur in Deum, infantes, paruulos, pueros, iuuenes & seniores. Origenes in Leu. Pro illis tantum exorat Pontifex & aduocatus tus Christus, qui sunt fors Domini, qui eum præforibus exspectat, qui non recedit à tepla, ieiunijs & obsecrationibus vacates. Rursum Iren.lib.4.c.24. libertatem Christus detulit his qui legitimè & prono animo, & toto corde deseruiunt ei: contemtoribus, & non subiectis Deo, sempiternam attulit perditionem, abscindens eos à vita.
units.tr: Irenaeus, in book 5: "The Word of God himself, made flesh, was hung upon the wood, so that he might recapitulate all things in himself. 'I,' he says, 'when I have been lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself.' He said this, signifying by what death he was to die. By his passion, Christ, suspended on the cross, alone saves all, those who do not depart from the land of promise, that is, the faithful who remain in grace to the end." The same writer, in book 4, chapter 37, says that, like Rahab the harlot, we are kept safe by faith in the sign of the scarlet thread (that is, by the passion and blood of Christ through faith). "Those who nullify this sign of scarlet, like the Pharisees, have no part in the kingdom of heaven." And in book 2, chapter 39, he says: "Christ came to save all through himself: all, I say, who are born again into God through him, infants, little children, boys, youths and old men." Origen, on Leviticus: "The high priest and advocate Christ prays only for those who are, perhaps, the Lord's, who wait for him at the doors, who do not withdraw from the warmth of fasting and prayer." Again, Irenaeus, book 4, chapter 24: "Christ has brought liberty to those who serve him lawfully, willingly and with their whole heart; to those who despise him and are not subject to God he has brought eternal destruction, cutting them off from life."

units.la: Ambrosius de fide ad Gratianum Augustum lib.4.cap.1. Si non credis, non descendit tibi Christus, non tibi passus est. Idem in 1.Cor. 15. Sicut Adam peccans mortem invenit, & omnes ex eius origine mors tenet: ita & Christus non peccans, & per hoc vincens mortem, omnibus qui sunt ex eius corpore vitam acquisiuit. Similem restrictionem adhibet in dictum ad Rom. 5. quod vnius iustitia in omnes homines redundet ad iustificationem vitæ: iustitia, inquit, vnius Christi omnes iustificat credentes, & per eius obedientiam iusti constituuntur multi, non omnes. Neque id tantum, verum etiam expresse reijcit commentum aduersariorum de iustificatione tàm generali, quàm generalis sit condemnatio.
units.tr: Ambrose, On Faith, addressed to the emperor Gratian, book 4, chapter 1: "If you do not believe, Christ has not descended for you, and has not suffered for you." The same writer, on 1 Corinthians 15: "As Adam, sinning, found death, and death holds all who are of his origin, so also Christ, not sinning, and by this conquering death, has gained life for all who are of his body." He applies a similar restriction in his comment on Romans 5, where he says that the righteousness of one man abounds to all men unto justification of life: "The righteousness of the one Christ, he says, justifies all who believe, and through his obedience many are made righteous, not all." And not only this, but he also expressly rejects the adversaries' fiction of a justification as general as the condemnation is general.

units.la: Hub. thef. 49. Idem in cap.8.Luc\u00e6 inquit, Etsi Christus pro omnibus mortuus est, pro nobis tamen specialiter passus est, quia pro Ecclesia passus est. Quomodo specialiter pro Ecclesia, & tamen pro omnibus? nisi quoniam fructus passionis, reconciliatio, libertas, adoptio, hereditas, ad Ecclesiam proprie pertinent?
units.tr: Hub. thef. 49. The same writer, in chapter 8 of Luke, says: "Although Christ died for all, he nevertheless suffered specially for us, because he suffered for the Church." How specially for the Church, and yet for all? Unless because the fruits of the passion, reconciliation, liberty, adoption and inheritance properly belong to the Church?

units.la: Hinc Epist. 20. idem pater ait: Bonus cibus omnium Christus est: bonus cibus est fides: suavis cibus misericordia: iucundus cibus gratia: bonus cibus spiritus Dei: bonus cibus peccatorum remissio. At hos cibos epulatur populus Ecclesiae.
units.tr: Hence the same Father says in Epistle 20: "Christ is the good food of all. Faith is good food; mercy is sweet food; grace is pleasant food; the Spirit of God is good food; the forgiveness of sins is good food. And the people of the Church feast on these foods."

units.la: Et clarius Epistola 73. postquam venit plenitudo temporis & Christus advenit, non iam sumus servi sed liberi, si credamus in Christo. Ubi fides, ibi libertas: servus enim sub metu, liber ex fide: ubi libertas, ibi gratia, ibi hereditas. Ubi autem nulla libertas, nulla gratia: ubi nulla gratia, nulla adoptio: ubi nulla adoptio, nulla successio.
units.tr: And more clearly in Epistle 73: "When the fullness of time has come and Christ has arrived, we are no longer slaves but free, if we believe in Christ. Where there is faith, there is liberty; for the slave lives under fear, the free man from faith. Where there is liberty, there is grace, there is inheritance. But where there is no liberty, there is no grace; where there is no grace, there is no adoption; where there is no adoption, there is no succession."

units.la: Prima item Epistola, cum praemisisset Christum universorum redemtorem descendisse, ut omnibus peccatum dimitteret: & se ipsum exinaniuisse, ut omnibus libertatem daret, carnem suscepisse vt morte sua omnibus resurrectionem acquireret, subijcit verba hæc: Qui, inquit, verus est liber, verus Hebræus, totus Dei est, totum quod habet libertatis est, nihil habet illius qui libertatem recusat mundi amore.
units.tr: In the first Epistle likewise, after premising that Christ, the redeemer of all, came down so that he might forgive sin to all, and emptied himself so that he might give liberty to all, and took on flesh so that by his death he might obtain resurrection for all, he adds these words: "He who, he says, is truly free, a true Hebrew, is wholly God's, and all that he has is of liberty; he has nothing of him who refuses liberty through love of the world."

units.la: Sic alibi docet redemtionem esse pœnitentium & abhærentium Dei præceptis: veniam peccati ex fide esse: & per gratiam fidei adlutionem accipi criminum: crucem Domini credentibus vitam, non credetibus præcipitium esse: Et alibi, Crux ergo, inquit, opprobrium perfido: fideli autem gratia, fideli redemtio, fideli resurrectio est.
units.tr: Elsewhere he teaches in the same way that redemption belongs to those who repent and cling to God's precepts; forgiveness of sin comes through faith; and through the grace of faith the cleansing of crimes is received; the cross of the Lord is life to those who believe, but a precipice to those who do not believe. And elsewhere: The cross, then, is a reproach to the faithless; but to the faithful it is grace, to the faithful it is redemption, to the faithful it is resurrection.

units.la: Atque hæc omnia pulcerrima lucis similitudine illustrat alio loco. Nam Christus lux mundi est, sufficiens quidem illuminandis & conuertendis omnibus hominibus, non tamen actu & opere ipso tenebras omnes dispellens: sed vt ipse ait: Ego sum lux mundi, vt nullus qui venit ad me, maneat in tenebris. Ambrosij verba hæc sunt: Quamuis diffusa in omnes & super omnes potestate sit, qui omnibus artus ex virgine est, & bonis & malis: sicut & solem solem suum oriri iubet super bonos & malos: illum tamen fouet, qui appropinquat sibi. Sicut enim a se fulgorem solis excludit, qui fenestras clauserit: ita auersus a sole iustitia non potest splendorem eius adspicere: In tenebris ambulat, & in omnium luce ipse sibi causa est caecitatis: Aperi ergo oculos vt videas orientem tibi solem iustitiae. Nunquid si quis ostia domus suae claudat, solis est culpa, quod non illuminet domum eius?
units.tr: He illustrates all these points most beautifully, in another place, by the likeness of light. For Christ is the light of the world, sufficient indeed to enlighten and convert all men, yet not actually dispelling all darkness by his own work; but, as he himself says: "I am the light of the world, so that no one who comes to me may remain in darkness." These are the words of Ambrose: Although his power is poured out over all and above all, he who was born of a virgin for all, both good and bad, nevertheless cherishes him who draws near to him, just as he bids his sun rise upon the good and the bad. For as one who has closed the windows shuts out the light of the sun from himself, so justice, turned away from the sun, cannot look upon its brightness. He walks in darkness, and in the light of all he is himself the cause of his blindness. Open your eyes, then, that you may see the sun of righteousness rising for you. If someone shuts the doors of his house, is it the sun's fault that it does not light his house?

units.la: Ex Augustino, principe orthodoxorum, inter alia haec nobis suppetunt testimonia. Tomo 7, ad articulos aliquot falso ipsi impositos, Ad articulum primum, qui erat quod Christus non pro omnium hominum redemtione esset passus, distinctione adhibita ad hunc modum de tota controuersia pronunciat: Quod ad magnitudinem & potentia pretij, & quod ad vnam pertinet causam generis humani, sanguis Christi est redemtio totius mundi. Sed qui hoc seculum sine fide Christi & sine regeneratione sacramento pertranseunt, redemtionis alieni sunt. Cum itaque per vnam omnium naturam & omnium causam a Domino nostro in veritate susceptam, redemti omnes nes recte dicantur: non tamen omnes captiui-tate sint eruti, redemtionis proprietas haud dubie penes illos est de quibus Princeps huius mundi missus est foras, & iam non vasa Diaboli sed membra sunt IesuChristi. Cuius mors non ita impensa est generi humano vt adredemtione eius etiam qui regenerandi non sunt, pertinerent, sed ita, vt quod per vnicum exemplum gestum est pro vniuersis, per singulare sacramentu celebraretur in singulis. Poculum quippe immortalitatis, quod confectum est de infirmitate nostra & virtute diuina (Christi mortem intellige) habet quidem in se vt omnibus prosit, sed si non bibitur non proficit.
units.tr: From Augustine, the prince of the orthodox, the following testimonies, among others, are available to us. In the seventh volume, in answer to some articles falsely imposed on him, Against the first article, which was that Christ did not suffer for the redemption of all men, he pronounces on the whole controversy in the following way, with a distinction: As to the greatness and the power of the price, and as to the one cause of the human race, the blood of Christ is the redemption of the whole world. But those who pass through this age without faith in Christ and without the sacrament of regeneration belong to a redemption that is not theirs. Since, therefore, all are rightly said to be redeemed through the one nature of all and the one cause of all, which our Lord truly assumed, yet not all have been rescued from captivity, the proper possession of redemption undoubtedly belongs to those over whom the prince of this world has been cast out, and who are no longer vessels of the Devil but members of Jesus Christ. His death was not so applied to the human race that those who are not to be regenerated would also belong to his redemption; rather, what was done once, by a single example, for all, is celebrated in each individual by a unique sacrament. For the cup of immortality, which has been prepared from our weakness and God's power (understand the death of Christ), has indeed in itself the power to benefit all; but if it is not drunk, it does not profit.

units.la: Contra Faustum Manichaeum lib.11. cap.7.
units.tr: Against Faustus the Manichaean, book 11, chapter 7.

units.la: Eorum pro quibus Christus mortuus est & resurrexit, & qui iam non sibi sed illi viuunt, hoc est, populi innouati per fidem, vt habeat interim in se quod in re postea perficiatur, eorum (inquit) neminem amplius secundum carnem nouerat. Conuertibiliter hic sumit, innouatos per fidem, seruandos, & eos pro quibus Christus mortuus est & resurrexit.
units.tr: Of those for whom Christ died and rose, and who now live not to themselves but to him, that is, the people renewed through faith, so that in the meantime they may have in themselves what will afterwards be perfected in reality, of these, he says, he knew no one any longer according to the flesh. Here he takes the renewed through faith, the saved, and those for whom Christ died and rose as interchangeable terms.

units.la: De trinitate lib.13. cap.15. negat quam eorum quos Christus fuso suo sanguine redemerit, peccatorum reti- bus inuolutos ad secundæ ac sempi- ternæ mortis exitium trahi à Diabolo: & carnis tantum, non spiritus morte, mori tales affirmat. Apertissime dam- nandos redetione summouet: additq; statim expressis verbis, præcognitos, prædestinatos & electos ante constitutionem mundi, ad Christi gratiam pertinere, & pro illis Christum mortuum.
units.tr: In his book On the Trinity, book 13, chapter 15, he denies that those whom Christ redeemed with his poured-out blood, entangled in the nets of sin, are dragged by the Devil to the ruin of the second and eternal death; and he affirms that such people die only in the flesh, not in the spirit. He most clearly removes them from redemption, though they are to be condemned; and he adds at once, in express words: those foreknown, predestined and elect before the foundation of the world belong to the grace of Christ, and Christ died for them.

units.la: Idem in Psal. 21. scribit, Christum passum propter Ecclesiam, & Ecclesiam magnā totum esse orbem pro quo sanguinem suum illefuderit.
