Ne contristetis Spiritum, quo obsignati estis in diem redemptionis. 2. Cor. 1. Deus est, qui obsignauit nos, deditque arrhabonem Spiritus in cordibus nostris. En Spiritus sanctus, qui datur omnibus Christi fidelibus (nam qui Spiritum Christi non habet non est eius) instar diuini signaculi & arrhabonis minimè sal-
units.tr: There remains a third way by which God reveals election to his saints, namely through the sealing of the Holy Spirit in our hearts, according to the words of Eph. 1: After you believed, you were sealed with that Holy Spirit of promise, who is the pledge of our inheritance, until we are set free to be redeemed etc. And in ch. 4: Do not grieve the Holy Spirit, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption. 2 Cor. 1: It is God who sealed us and gave the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts. Behold the Holy Spirit, who is given to all Christ's faithful (for whoever does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his). Like a divine seal and pledge, he is by no means deceptive,

units.la: Rom. 8. fallacis, certos non reddit de hæreditate nostra in cœlis: & per consequens, quod & nomina nostra in libro vitæ scripta sint in cœlis.
units.tr: [Rom. 8.] and he does not fail to make us certain of our inheritance in heaven; and consequently he also makes us certain that our names are written in the book of life in heaven.

units.la: Eodem pertinent dulcissimæ sententiæ, quibus metaphoræ istæ alibi explicantur. 1. Ioh. 4. Per hoc cognoscimus nos in Deo habitare, & ipsum in nobis, quod de spiritu suo dedit nobis. 1. Cor. 2. Accepimus spiritum à Deo, vt sciamus quæ Deus nobis donauit. Rom. 8. Si spiritus eius, qui suscitauit Iesum à mortuis, habitat in vobis, is qui Christum excitauit ex mortuis, etiam vi-ficabit mortalia corpora vestra, per inhabi-tantem eius spiritum in vobis. Et sequitur idem locus vere aureus, ac in primis diligenter in toto hoc negocio consi-derandus: Si Spiritu actiones corporis mor-tificetis, viuetis, inquit. Quotquot enim Spi-ritu Dei ducuntur, ij sunt filij Dei. Non enim accepistis spiritum seruitutis rursus ad me-tum, sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis, per quem clamamus, Abba pater: qui ipse spiri-tus vna cum spiritu nostro testatur nos esse fi-lios Dei: quod si filij, etiam hæredes: hæredes quidem Dei, cohæredes autem Christi.
units.tr: To the same point belong the sweetest sayings by which these metaphors are explained elsewhere. 1 John 4: By this we know that we abide in God and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. 1 Cor. 2: We have received the Spirit from God, that we may know what God has freely given us. Rom. 8: If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you. And the same passage follows, truly golden, and above all to be carefully considered in this whole matter: If by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live, he says. For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are sons of God. For you have not received the spirit of bondage to fear again, but you have received the spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit himself, together with our spirit, testifies that we are children of God; and if children, then also heirs: heirs indeed of God, and co-heirs with Christ.

units.la: Demonstratio Apostoli talis est: Qui-cunque sunt filij Dei, consequentur haereditatem regni coelorum. Nam sicut filij etiam haeredes. Sed quicunque regutur Spiritu sancto, sunt filij Dei. Ergo quicunque regutur Spiritu sancto, consequentur haereditatem regni coelorum.
units.tr: The Apostle's argument is this: Whoever are sons of God will obtain the inheritance of the kingdom of heaven. For if sons, then also heirs. But whoever are led by the Holy Spirit are sons of God. Therefore whoever are led by the Holy Spirit will obtain the inheritance of the kingdom of heaven.

units.la: Assumptio tripliciter in textu probatur. i. Quia Spiritus est adoptionis, ad obsignandam nempe adoptionem in renatis: de his enim loquitur. Caeteroquin satis constat multa esse dona Spiritus sancti communia pijs & impijs, electis & reprobis. ii. cum dicit, in quo clamamus, Abba pater: idem probat a confessione piorum, Deum ut patrem invocantium: prout etiam a Domino instructi sumus in precationis Christianae exordio: pater noster qui es in coelis. Hoc autem dicunt & clamant pij, non tam sono vocis quam intentione cordis, quae ex conueniente filijs Dei fiducia oritur.
units.tr: The minor premise is proved from the text in three ways. First, because the Spirit is the Spirit of adoption, namely to seal adoption in the reborn, for it is of these that he speaks. Otherwise it is quite plain that there are many gifts of the Holy Spirit common to the godly and the ungodly, the elect and the reprobate. Second, when he says by whom we cry, Abba, Father, he proves the same from the confession of the godly, who call upon God as Father, as we too were taught by the Lord at the beginning of Christian prayer: Our Father, who art in heaven. The godly say and cry this not so much with the sound of the voice as with the intention of the heart, which arises from that trust which befits the children of God.

units.la: iii. Ne quis forte suspicetur quod in confessione nostra decipiamur, idem confirmat testimonio Spiritus sancti. Ipse enim Spiritus testatur nos esse filios lios Dei, & hoc non ad aures hominū, quemadmodum pater testabatur de suo filio, sed ad cor hominis; quia vt alibi scribit Apostolus, diffunditur caritas Dei in cordibus nostris per Spiritū sanctum, qui datus est nobis. Vnde Spiritus gratiæ apud Prophetam nuncupatur, propter gratiæ & miserationis diuinæ in animis nostris testificatione. Hoc autem testimonio Spiritus nihil est firmius. Neque enim fallitur Spiritus Dei, qui omnia scrutatur, etiam profunditates Dei. Neque fallit; vt pote verax, & ducens in omnem veritatem.
units.tr: Third, lest anyone perhaps suspect that we are deceived in our confession, he confirms it by the testimony of the Holy Spirit. For the Spirit himself testifies that we are children of God, and he does so not to the ears of men, as the Father testified concerning his Son, but to the heart of man. For, as the Apostle writes elsewhere, the love of God is poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us. Hence the Spirit is called by the Prophet the Spirit of grace, on account of the testimony of divine grace and mercy in our souls. Nothing is firmer than this testimony of the Spirit. For the Spirit of God, who searches all things, even the depths of God, is not deceived; nor does he deceive, since he is true and leads into all truth.

units.la: Hæc de electionis reuelatione ex verbo Dei desumta & plana sunt. Idcirco falsò à quibusdam insimulamur, quasi absque verbo ad electionem accedere gestiamus.
units.tr: These things about the revelation of election, taken from the Word of God, are clear. Therefore we are falsely accused by some of eagerly seeking election without the Word.

units.la: Aduersus calumniam istam aperte profitemur, quòd semota omni curiositate & periculosis quæstionib. de arcanis Dei consilijs, nō nisi ex verbi Dei prescripto percontemur beneuolam ipsius erga nos voluntatem & caritatem, qua
units.tr: Against this calumny we openly profess that, setting aside all curiosity and dangerous questions about the secret counsels of God, we inquire only according to what is prescribed in the Word of God into his benevolent will and love towards us, by which

units.la: Zach. 12. Ioh. 16 & Ephes. 2. Hub. thef. nu. qua elegit nos in Christo ante tempora saecularia. Et ne dubites, Christiane lector, en tibi duorum praestantissimorum, qui praedestinationis doctrinam diligentissime inculcarunt, scriptorum, ea de re testimonia: Calvini in quam & Lutheri. Sic ergo Cal. lib.3. Instit. cap. 24. §.3. ut certi de salute nostra fiamus, initium a verbo Dei fieri debet, eoque debemus ad fiduciam nostram esse contenti, ut Deum partem innocemus. Praepostere enim quidam, ut de consilio Dei (quod nobis prope est in ore et in corde) certiores reddantur, supra nubes volitare cupiunt. Cohibenda est illa temeritas sobrietate fidei: ut Deus occulta sua gratia testis nobis sufficiat in externo verbo. Et parag. sequenti: optimum tenebimus ordinem, si in quaerenda electionis nostra certitudine, in iis signis posterioribus, quae sunt certa eius testificationes, haeream us, nec extra viam electionem nostram inquiramus. Extra viam inquirere voco, ubi in abditos divina sapientia recessus perrumpere homuncio conatur, ut intelligat quid de se fit constitutum apud Dei tribunal. Sed quemadmodum in exitialem abyssum se ingurgitat gurgitant, qui vt de fui electione fiant certiores, æternum Dei consilium sine verbo percontantur: ita qui recte atque ordine ipsam inuestigant, qualiter in verbo continetur, maximum inde referunt consolationis fructum.
units.tr: [Zech. 12.; John 16; Eph. 2.; Hub. thef. nu.] he chose us in Christ before the ages of the world. And so that you may not doubt, Christian reader, here are the testimonies on this matter of two most distinguished writers who most diligently inculcated the doctrine of predestination: Calvin's and Luther's. Thus Calvin, Institutes 3, ch. 24, §3: In order that we may be made certain of our salvation, the beginning must be made from the Word of God, and we ought to be content with that for our confidence, so that we do not do God wrong. For some people, wishing to be more certain of God's counsel (which is near us, in our mouth and in our heart), are preposterously eager to fly above the clouds. That rashness must be restrained by the sobriety of faith, so that God, by his hidden grace, may suffice for us as witness in the external Word. And in the following paragraph: We shall hold the best order if, in seeking the certainty of our election, we cling to those later signs which are the sure testimonies of it, and do not seek our election outside the way. I call it seeking outside the way when a little man tries to break into the hidden recesses of divine wisdom, so as to understand what has been decided about himself before God's tribunal. But just as those who, in order to become more certain of their election, inquire into God's eternal counsel without the Word plunge themselves into a deadly abyss, so those who investigate it rightly and in order, as it is contained in the Word, derive from it the greatest fruit of consolation.

units.la: Lutherus vero hac ipsa de re agens in Gen. cap. 26. ad hunc modum scribit: Eiusmodi cogitationes quæ supra aut extra revelationem Dei sublimius aliquid rimantur, prorsus diabolicæ sunt, quibus nihil amplius proficitur quam vt in exitium nos ipsos precipitemus, quia obiciunt obiectum imperuestigabile, videlicet Deum non revelatum. Et multis ibidem taxat horribilem, vt ipse loquitur, morbum, quo homines in inquisitione Dei procedere volunt specu-latiue, & ruunt tandem in desperationem & contemtum. Contra autem docet Lutherus, ex fide in Christum, & fructibus veræ fidei, iudicium hoc pendere, an sis prædestinatus: inquiens, si filium audieris, & in nomen eius baptizatus fueris, & verbum eius diligis, tum certo es prædestinatus, & certus de tua salute. Item, si credis in Deum revelatum, & recipis verbum bum eius, paulatim etiam abscoditum Deum intelliges, imo iam de praesenti intelligis. Et aliquibus interiectis: de Deo certo & indubitater statuere debes, cum tibi esse propitium propter Christum, te redemtum & sanctificatum esse pretioso sanguine filij Dei: atque ita de praedestinatione tua eris certus, remotis omnibus curiosis & periculosis quaestionibus de arcanis consiliis Dei. En habes filium, qui credit & baptizatur, is in libro vitae scriptus est, &c.
units.tr: Luther, treating this very matter in his commentary on Genesis chapter 26, writes in this way: "Thoughts of this kind, which probe something more lofty above or beyond the revelation of God, are wholly diabolical. They accomplish nothing except to hurl us headlong into ruin, because they set before us an unsearchable object, namely God as he has not revealed himself." He also condemns at length the dreadful disease, as he calls it, by which people want to proceed in the inquiry into God in a speculative way, and at last fall into despair and contempt. On the other hand, Luther teaches that the judgement whether you are predestined depends on faith in Christ and the fruits of true faith. He says: "If you have heard the Son, and have been baptized into his name, and love his word, then you are certainly predestined and certain of your salvation." Likewise: "If you believe in God as revealed, and receive his word, you will gradually understand even the hidden God; indeed, you already understand him in the present." And after some words in between: "You ought to determine firmly and without doubt concerning God, that for Christ's sake he is gracious to you, and that you have been redeemed and sanctified by the precious blood of the Son of God. In this way you will be certain of your predestination, with all curious and dangerous questions about the secret counsels of God set aside. Behold, you have the Son: whoever believes and is baptized is written in the book of life," and so on.

units.la: Atque hanc viam inquirendae electionis nostrae a posteriore, eleganter comparat cum visione Mosis, cui petenti ut faciem Dei videret, respondit Dominus: Posteriora mea tibi ostendam: faciem autem meam videre non potes. Quasi unicuique nostrum Deus dicat, Luth. interprete: Ego tibi praescientiam & praedestinationem egregie manifestabo, sed non via naturalis speculationis, & sapientia carnalis: ex Deo non revelato fiam revelatus: & tamen idem Deus manebo. Mittam filium meum, hunc audito, hunc aspice, quid is faciat, quid loquatur: si hunc audieris, certo es praedestinatus. De hac visione Domini visur-pare
units.tr: And this way of inquiring into our election from what comes after, he neatly compares with the vision of Moses, who asked to see the face of God, and the Lord answered: "I will show you my back parts, but you cannot see my face." As if the Lord were saying to each of us, as Luther interprets it: "I will plainly reveal to you my foreknowledge and predestination, but not by the natural way of speculation or by carnal wisdom. From the God who is not revealed I shall become revealed, and yet I shall remain the same God. I will send my Son; hear him, look upon him, see what he does and what he says. If you hear him, you are certainly predestined."

units.la: Exod.33. pare est illud Bernardi: O vere quietis locus, visio ista no terret, sed mulcet: inquietam curiositatem non excitat, sed sedat: nec fatigat sed tranquillat: hic vere quiescitur, tranquillus Deus tranquillat omnia, & quietum assi-cere, quiescere est.
units.tr: Concerning this vision of the Lord, Exod. 33. It is fitting to borrow the saying of Bernard: "O truly a place of rest! This vision does not terrify but soothes; it does not stir up restless curiosity but calms it; it does not weary but tranquillizes. Here one truly rests; the tranquil God brings tranquillity to all things, and to make a person quiet is to give rest."

units.la: Porrò non omittenda est & hæc admonitio, quod fi quis signa ista posteriora, de quibus dictum est, nec dum apud fe ipsum deprehendat, nequaquâ propterea de fui prædestinatione ad vitam desperare debere. Sunt enim xii. horæ diei, & qui prima luce, aut circa horam tertiam non est vocatus, potest hora sexta vel nona, forte & vndecima, diuinæ vocationis fieri particeps. Quâquam nostrum interim non est pœnitentiam differre, sicut scriptum est: Ne tardes conuerti ad Dominum, neque differas de die in diem subito enim veniet ira eius & in tempore vindicta disperdet te. Et Pfal.95. Hodie fi vocem eius audieritis, ne obturate corda vestra.
units.tr: Moreover, this admonition must not be omitted: if anyone does not yet find in himself those later signs of which we have spoken, he ought by no means on that account to despair of his predestination to life. For there are twelve hours of the day, and whoever was not called at first light, or about the third hour, may still become a partaker of the divine calling at the sixth or ninth hour, perhaps even at the eleventh. Nevertheless, meanwhile it is not for us to postpone repentance, as it is written: "Do not delay to turn to the Lord, nor put it off from day to day; for his wrath will come suddenly, and in the time of vengeance he will destroy you." And in Ps. 95: "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts."

units.la: CAPVT XXV.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXV.

units.la: Quid de aliorum electione sentire nos conueniat.
units.tr: What we ought to think about the election of others.

units.la: PRÆTEREA ex fundamétis quæ de electionis noftrę certitudine adhuc exposita sût, nô difficile est iudicare, quid homini Christiano de aliorum in Christo electione fentiédum fit, fecundum legem Christi, hoc est, caritatis. Nimirum, debemus non solùm de nostri in Christo præde ftinatione certi esse, verùm etiam idem de fratribus nostris in Christo statuere: de alijs autem nô desperare, ante obitum præsertim supremaque funera.
units.tr: Furthermore, from the foundations that have been set out so far concerning the certainty of our own election, it is not difficult to judge what a Christian ought to think about the election of others in Christ, according to the law of Christ, that is, of love. Surely we ought not only to be certain of our own predestination in Christ, but also to judge the same about our brothers in Christ; yet we should not despair of others, especially before death and the last funeral rites.

units.la: Discernimus hic inter fratres, qui eandem fidem nobiscum colunt, & extraneos, qui infideles adhuc & à sociétate sanctæ fraternitatis alieni exiftút.
units.tr: Here we distinguish between brothers, who hold the same faith with us, and outsiders, who are still unbelievers and stand apart from the fellowship of the holy brotherhood.

units.la: Quod ad fratres, quamvis non eadem de alijs, qua de seipso certitudine, homo fidelis statuere potest, debet tamen pro electis ipsos reputare & agnoscere, quantifper contrarium non liquet. Ratio est, quia fides & conuersio inindicia sunt electionis. Proinde quos fidei & conuersionis iudicamus consortes, eos etiam in electione comprehendamus necesse est. Et huius iudicij Apostolos Domini habemus auctores r. Pet.1.AdEph.1.&1.Thess.1.vbi ait Paulus: Scimus fratres electi, vos electos a Deo, quoniam Euangelium nostrum constitit apud vos non locutione duntaxat, sed virtute, cum in Spiritu Sancto tum in perfuasione multa. Et 1. Thes. 1. Gratias Deo agere debemus, fratres, dilecti a Domino, quoniam elegit vos Deus ad salutem ab initio per sanctificationem Spiritus, & fidem habitam veritati.
units.tr: As for brothers, although a faithful person cannot have the same certainty about others as about himself, he ought nevertheless to regard and acknowledge them as elect, so long as nothing shows the contrary. The reason is that faith and conversion are signs of election. Therefore those whom we judge to share in faith and conversion must necessarily be included in election as well. We have the Apostles of the Lord as authors of this judgment: 1 Pet. 1; Eph. 1; and 1 Thess. 1, where Paul says: "We know, brothers beloved of God, that you are elect, because our gospel came to you not in word only but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit and in much assurance." And 1 Thess. 1: "We ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers beloved by the Lord, because God chose you for salvation from the beginning, through the sanctification of the Spirit and faith in the truth."

units.la: At contingit multos tales gratia excidere. Resp. Nihil refert: quia iudicium hoc de aliis non tam est certitudinis quam caritatis. Quippe nemo alteri, sicut sibi quisquam notus est. Quis enim hominum novit ea quae sunt hominis, nisi spiritus hominis, qui est in eo? Homo tantum inspicit quae sunt prae oculis: at Deus quae in corde. Inde Aug. de Trinitate lib. 13. cap. 2. Suam quisque fidem apud sei ipsum videt: in altero aute credit eam esse, non videt; & tanto firmius credit, quanto frufructus eius magis novit, quos operari solet fides per dilectionem.
units.tr: But it happens that many such people fall away from grace. Answer: It makes no difference, because this judgment about others is less a matter of certainty than of love. Indeed no one knows another as he knows himself. For who among men knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man that is in him? Man looks only at what is before his eyes, but God at what is in the heart. Hence Augustine, On the Trinity book 13, chapter 2: "Each person sees his own faith within himself; but in another he believes it is there and does not see it; and he believes it all the more firmly, the more he knows its fruits, which faith usually produces through love."

units.la: „ Quoniam igitur caritas omnia cre-„ dit, omnia sperat, hinc sane fit, ut licet „ multi sint vocati, pauci vero electi, se-„ cundum caritatem tamen plane dicantur „ credentes, couerfi, iustificati, redemti, „ sanctificati, discipuli & membra Christi templa & filij Dei, imo electi Dei, ij qui eandem nobiscum fidem & conuersa-tione Christianam profitentur, vt tua-pud Deum, qui cogitationes & concep-„ tiones cordis dijudicat, sepe non sint, „ quod vocantur.
units.tr: "Since therefore love believes all things and hopes all things, it certainly follows that, although many are called and few are chosen, nevertheless, according to love, those who profess the same faith with us and a Christian way of life are plainly to be called believers, converted, justified, redeemed, sanctified, disciples and members of Christ, temples and sons of God, indeed elect of God; and yet, in the sight of God, who judges the thoughts and conceptions of the heart, they are often not what they are called."

units.la: Quod autem ad eos qui foris sunt, cum repente ex Saule euaserit Paulus, nullius desperanda est conuersio, eo-que nec salus & electio. Quam multi quotidie conuertuntur? Quam multi praedestinati, etsi nondum congregati? Sed nouit illos qui praedestinauit: nouit qui redimere sanguine suo venit, ait Augustinus Serm. 50. de verbis Domini in Ioh. Quapropter etiam nos, vt idem scribit de Corrept. & grat. cap. 15. nescien-tes quis pertineat ad praedestinatorum numerum, quis non, sic affici debemus caritatis affectu, vt omnes velimus salvos fieri, pro infidelibus orando & singulos vt occurrerit, docendo, exhortando. Atque haec de divinae electionis certitudine quantum ad nos.
units.tr: As for those who are outside, since Paul was suddenly turned from Saul, no one's conversion is to be despaired of, and therefore neither is his salvation or election. How many are converted every day? How many are predestined, even if not yet gathered in? But he knows those whom he predestined; he knows the one who came to redeem with his own blood, as Augustine says in Sermon 50, on the words of the Lord in John. Therefore we too, as he writes in On Correction and Grace, chapter 15, not knowing who belongs to the number of the predestined and who does not, ought to be so moved by the affection of love that we wish all to be saved: praying for unbelievers, and teaching and exhorting each one as opportunity arises. And this is enough about the certainty of divine election as far as we are concerned.

units.la: VLTIMA PARS, VSVS videlicet doctrinae de praedestinatione, contra illos, qui ab eius praedicatione tanquam non modo non salutari, verum etiam periculosa & aedificationi contraria, abstinendum censent. CAPVT XXVI. Recitatur & refellitur iam dictus error.
units.tr: THE LAST PART, namely the use of the doctrine of predestination, against those who judge that it should be avoided in preaching, as not only unhelpful but also dangerous and opposed to edification. CHAPTER 26. The error just mentioned is set out and refuted.

units.la: DOCTRINA praedestinationis nati nis qua & qualis sit, explicatum est. Quoniam vero nonnulli omnem eius mentionem, apud vulgus praesertim, tanquam vtilitati aedificationis inimicam, reformidare solent: haec quoque opinio minuenda est. Qua eadem opera & vsus co-
units.tr: We have explained what the doctrine of predestination is and what kind of doctrine it is. But since some people usually shrink from any mention of it, especially among the common people, as hostile to the benefit of edification, this opinion too must be diminished. By the same token the use of this doctrine will also become plain, and how it is to be preached so that it benefits the hearers.

units.la: doctrinæ huius patescit, & quomodo fit prædicanda, quo vtilitatem afferat audientibus.
units.tr: ...of this doctrine, and how it is to be preached so that it benefits the hearers.

units.la: Testatur sanè Prosperi Epistola de reliquijs Pelagianæ hæreseos, multos feruorum Christi in Maffilienfi vrbe, eosque egregios in omnium virtutum studio, nisi quòd à Pelagianæ impietatis Spiritu eludi fe patiebantur, editis ab Auguft. scriptis quibusdam contra Pelagianos, quibus multa inseruerat de prædestinatione, vt hac ratione defenderet gratiam Dei non fecundum merita nostra dari, sed fecundum propositum voluntatis Dei; ita offensos fuisse, vt Augustini, & aliorum recte de hoc sentientium fidemædificationi contrariam esse definirent, ideoque etiamsi vera effet, non promendam sed silentio potius premenda im, dicerent. Idem Hilarius, non ille Pictauiensis, sed Arelatensis Episcopus, sua ad Augustinum Epistola, non solum de Maffiliensibus, sed de alijs etiam fratribus in Gallia referт.
units.tr: Prosper's letter on the remnants of the Pelagian heresy testifies that many fervent followers of Christ in the city of Marseilles, men outstanding in their zeal for every virtue, were offended, unless they allowed themselves to be deceived by the spirit of Pelagian impiety, by certain writings of Augustine against the Pelagians, into which he had inserted much about predestination, so that by this means he might defend the view that the grace of God is given not according to our merits but according to the purpose of God's will. They were so offended that they judged the faith of Augustine and of others who thought rightly on this point to be contrary to edification, and therefore, even if it were true, they said it should not be brought forward but rather kept under silence. Hilary likewise, not the one of Poitiers but the bishop of Arles, in his letter to Augustine, reports this not only of the Massilians but also of other brethren in Gaul.

units.la: Mouebanturautem his potissimum ratiorationibus. 1. Quod doctrina hæc gratiæ & prædestinationis Dei, occulto iudicio, sed opere manifesto, aliud vas condentis ad honorem, & aliud in contumeliam, videatur omnem remouere industriam in hominibus. Cum enim cogitent, à prædestinatione pendere omnia, qui crediturisint, qui non, qui saluandi, qui damnandi, & cå quidem immutabili, vt neq; reiectus vlla industria possit intrare, neq; electus vlla negligentia possit excidere, in torporem verti, vt à labore proclives ad libidinem post concupiscentias suas eant.
units.tr: Moreover, they were moved chiefly by these reasons. (1) This doctrine of the grace and predestination of God, by a hidden judgement yet manifest in its working, that the Maker makes one vessel to honour and another to dishonour, seems to remove all industry from men. For since they think that everything depends on predestination (who will believe, who will not, who is to be saved, who condemned), and that this is so by an immutable decision, so that the rejected cannot enter by any industry and the elect cannot fall away by any negligence, men are turned into torpor. From labour they incline to lust and go after their desires.

units.la: Periculum etiam esse aiebant, ne correptiones & exhortationes repesceret. Dicturos enim inobedientes, cur corripimur, accusamur, arguimur? Cuius vult miseretur, & quem vult, indurat. Munus obedientiæ non accepimus. Quid adhuc succenset? voluntati eius quis resistet? Huc accedunt quæ superius obiecta & soluta sunt, de auctore peccati, de fatali necessitate, & quicquid præterea in veritatis inuidiam excogitauit Dei ignara & peruicax ratio.
units.tr: They also said there was a danger that it would encourage disobedience to rebukes and exhortations. For the disobedient will say: why are we rebuked, accused, convicted? "He has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens." We have not received the office of obedience. Why does he still find fault? Who can resist his will? To this are added the matters objected to and answered above, about the author of sin, about fatal necessity, and whatever else the ignorant and stubborn reason of men has devised out of envy of the truth.

units.la: Propter hæc igitur & similia, olim fratres illi per Galliam, etiam qui orthodoxorum de gratia & prædeft. sententiam improbare non audebant, e re Ecclesiæ fore iudicabant, si doctrina tam dura carni, in gratiam infirmiorum & capere non valentium, omitteretur: & addebant exemplum aliorum patrū ante Augustinum, quos dicebant, non minus vtiliter sine hac definitione tot annos, cum contra alios, tum maxime contra Pelagianos catholicam fidem defendisse. Nihil ergo opus fuisse huiusmodi disputationis incerto, totmi-nus intelligentium corda turbari: suffi-cere hanc definitionem ac professione, omnem quidem hominē Adamo pec-cante peccasse, & neminem per opera sua, sed per Dei gratiam regeneratione saluari: vniuersis tamen hominibus propitiationem per sanguinem Chri-sti sine exceptione esse propositam, & neminem prorsus à redemtione eius exceptum, vt qui voluerint, fiant filij Dei, & inexcusabiles sint, qui fideles es-se noluerint: quia iustitia Dei in eo sit, vt qui non crediderit, pereat: bonitas in hoc spectetur, si indifferenter vniuersos velit saluos fieri, & ad agnitionem veritatis venire, vita æterna quantum ad ipsum, parata omnibus, licet quantum ad arbitrij libertatem alij eam side arripiant, alij incredulitate repudient. Qui porrò credituri sint, & in fide mansuri, præsciesse ante mundi constitutionem Deum, & eos prædestinasse in regnum suum, reiectis contrà aliis.
units.tr: On account of these and similar things, those brethren throughout Gaul, even those who did not dare to disapprove of the orthodox view on grace and predestination, judged that it would be for the good of the Church if so hard a doctrine, hard for the flesh, were left out for the sake of the weaker ones who cannot grasp it. They added the example of the Fathers before Augustine, who, they said, had for so many years defended the catholic faith no less usefully without this definition, both against other opponents and especially against the Pelagians. Therefore there was no need for a dispute of this uncertain kind, which would disturb the hearts of all who understand. It was enough to profess this definition: that every man sinned when Adam sinned, and that no one is saved by his own works but by God's grace through regeneration. Yet propitiation through the blood of Christ is set forth to all men without exception, and no one whatever is excluded from his redemption, so that those who wish may become children of God, and those who are unwilling to be faithful are without excuse. For the justice of God lies in this, that whoever does not believe shall perish; his goodness is seen in this, that he indifferently wills all to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth. Eternal life, as far as he is concerned, is ready for all, although, as far as freedom of the will goes, some grasp it by faith and others reject it by unbelief. But that those who will believe and remain in faith were foreknown by God before the foundation of the world, and that he predestined them into his kingdom while the rest were rejected.

units.la: Veruntamen opinio hæcsquæ & suos hodie fautores habet, quorum alij tantum non sepeliri iubent omnem prædestinationis mentionem: alij verò in scholis quidem & inter doctos de ea tractari posse concedunt, sed apud plebem in concionibus proponendam esse negant: nullo negocio refelli potest. Neque enim nos decet sapientiores esse ipso Christo, eiusque Apostolis & sanctis Prophetis, qui omnes veram de prædestinatione doctrinam, vt ut carni dura videatur, libere testificati sunt, doctis & indoctis. Verbi gratia: Christus dixit, Multi vocati, pauci electi. Et iterum:
units.tr: Yet this opinion, which has its supporters today, some of whom would have every mention of predestination simply buried, while others concede that it may be treated in the schools and among the learned but deny that it should be set forth to the common people in sermons, can be refuted without any trouble. For it does not befit us to be wiser than Christ himself, and his apostles and holy prophets, who all freely testified to the true doctrine of predestination, to learned and unlearned alike, however hard it may seem to the flesh. For example, Christ said: Many are called, few are chosen. And again:

units.la: Omne quod dat mihi pater, venit ad me. Oues meæ vocem meam audiunt, sed vos non creditis, quia non estis ex ovibus meis. Paulus certe ad Rom. non in angulum, sed in publicum, & coram toto mundo dicit: Non est volentis aut currentis, sed miserentis Dei, &c. Et iterum: Deus volens notam facere bonitatem suam, &c. Scilicet haec omnia talia sunt, si moderatoribus istis credimus, ut nihil possit inutilius dici. At inquam ego: Si Deus voluit talia palam dici & innulgari, nec spectari quid fiat quaeretur, aut quid sapientia carnis indeliberatura esseт: tu quis es o homo, qui vetes? Scilicet creator tuus à te creatura sua discet, quid utile, quid inutile sit praedicatu? Aut quod secundum sensum hominum, & quidem imperitorum, ne dicam saepe impiissimorum, tolerabile visum fuerit, id demum salutare erit: quod contra, id mox inutile & perniciosum reputabitur? Quid stultius, quàm Dei verbum ita subiicere hominum arbitrio? Sileat potius omnis terra à facie Domini, & adorent omnes incolae terrae verba oris eius.
units.tr: All that the Father gives me comes to me. My sheep hear my voice, but you do not believe, because you are not of my sheep. Paul, certainly, in Romans does not speak in a corner but in public and before the whole world: "It is not of him who wills or of him who runs, but of God who shows mercy," etc. And again: "God, willing to make known his goodness," etc. Clearly, if we believe those moderators, all these things are such that nothing could be said to be more useless. But I say: if God wished such things to be said openly and published, without asking what would happen or what the deliberating wisdom of the flesh would think, who are you, O man, to forbid it? Will your Creator learn from you, his creature, what is useful and what is useless to preach? Or will that be salutary which seemed tolerable to the sense of men, and indeed of the unskilled (not to say often most impious), while that which is contrary is at once reckoned useless and pernicious? What is more foolish than to subject the word of God in this way to the judgement of men? Let rather all the earth keep silence before the face of the Lord, and let all the inhabitants of the earth worship the words of his mouth.

units.la: „ marks in the left margin are dialogue markers, not text.
CAPVT XXVII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XXVII.

units.la: Doctrinam de prædestinatione utilem & necessariam esse: & solutiones eorum quæ obijciebantur.
units.tr: On the doctrine of predestination, that it is useful and necessary, and the answers to the objections raised against it.

units.la: Quæ igitur utilitas, aut quæ necessitas talia in publicum proferre suadet, cum tot inde mala & offendicula ad turbanda imperitorum corda oriri videantur?
units.tr: What usefulness, then, or what necessity urges us to proclaim such things in public, since so many evils and stumbling-blocks seem to arise from them, disturbing the hearts of the unlearned?

units.la: Resp. Satis quidem erat dicere, quia Deus sic voluit, in cuius voluntate simpliciter acquiescendum nobis est, data ei gloria, quod sit sapientissimus & iustissimus, nemini faciat iniuriam, nec stulte ac temere aliquid agere possit quicquid caro statuat. Etenim stultitia Dei sapientior est quam homines, & similiter iniustitia eius iustior quam homines. Hac responsione pij sunt contenti. Attamen ad maiorem confusionem erroris iam profligati, & ut nos in veritate magis instituamur, paucis ostendam, non solum utile, sed & necessarium esse, ut doctrina prædestinatione doceatur & conservetur in populo Christiano.
units.tr: Answer: It would indeed be enough to say that God willed it so, and that we must simply rest in his will, while ascribing to him the glory that he is most wise and most just, that he does wrong to no one, and that he cannot act foolishly or rashly, whatever flesh may decide. For the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and likewise his injustice is more just than men. The godly are content with this answer. Nevertheless, to further confound an error already overthrown, and so that we may be better instructed in the truth, I will show briefly that it is not only useful but also necessary that the doctrine of predestination be taught and preserved among the Christian people.

units.la: Prin-
units.tr: First-

units.la: Cap.27. DE DIVINA
units.tr: Chapter 27. On Divine Predestination

units.la: Principio quidem hoc vtile & ne-cessarium est hac de causa, vt verus De-us, qualem se in verbo suo patefecit, re-&è agnoscatur: videlicet, quòd cuius vult misereatur, &c quem vult induret, atque ex eadem massa faciat aliud qui-dem vas ad decus, aliud ad dedecus; hoc est præparatis à se vasis misericor-dię gratiam constituerit largiri indebi-tam, qua discreti à vitiata & damnata massa generis humani, seruarentur, cæ-teris in eadem massa perditionis dere-lictis & damnandis propter peccatum. quorum illud ad misericordiam, hoc ad iustitiam pertinet eius, cui miseri-cordiam & iudicium cantat Ecclesia.
units.tr: In the first place this is useful and necessary for this reason: that the true God, as he has revealed himself in his word, may be rightly acknowledged, namely that he has mercy on whom he wills, and hardens whom he wills, and from the same lump makes one vessel to honour and another to dishonour. That is, he has decided to bestow undeserved grace of mercy on the vessels he has prepared, by which they are set apart from the corrupted and condemned mass of the human race and saved, while the rest are left in that same mass of perdition and condemned on account of sin. The former belongs to his mercy, the latter to his justice, the God whose mercy and judgment the Church sings of.

units.la: Et quis est qui dicat ei, quare facis sic? Num dicet figmentum fictori, cur me facis sic? An non habet potestatem figulus in lutum? An oculus tuus malus est, quia Dominus bonus est? Talem Deum nobis sacra scriptu-ra prædicat. Spoliatus verò Deus, vt ser-uum arb. Luth. contendit, virtute & sapientia eligèdi, quid erit nisi idolum Fortunæ, cuius numine omnia temerè fiant? Et tandem eò venietur, vt homi-nes
units.tr: "And who is there who says to him, Why do you make me thus? Will the thing formed say to the one who formed it, Why have you made me so? Does not the potter have power over the clay? Is your eye evil because I am good?" Holy Scripture proclaims such a God to us. But if God is stripped, as Luther contends in his book on the bondage of the will, of the power and wisdom of choosing, what will he be but an idol of Fortune, by whose will everything happens at random? And in the end it will come to this: that men

units.la: Psal. 101. Dan. 4.32. Rom. 9. Matth. 20. cap. 14. nes salui fiant & damnentur ignorante Deo, vt qui non discreuerit certa electione saluandos & damnados, sed oblata omnibus generali bonitate & misericordia, hominibus reliquerit vtri velint salui fieri aut damnari, ipse interim forte ad conuiuium Æthiopum profectus, vt Homerus dicit de suo Ioue.
units.tr: Ps. 101. Dan. 4.32. Rom. 9. Matt. 20. ch. 14. are saved and damned with God ignorant of it. For he has not distinguished by a certain election those to be saved and those to be damned, but, offering general goodness and mercy to all, has left it to men to be saved or damned as they wish, while he himself has perhaps gone off to the feast of the Ethiopians, as Homer says of his Jove.

units.la: II. Prædicatu vtilis & necessaria est doctrina prædestinationis ad cognitionem gratiæ Dei contra Pelagianos, & Semipelagianos, atque ita ad humilia-tionem nostri, vt qui gloriatur, glorietur in Domino. Vidit hoc Augustinus de bono perseu. ca. 16.
units.tr: II. The doctrine of predestination is useful and necessary to preach, for the knowledge of God's grace against the Pelagians and Semipelagians, and so for our humbling, so that whoever glories may glory in the Lord. Augustine saw this in his book On the Gift of Perseverance, chapter 16.

units.la: Aut sic prædicanda est, inquit, prædestinatio, quemadmodum eam sacra scriptura euidenter loquitur, vt in prædestinatis sint sine pœnitentia, dona & vocatio Dei; aut gratiam Dei secundum merita nostra dari confitendum, quod sapiunt Pelagiani. Et capite sequenti. Non impediuntur exhortationes, si fides & perseuerantia, sicut & ipsa opera bona, esse Dei dona, eaque præcognita, id est, ad donandum prædestinata esse dicantur: sed impeditur potius, & subuertitur hac prædestinationis prædicatione il-le perniciosissimus error, quo dicitur gratia Dei secundum merita nostra dari, ut qui glo-riatur non in domino, sed in se ipso glorietur. Hinc idem cap.20. eiusdem libri, testa-tur copiosius de prædestinatione scri-bedi necessitatem sibi impositam propter Pelagianos, dicentes gratiam Dei secundū merita dari: quod nihil aliud est, ait, quàm gratiæ omnino negatio. Fingebant Pelagiani, gratiam om-nibus hominibus ex æquo offerri, & quantum ad Deum attinet, omnibus paratam vitam æternam: in hominum autem esse potestate, gratiā & salutem oblatam reijcere vel accipere. Nonul-los seruari, quia gratiam amplectantur tanquam ex se, & suo libero arbitrio: alios vero damnari, quia cum possint, nolint tamen oblatam gratiam recipe-re. Quid hoc aliud est, quàm gratiæ & prædestinationi pariter bellū mouere? Iam qui moderatiores ex ipsis videri volebant, & non tàm Pelagianissimum præ se ferebant, quàm occultè & quasi eminus tantummodò sequebantur, si-cut eut illæ reliquiæ Pelagianorum, de quibus Prosper & Hilarius, confitebantur quidem, ad nullum opus bonum vel incipiendum, nedum perficiendum, quemque sibi sufficere posse (tam esse prostratam hominis naturam) at aliquē tamen conatum & voluntatem, quæ tantum medicum quærat, non autem quicquam ipsa iam valeat, in homine corrupto restare volebant: nullam naturam ita depravatam vel extinctam putantes, vt nō debeat vel possit se velle sanari. Et hoc posito, talem videlicet omnibus remansisse voluntatem, qua vel contemnere quis valeat vel obedire, de compendio putabant rationem reddi electorum & reiectorum præscientia eligente creditu ros, & damnante incredulos.
units.tr: Either predestination, he says, must be preached just as Scripture plainly speaks of it, so that in the predestined the gifts and calling of God are without repentance; or we must confess that grace is given according to our merits, which is what the Pelagians hold. And in the following chapter: The exhortations are not hindered if faith and perseverance, like the good works themselves, are said to be gifts of God, and to have been foreknown, that is, predestined to be given. But that most pernicious error is rather hindered and overturned by this preaching of predestination, by which it is said that grace is given according to our merits, so that whoever glories should glory not in the Lord but in himself. Hence the same author, in chapter 20 of the same book, testifies at greater length that he was obliged to write about predestination because of the Pelagians, who said that grace is given according to merits; which, he says, is nothing other than the complete denial of grace. The Pelagians pretended that grace is offered equally to all men, and that as far as God is concerned eternal life is prepared for all, but that it is within men's power to reject or accept the grace and salvation offered. Some are saved, they said, because they embrace grace as coming from themselves and their own free will; others are damned because, though they could, they are unwilling to receive the grace offered. What is this, he asks, but to wage war equally on grace and on predestination? As for those more moderate Pelagians who wished to seem less so, and did not openly display the full Pelagian doctrine but followed it secretly and, as it were, from a distance, like those remnants of the Pelagians of whom Prosper and Hilary speak: they did confess that the nature of man has been so prostrated that no one is sufficient for himself to begin, much less to complete, any good work. Yet they wished that some effort and will remained in corrupted man, which seeks only a physician and by itself can accomplish nothing; for they thought no nature was so depraved or extinguished that it cannot, or ought not, to will to be healed. Granting this, they thought, namely that all have kept such a will by which a man is able either to despise or to obey, the reason why the elect are chosen and the rejected are rejected could briefly be given: God foresees who will believe and, choosing them, saves them, and who will not and so condemns them.

units.la: Cui errori nō absimile est, quod hae nostræ ætate quidam afferere tentant, vnicuique homini eas inesse vires, vt possit credere, nisi quod illi hoc vitium non ex vitiatæ naturæ qualibuscunque reliquijs, sed ex renouatione esse dicūt, quam nouo errore omnibus homini-bus bus, nemine excepto, commune esse statuunt. Quasi vero Deus tantum largiatur, ut credere possimus, ac non potius fidem ipsam, qua credentes ab incredulis discernuntur.
units.tr: Not unlike this error is what certain people in our own age try to assert: that every man has such powers that he is able to believe, except that they say this defect does not come from some remnants, of whatever kind, of corrupted nature, but from renewal. They lay down, by a new error, that this renewal is common to all men without exception. As if God bestows only so much that we are able to believe, and not rather the faith itself by which believers are distinguished from unbelievers.

units.la: Sed ut de eo nunc non laborem, hoc certum est, quamdiu aliquid in nobis esse dicimus, sive initium fidei, sive vsum bonum liberi arbitrij, aut etiam gratiæ illius communis, aut quicquid illud fit, quo à reliquis discernamur, præter solam Dei gratiam, semper concludent Pelagiani, gratiam secundum merita nostra dari: & cōcidet illud Cypriani. In nullo gloriandum, quia nihil nostrum est: Imo illud Apostoli. Quis te discernit? aut quid habes quod non accepisti? Nunquid enim per hæc dona, quæ sive ex natura sive per gratiam, omnibus communia sunt, homines ab hominibus discernuntur?
units.tr: But, not to labour on that point now, this is certain: as long as we say that something is in us, whether the beginning of faith, or the good use of free will, or even that common grace, or whatever it is by which we are distinguished from others, apart from God's grace alone, the Pelagians will always conclude that grace is given according to our merits; and that saying of Cyprian will fall: Let no one glory in anything, since nothing is our own. Rather, the saying of the Apostle: Who makes you to differ? Or what do you have that you did not receive? For are men distinguished from men by those gifts which are common to all, whether they come from nature or from grace?

units.la: Ut autem gratia sit gratia, necesse est ut omni dignitatis aut dispositionis pro priæ respectu sepositio, fateamur, quod res est, tantummodo diuini esse muneris, & quidem prorsus gratuiti, non solum
units.tr: But so that grace may be grace, it is necessary, setting aside all regard for one's own dignity or disposition, to confess what is the case: that it is purely a gift of God, and indeed entirely free, not only
1 Cor. 4.

units.la: Orthodoxa fides. lùm quòd gratia nobis offertur, verùm etiam multò magis, quòd oblatæ & ab alijs repudiatæ gratiæ, nos fide assentimur, & in fide ad finem usque perseueramus ad salutem: sicut Apostolus totum hoc Deo vendicat, & quod cœperit in nobis opus bonum, & quod idem perficiat ad diem Iesu Christi, operetur que in nobis velle & perficere, pro beneplacito. Et expressissima est dominica sententia: sine me nihil potestis.
units.tr: Orthodox faith. In that grace is offered to us, but much more in that, when the grace has been offered and rejected by others, we assent to it in faith, and persevere in faith to the end for salvation. So the Apostle ascribes all this to God: that he who began a good work in us will bring it to completion by the day of Jesus Christ, and that he works in us both to will and to accomplish, according to his good pleasure. And the Lord's saying is most express: Without me you can do nothing.

units.la: Si autem ea omnia à gratia pendent donantis, etiam quibus ea donaturus esset, quibus non, ex omni æternitate præscivit, ac in sua, quæ ffalli mutarique non potest præscientia dispositum, id est, prædestinavit. Nam vt supra etiam dictum est, gratia & prædestinatio illa sanctorum, hoc tantum differunt, quod prædestinatio est præparatio gratiæ, qua certissime liberantur, quicunque liberandi sunt: gratia vero iam ipsa donatio, & effectus prædestinationis. Vnde & Apostolus gratiæ prædestinationem annectens, ait: Gratia estis servati per fidem, idque non ex vobis, Dei donum est non ex ex operibus, ne quis glorietur. Ipsius enim opus sumus, conditi in Christo Iesu ad opera bona, quae praeparavit Deus, ut in iis versare-mur. Similiter ad Tim. Qui servavit nos, & vocavit vocatione sancta, non ex operibus nostris, sed ex suo proposito & gratia, quae data est nobis in Christo ante tempora saecularia.
units.tr: If, however, all these things depend on the grace of the giver, then he foreknew from all eternity to whom he would give them and to whom not, and he arranged this in his foreknowledge, which cannot fail or change, that is, he predestined it. For, as has been said above, the predestination of the saints and their grace differ only in this: predestination is the preparation of grace, by which all who are to be delivered are most certainly delivered; grace is the bestowal itself and the effect of predestination. Hence the Apostle, joining predestination to grace, says: By grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast. For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God has prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them. Similarly to Timothy: He who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works but according to his own purpose and the grace given to us in Christ before the world began.

units.la: Nimiae igitur contentionis est praedestinationi contradicere, vel suppressam eam cupere, si gratiam Dei, qua solaa pereuntibus discernimur, sincere, ut par est, confitemur, ut qui gloriatur in Domino glorietur.
units.tr: It is therefore excessive contention to contradict predestination, or to wish it suppressed, if we sincerely confess, as is right, the grace of God by which alone we are distinguished from those who perish, so that whoever glories may glory in the Lord.

units.la: III. Est & hic visus doctrinae de praedestinatione, quo ad patientiam nos instruit, & munit vera ac viva fide in afflictionibus & tentationibus quibuscunque huius aerumnosae vitae. Hinc Apostolus: Novimus diligentibus Deum omnia cooperari in bonum, iis qui secundum propositum vocati sunt. Nam quos praescivit, etiam praedestinavit, quos praedestinavit etiam vocavit, &c. Si ergo Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Quis nos separabit a caritate Dei? num persecutio? num periculum? Et passim scriptura in hunc ipsum fine inculcat prae-dedestinationem, vt scilicet firmam in Deo spem repositam habeamus, & vel in medijs oppressionibus gloriemur sub spe gloriæ Dei: vt pluribus suprà ostensum fuit contra calumniantes, quaï plus desperationis quàm consolationis doctrina hæc contineat.
units.tr: III. This aspect of the doctrine of predestination also teaches us patience and fortifies us, with a true and living faith, in whatever afflictions and temptations belong to this wretched life. Hence the Apostle: We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose. For whom he foreknew, he also predestined; whom he predestined, he also called, etc. If God is for us, who is against us? Who will separate us from the love of God? Will persecution? Will danger? And Scripture everywhere urges predestination for this very end: that we may hold a firm hope fixed in God, and may glory even in the midst of oppressions under the hope of the glory of God, as has been shown at length above against those calumniators who say that this doctrine contains more despair than consolation.

units.la: iv. Seruit excitando in nobis amori Dei, & studio bonorum operum. Quid ni enim toto pectore diligamus Deum, qui prior dilexit nos, & præteritis aliis innumeris, quibus cum æqualia nobis erant merita damnationis, elegit nos gratis ante iacta mundi fundamenta, in Christo filio suo dilecto? Et huius cum dilectionis tum electionis sensum in cordibus nostris diffundit per Spiritum sanctum? Fieri etiam non potest, quin ad studium bonorum operum incitemur, cogitantes, nos non solum ad finem, sed etiam ad media prædestinatos, qualia sunt, fides & bona opera, quæ, teste Paulo, præparauit Deus, vt in iis ambulemus. Et quid efficacius ad vitam recte instituendam vt dignum est fidelibus, quàm si assiduè recordentur. tur, fe filios & hæredes altissimi? acad tantæ gloriæ sublimitatem prædestina- tos fe, antequam nati eífent, imò ante- quam mundus eífet? vocatos, cùm ef- fent abalienati? iustificatos, cùm dam- nati? viuificatos, cùm mortui in offen- fis & peccatis? Idque nullo suo præexi- stente aut præuiflo merito, sed ex sola gratia vocantis? Quis non pro tantis beneficijs obstrictum fe Deo sentiat ad gratitudinis officia?
units.tr: It serves to kindle in us love for God and zeal for good works. Why should we not love God with our whole heart, who loved us first, and who, passing over countless others whose merits for condemnation were equal to ours, chose us freely before the foundations of the world were laid, in Christ his beloved Son? And who pours the sense of both this love and this election into our hearts through the Holy Spirit? Nor can it be that we are not stirred to zeal for good works when we consider that we are predestined not only to the end but also to the means, such as faith and good works, which, as Paul witnesses, God prepared that we should walk in them. And what is more effective for rightly ordering life, as befits the faithful, than to remember constantly that they are sons and heirs of the Most High, and that they were predestined to the height of such glory before they were born, indeed before the world was? That they were called when they were alienated, justified when they were condemned, made alive when they were dead in offences and sins? And that this happened without any merit preceding or foreseen in them, but from the grace of the one who calls alone? Who would not feel himself bound to God by the duties of gratitude for such benefits?

units.la: Atque hæc de vtilitate & necessitate doctrinæ huius attigisse sufficiat. Si quis plura nolle defiderat, legat Bucerū in cap.1. ad Eph.Zanchium lib.3.Mifcell.c.f. nec non libellum D. Lutheri de feruo arb. à cap.38.& deinceps. Vbi contra Erafmum multis defendit, doctrinam de feruo arbitrio & prædestinatione minimè reti- cendam, sed publicè & liberè prædi- candam, non obstante iudicio rationis humanæ in contrarium.
units.tr: Let this suffice concerning the usefulness and necessity of this doctrine. If anyone wishes for more, let him read Bucer on the first chapter of Ephesians, Zanchius, Miscellanies, book 3, and also Luther's little book on the bondage of the will, from chapter 38 onwards. There, against Erasmus, he defends at length that the doctrine of the bondage of the will and of predestination is by no means to be suppressed, but to be preached publicly and freely, notwithstanding the judgment of human reason to the contrary.

units.la: Nam quod ratio impia dictat, hanc doctrinam vtilitati prædicationis ad- uersam esse, quasi torpori & cupidita- tibus carnis patrocinetur, exhortationum stimulos excludat, homines ad desperationem solicitet, peccantes excusset & (quod absit) Deum iniustitiæ insimulet, & tantum non peccati autorem faciat, fatalem necessitatem stabiliat: hæc & similia meræ sunt calumniæ, & supra abunde refutata sunt suis locis.
units.tr: For the claim that this doctrine is opposed to the usefulness of preaching, since it seems to favour sloth and the desires of the flesh, removes the spur of exhortations, drives men to despair, excuses sinners and (God forbid) charges God with injustice, and all but makes him the author of sin, establishing a fatal necessity: this, and things like it, are mere calumnies, which have been abundantly refuted above in their proper places.

units.la: At inquiunt, etiamsi sequelæ istæ rationis humanæ male extruantur ex definita sententia voluntatis Dei de saluandis & damnandis, quam prædestinationem appellamus: tamen propter eos qui offenduntur, doctrina hac tametsi vera, tacenda potius quam diceda & proponenda est. Argumentum erit tale:
units.tr: But they say: even if these consequences are wrongly drawn by human reason from the fixed decision of God's will concerning whom to save and whom to damn, which we call predestination, nevertheless, on account of those who take offence, this doctrine, although true, ought rather to be kept silent than spoken and proposed. The argument will run thus:

units.la: Verum sæpe tacendum est propter eos qui capere non possunt: exemplo Christi. Adhuc habeo vobis multa dicere, sed non potestis modo portare: & Apostoli, Non potui vobis loqui quasi spiritualibus, sed quasi carnalibus, quasi pueris in Christo lac dedi, non escam. Nondum enim poteratis: sed nec adhuc quidem potestis.
units.tr: It is often necessary to keep silent on account of those who cannot grasp a thing, as in the example of Christ: "I have yet many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now." And the Apostle: "I could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to carnal people, as to infants in Christ; I gave you milk, not solid food. For you were not yet able, nor are you even now able."

units.la: In confessio autem est, plurimos doctrinam prædestinationis non posse capere.
units.tr: But it is agreed that very many cannot grasp the doctrine of predestination.

units.la: Ergo propter eos tacenda est: ne videlicet dolores eos faciamus qui non intelligunt, dum voluvolumus eos qui intelligunt facere doctiores.
units.tr: Therefore it must be kept silent on their account, namely lest we cause pain to those who do not understand, while we wish to make those who do understand more learned.

units.la: Ad hoc argumentum quondam ia- statum à Semipelagianis, respodet Au-gust. noster de bono perseu. cap.16. Respo-det autem ad maiorem, quę nō nisi par-ticularis est, & tum valet cum periculū tantum incurritur verum dicendo, non etiam tacendo. August. verbis explica-bo. Causas, inquit, verū tacendi longum est omnes quærere, vel inserere: hæc tamen vna est, ne peiores faciamus eos qui non intelligut, dum volumus eos qui intelligut facere doctio-res, qui nobis aliquid tale tacentibus doctiores quidem non fiunt, sed nec peiores fiunt. Cum au-te res vera ita se habet, vt peior fiat nobis eam dicentibus, ille qui capere nō potest, nobis autē tacentibus, ille qui potest: nōne potius est dice-dum verū, vt qui potest capere, capiat, quàm tacendum, vt non solum id ambo nō capiant, verūm etiam qui est intelligentior, peior eua-dat: quī si caperet, per illum etiā plures disce-rent? Dicatur ergo verū, maximē vbi quæstio aliqua vt dicatur, impellit, & capiant qui pos-sunt: ne forte cum tacetur propter eos qui ca-pere non possut, non solum, veritate frauden-tur, verūm etiā falsitate capiantur, qui capere possunt.
units.tr: He answers this argument, which the Semipelagians once put forward, in his book On the Gift of Perseverance, chapter 16. He answers the major premise, which is only particular, and which holds only when the danger is incurred by speaking the truth, not also by keeping silent. I will explain it in Augustine's words: "It would be a long task to seek out and set down all the reasons for concealing the truth; yet this one is the only one: lest we make worse those who do not understand, while we wish to make those who understand more learned, who, if we were to keep silent about such things, do not become more learned but also do not become worse. But when the truth is such that it makes worse those who hear it from us, the one who cannot grasp it, while if we keep silent, it is the one who can grasp it who suffers: is it not rather to be spoken, so that he who can grasp it may grasp it, than kept silent, so that not only do both fail to grasp it, but also the one who is more intelligent becomes worse? For if he grasped it, through him many more would be taught. Let the truth therefore be spoken, especially where some question presses for it to be spoken, and let those who can grasp it, grasp it: lest perhaps, when it is kept silent on account of those who cannot grasp it, not only are those who can grasp it deprived of the truth, but they are also caught in falsehood."

units.la: Verum quidam ita, ut qui capere queat. possunt. Eadem, licet aliis verbis Lutheri quoque solutio est de servo arb. cap. 40.
units.tr: Some, however, read it thus: "the one who is able to grasp it," and "who can." The same solution, though in other words, is also Luther's, in On the Bondage of the Will, chapter 40.

units.la: Facilime autem distinctio illa confirmatur. Nonne doctrina gratiæ & iustificationis per solam fidem in Iesum Christum, multi hodie offenduntur, & offendebantur iam olim, ut de ipsis Apostolis male loquerentur, & metiren- tur eos dicere, faciamus mala ut eveniant bona: peccemus, ut gratia augustior fiat? Nec tamen nostro silentio idcirco vera de gratia & iustificatione hominis doctrina premenda est, committendumue, ut quisquam falsa persuasione operum & meritorum suorum illusus, pereat. Sic, teste Paulo, Christus crucifixus Iudæis quidem offendiculum, Græcis vero stultitia erat. An propterea quicquam Paulus de solita sua diligentia in annunciando sermone crucis remisit? Imo quia per stultam prædicationem Deo visum est servare credentes, non decreuit quicquā scire nisi Iesum Crucifixum. Valeat igitur præpostera cautio illorum, qui doctrinam prædestinationis, quod a iudicio carnis abhorreat
units.tr: That distinction is very easily confirmed. Do not many today take offence at the doctrine of grace and of justification by faith alone in Jesus Christ, and did they not take offence long ago too, so that they spoke ill of the Apostles themselves and judged them, saying: "Let us do evil that good may come; let us sin so that grace may abound"? Yet for all that, the true doctrine of grace and of man's justification must not on that account be suppressed in our silence, nor should anyone, deceived by a false confidence in his works and merits, be allowed to perish. So, as Paul witnesses, Christ crucified was indeed a stumbling block to the Jews and foolishness to the Greeks. Did Paul therefore relax anything of his customary diligence in preaching the word of the cross? Rather, because it pleased God to save believers through foolish preaching, he resolved to know nothing except Jesus Christ crucified. Let, then, the preposterous caution of those who think the doctrine of predestination, because it shrinks from the judgment of the flesh, should be buried in silence, be of no avail.

units.la: 1. Cor. 1. „reat, silentio sepeliendam autumant. „ Nos contra stamus iudicio spiritus, & „ imperandum dicimus rationi, cū vbi- „ que alibi in causis fidei, tum praesertim „ in hac.Sic futurum est,vt doctrinae cae- „ lestis mysteria nobis patescant & dul- „ cefcant.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 1. They think it should be buried in silence. We, on the contrary, stand by the judgment of the Spirit, and we say that reason must be brought under command, both everywhere else in matters of faith and especially in this one. So it will come about that the mysteries of heavenly doctrine are opened to us and become sweet.

units.la: Quod porrò afferebatur, antiquio- res Patres ante Augustinum catholi- cam fidem per tot annos defendisse, etiam sine hac praedestinationis definitione; Ad id respondetur, Patres aliquos non prorsus hac de re tacuisse. Nam & ipsi gratiam Dei veram, sicut praedicada est,praedicarunt:id est,quā nulla humana merita praecedūt: Quod Aug.testimonijs Cypriani Ambrosij & aliorū luculenter ostendit cap. 19. de bono perf.
units.tr: As for the further objection, that the earlier Fathers before Augustine defended the catholic faith for so many years even without this definition of predestination: to this it is answered that some of the Fathers did not altogether keep silent on this matter. For they too preached the true grace of God, as it must be preached, that is, the grace which no human merits precede. Augustine shows this clearly from the testimonies of Cyprian, Ambrose and others, in chapter 19 of On the Gift of Perseverance.

units.la: Cypriani illa celebris vox est.In nullo gloriandum, quando nihil nostrum est. Ambrosius vero dixit,Non est in potestate nostra cor nostrum & cogitationes nostrae: Item, a Deo praeparatur voluntas hominum, & quod honorificatur in sanctis, id ipsius gratia est.Idem super Lucam, tractans de Samaritanis Christum recipere nolentibus: bus:Simul disce, inquit, quia recipere noluit non simpliciter conuersos. Nam si voluisset, ex in deuotis fecisset deuotos. Nam quos dignatur, vocat, & quem vult, religiosum facit. Citatur ab Augustino & Gregorius Nazianzenus, qui vtrumque donum Dei esse testatur, & credere in Deum, & quod credimus confiteri. Accedit huc etiam Ecclesiæ totius consensus, quæ nunquam de hac re tacuit in precibus suis. Quando enim non orauit Ecclesia pro infidelibus & inimicis suis vt crederent? & pro fidelibus, vt in fide ad fidem vsque perseuerarent? Neque aliud in oratione Dominica orant fideles, præsertim dicentes: Ne nos inducas in tentationem, nisi vt in sancta obedientia diuino munere perseueret. Sicut ergo in his orationibus, ita & in hac fide, qua creditur gratiam Dei non secundum merita accipientium dari, nata est, creuit, & crescit Ecclesia: quandoquidem non oraret Ecclesia, vt daretur infidelibus fides, fidelibus in fide perseuerantia, nisi semper ea dona Dei vtique credidisset.
units.tr: Cyprian's famous saying is: "There is no ground for boasting, since nothing is ours." Ambrose said: "Our heart and our thoughts are not in our power." Likewise: "The will of men is prepared by God, and what is honoured in the saints is his grace." The same, on Luke, treating of the Samaritans who refused to receive Christ: "Learn at the same time that he did not wish to receive those who were not simply converted. For if he had wished, he would have made devout ones out of the undevout. For whom he deigns to call, he calls; and whom he wills, he makes religious." Gregory Nazianzen is also cited by Augustine, who testifies that both are God's gift: to believe in God, and that we confess what we believe. To this is added the agreement of the whole Church, which has never kept silent about this matter in its prayers. For when has the Church not prayed for unbelievers and its enemies, that they might believe, and for the faithful, that they might persevere in faith unto faith? Nor do the faithful pray anything else in the Lord's Prayer, especially when they say: "Lead us not into temptation," except that they may persevere in holy obedience by the divine gift. So, just as in these prayers, so too in this faith, by which it is believed that grace is given not according to the merits of those who receive it, the Church was born, has grown, and grows; since the Church would not pray that faith be given to unbelievers and perseverance in faith to believers, unless it had always believed that those gifts were of God.

units.la: Quis
units.tr: Who

units.la: Cap. 27. De Divina
units.tr: Chapter 27. On the Divine

units.la: Quis autem dicet, patres istos & vniuersam adeo Ecclesiam, sic confef- fos Dei gratiam, vt auderent negare eius praescientiam, quam non solum docti sed etiam indocti confitentur?
units.tr: But who will say that those Fathers, and the whole Church too, who confessed the grace of God so thoroughly, would dare to deny his foreknowledge, which not only the learned but also the unlearned acknowledge?

units.la: Porro ii haec ita Deum nouerant dare, vt non ignorarent eum daturum se ef- fe praescijse, & quibus daturus esset; procul dubio nouerant praedestinatio- nem sanctorum. Haec enim nihil aliud est quàm praescientia & praeparatio be- neficiorum Dei, quibus certissime li- berantur, quicunque liberantur: caete- ris in massa perditionis iusto diuino iu- dicio relictis.
units.tr: Moreover, they understood God to give these things in such a way that they did not fail to know that he had foreseen that he would give them, and to whom he would give them; without doubt they knew the predestination of the saints. For this is nothing other than the foreknowledge and preparation of the benefits of God, by which those who are delivered are most certainly delivered, the rest being left in the mass of perdition by the just judgement of God.

units.la: Tota haec refponsio Augustini est cap.14.19.24. & passim de bono perseueran- tia. Sciendum tamen hic est, priusquam haeresis Pelagiana oriretur (quod euenit Augustino iā Episcopo) Patres breuiter duntaxat quibusdam scriptorum suorum locis, quid de gratia Dei senti- rent attigisse; immorantes interim in alijs quae aduersus alios inimicos Ecclesiae disputabant, & in exhortationi- bus ad quasque virtutes, quibus Deo seruiseruiendum est. Sed alia est ratio temporum, ex quo Pelagius virus suum euomuit: tum necessitas ipsa coegit orthodoxos, loca scripturarum quibus prædestinatio, & quæ secundum eam datur gratia, commendatur, copiosius & enucleatius defendendi. Nam tcfte Auguft. singulæ quæque hæresis propriæ quasdam quæstiones intulerunt & necessitatem attulerunt diligentius scrutandi & defendendi scripturas diuinas, quàm si nulla talis necessitas cogeret.
units.tr: This whole response is Augustine's, in chapters 14, 19 and 24, and passim, concerning the gift of perseverance. Yet it must be noted here that, before the Pelagian heresy arose (which happened to Augustine when he was already a bishop), the Fathers had touched only briefly, in certain passages of their writings, on what they thought about the grace of God, dwelling meanwhile on other matters which they disputed against other enemies of the Church, and in exhortations to each of the virtues by which God must be served. But the circumstances of the times changed from the moment Pelagius spewed out his poison: then the very necessity compelled the orthodox to defend more fully and clearly the passages of Scripture by which predestination, and the grace given according to it, are commended. For, as Augustine witnesses, each heresy brought its own particular questions and created a necessity of examining and defending the divine Scriptures more diligently than if no such necessity had compelled them.

units.la: CAPVT VLTIMVM. Quod sobrie & prudenter prædicanda sit prædestinatio.
units.tr: THE LAST CHAPTER. That predestination ought to be preached soberly and prudently.

units.la: DOCTRINA Migitur de prædestinatione vtiliter in Ecclesia retineri, atque etiam postulante occasione recte ad populum prædicari, manifestu factu est. Sed quomodo & quo sermone id fiat, magni ad ædificationem interest. Ad hoc autem & sobrietate & prudentia Christiana opus est.
units.tr: It has now been made clear that the doctrine of predestination is usefully retained in the Church, and that it is rightly preached to the people when the occasion calls for it. But how and in what manner this is done is of great importance for edification, and for this both Christian sobriety and prudence are required.

units.la: Nā si vsquam alibi, certè hic tenendū est, quod Apostolus ait, Δεῖ φρονεῖν τὸ σωφρονεῖν sapiendum ad sobrietatem. Nimi-rum iuxta ea duntaxat de praedestina-tione sentiendum & loquendum est, quæ in scripturis tradita sunt. Ijs enim quod satis, quodq; certū & solidum est, continetur: quæ si cui non satissaciant, is ne speret aliunde veritatis cognitio-nem. Coerceatur ergo ratio impia & dicax, quæ dum verbo Dei obstrepere audet, omnem in hoc negocio difficul-tatem parit, &labyrinthum ingreditur, cuius nullum postea reperit exitum. Coërceatur etiam curiositas in genere, ne vltra quàm tutum est, quámque nostra patitur infirmitas, progredia-mur, ad scrutandum quæ Deus in se-ipso abscondita esse voluit. Quoniam potentia Dei magna est, inquit Sapiens, & ab humilibus consequitur gloriam. Altiora te ne quæsieris, & quæ tuas vires superant: sed quæ tibi mandata sunt à Deo, ea meditare sanctè. Neque enim opus tibi est, quæ sunt arcana, oculis cernere, & iam an-tea plura quàm humanus sensus capiat, patefacta tefacta sunt &c. Unde ab Augustt. scite dictum est, esse quandam doctam ignorantiam, eamque præferendam scientiæ temerariæ.
units.tr: For if anywhere, surely here we must hold to what the Apostle says: "Δεῖ φρονεῖν τὸ σωφρονεῖν" [we must think so as to be sober]. Namely, we are to think and speak of predestination only according to what has been handed down in the Scriptures. For in these is contained whatever is sufficient, and certain and solid; and if anyone is not satisfied by these, let him not hope to gain knowledge of the truth from elsewhere. Thus the impious and insolent reason is to be restrained, which, while it dares to clamour against the Word of God, creates every difficulty in this matter and enters a labyrinth from which it afterwards finds no way out. Curiosity in general is also to be restrained, so that we do not advance further than is safe, and further than our weakness allows, to search into what God has willed to keep hidden in himself. "For the power of God is great," says the Wise Man, "and he gains glory from the humble. Do not seek out things higher than you, nor things that exceed your strength; but meditate reverently on what God has commanded you. For you have no need to see with your eyes what is secret, since many things beyond the grasp of human sense have already been disclosed to you, etc." Hence Augustine rightly said that there is a certain learned ignorance, and that it is to be preferred to rash knowledge.

units.la: Verum vt odiosæ curiositatis est scrutari occulta : ita negligere quæ Dominus reuelata esse voluit, ingratitudinis est nô ferendæ. Medium autem est sobrietas Christiana, vt quod tuto facere possumus, scripturam sequamur, quæ velut materno incessu submissius graditur, ne infirmitatem nostram deserat.
units.tr: Yet just as it is the mark of a hateful curiosity to search out hidden things, so to neglect what the Lord has willed to be revealed is an ingratitude that cannot be tolerated. Christian sobriety stands between the two: what we can safely do, we should follow in Scripture, which walks more humbly, as with a mother's step, so that it does not leave behind our weakness.

units.la: Sed & prudentia sobrietati adiungenda est, quæ obseruabit, vt ad captum auditorum, & monstrato vero vsu, & sine verborum offensione doctrina hæc proponatur ad ædificationem auditorum. Nam dolosi vel imperiti medici est, etiam vtile medicamentum sic allegare, vt non prosit, imo obsit.
units.tr: But prudence must also be joined with sobriety, which will take care that this doctrine is set forth in a way suited to the capacity of the hearers, both by showing the true use of it and without offence to their words, for the edification of the hearers. For it is the mark of a deceitful or unskilled physician to prescribe even a useful medicine in such a way that it does not help but harms.

units.la: Quod de captu auditorum dico, eadem hoc loco valet admonitio, quæ alibi, vt discernatur, quibus lactis potu tanquam pueris in Christo, quibus solidiore lidiore cibo, tanquam adultiore ætates opus sit. Qua de re optimè Lutherus præf. ad Rom. Necesse est, inquit, lactentes in Christo primum adolescere, antequam meracum hoc bibant. Nam & hic est sua quædam pueritia, cui lacte interim opus est, dum solido cibo assuescat. Ideoque perstringit curiosulos, qui antequam Christum & virtutem crucis discant, abyssum illam prædestinationis scrutantur, cum iuxta seriem Apost. ad Rom. prius discenda sit cognitio Christi, & mortificatio veteris hominis, atque hinc ad crucem & tribulationes progrediendum. Tum vero inquit, dulcescet necessitas hæc prædestinationis, & quam plena consolationis sit sententiæ.
units.tr: What I say about the capacity of the hearers, the same admonition applies here as elsewhere: they must be distinguished, so that some are given milk to drink, as infants in Christ, and others need more solid food, as those of riper age. On this matter Luther well says in his preface to Romans: "It is necessary," he says, "that those who are milk-fed in Christ first grow up before they drink this unmixed wine. For there is here also a certain childhood of its own, which for the time needs milk, until it becomes accustomed to solid food. Therefore he rebukes the over-curious, who, before they learn Christ and the power of the cross, search into that abyss of predestination, whereas, according to the sequence of the Apostle in Romans, the knowledge of Christ and the mortification of the old man must first be learned, and from there one must proceed to the cross and tribulations. Then, he says, this necessity of predestination will become sweet, and how full of consolation is the sentence."

units.la: Porro de usu prædestinationis simul commonefaciendi sunt auditores, cum sermo de ea instituitur: ne scilicet ea abutantur ad licentiam carnis, vel ad desperationem, odium & blasphemiā Dei: sed utantur potius ad Dei gloriam & amorem, studiumque bonorum operum excitandum, sustentandamque fidem cum omni tolerantia & consolatione in omnibus afflictionibus, certò stastatuendo nihil esse quod nos separare queat à caritate Dei erga nos in Christo Iesu, Domino nostro.
units.tr: Moreover, when the sermon on predestination is undertaken, the hearers must at the same time be reminded of its use, lest they abuse it for licence of the flesh, or for despair, hatred and blasphemy of God; but rather let them use it to kindle the glory and love of God and the zeal for good works, and to sustain faith with all patience and consolation in all afflictions, firmly holding that nothing can separate us from the love of God toward us in Christ Jesus our Lord.

units.la: Denique quod ad modum & forma docendi pertinet, cautione opus est, vt quæ vere dicuntur, congruenter etiam dicantur, ad cauendam, quoad licet, offensionem audientium. Quippe plurimum refert, quomodo & qua docendi ratione quippiam proponatur.
