Exempli gratia: si quis ad Ecclesiam de prædestinatione verba faciens dicat, sive curratis siue dormiatis, quod vos prædestinauit, qui falli non potest, hoc eritis: ipsa sui prædicatione apud impe- ritos redargui quodammodo videtur prædestinatio, sicut redargui videtur & præscientia Dei (quam certè negare nemo potest) si dicatur hominibus: si- ue curratis siue dormiatis, quod vos præsciuit, qui falli non potest, hoc eri- tis. Conuenientius dicitur: Sic curri- te, vt comprehendatis, atque vt ipso cursu vestro noueritis vos esse præco- gnitos, & ad prædestinationem diuinæ gratiæ pertinere. Ita durius dicitur, si
units.tr: Finally, as regards the manner and form of teaching, care is needed so that what is said truly is also said fittingly, in order to avoid, as far as possible, offence to the hearers. Indeed it matters greatly how and by what method of teaching something is set forth. For example: if someone, speaking to the Church about predestination, should say, "whether you run or sleep, you will be what he who cannot be mistaken has predestined you to be," then predestination, by its very proclamation, seems in some way to be refuted among the unskilled, just as the foreknowledge of God (which no one can certainly deny) would seem to be refuted if it were said to men, "whether you run or sleep, you will be what he who cannot be mistaken has foreknown you to be." It is more fittingly said: "Run so that you may obtain, and so that by your very running you may know that you are foreknown and belong to the predestination of divine grace." It is put more harshly if one should address the Christian people in this way:

units.la: „ quis plebem Christianam ad huc mo- „ dum compellet : Quod alij ex vobis „ creditis, alij non creditis, ideo fit,quia „ adiutorium gratiæ miserantis alij acce- „ pistis,alij nondu accepistis. Veruntame „ li qui estis electi,licet nondu vocati,ac- „ cipietis eandé gratiá. Quid opus est di- „ ci: alij ex vobis? Si enim Ecclesiæ Dei „ loquimur , li credentibus loquimur, „ cur gratiam aliquos eorum accepisse „ dicentes,cæteris facere iniuriam iudi- „ camur? Conuenietius ita dici poterat. „ Ita fe habet prædestinatio voluntatis „ Dei, vt accepta gratia ex infidelitate „ veneritis ad fide, idque non ex vobis, „ Dei donam est,ne quis glorietur.Si qui „ autem adhuc in peccatis versamini:có- „ uertimini, excitamini, surgite a mor- „ tuis:Itɛm,fi qui sunt nondum vocati, „ pro eis vt vocentur oremus. Fortassis „ enim sic electi sunt,vt nostris orationi- „ bus concedantur,&accipiant nobifcu „ eandem gratiam. Nonne sic & verius eadem res & congruentius dicitur? De hoc plura Augustinus noster,quem fe- pius citaui,theologus fine controuer- fia*
units.tr: "Because some of you believe and others do not, this happens because some of you have received the help of merciful grace, and others have not yet received it. Yet those of you who are elect, although not yet called, will receive the same grace. What need is there to say 'some of you'? For if we are speaking to the Church of God, we are speaking to believers; why, in saying that some of them have received grace, do we judge that we do an injury to the others? It could be said more fittingly thus: 'Such is the predestination of the will of God, that, having received grace, you have come from unbelief to faith, and this not from yourselves, it is the gift of God, lest anyone should boast. But if any of you still live in sins, be converted, be roused, arise from the dead. Likewise, for those who are not yet called, let us pray that they may be called. For perhaps they are so elect that through our prayers they may be granted, and receive the same grace with us.'" Is not the same matter put thus, and more truly and more fittingly? Our Augustine, whom I have often cited, a theologian without controversy great, learned, candid, orthodox, and an outstanding patron of the orthodox faith, as Hilary praised him, writes more about this. Let those who desire more exact knowledge go to him.

units.la: {*} De bono perf.ca.14 fia magnus, eruditus, candidus, ortho-doxus, & orthodoxæ fidei insignis patronus, vt ab Hilario laudatus est. Eum igitur adeant qui exactiora nosse desiderant.
units.tr: Such is what I have said so far about the eternal predestination of God, who alone is wise, merciful and just. To him be honour and blessing for ever and ever. Amen, etc.

units.la: Atque hæc hactenus de æterna Dei, solius sapientis, misericordis, iusti prædestinatione. Ei sit honor & benedictio in sæcula sæculorum Amen, &c. ★ ✶ ✶
